title: CHANGE PARK ASSIST DELAY TIMER
text:
# CHANGE PARK ASSIST DELAY TIMER

## Knowledge

### Concept

 In the Vehicle Setup screen, navigate to and select the Park Assist option. The system displays the Park Assist Setup screen.

### Concept

 Tap on Tone Type and select the required tone from the list provided.

### Concept

The system allows you to retain the Park Assist display screen even after the Reverse gear is disengaged. This feature is called as Park Assist Delay Timer.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p59_img00` (page 59, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p59_img00.png`

### Concept

When in a closed parking lot, you have to disen- gage and engage the Reverse gear multiple times for parking your vehicle within the availa- ble space. The Park Assist Delay Timer feature, when enabled, will retain the park assist screen for a pre-configured time even when the Re- verse gear is disengaged

### Concept

To change park assist delay timer:

### Concept

 In the Vehicle Setup screen, navigate to and select the Park Assist option. The system displays the Park Assist Setup screen.

### Concept

 Tap on Delay Timer and select the required timer option from 0 sec/5 sec/10 sec. When the Park Assist compo- nent is enabled next, the system retains the Park Assist display screen even after the Reverse gear is disen- gaged for the selected time period.

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to control lighting fea- tures like Approach Lamp and DRL if your vehicle is equipped with these features.

### Concept

If the vehicle is equipped with this feature, you can set the Approach Lamp illumination time period from the infotain- ment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p59_img01` (page 59, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p59_img01.png`

## Provenance

title: CONFIGURING AUTO SMS ON CALL REJECTION
text:
# CONFIGURING AUTO SMS ON CALL REJECTION

## Knowledge

### Concept

If you select the Notify with Popup option, the system can also readout the new SMS to you. Refer to “Enable SMS Readout” section.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p76_img01` (page 76, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p76_img01.png`

### Procedure

When you receive an incoming phone call, you can either ac- cept or reject it. If you reject a call, you can set an automatic reply to the caller via SMS. You can select from a list of pre- defined texts or you can configure your own text for the SMS which will be sent using Configuring Auto SMS feature.

### Concept

To configure the automatic SMS text:

### Concept

 In the Phone Setup, navigate to and open Configuring Auto SMS.

### Concept

 The system lists various options with different texts.

### Concept

 Scroll to and select the required SMS text. The system sets the selected option for automatic reply and sends the text as SMS when you reject an incoming call with SMS next time.

### Concept

 You can write your own text in last two options as per your requirement.

### Concept

Figure 36: On Screen Keypad

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p76_img00` (page 76, confidence 0.966)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p76_img00.png`

### Concept

The SMS text message can be of maximum 120 characters.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p76_img02` (page 76, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p76_img02.png`

### Concept

The system allows you to manage different volume settings as per your need, like:

### Concept

### Concept

 Notification volume

title: SYSTEM CARE AND MAINTENANCE
text:
# SYSTEM CARE AND MAINTENANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Please read and follow the safety guidelines listed in this sec- tion to avoid injury or property damage .

### Concept

GENERAL SAFETY GUIDELINES

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p9_img00` (page 9, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p9_img00.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system is a sophisticated elec- tronic device. Do not allow improper access of the infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p9_img01` (page 9, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p9_img01.png`

### Warning

Permanent hearing loss may occur if you play your music at loud volumes for prolonged dura- tion. Exercise caution when setting the volume of your infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p9_img02` (page 9, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p9_img02.png`

### Concept

Exposure of the infotainment system to water or excessive moisture can cause electric shocks, fire, or other damages.

### Concept

SAFETY GUIDELINES WHILE DRIVING

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p9_img03` (page 9, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p9_img03.png`

### Concept

Glance at the screen of the infotainment system only when necessary and safe to do so. If pro- longed viewing of the screen is necessary, park the vehicle at a safe location and engage the park brake.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p9_img04` (page 9, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p9_img04.png`

### Concept

Make certain that the volume level of the info- tainment system is set to a level that allows you to hear outside traffic and other warnings.

### Concept

Exert utmost care while handling the infotainment system, as partial or complete loss of the infotainment system functions due to intentional misuse is not covered under warranty. Some guidance for using or maintaining the system are listed below:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p9_img05` (page 9, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p9_img05.png`

### Concept

Parking under direct sunlight for prolonged du- ration can result in high temperatures inside your car, which can damage your infotainment system, if used. So, before using the system let the car interior to cool down.

### Concept

Do not open the infotainment system, as incor- rect handling can damage the system. Further, warranty is void, if seal is broken.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p10_img00` (page 10, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_002_p10_img01` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not replace the vehicle speakers or fit addi- tional speakers with aftermarket speakers. It may lead to the malfunctioning or even damage of the infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p10_img02` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img02.png`

### Concept

Do not apply sticky or strong alcohol based spray, lotion or liquid on the infotainment sys- tem while cleaning the vehicle dashboard. This may cause permanent damage to the system button functions, knob operations or the display screen. It may also lead to the deterioration of the system paint.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p10_img03` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img03.png`

### Concept

Usage of paint or color on the infotainment sys- tem can make the moving parts sticky and stop them from functioning correctly.

### Concept

Avoid addition of any accessories such as exter- nal amplifiers, which will lead to the modifica- tion of the standard factory wiring connections. As such unauthorized interconnections can re- sult in the malfunctioning of the infotainment system. Always contact the Tata Authorized Dealer for the changes to the vehicle or system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p10_img04` (page 10, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img04.png`
- Image: `doc_002_p10_img05` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img05.png`

### Concept

Ensure that any liquid does not enter the info- tainment system, as it will lead to the failure of radio. The warranty of the system will be void, if liquid ingress marks are observed inside the system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p10_img06` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img06.png`

### Concept

Do not use excessive force while handling the infotainment system, USB slot, AUX-In slot and so on. It might cause damage to the system or component.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p10_img07` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p10_img07.png`

### Concept

Avoid usage of hard or sharp objects like pen, key, USB stick etc. to touch the screen, as it can cause scratches on the screen surface.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p11_img00` (page 11, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p11_img00.png`

### Concept

Use a soft, clean and dry cleaning cloth to clean the touch screen surface. If required, use a lint- free cloth damped with a cleaning solution such as isopropyl alcohol, or an isopropyl alcohol and water solution ratio of 50:50. Be sure to follow the solvent manufacturer's precautions and di- rections.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p11_img01` (page 11, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p11_img01.png`

### Concept

Avoid spraying or spilling of cleaning solutions, perfumes, car fresheners, beverages, caustic chemicals or any liquids on the touch screen surface, as it can damage the screen or the info- tainment system.

### Concept

The warranty clauses applicable to the infotainment system are listed below:

### Concept

1. Warranty is applicable only in India.

2. Warranty for the product is against defective materials and manufacturing faults for 36 months / 60,000 km (whichever comes earlier) from the date of the first sale of vehicle. 3. text:
# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)

## Knowledge

### Concept

files. It is to be noted that this behavior might vary from phone to phone based your phone specific implementation.

### Concept

From what all the Media sources I can play video?

### Concept

You can play video only from USB.

### Concept

Can I See / Play audio / Video / pictures from my smartphone when connected through USB port?

### Concept

Yes. However you have to enable your phone in Mass Storage Class mode just after connection to Car USB port. This behav- ior might vary based on smartphone which you are using.

### Concept

What are the supported video and audio codecs?

### Concept

The supported video and audio codecs are as follows:

### Concept

 Video Codecs: H.264 (BP, MP and HP up to AVC Level 3.2), MPEG4 (Simple and Advanced Simple Profile - All Levels)

### Concept

 Audio Codecs - Profile Supported: MP3, AAC

### Concept

 Container File: AVI, MP4

### Concept

I am unable to connect my Phone to the infotainment system using a USB cable however, I am able to connect through Bluetooth. Can you please help me with a solution?

### Concept

The USB cable that you are using to connect the Phone with the infotainment system might not be compatible with your Phone. Please use only the USB cable provided by the Phone Manufacturer.

### Concept

I am unable to connect to Android Auto. I have followed all steps specified. What could be the cause of the problem?

### Concept

If the connection between the Android Auto application and the infotainment system fails, this problem could arise. The connection will fail due to one of the following reasons:

### Concept

 Bluetooth connection was unsuccessful or connection was lost

### Concept

 If the infotainment system date and time does not match with the Phone data and time settings.

## Knowledge

The infotainment system allows you to access various media, climate, phone and other controls using voice commands.

### Concept

The system will start recognizing your voice commands only after the beep. So, speak your command only after you hear the voice activa- tion beep. If no command is spoken after the beep, the system will prompt you to say a com- mand.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p61_img03` (page 61, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p61_img03.png`

### Concept

 When similar sounding contact names/song names are spoken, the system will display a list of options match- ing the spoken name. You can choose the required op- tion from the list by calling out the corresponding line number or touching the required option on the screen.

### Concept

 Only speak the commands that are listed in the “Voice Recognition Commands” section.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_002/p61_img04.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system also displays the voice recognition commands. You can se- lect and view the required command de- tails from within the Voice screen.

### Concept

 Speak the commands and names in a neutral English accent for best results.

### Concept

 Do not take long pauses (greater than 1 second) while speaking the words in a command. Speak the words of the command at a constant rate.

### Concept

 Avoid varying your pitch and volume while speaking the commands. Speak clearly and loudly at a reasonable speed.

### Concept

 Ensure that there is no noise disturbance when you speak the commands like, other passengers in the ve- hicle are talking or there is lot of wind noise. Disturb- ance from external sound sources may result in poor voice recognition.

### Concept

 Always face forward while speaking your commands as the voice recognition quality is best in this orientation.

title: ANDROID AUTO CONFIGURATION
text:
# ANDROID AUTO CONFIGURATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

Android Auto is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Android smartphones from your vehicle infotain- ment system. You can use voice actions or simple arrange- ment of Google Maps, Google Play Music and other important phone functions to access the required functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

### Concept

The Android Auto feature requires the installation of the An- droid Auto Mobile App, which can be downloaded on your smartphone from Google Play Store.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p82_img00` (page 82, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p82_img00.png`

### Concept

Android smartphones with android version 5.0 (Lollipop) or greater supports the Android Auto app. For best performance, Google recom- mends Android version 6.0 (Marshmallow) or above. For more information, refer to

### Concept

https://support.google.com/androidauto/an- swer/6348190?hl=en

### Concept

Before you connect the Android Auto app on your smartphone with the infotainment system, you need to perform the some one-time configuration steps:

### Concept

 Make sure your phone is running Android 5.0 (Lollipop) and up. For best performance, Google recommend An- droid 6.0 (Marshmallow) and up.

### Concept

 Download the Android Auto app from Google Play.

### Concept

 Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection

### Concept

Android Auto is by default enabled on your vehi- cle. (if available)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p82_img01` (page 82, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p82_img01.png`

### Concept

 For your safety, ensure your vehicle is ON and in the parked condition and the Park Brake is engaged.

### Concept

 Connect your phone to your car using a USB cable.

### Concept

 Your phone might ask you to download or update cer- tain apps, like Google Maps.

### Concept

 Review the Safety Information and Android Auto permis- sions to access your apps.

### Concept

 Turn on notifications for Android Auto. For the best ex- perience, we recommend accepting all requests.

### Concept

Your phone’s Bluetooth will be turned on auto- matically when Android Auto is connected to the car via USB.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p83_img00` (page 83, confidence 0.979)

title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
text:
# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)

## Knowledge

### Concept

How do I initiate/ start Android Auto/CarPlay in the infotain- ment system?

### Concept

Please refer to Android Auto and Apple CarPlay sections for details.

### Concept

To use Android Auto/CarPlay, do we have any specific Smartphone/iPhone version requirements?

### Concept

For Android Auto the required specification is, Android smartphones with android version 5.0 or greater. For CarPlay the requirement is, iPhone 5 and above versions.

### Concept

Can I use my phone while I have connected to the infotain- ment system for Android Auto and I am currently using its functionalities?

### Concept

Yes, you can use your phone, while connected to the infotain- ment system for Android Auto and the application is currently in use.

### Concept

Where can I get the list of apps that are compatible with An- droid Auto/Car Play?

### Concept

 Apps compatible with Android Auto: From Android Auto Browse menu-> More Apps option.

### Concept

 Apps compatible with CarPlay: Listed on the CarPlay app Home screen.

### Concept

How do I use Google Voice Recognition while Android Auto is connected and running on the infotainment system?

### Concept

You can enable OK Google using any one of the following ways:

### Concept

 To activate OK Google (voice recognition) so that your voice actions are recognized, press the mike icon.

### Concept

 You can also enable OK Google by doing a Long Press on the Voice command Steering Wheel control element.

### Concept

Can Android Auto and CarPlay be used simultaneously?

### Concept

No, Android Auto and CarPlay cannot be used simultaneously from the infotainment system. You need to disconnect one app before connecting and using the other.

title: TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS FOR PAIRING DEVICES
text:
# TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS FOR PAIRING DEVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

 The system searches and displays a list for nearby Blue- tooth Devices, tap or select your device name to pro- ceed.

### Concept

 On selection, the system initiates the pairing by prompt- ing a confirmation message for passcode matching on both devices.

### Concept

 On confirmation, the pairing is successful and you can use Phone features as per your need, the system dis- plays your device name in the Paired Devices screen and in QAD.

### Concept

When the pairing is initiated, the currently con- nected device(s) must be temporarily discon- nected. The system will prompt you with a con- firmation message for disconnecting the con- nected paired devices.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p45_img00` (page 45, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p45_img00.png`

### Concept

GUIDELINES FOR PAIRING DEVICES

### Concept

Some of the guidelines for successfully pairing and connect- ing your phone with the infotainment system are:

### Concept

 Ensure that Bluetooth feature is switched ON in your phone for successful pairing or auto-reconnection with the infotainment system.

### Concept

 Ensure that the phone and the infotainment system are set to be visible to one another (refer to the Bluetooth Setup settings of your phone and infotainment system).

### Concept

 Ensure that your phone is not in Battery Saver or Air- plane mode.

### Concept

 Ensure that the phone and infotainment system are in proximity.

### Concept

 Ensure that your phone book contacts do not have spe- cial characters or blanks before their name. If there are such Contacts, please rename them.

### Concept

If you are unable to pair your phone with the infotainment sys- tem even after following the guidelines, try the following trou- bleshooting steps:

### Concept

 Refer to the user manual of your phone to verify whether all instructions for reset, connection and pair- ing have been followed.

### Concept

 Re-initiate Bluetooth pairing search or connection re- quest either from the phone or the infotainment system.

# INTRODUCING CONNECTNEXT INFOTAIN- MENT SYSTEM

## Knowledge

### Concept

INTRODUCING CONNECTNEXT INFOTAINMENT SYSTEM

### Concept

The ConnectNext infotainment system provides you with a bundle of high-end functionalities to:

### Concept

 Manage in-vehicle entertainment capabilities

### Concept

 Handle certain vehicle feature controls

### Concept

 View information about some vehicle features

### Concept

Key features of the infotainment system include:

### Specification

 8.8 inch display 1600 X 600 resolution touch screen

### Concept

 4 channel audio output supported with external branded audio amplifier interface

### Concept

 AM and FM Tuner bands with 20 memories each

### Concept

 USB, iPod, AUX and Bluetooth ® Audio multimedia sup- port

### Concept

 Video Playback and Image viewing support from USB sources

### Concept

 Bluetooth ® connectivity for simultaneous pairing with up to 10 devices, hands free calling, phonebook access and set favourite contacts capability.

### Concept

 Bluetooth ® remote control support with Tata Smart Re- mote App

### Concept

 Vehicle Controls, like Park Assist System, DRL, Ap- proach Light and Illumination Controls

### Concept

 Climate Control from infotainment system

### Concept

 Voice Assistance to operate your infotainment system functionality using voice commands

### Concept

 Android Auto™ and Apple CarPlay™ compatibility for smartphone control using infotainment system (once available)

### Concept

 DriveNext for real-time driving behavior analysis

### Concept

 Display OFF feature for distraction free night drive

### Concept

 Speed Dependent Volume Control

### Concept

 Infotainment controls from steering Wheel and island mounted button panel

### Concept

Some of the vehicle are not standard in every vehicle variant. Features that are unavailable in the vehicle cannot be controlled using the info- tainment system. Please refer to the Owner’s

# CARPLAY CONFIGURATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Apple iPhone from your vehicle infotainment sys- tem. You can use voice commands or the simple iPhone like interface on your infotainment system to operate your phone functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p84_img00` (page 84, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p84_img00.png`

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is compatible from iPhone 5 and up. For more information, refer to

### Concept

https://www.apple.com/in/ios/carplay/

### Concept

Before you connect the iPhone to infotainment system to use CarPlay, you need to perform the some one-time configuration steps:

### Concept

 Make sure you have iPhone 5 or up device, running on latetst iOS.

### Concept

 Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is by default enabled on your ve- hicle (if available).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_002_p84_img01` (page 84, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_002/p84_img01.png`

### Concept

 For your safety, ensure your vehicle is ON and in the parked condition and the Park Brake is engaged.

### Concept

 Connect your phone to your car using a USB cable.

### Concept

 Make sure that CarPlay isn't restricted. Go to Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions, tap Al- lowed Apps and make sure that CarPlay is enabled.

### Concept

Apple CarPlay will automatically get started in Connection. If CarPlay doesn't activate automatically, you can access CarPlay through:

### Concept

 Tap on to open Quick Access Drawer

# 7. About Details about the features and how to use the application

## Knowledge

### Concept

APPLICATIONS What3words*

### Note

Note: * sign denotes = If Applicable / Available feature in your car.

### Specification

What3words is a precise and incredibly simple way to talk about locations. What3words has assigned each 3m square in the world a unique 3 word address that is easy to say, share and is as accurate as GPS coordinates. Now you can drive to any precise location simply by saying or typing the 3 words. For example: ///glorious.performers.hidden marks the exact 3X3m square in Lavasa, India.

### Concept

1. What3words Address Bar

### Concept

To enter the desired 3 words address by typing or using voice command.

### Concept

To save entered address as favorite.

### Concept

To navigate to the entered 3- word address.

### Concept

4. Recent Addresses Title

### Concept

Displays a list of recently visited addresses.

### Concept

5. Favorite Addresses Title

### Concept

Displays a list of saved as favorite addresses.

### Concept

To share the 3-word address by SMS.

### Note

Note: The Navigate via SMS feature is unavailable in projection mode (Android Auto/Apple CarPlay).

### Note

Note: To use Navigate via SMS feature, the user must return to the What3words Home screen.

### Concept

Figure 42 What3words Search Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p54_img00` (page 54, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p54_img00.png`

### Concept

To use the What3words feature:

### Concept

What3words* APPLICATIONS

### Concept

1. Download and install What3words App on your smartphone and find the 3-word address of any location. 2. Connect your phone with the infotainment system. 3. Tap App launcher from the Status bar and tap What3 words icon. 4. Tap the Search Bar or use the mic icon to enter the 3 word address. 5. Type 3 word address (for example, glorious.performers.hidden) or say the 3 words (for example, glorious performers hidden), the system displays suggestions for the three word addresses. 6. ### Note

The infotainment system supports the following media sources from which you can play music, videos, and view pictures:

### Concept

Connecting to a Media Source

### Concept

Pen Drive : Pen Drive must be connected to the system for them to be recognized and accessed. Refer to your vehicle Owner’s Manual for information on how to connect the USB devices.

### Concept

Bluetooth Audio : Bluetooth devices do not require any physical connection with the system. Once you enable Bluetooth feature in the media device and the system, both

### Concept

the devices can be connected and paired with each other for them to be recognized and accessed.

### Note

Note: The supported video formats are .mp4 and .avi.

### Concept

Selecting a Media Source

### Concept

If multiple media sources are connected to the infotainment system or to play a particular media source that was stopped earlier, you can select the required source from the list of available Media Sources.

### Concept

To select the required media source:

### Concept

1. Tap the Media Source icon on the Widgets Home screen. The system displays the source drawer and plays the media source that was played last if the source is still connected.

### Concept

2. If no source is connected, select the required currently available media source. The system plays music track from the selected source.

### Concept

Music Related Functions

### Concept

The system allows you to perform the following Media operations:

### Concept

• Repeat music track.

### Concept

• Shuffle music tracks in a folder/media source

### Concept

• Play next/previous music tracks.

### Concept

• Perform fast forward/fast rewind.

### Concept

• Play next/previous folder.

### Concept

• Browse through the media content available for USB Playback source only.

### Concept

• View Pictures via USB.

### Concept

• Play Videos via USB.

### Note

### Note

### Note

### Concept

To repeat a track or tracks in a folder:

### Concept

− In the Media screen, press the Repeat icon to switch On/Off repeat functionality. − Repeat Once: The system repeats the current track

### Concept

### Concept

You can enable the system to randomly select and play music tracks available in a folder or all music tracks in the media source, instead of playing them in the sequence they are stored.

### Concept

To Shuffle music tracks in a folder/media source:

### Concept

View Next/Previous Music Track Names

### Concept

When in a music track, the system allows you to view the next/previous music track names. This functionality is supported only for USB and iPod devices. In the Media screen, Tap the Menu icon to view the next/previous music track.

### Concept

Play Next/Previous Music Tracks

### Concept

While playing a music track, the system allows you to play the next/previous music tracks.

### Concept

To play the next/previous music tracks

### Concept

− In the Media screen, tap on the Next Track icon or the Previous Track icon to play the next/previous

track respectively, or − Short Press the Up or Down switches from Steering Wheel to play the next/previous track respectively

### Concept

### Concept

You can fast forward or fast rewind the music tracks to quickly complete playing them and move ahead or backward in the folder.

### Concept

To fast forward or fast rewind:

### Concept

− In the Media screen, long tap on the Next Track icon or the Previous Track icon to play the

next/previous track respectively, or − Long Press the Seek Up or Seek Down button from Button Panel to play the next/previous track, respectively.

### Concept

Play Next/Previous Folder

### Concept

While playing a music track from the USB Stick, the system allows you to shift to the next/previous folder and play the music tracks in them.

### Note

Note: This functionality is supported only for USB.

### Concept

To shift to the next/previous folder:

### Concept

− In the Media screen, tap on the Folder Up or

the Folder Down icon to shift to the next or previous folder respectively. The system plays the first music track in the selected folder, or − Long Press Up or Down switches from Steering Wheel.

### Note

### Concept

To browse through the media content:

− In the Media screen, tap the Browse icon. The system displays the Browse screen with applicable categories list. − Select the required category from the list. The system displays the music tracks grouped under the selection. − From the available music tracks, chose the required music track. The system plays the selected music track.

- Image: `doc_006_p28_img02` (page 28, confidence 1.0)

### Concept

If your USB media device has picture files, you can view them in the infotainment system. The system supports viewing of JPEG, BMP and PNG picture file formats.

### Concept

Accessing the Picture Files

### Concept

• You can view picture files by using the picture viewer application.

### Warning

Note: The feature is unavailable when the vehicle is in motion. While driving, if you select a picture file, the system displays a popup message warning you not to open picture files while driving.

### Note

Note: While viewing picture files, if you start and drive your vehicle, and the vehicle reaches a speed of 5 km/hr or more, the system closes the picture viewer and displays a

### Concept

popup message indicating that the picture viewer is unavailable at high speed.

### Concept

If your USB media device contains video files, you can play them in the infotainment system. The system supports playback of .mp4 and .avi video file formats.

### Note

Note: While playing video files, if you start and drive your vehicle and the vehicle reaches a speed of 5 km/h or more, the system closes the video playback screen and displays a popup message indicating that the video playback is unavailable at high speed.

## Knowledge

FAQs FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

### Concept

7 FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

### Concept

Frequently asked questions related to the features and functions of the iRA infotainment system are listed below along with their answers.

### Concept

1. I am playing the audio files in my Phone, connected through Bluetooth. However, I am unable to repeat tracks and play tracks in random. The Bluetooth connection is fine and all other media functionalities are working. Why am I facing this issue?

### Concept

Some of the Media functionalities are phone dependent and are supported only in phones with AVRCP version 1.3 and above. Please check the AVRCP version of your phone.

### Concept

2. Why am I unable to fast forward or fast rewind music tracks when I play them from my phone?

### Concept

You can fast forward or fast rewind the track from your phone. Please check if you have connected your Phone to the infotainment system through Bluetooth connection. If yes, check the AVRCP version of your Phone. As, some of

### Concept

the Media functionalities are phone dependent and are supported only in phones with AVRCP version 1.3 and above.

### Concept

Fast forward and fast rewind from the infotainment system is available for USB Stick source only.

### Concept

3. How to Play video in the infotainment system?

### Concept

Video Player is available in “Browse” option of Media screen and select “Video” option. Through this you can browse through the Video files available in the current media source only (USB Stick).

### Concept

You can play video only from USB.

### Concept

5. I am unable to connect my Phone to the infotainment system using a USB cable however, I can connect through Bluetooth. Can you please help me with a solution?

### Concept

The USB cable that you are using to connect the Phone with the infotainment system might not be compatible with your Phone. Please use only the USB cable provided by the Phone Manufacturer

### Concept

6. Can I use other functionalities of the infotainment system while connected for Android Auto/Apple CarPlay?

text:
# 20. Driver Assistance and advanced safety features such as

## Knowledge

### Concept

Overview INTRODUCTION

### Concept

Tata iRA is a powerful multimedia and navigation system featuring a wide touch screen with easy to navigate through touch and swipe controls.

### Concept

The infotainment system provides an ideal in-car experience, supporting a wide range of media formats and devices. The system’s enhanced sound controls ensure that all sources sound great.

### Concept

Key Features of the multimedia system are:

### Specification

1. 10.25-inch display with 1920x 720 resolution

### Concept

2. 4 channels (Non JBL Brand Audio)/ 8 channel (JBL Brand audio) output supported with internal audio amplifier interface.

### Note

Note: Channel output is based on vehicle variant.

### Concept

3. AM and FM Tuner bands with 20 memories each

### Concept

4. USB, iPod, Wi-Fi/Hotspot and Bluetooth Audio multimedia support

### Concept

5. Video Playback and Image viewing support from USB source (Pen Driver only)

### Concept

6. Bluetooth connectivity for pairing with up to ten devices, maximum 1 device can be connected at a time, hands free calling, phonebook access and set favorite contacts capability.

### Concept

7. Bluetooth remote control support with ConnectNext App

### Concept

8. Vehicle Controls, like Park Assist System, DRL, Approach Light and Illumination Controls

### Concept

9. Climate Control from infotainment system

### Concept

10. Voice Assistance to operate your infotainment system functionality using voice commands.

### Concept

11. Built in Alexa app, directly talk with Alexa (voice assistant through microphone and speakers

### Concept

12. Wireless Android Auto™ and Wireless Apple CarPlay™ compatibility for infotainment system.

### Concept

13. Drive Next Application for real-time driving behavior analysis.

### Concept

14. Display OFF feature for distraction free night drive.

### Concept

15. Speed Dependent Volume Control

### Concept

16. Infotainment controls from Steering Wheel Switch Board

### Concept

17. Mood Light and JBL Mode features to setup the inside cabin lively and give amazing driving experience.

### Concept

18. Current and Live Location sharing application

### Concept

19. Emergency and Break down calling feature.

a. Front Collision Warning System

### Concept

### Warning

### Concept

# HMI Doodle APPLICATIONS

## Knowledge

### Note

Note: Startup image is visible on Doodle settings screen during preview and while infotainment system startup.

### Note

Note: My Sticker is visible on Media OFF/Home screen only after predefined time out, it can be disabled by user action on home screen or by Steering Wheel Phone/SRC button press.

### Note

Note: You can move the sticker on home screen/Media OFF screen at desired position by touching and dragging it

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Voice Assistant

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to access various media, climate, phone, and other controls using voice commands. This feature has defined Voice commands which are recognized by the Voice Assistant.

### Concept

To activate the voice recognition feature:

### Concept

1. Say wake-up word “Hey Tata”, or “Hi Tata”, or “Hello Tata” and you will be connected to a Voice Assistant or

### Concept

2. Press the Voice Activation button on the Steering Wheel control element.

### Concept

The system mutes/pauses the currently playing audio and you will hear a beep sound indicate the activation of the voice recognition feature.

### Note

Note: The system will start recognizing your voice commands only after the beep. So, speak only after you hear the voice activation beep. If no command is spoken after the beep, the system will prompt you to say a command.

### Concept

Figure 45 Voice Assistant Home Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p58_img00` (page 58, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p58_img00.png`

### Concept

You can setup the language of the Voice Assistant and communicate in the selected language.

### Concept

Go to Voice Assistant > Settings > Language Selection

### Concept

Select the language from following options

### Concept

1. Tamil & English 2. Telugu & English 3. Hindi & English 4. Marathi & English 5. Bengali & English

### Concept

### Concept

Voice Command Guidelines

### Concept

• Only speak the commands that are listed in the “Voice Recognition Commands” section.

### Concept

• When similar sounding contact names/song names are spoken, the system will display a list of options matching the spoken name. You can choose the required option from the list by calling out the corresponding line number or touching the required option on the screen.

### Note

Note: The infotainment system also displays the voice recognition commands. You can select and view the required command de-tails from within the Voice screen.

### Concept

• Speak the commands and names in a neutral English accent for best results.

### Concept

• Do not take long pauses (greater than 1 second) while speaking the words in a command. Speak the words of the command at a constant rate.

### Concept

• Avoid varying your pitch and volume while speaking the commands. Speak clearly and loudly at a reasonable speed.

### Concept

• Ensure that there is no noise disturbance when you speak the commands like, other passengers in the vehicle are talking or there is lot of wind noise. Disturbance from external sound sources may result in poor voice recognition.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Voice Assistant

### Concept

Always face forward while speaking your commands as the voice recognition quality is best in this orientation.

### Concept

1. Warranty is applicable in India only.

### Concept

2. Warranty for the product is against defective materials and manufacturing faults for 4 years / 2 lakh kms (whichever comes earlier) from the date of the first sale of vehicle.

### Concept

3. Display and touch panel, if applicable to your system, are covered for 36 months / 60000 kms from the date of the first sale of vehicle.

### Concept

text:
# VEHICLE FUNCTIONS Lighting

## Knowledge

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to control lighting features like Approach Lamp and DRL if your vehicle is equipped with these features.

### Concept

When you approach your car in the dark, you can switch on the Approach Lamps (some exterior and interior lights of the vehicle) to identify your car as well as to find your way safely to it.

### Concept

The system allows you to set the time for which the Approach lamps will be illuminated after you switch them ON.

### Concept

To set the Approach lights illumination time:

### Concept

1. In the Vehicle Settings screen, navigate to and select the Approach Lamps option. The system displays the various illumination time options.

### Concept

2. Navigate to and select the required illumination time option from 30 seconds/60 seconds/90 seconds.

### Concept

Figure 68 Approach lamp

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p86_img00` (page 86, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p86_img00.png`

### Concept

DRL (Daytime Running Lamps)

### Concept

If the vehicle is equipped with this feature, you can ON/OFF DRL (Daytime Running Lamps) from the infotainment system.

### Concept

1. In the Vehicle Setup screen, navigate to and select the Lights option.

### Concept

2. In the Lighting screen tap on DRL tap the DRL bar icon to ON/OFF DRLs.

### Concept

Figure 69 Daytime Running Lamps

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p87_img00` (page 87, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p87_img00.png`

### Concept

VEHICLE FUNCTIONS TATA Assist Call (Breakdown Call)*

### Concept

TATA Assist Call (Breakdown Call)*

### Concept

In case of vehicle break down, the infotainment system helps you to reach you to Tata Motors service centre.

### Note

Note: This feature requires active inbuilt internet connectivity in the car.

### Concept

1. Tap the Break Call application, from the App launcher Screen.

### Concept

2. Tap B Call button, the infotainment system dials the Tata Break Down Service centre.

### Concept

3. Swipe right on the ‘Slide to End Call’ bar to disconnect the call.

### Concept

Figure 70 Break Down Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p88_img00` (page 88, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p88_img00.png`

### Concept

In case of Emergency, the infotainment system helps you to call Emergency SOS number.

### Note

Note: This feature requires active inbuilt internet connectivity in the car.

### Concept

1. Tap the Emergency Call application, from the App launcher Screen.

### Concept

2. Tap E Call button, the infotainment system dials the Tata Emergency SOS number.

### Concept

3. Swipe right on the ‘Slide to End Call’ bar to disconnect the call.

### Concept

Figure 71 Emergency Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p88_img01` (page 88, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p88_img01.png`

### Note

Note: For more details, please refer hard copy of owner's manual

You can reset your system to factory default settings in case you are giving your vehicle to someone for temporary usage or when you are selling out your vehicle. On performing this, system will reset all personalized settings to factory default settings.

### Concept

To perform Factory Reset:

### Concept

1. In the System, navigate to and select the Factory Reset option. The system displays the confirmation pop-up to perform Reset.

### Concept

2. On confirmation, system the system initiates the restoring to factory default settings action. The media source/radio that is currently playing will be stopped and the Phone will be disconnected.

### Concept

3. Once the reset is completed, the system prompts you to switch OFF the infotainment system by doing Ignition OFF.

### Concept

4. The reset action is completed, when you insert the key again (after 10 seconds at least) and switch ON the ignition and the infotainment system.

### Concept

# 4. Mood Light zone selection will be available for theme selection

## Knowledge

### Concept

VEHICLE FUNCTIONS Mood Light

### Concept

Mood Lighting is a part of interior lights. It utilizes the LED lights mounted around the cabin to enhance the design and give a soothing experience to driver and other passengers inside car. It is an add on feature to create a lively atmosphere inside cabin.

### Concept

Mood lighting can influence the mood, eye fatigue, circadian rhythms, and concentration of drivers which in turn relates to safety

### Concept

a. Mood Light icon in ‘Settings’ screen (Icon is enabled in IGN ON/Engine-RUN) b. Mood Light icon in Settings screen (Icon is disabled in IGN OFF/Engine-OFF condition) c. Mood Light icon in Settings screen (Icon is disabled in IGN ON/Engine condition)

### Concept

To access Mood Light screen from

### Concept

1. Settings>Mood Light

### Concept

### Concept

2. Tap OFF button, to Turn off the Mood Light Feature

### Concept

3. Tap ON button to Turn On the Mood Light Feature

### Procedure

5. Select the ZONE icon to turn on the front and rear mood lighting zone. You can enable both the zones or front or rear zone only

### Concept

Figure 73 Mood Light Feature – Home Screen

text:
# 2. Long Press Up or Down switches from Steering Wheel Controls

## Knowledge

### Concept

1. Slide left/right your finger on Radio screen rotary element and tune the frequency as per your need, or you can scan the station from steering wheel as well

### Concept

To perform Auto tuning:

### Concept

1. Tap Seek up Seek Down icon or

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p31_img00` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p31_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_006_p31_img01` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p31_img01.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system provides the option of automatically searching and storing available radio stations as presets. When initiated, the Auto Store feature stores the available stations, in the ascending order of their frequency, in the pre-sets bar.

### Concept

To perform Auto store

### Concept

1. Tap Browse on Radio Screen, the system will display various options.

### Concept

2. Navigate to Autostore and touch on screen to start Auto Store.

### Concept

Figure 14 Auto Store

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p31_img02` (page 31, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p31_img02.png`

### Concept

The system will search for the available radio stations and when found, you can tune in the station from the list displayed.

### Concept

1. In the Phone Setup options, navigate to and select Pair New Device option. The system searches for Bluetooth enabled devices within its range.

### Concept

2. Navigate to and select the required phone from the list of currently available Bluetooth enabled devices.

### Concept

3. The system prompts you to confirm the Bluetooth pass key of the phone. Select Yes. The system initiates the pairing of the infotainment system and the selected phone. If the pairing is successful, the system displays the phone in the Paired Devices screen. A copy of your phone data like call logs (phone numbers and other contact details) is also created in the system.

### Concept

4. Tap Allow to allow all the requested notifications of the phone once paired with the Infotainment system via Bluetooth.

### Concept

Figure 16 Pair New Device

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p33_img00` (page 33, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p33_img00.png`

### Concept

To delete a device from the list, Select the device and tap Delete icon

### Concept

To delete all devices connected to the infotainment system.

### Concept

1. Tap Delete All devices tab.

### Concept

When a mobile phone is paired and connected to the infotainment system, you can manage the following phone operations through the hands-free capability of the system:

### Concept

• View call log and contacts.

### Concept

• Make an outgoing call (Last 20 call Logs)

### Concept

• Accept/reject an incoming call.

### Concept

• Reject Incoming call with SMS.

### Concept

• Put a call on hold.

### Concept

• Manage two calls at a time.

### Concept

• Conduct a conference call.

### Concept

• Toggle between the Phone handset and the hands-free capability

### Concept

• SMS read out by the system.

### Concept

You can view all calls, received, or dialed from the infotainment system or missed when connected to the system, in the call log. The system displays up to 20 missed calls, 20 dialed calls and 20 received calls.

### Concept

To view the call log:

### Concept

1. In the Phone Browse screen, tap Call Logs. The system displays the details of up to 60 past calls in the Call Log screen.

### Concept

1. The infotainment system allows you to view up to five thousand contacts stored in your phone book.

### Concept

2. To view the contacts a. In the Phone Browse screen, tap Contacts. The

### Concept

system displays the Contacts screen with the list of contacts stored in your phone book.

### Concept

Making Outgoing Calls

### Concept

The infotainment system supports 5 ways to make a phone call. They are:

### Concept

• Dialing by selecting the phone number from the call log

### Concept

• Dialing by selecting the phone number from the contacts

### Concept

• Dialing the phone number manually using Dialpad

### Concept

• Dialing by selecting the phone number from the Favorites

### Concept

• Dialing using voice command.

### Concept

Figure 17 Outgoing Call Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p34_img00` (page 34, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p34_img00.png`

### Concept

Dialing Using the Call Log

### Concept

To dial a number from the list of previous calls (call log):

### Concept

1. Display the call log. Refer to the “Viewing Call Logs” section for information on displaying the call log.

### Concept

2. Select the required number from the list. The system dials the selected number and initiates the outgoing call.

### Concept

Figure 18 Call Log Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p35_img00` (page 35, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p35_img00.png`

### Concept

Dialing Using the Contact

### Concept

To make a call by dialing a number from the contacts:

### Concept

1. Open the Contacts screen. Refer to the “Viewing Contacts” section for the steps to open the Contacts screen.

### Concept

2. Navigate through the contacts and select the required number. The system dials the selected number and initiates the outgoing call.

### Note

Note: The contact numbers that do not have a name defined for them will be displayed Last in the Contact list with an #.

### Concept

Dialing the Phone Number Manually using Dialpad

### Concept

To make a call by manually dialing a phone number:

### Concept

1. In the Phone Browse screen, select the Dialpad. The system displays the Keypad to enter the phone number.

### Concept

2. Enter the digits of the phone number in the Dialpad.

### Concept

3. After entering the phone number, tap Call. The system initiates the outgoing call.

### Note

Note: The system retains the phone number that was last dialed in the Dialpad. So, to redial the phone number, you can just open the Dialpad and select the Call icon.

### Concept

Dialing Using the Favorites

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p35_img01` (page 35, confidence 0.963)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p35_img01.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system supports marking contacts as favorites. The system also allows you to view and access these favorite contacts separately from the Favorites screen, in addition to the Contacts screen.

### Concept

Marking a Contact as Favorite

### Concept

To mark a contact as favorite:

### Concept

1. In the Contacts screen, select the required contact and tap displayed beside the contact number. The system highlights the star icon, and the contact is marked as favorite.

### Note

Note: You can save maximum 20 contacts to the favorite list.

### Concept

Viewing the Favorites List

### Concept

You can identify the contacts marked as favorite with the highlighted star in the Contacts screen. All favorite contacts can also be separately viewed in the Favorites screen.

### Concept

To display the Favorites screen:

### Concept

1. In the Phone Browse screen, tap Favorites. The system displays the Favorites screen with the list of favorite contacts.

### Concept

Dialing from Favorite Contact List

### Concept

To dial a favorite contact

### Concept

Open the Favorites screen. The system lists all contacts marked as favorite. Navigate to the required favorite contact and tap Call. The system dials the number of the selected favorite contact and initiates the outgoing call.

### Concept

Accepting/Rejecting Incoming Calls

### Concept

When you receive a phone call, you can either accept or reject it from the infotainment system.

### Concept

If your mobile phone is paired and currently connected to the system, the system notifies you with a popup message when you receive a phone call. The system allows you to Accept, Reject or Reject Incoming call with Message.

### Concept

To accept incoming call:

### Concept

Select the Accept icon in the popup message. The system connects the call to enable you to talk to the caller.

### Note

Note: You can also accept the call using the button Steering Wheel control.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p36_img00` (page 36, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p36_img00.png`

### Concept

To reject incoming call:

### Concept

1. Select the Reject icon in the popup message. The system disconnects the call.

### Note

Note: You can also reject the call using the

### Concept

Steering Wheel control.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p36_img01` (page 36, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p36_img01.png`

### Concept

Reject Incoming call with Message

### Concept

In the Reject with Message option, the system rejects the call and sends a SMS to the caller with the configured text.

### Concept

Figure 20 Reject Call with Message

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p37_img00` (page 37, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p37_img00.png`

### Concept

Handling Call Functions

### Concept

When you are in a call (outgoing or incoming), the system supports you to perform any of the following functions:

### Concept

• Respond to the Interactive Voice Response (IVR) with the required details.

### Concept

• Put the call on hold.

### Concept

• Switch between phone (handset) and system (hands- free) capability

### Concept

• Accept another incoming call.

### Concept

• Switch between Calls

### Concept

• Conduct a conference call by adding another number or by merging two existing calls.

### Note

Note: Maximum 5 contacts/ participants can be added to a conference call.

### Concept

Responding to the IVR

### Concept

When you have called a contact with Interactive Voice Response (IVR) like customer care number of bank and so on, you will have to enter some details through the phone. For example, you might have to enter your bank account number, when prompted by the IVR. You can use the Dialpad in-call option to enter such details through the infotainment system.

### Concept

To display the Dialpad and to respond to the IVR with details:

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, tap Dialpad and enter the details as prompted by the IVR.

### Concept

Putting a Call on Hold

### Concept

To put a call on hold:

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, tap Hold. The system puts the currently active call on hold.

### Concept

Switching Between Handset and Hands-Free

### Concept

When in an active call, the system allows you to switch between the phone handset and its hands-free capability and vice versa.

### Concept

To toggle between phone and system:

### Concept

In the active call screen, tap Handset icon to switch the call from system to phone or Handsfree to switch from phone to system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p38_img00` (page 38, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p38_img00.png`

### Concept

Accepting Another Incoming Call

### Concept

When you are in an active call and receive another incoming call, you can put the active call on hold and accept the new call. The system allows you to have a maximum of 2 calls at any given time, one on hold and the other active. To accept another incoming call:

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, the system displays a new call popup message with Accept, Reject and Reject with Message icons, when you receive a new incoming call. Select Accept in the new call popup message. The system puts the first call on hold and activates the new call.

### Concept

Switching Between Calls

### Concept

When you have 2 calls simultaneously (one on hold and other active), the system allows you to switch between the calls without ending either of them.

### Concept

To switch between calls: 1. Tap switch calls option.

### Concept

Conducting a Conference Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p38_img01` (page 38, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p38_img01.png`

### Concept

When in an active call, you can connect an additional phone number to create a conference call between the contacts. You can create a conference call by either dialing to an additional number or by accepting a new incoming call.

### Concept

To create a conference call by dialing additional number

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, tap Add Call . The system puts the active call on hold and displays the Contacts screen. You can dial the additional number from the contacts list or from the call log, the favorites list.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p38_img02` (page 38, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p38_img02.png`

### Concept

2. Follow the steps listed in the “Making an Outgoing Call” section for dialing a number using the various options. The system initiates an outgoing call for the selected number.

### Concept

3. In the new call screen, tap Merge. The system merges the 2 calls (one on hold and the new call) to create a

### Concept

conference call. The first call is activated before merging.

### Concept

To create a conference call by accepting a new incoming call:

### Concept

1. Accept a new incoming call as detailed in the “Accepting/Rejecting an Incoming Phone Call” section.

### Concept

2. In the new call screen, tap Merge. The system merges the 2 calls (one on hold and the new call) to create a conference call. The first call is activated before merging.

### Note

Note: You can view the list of participants in a conference call by taping the Participants icon.

### Note

Note: There can be maximum 5 participants in a conference call.

### Concept

Figure 21 Add Call to Conference

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p39_img00` (page 39, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p39_img00.png`

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Wireless Charger

### Concept

Wireless Phone Charger (WPC) is available in Tata vehicle to give an experience to charge your smart devices wirelessly. This refrains the anxiety of smartphone discharge during the drive. Popup indication appears on the screen to show the status of charging.

### Concept

Following screen is displayed when the phone is charged using the charging Pad.

### Concept

When no phone is placed on the charging pad, the charging on icon is hidden.

### Concept

When the phone is being charged using charging pad, wireless Charger icon pops up on the top right corner of the status bar.

### Concept

Figure 22 Wireless Charing On

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p40_img00` (page 40, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p40_img00.png`

### Concept

In case of charging error, the error charging icon is displayed on the top right corner of the status bar.

### Concept

Battery full charge pop appears on the system screen once the phone is fully charged.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Android Auto

### Concept

Android Auto is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Android smartphones from your vehicle infotainment system. You can use voice actions or simple arrangement of Google Maps, and other important phone functions to access the required functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

### Concept

The Android Auto feature requires the installation of the Android Auto Mobile App, which can be downloaded on your smartphone from Google Play Store.

### Note

Note: Applicable only for Android Smartphones with Android Version 10 and above

### Concept

• Make sure your phone is running Android 5.0 (Lollipop) and up. For best performance, Google recommend An- droid 6.0 (Marshmallow) and up.

### Concept

• Download Android Auto - Apps on Google Play from Google Play.

### Concept

• Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection.

### Note

Note: By default, Android Auto is configured in the infotainment system. Thereby, when you connect your Android Auto enabled smartphone with the infotainment

### Concept

system you will be prompted to select whether you would like to continue the phone connection for Android Auto.

### Note

Note: Android Auto is by default enabled on your vehicle.

### Concept

Connect - Wireless Android Auto

### Concept

1. Pair/connect your phone to the infotainment system using Bluetooth ® .

### Concept

2. Follow the prompts on the screen and on your phone to start.

### Concept

3. You will be asked to accept Terms before using the feature.

### Concept

Connect – Wired Android Auto

### Concept

1. Ensure your vehicle is in the parked condition and the Park Brake is applied.

### Concept

2. Connect your phone using USB cable to the Infotainment to start Android Auto

### Concept

3. Follow the prompts on the screen and on your phone to start.

### Note

Note: Your phone’s Bluetooth will be turned on automatically when wired Android Auto is connected to the car via USB.

### Concept

Android Auto APPLICATIONS

### Concept

Figure 24 Android Auto Projection

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p43_img00` (page 43, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p43_img00.png`

### Concept

Tap on Android Auto application from the App Launcher screen. Follow the instructions to get started.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p43_img01` (page 43, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p43_img01.png`

### Note

Note: If the connection with the infotainment system is lost, the app will get disconnected and infotainment system displays the home screen.

### Note

Note: Ensure you have enabled your Location in the Phone settings for using Android Auto Google Map navigation.

### Note

Note: Android Auto settings can be accessed from your phone only. Refer to your phone for settings details.

### Note

Note: For better usability of the Android Auto app, the Internet connectivity of phone must be good.

### Concept

You can access the Google Maps, communication functionalities (receives and make phone calls, receive, and send messages and so on) of your smartphone through the infotainment system. Even in the infotainment system, you just need to provide voice actions to control these functionalities, without removing your hand from the steering wheel.

### Concept

Any new message that you receive on your phone is displayed on the home screen and readout to you. You can either reply to the SMS with a default message like “I am Driving.

### Concept

You can use Google Assistant (voice recognition) so that your voice actions are recognized. To activate, tap the Mic icon (highlighted in the above figure) on the Android Auto Home screen.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p43_img02` (page 43, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p43_img02.png`

### Note

Note: Click the icon to go to the Android Auto Home screen from any other Android Auto screens.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Android Auto

### Concept

Access Google Maps using Android Auto

### Concept

To access Google Maps and its navigation support features from Android Auto on the infotainment system:

### Concept

1. Tap the icon on the Android Auto Home screen on the infotainment system. The Google Maps screen is displayed. You can now initiate and use the various features of Google Maps from the infotainment system, as you handle it from your Android smartphone.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p44_img00` (page 44, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p44_img00.png`

### Concept

Figure 25 Android Auto Google Map Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p44_img01` (page 44, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p44_img01.png`

### Concept

Handle Calls using Android Auto

### Concept

To handle calls or other communication related actions from Android Auto on the infotainment system:

### Concept

1. Tap the icon on the Android Auto Home screen on the infotainment system. The Dialer screen is displayed. You can now make calls, receive calls, or handle any other communication or other communication actions from the infotainment system, as you handle it from your Android smartphone.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p44_img02` (page 44, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p44_img02.png`

### Concept

1. On your display, select the app launcher . 2. Tap Android Auto 3. Select your favorite music app to browse and play music

### Concept

Apple CarPlay APPLICATIONS

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Apple iPhone from your vehicle infotainment system. You can use voice commands or the simple iPhone like interface on your infotainment system to operate your phone functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

### Note

Note: Applicable only for iPhones. Apple CarPlay is compatible from iPhone 5 and above versions. For more information, refer to

### Concept

https://www.apple.com/in/ios/carplay/

### Concept

Before you connect the iPhone to infotainment system to use Apple CarPlay, you need to perform some one-time configuration steps:

### Concept

1. Make sure you have iPhone 5 or up device, running on latest iOS.

### Concept

2. Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection.

### Note

Note: Apple CarPlay is by default enabled on your vehicle (if available).

### Concept

Connect – Wireless Apple CarPlay 1. Pair/connect your phone to the infotainment system using Bluetooth ® . 2. Follow the prompts on the screen and on your iPhone to start a wireless Apple CarPlay session. 3. You will be asked to accept Terms of Use before using the feature.

### Concept

Connect – Wired Apple CarPlay

### Concept

1. Connect your iPhone to the infotainment system, using the original Apple or Apple certified Lightning USB cable. On successful establishment of the connection, the infotainment system displays a popup or highlights the Apple CarPlay menu, if in focus in the home screen

### Concept

2. Tap on the popup/menu to launch the Apple CarPlay Home screen.

### Note

Note: If the connection with the infotainment system is lost, the app is disconnected, and the infotainment system Home screen is displayed.

### Note

Note: The settings of Apple CarPlay can be accessed from your iPhone only.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Apple CarPlay

### Concept

You can access the Music, Message, communication functionalities (receives and make phone calls and so on) of your iPhone through the infotainment system. In the infotainment system, in addition to using the touch screen, control elements and SWC controls, you can just provide voice actions to control these functionalities, without removing your hand from the steering wheel.

### Concept

Figure 26 Apple CarPlay Home Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_006_p46_img00` (page 46, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_006/p46_img00.png`

### Concept

# 7. About Details about the features and how to use the application

## Knowledge

### Concept

APPLICATIONS What3words*

### Note

Note: * sign denotes = If Applicable / Available feature in your car.

### Specification

What3words is a precise and incredibly simple way to talk about locations. What3words has assigned each 3m square in the world a unique 3 word address that is easy to say, share and is as accurate as GPS coordinates. Now you can drive to any precise location simply by saying or typing the 3 words. For example: ///glorious.performers.hidden marks the exact 3X3m square in Lavasa, India.

### Concept

1. What3words Address Bar

### Concept

To enter the desired 3 words address by typing or using voice command.

### Concept

To save entered address as favorite.

### Concept

To navigate to the entered 3- word address.

### Concept

4. Recent Addresses Title

### Concept

Displays a list of recently visited addresses.

### Concept

5. Favorite Addresses Title

### Concept

Displays a list of saved as favorite addresses.

### Concept

To share the 3-word address by SMS.

### Note

Note: The Navigate via SMS feature is unavailable in projection mode (Android Auto/Apple CarPlay).

### Note

Note: To use Navigate via SMS feature, the user must return to the What3words Home screen.

### Concept

Figure 42 What3words Search Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p54_img00` (page 54, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p54_img00.png`

### Concept

To use the What3words feature:

### Concept

What3words* APPLICATIONS

### Concept

1. Download and install What3words App on your smartphone and find the 3-word address of any location. 2. Connect your phone with the infotainment system. 3. Tap App launcher from the Status bar and tap What3 words icon. 4. Tap the Search Bar or use the mic icon to enter the 3 word address. 5. Type 3 word address (for example, glorious.performers.hidden) or say the 3 words (for example, glorious performers hidden), the system displays suggestions for the three word addresses. 6. Tap the correct 3 word address and you will be displayed with the Address options screen with Share, Favorite and Navigate icons enabled.

### Note

Note: Auto Launch Permission are required for launching navigation automatically through Android Auto (for Android smartphones)/Apple CarPlay (for Apple iPhone). To enable Auto Launch Permission: 1. Tap Allow on the permission popup. 2. Tap More icon and check Auto Launch Permission (if unchecked).

### Note

Note: You can also share the entered 3 words destination address via SMS.

### Note

Note: To use the share 3-word address option, the smartphone must be connected to the infotainment system and the view/send SMS permissions must be enabled on the phone.

### Note

Note: Using the save as Favorite Addresses feature, you can save the desired address as favorite for quick access.

### Note

Note: By default, at any given time when you type a destination or provide voice commands, the system displays 3 auto suggestions to assist you.

### Concept

Help option Opens more options and settings for What3words feature. You can explore more functionalities so that you understand and use What3words effectively. This also leads to better settings according to convenience.

To select the required media source:

### Concept

popup message indicating that the picture viewer is unavailable at high speed.

### Concept

If your USB media device contains video files, you can play them in the infotainment system. The system supports playback of .mp4 and .avi video file formats.

### Note

Note: While playing video files, if you start and drive your vehicle and the vehicle reaches a speed of 5 km/h or more, the system closes the video playback screen and displays a popup message indicating that the video playback is unavailable at high speed.

# 4. From which Media sources can I play video?

## Knowledge

### Concept

FAQs FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

### Concept

7 FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

### Concept

Frequently asked questions related to the features and functions of the iRA infotainment system are listed below along with their answers.

### Concept

1. I am playing the audio files in my Phone, connected through Bluetooth. However, I am unable to repeat tracks and play tracks in random. The Bluetooth connection is fine and all other media functionalities are working. Why am I facing this issue?

### Concept

Some of the Media functionalities are phone dependent and are supported only in phones with AVRCP version 1.3 and above. Please check the AVRCP version of your phone.

### Concept

2. Why am I unable to fast forward or fast rewind music tracks when I play them from my phone?

### Concept

You can fast forward or fast rewind the track from your phone. Please check if you have connected your Phone to the infotainment system through Bluetooth connection. If yes, check the AVRCP version of your Phone. As, some of

### Concept

the Media functionalities are phone dependent and are supported only in phones with AVRCP version 1.3 and above.

### Concept

Fast forward and fast rewind from the infotainment system is available for USB Stick source only.

### Concept

3. How to Play video in the infotainment system?

### Concept

Video Player is available in “Browse” option of Media screen and select “Video” option. Through this you can browse through the Video files available in the current media source only (USB Stick).

### Concept

You can play video only from USB.

### Concept

5. I am unable to connect my Phone to the infotainment system using a USB cable however, I can connect through Bluetooth. Can you please help me with a solution?

### Concept

The USB cable that you are using to connect the Phone with the infotainment system might not be compatible with your Phone. Please use only the USB cable provided by the Phone Manufacturer

### Concept

6. Can I use other functionalities of the infotainment system while connected for Android Auto/Apple CarPlay?

# 20. Driver Assistance and advanced safety features such as

## Knowledge

### Concept

Overview INTRODUCTION

### Concept

Tata iRA is a powerful multimedia and navigation system featuring a wide touch screen with easy to navigate through touch and swipe controls.

### Concept

The infotainment system provides an ideal in-car experience, supporting a wide range of media formats and devices. The system’s enhanced sound controls ensure that all sources sound great.

### Concept

Key Features of the multimedia system are:

### Specification

1. 10.25-inch display with 1920x 720 resolution

### Concept

2. 4 channels (Non JBL Brand Audio)/ 8 channel (JBL Brand audio) output supported with internal audio amplifier interface.

### Note

Note: Channel output is based on vehicle variant.

### Concept

3. AM and FM Tuner bands with 20 memories each

### Concept

4. USB, iPod, Wi-Fi/Hotspot and Bluetooth Audio multimedia support

### Concept

5. Video Playback and Image viewing support from USB source (Pen Driver only)

### Concept

6. Bluetooth connectivity for pairing with up to ten devices, maximum 1 device can be connected at a time, hands free calling, phonebook access and set favorite contacts capability.

### Concept

7. Bluetooth remote control support with ConnectNext App

### Concept

8. Vehicle Controls, like Park Assist System, DRL, Approach Light and Illumination Controls

### Concept

9. Climate Control from infotainment system

### Concept

10. Voice Assistance to operate your infotainment system functionality using voice commands.

### Concept

11. Built in Alexa app, directly talk with Alexa (voice assistant through microphone and speakers

### Concept

12. Wireless Android Auto™ and Wireless Apple CarPlay™ compatibility for infotainment system.

### Concept

13. Drive Next Application for real-time driving behavior analysis.

### Concept

14. Display OFF feature for distraction free night drive.

### Concept

15. Speed Dependent Volume Control

### Concept

16. Infotainment controls from Steering Wheel Switch Board

### Concept

17. Mood Light and JBL Mode features to setup the inside cabin lively and give amazing driving experience.

### Concept

18. Current and Live Location sharing application

### Concept

19. Emergency and Break down calling feature.

### Warning

a. Front Collision Warning System

### Concept

INTRODUCTION Overview

### Concept

b. Traffic Sign Recognition

### Warning

### Concept

### Concept

| 4. | Scroll Up | Short Press: • USB, iPod, Video Playback & Bluetooth Audio: Plays the next track. Radio: Plays next preset radio station. |
|  |  | Long Press: USB: • In Folder Mode: Plays track from next folder. • If Non-folder Mode: Fast Forwards the current track. iPod, Video Playback & Bluetooth Audio: • Fast forwards the current track Radio: Starts Auto Seek up. |
| 5. | Scroll Down | Short Press: USB, iPod, Video Playback & Bluetooth Audio • If track played duration is less than 3 secs: Plays the previous track. • If track played duration is more than 3 secs: Replays the current track Radio: • Plays previous preset radio station. |
|  |  | Long Press: USB: • In Folder Mode: Plays track from previous folder. • If Non-folder Mode: Fast rewind the current track. iPod, Video Playback & Bluetooth Audio: • Fast rewinds the current track Radio: • Starts Auto Seek down. |
| 6. |  | Short Press / Long Press: Toggles between available media sources in below sequence: If Android Auto/Apple CarPlay device not connected: |
|  |  | • Radio (last band FM / AM) --> USB/iPod--> BT streaming If Android Auto/Apple CarPlay device connected: • Radio (last band FM / AM) --> AA/CPY |
| 7. | End Call | Short Press & Long Press: • If Incoming Phone Call: Reject call. • If Outgoing Phone Call: Cancel call. • If Active Phone Call: End call. |
| 8. |  | Short Press: • Activates Native Voice Assistance. Alexa whichever is mapped to this button • Display OFF Mode: Turns on the display and executes selected option. • SMS Readout Popup: Starts reading the SMS. Voice Alert: Cancels Voice Alert and activates native Voice Assistance. |
|  |  | Outgoing Call, Active Call, Voice Assistance active and SMS Reading: No Action Long Press: • Android Auto/ Apple CarPlay: Activates Google Assistance / Siri (whichever is applicable). • Others: Same as short press. |
| 9. |  | If Media is Playing: Mutes/Unmutes the track. |

## Knowledge

### Concept

SETTINGS Connectivity

### Concept

The infotainment system is Internet enabled with Wi-Fi and Hotspot features. It has a in-built internet connectivity to access internet.

### Concept

To connect with internet:

### Concept

1. Tap App Launcher Icon, navigate to Settings and select Connectivity.

### Concept

2. Enable Wi-Fi. The system will list the available networks.

### Procedure

3. Select the network you want to connect, enter the password.

### Concept

If the in-built internet connectivity feature is available, you can use the Hotspot feature to provide internet connectivity to other devices.

### Concept

To provide internet access via Hotspot

### Concept

1. Navigate to Connectivity Application, Enable Hotspot.

### Concept

2. The system will display Hotspot Name and password.

### Concept

3. Look for the same hotspot name in the device you want to connect with, enter the password and to get connected.
