text:
# HMI Doodle APPLICATIONS

## Knowledge

### Note

Note: Startup image is visible on Doodle settings screen during preview and while infotainment system startup.

### Note

Note: My Sticker is visible on Media OFF/Home screen only after predefined time out, it can be disabled by user action on home screen or by Steering Wheel Phone/SRC button press.

### Note

Note: You can move the sticker on home screen/Media OFF screen at desired position by touching and dragging it

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Voice Assistant

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to access various media, climate, phone, and other controls using voice commands. This feature has defined Voice commands which are recognized by the Voice Assistant.

### Concept

To activate the voice recognition feature:

### Concept

1. Say wake-up word “Hey Tata”, or “Hi Tata”, or “Hello Tata” and you will be connected to a Voice Assistant or

### Concept

2. Press the Voice Activation button on the Steering Wheel control element.

### Concept

The system mutes/pauses the currently playing audio and you will hear a beep sound indicate the activation of the voice recognition feature.

### Note

Note: The system will start recognizing your voice commands only after the beep. So, speak only after you hear the voice activation beep. If no command is spoken after the beep, the system will prompt you to say a command.

### Concept

Figure 45 Voice Assistant Home Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p58_img00` (page 58, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p58_img00.png`

### Concept

You can setup the language of the Voice Assistant and communicate in the selected language.

### Concept

Go to Voice Assistant > Settings > Language Selection

### Concept

Select the language from following options

### Concept

1. Tamil & English 2. Telugu & English 3. Hindi & English 4. Marathi & English 5. Bengali & English

### Concept

### Concept

Voice Command Guidelines

### Concept

• Only speak the commands that are listed in the “Voice Recognition Commands” section.

### Concept

• When similar sounding contact names/song names are spoken, the system will display a list of options matching the spoken name. You can choose the required option from the list by calling out the corresponding line number or touching the required option on the screen.

### Note

Note: The infotainment system also displays the voice recognition commands. You can select and view the required command de-tails from within the Voice screen.

### Concept

• Speak the commands and names in a neutral English accent for best results.

### Concept

• Do not take long pauses (greater than 1 second) while speaking the words in a command. Speak the words of the command at a constant rate.

### Concept

• Avoid varying your pitch and volume while speaking the commands. Speak clearly and loudly at a reasonable speed.

### Concept

• Ensure that there is no noise disturbance when you speak the commands like, other passengers in the vehicle are talking or there is lot of wind noise. Disturbance from external sound sources may result in poor voice recognition.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Voice Assistant

### Concept

Always face forward while speaking your commands as the voice recognition quality is best in this orientation.

ABOUT THIS MANUAL Warranty

### Concept

The warranty clauses applicable to the infotainment system are listed below:

### Concept

1. Warranty is applicable in India only.

### Concept

2. Warranty for the product is against defective materials and manufacturing faults for 4 years / 2 lakh kms (whichever comes earlier) from the date of the first sale of vehicle.

### Concept

3. Display and touch panel, if applicable to your system, are covered for 36 months / 60000 kms from the date of the first sale of vehicle.

### Concept

− Where the product has been dismantled, repaired, altered, modified, or damaged due to user negligence and misuse. − The serial number of the product been removed, defaced, or altered. − Warranty void sticker is removed or tampered. − Improper usage such as wrong electrical supply/voltage setting causing damage to the equipment.

title: VEHICLE FUNCTIONS Lighting
text:
# VEHICLE FUNCTIONS Lighting

## Knowledge

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to control lighting features like Approach Lamp and DRL if your vehicle is equipped with these features.

### Concept

When you approach your car in the dark, you can switch on the Approach Lamps (some exterior and interior lights of the vehicle) to identify your car as well as to find your way safely to it.

### Concept

The system allows you to set the time for which the Approach lamps will be illuminated after you switch them ON.

### Concept

To set the Approach lights illumination time:

### Concept

1. In the Vehicle Settings screen, navigate to and select the Approach Lamps option. The system displays the various illumination time options.

### Concept

2. Navigate to and select the required illumination time option from 30 seconds/60 seconds/90 seconds.

### Concept

Figure 68 Approach lamp

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p86_img00` (page 86, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p86_img00.png`

### Concept

DRL (Daytime Running Lamps)

### Concept

If the vehicle is equipped with this feature, you can ON/OFF DRL (Daytime Running Lamps) from the infotainment system.

### Concept

1. In the Vehicle Setup screen, navigate to and select the Lights option.

### Concept

2. In the Lighting screen tap on DRL tap the DRL bar icon to ON/OFF DRLs.

### Concept

Figure 69 Daytime Running Lamps

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p87_img00` (page 87, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p87_img00.png`

### Concept

VEHICLE FUNCTIONS TATA Assist Call (Breakdown Call)*

### Concept

TATA Assist Call (Breakdown Call)*

### Concept

In case of vehicle break down, the infotainment system helps you to reach you to Tata Motors service centre.

### Note

Note: This feature requires active inbuilt internet connectivity in the car.

### Concept

1. Tap the Break Call application, from the App launcher Screen.

### Concept

2. Tap B Call button, the infotainment system dials the Tata Break Down Service centre.

### Concept

3. Swipe right on the ‘Slide to End Call’ bar to disconnect the call.

### Concept

Figure 70 Break Down Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p88_img00` (page 88, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p88_img00.png`

### Concept

In case of Emergency, the infotainment system helps you to call Emergency SOS number.

### Note

Note: This feature requires active inbuilt internet connectivity in the car.

### Concept

1. Tap the Emergency Call application, from the App launcher Screen.

### Concept

2. Tap E Call button, the infotainment system dials the Tata Emergency SOS number.

### Concept

3. Swipe right on the ‘Slide to End Call’ bar to disconnect the call.

### Concept

Figure 71 Emergency Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p88_img01` (page 88, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p88_img01.png`

### Note

Note: For more details, please refer hard copy of owner's manual

### Concept

Voice Alerts VEHICLE FUNCTIONS

### Warning

Voice Alert system alerts or informs you regarding the condition of some critical components or actions performed in your vehicle like warning for door open, change in drive mode and more.

### Concept

The infotainment system plays all the alerts, and you can also view them in the Notification Bar.

### Concept

To turn On/Off Voice Alerts:

### Concept

• In the Vehicle Settings screen, navigate to Voice Alerts option

### Concept

• Tap to turn On/Off Voice Alerts based on your requirement

## Knowledge

### Concept

The Infotainment system allows you to manage various system level settings, like:

### Concept

• Clock – Date and Time

### Concept

To access System Setup:

### Concept

1. Tap Settings, the system displays the Settings screen with various settings list, navigate to and open System Setup Application

### Concept

To set the system date:

### Procedure

1. In the System Setup, navigate to and select the Set Date option. The system displays the Set Date screen.

and down arrows to change the Day, Month and Year accordingly.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_007/p102_img02.png`

### Concept

To set the system time:

### Procedure

1. In the System app, navigate to and select the Set Time option. The system displays the Set Time screen.

### Concept

2. In the Set Time screen, use the up and down arrows to change the Hour and Minute and AM/PM (in case of 12hr format) accordingly.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p102_img03` (page 102, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p102_img03.png`

### Concept

You can reset your system to factory default settings in case you are giving your vehicle to someone for temporary usage or when you are selling out your vehicle. On performing this, system will reset all personalized settings to factory default settings.

### Concept

To perform Factory Reset:

### Concept

1. In the System, navigate to and select the Factory Reset option. The system displays the confirmation pop-up to perform Reset.

### Concept

2. On confirmation, system the system initiates the restoring to factory default settings action. The media source/radio that is currently playing will be stopped and the Phone will be disconnected.

### Concept

3. Once the reset is completed, the system prompts you to switch OFF the infotainment system by doing Ignition OFF.

### Concept

4. The reset action is completed, when you insert the key again (after 10 seconds at least) and switch ON the ignition and the infotainment system.

### Note

Note: Do not OFF the Ignition during the reset process is in progress.

### Concept

### Concept

1. Press Mute button on the Steering Wheel switches for 10 sec and press source change for 10 sec, time gap between two switches should be less than 3 seconds.

### Concept

To force restart the infotainment system. 1. Tap Settings, Select System Settings. 2. Navigate to Force Restart Tab, 3. Tap Restart

### Note

Note: Park your vehicle safely before performing forced restart of Infotainment system

title: 4. Mood Light zone selection will be available for theme selection
text:
# 4. Mood Light zone selection will be available for theme selection

## Knowledge

### Concept

VEHICLE FUNCTIONS Mood Light

### Concept

Mood Lighting is a part of interior lights. It utilizes the LED lights mounted around the cabin to enhance the design and give a soothing experience to driver and other passengers inside car. It is an add on feature to create a lively atmosphere inside cabin.

### Concept

Mood lighting can influence the mood, eye fatigue, circadian rhythms, and concentration of drivers which in turn relates to safety

### Concept

a. Mood Light icon in ‘Settings’ screen (Icon is enabled in IGN ON/Engine-RUN) b. Mood Light icon in Settings screen (Icon is disabled in IGN OFF/Engine-OFF condition) c. Mood Light icon in Settings screen (Icon is disabled in IGN ON/Engine condition)

### Concept

To access Mood Light screen from

### Concept

1. Settings>Mood Light

### Concept

Tap Mood Light Icon on QAD drawer or Application Drawer

### Concept

2. Tap OFF button, to Turn off the Mood Light Feature

### Concept

3. Tap ON button to Turn On the Mood Light Feature

### Procedure

5. Select the ZONE icon to turn on the front and rear mood lighting zone. You can enable both the zones or front or rear zone only

### Concept

Figure 73 Mood Light Feature – Home Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p92_img00` (page 92, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p92_img00.png`

text:
# 2. Long Press Up or Down switches from Steering Wheel Controls

## Knowledge

### Concept

1. Slide left/right your finger on Radio screen rotary element and tune the frequency as per your need, or you can scan the station from steering wheel as well

### Concept

To perform Auto tuning:

### Concept

1. Tap Seek up Seek Down icon or

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p31_img00` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p31_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_007_p31_img01` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p31_img01.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system provides the option of automatically searching and storing available radio stations as presets. When initiated, the Auto Store feature stores the available stations, in the ascending order of their frequency, in the pre-sets bar.

### Concept

To perform Auto store

### Concept

1. Tap Browse on Radio Screen, the system will display various options.

### Concept

2. Navigate to Autostore and touch on screen to start Auto Store.

### Concept

Figure 14 Auto Store

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p31_img02` (page 31, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p31_img02.png`

### Concept

The system will search for the available radio stations and when found, you can tune in the station from the list displayed.

### Concept

1. In the Phone Setup options, navigate to and select Pair New Device option. The system searches for Bluetooth enabled devices within its range.

### Concept

2. Navigate to and select the required phone from the list of currently available Bluetooth enabled devices.

### Concept

3. The system prompts you to confirm the Bluetooth pass key of the phone. Select Yes. The system initiates the pairing of the infotainment system and the selected phone. If the pairing is successful, the system displays the phone in the Paired Devices screen. A copy of your phone data like call logs (phone numbers and other contact details) is also created in the system.

### Concept

4. Tap Allow to allow all the requested notifications of the phone once paired with the Infotainment system via Bluetooth.

### Concept

Figure 16 Pair New Device

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p33_img00` (page 33, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p33_img00.png`

### Concept

To delete a device from the list, Select the device and tap Delete icon

### Concept

To delete all devices connected to the infotainment system.

### Concept

1. Tap Delete All devices tab.

### Concept

When a mobile phone is paired and connected to the infotainment system, you can manage the following phone operations through the hands-free capability of the system:

### Concept

• View call log and contacts.

### Concept

• Make an outgoing call (Last 20 call Logs)

### Concept

• Accept/reject an incoming call.

### Concept

• Reject Incoming call with SMS.

### Concept

• Put a call on hold.

### Concept

• Manage two calls at a time.

### Concept

• Conduct a conference call.

### Concept

• Toggle between the Phone handset and the hands-free capability

### Concept

• SMS read out by the system.

### Concept

You can view all calls, received, or dialed from the infotainment system or missed when connected to the system, in the call log. The system displays up to 20 missed calls, 20 dialed calls and 20 received calls.

### Concept

To view the call log:

### Concept

1. In the Phone Browse screen, tap Call Logs. The system displays the details of up to 60 past calls in the Call Log screen.

### Concept

1. The infotainment system allows you to view up to five thousand contacts stored in your phone book.

### Concept

2. To view the contacts a. In the Phone Browse screen, tap Contacts. The

### Concept

system displays the Contacts screen with the list of contacts stored in your phone book.

### Concept

Making Outgoing Calls

### Concept

The infotainment system supports 5 ways to make a phone call. They are:

### Concept

• Dialing by selecting the phone number from the call log

### Concept

• Dialing by selecting the phone number from the contacts

### Concept

• Dialing the phone number manually using Dialpad

### Concept

• Dialing by selecting the phone number from the Favorites

### Concept

• Dialing using voice command.

### Concept

Figure 17 Outgoing Call Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p34_img00` (page 34, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p34_img00.png`

### Concept

Dialing Using the Call Log

### Concept

To dial a number from the list of previous calls (call log):

### Concept

1. Display the call log. Refer to the “Viewing Call Logs” section for information on displaying the call log.

### Concept

2. Select the required number from the list. The system dials the selected number and initiates the outgoing call.

### Concept

Figure 18 Call Log Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p35_img00` (page 35, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p35_img00.png`

### Concept

Dialing Using the Contact

### Concept

To make a call by dialing a number from the contacts:

### Concept

1. Open the Contacts screen. Refer to the “Viewing Contacts” section for the steps to open the Contacts screen.

### Concept

2. Navigate through the contacts and select the required number. The system dials the selected number and initiates the outgoing call.

### Note

Note: The contact numbers that do not have a name defined for them will be displayed Last in the Contact list with an #.

### Concept

Dialing the Phone Number Manually using Dialpad

### Concept

To make a call by manually dialing a phone number:

### Concept

1. In the Phone Browse screen, select the Dialpad. The system displays the Keypad to enter the phone number.

### Concept

2. Enter the digits of the phone number in the Dialpad.

### Concept

3. After entering the phone number, tap Call. The system initiates the outgoing call.

### Note

Note: The system retains the phone number that was last dialed in the Dialpad. So, to redial the phone number, you can just open the Dialpad and select the Call icon.

### Concept

Dialing Using the Favorites

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p35_img01` (page 35, confidence 0.963)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p35_img01.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system supports marking contacts as favorites. The system also allows you to view and access these favorite contacts separately from the Favorites screen, in addition to the Contacts screen.

### Concept

Marking a Contact as Favorite

### Concept

To mark a contact as favorite:

### Concept

1. In the Contacts screen, select the required contact and tap displayed beside the contact number. The system highlights the star icon, and the contact is marked as favorite.

### Note

Note: You can save maximum 20 contacts to the favorite list.

### Concept

Viewing the Favorites List

### Concept

You can identify the contacts marked as favorite with the highlighted star in the Contacts screen. All favorite contacts can also be separately viewed in the Favorites screen.

### Concept

To display the Favorites screen:

### Concept

1. In the Phone Browse screen, tap Favorites. The system displays the Favorites screen with the list of favorite contacts.

### Concept

Dialing from Favorite Contact List

### Concept

To dial a favorite contact

### Concept

Open the Favorites screen. The system lists all contacts marked as favorite. Navigate to the required favorite contact and tap Call. The system dials the number of the selected favorite contact and initiates the outgoing call.

### Concept

Accepting/Rejecting Incoming Calls

### Concept

When you receive a phone call, you can either accept or reject it from the infotainment system.

### Concept

If your mobile phone is paired and currently connected to the system, the system notifies you with a popup message when you receive a phone call. The system allows you to Accept, Reject or Reject Incoming call with Message.

### Concept

To accept incoming call:

### Concept

Select the Accept icon in the popup message. The system connects the call to enable you to talk to the caller.

### Note

Note: You can also accept the call using the button Steering Wheel control.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p36_img00` (page 36, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p36_img00.png`

### Concept

To reject incoming call:

### Concept

1. Select the Reject icon in the popup message. The system disconnects the call.

### Note

Note: You can also reject the call using the

### Concept

Steering Wheel control.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p36_img01` (page 36, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p36_img01.png`

### Concept

Reject Incoming call with Message

### Concept

In the Reject with Message option, the system rejects the call and sends a SMS to the caller with the configured text.

### Concept

Figure 20 Reject Call with Message

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p37_img00` (page 37, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p37_img00.png`

### Concept

Handling Call Functions

### Concept

When you are in a call (outgoing or incoming), the system supports you to perform any of the following functions:

### Concept

• Respond to the Interactive Voice Response (IVR) with the required details.

### Concept

• Put the call on hold.

### Concept

• Switch between phone (handset) and system (hands- free) capability

### Concept

• Accept another incoming call.

### Concept

• Switch between Calls

### Concept

• Conduct a conference call by adding another number or by merging two existing calls.

### Note

Note: Maximum 5 contacts/ participants can be added to a conference call.

### Concept

Responding to the IVR

### Concept

When you have called a contact with Interactive Voice Response (IVR) like customer care number of bank and so on, you will have to enter some details through the phone. For example, you might have to enter your bank account number, when prompted by the IVR. You can use the Dialpad in-call option to enter such details through the infotainment system.

### Concept

To display the Dialpad and to respond to the IVR with details:

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, tap Dialpad and enter the details as prompted by the IVR.

### Concept

Putting a Call on Hold

### Concept

To put a call on hold:

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, tap Hold. The system puts the currently active call on hold.

### Concept

Switching Between Handset and Hands-Free

### Concept

When in an active call, the system allows you to switch between the phone handset and its hands-free capability and vice versa.

### Concept

To toggle between phone and system:

### Concept

In the active call screen, tap Handset icon to switch the call from system to phone or Handsfree to switch from phone to system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p38_img00` (page 38, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p38_img00.png`

### Concept

Accepting Another Incoming Call

### Concept

When you are in an active call and receive another incoming call, you can put the active call on hold and accept the new call. The system allows you to have a maximum of 2 calls at any given time, one on hold and the other active. To accept another incoming call:

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, the system displays a new call popup message with Accept, Reject and Reject with Message icons, when you receive a new incoming call. Select Accept in the new call popup message. The system puts the first call on hold and activates the new call.

### Concept

Switching Between Calls

### Concept

When you have 2 calls simultaneously (one on hold and other active), the system allows you to switch between the calls without ending either of them.

### Concept

To switch between calls: 1. Tap switch calls option.

### Concept

Conducting a Conference Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p38_img01` (page 38, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p38_img01.png`

### Concept

When in an active call, you can connect an additional phone number to create a conference call between the contacts. You can create a conference call by either dialing to an additional number or by accepting a new incoming call.

### Concept

To create a conference call by dialing additional number

### Concept

1. In the active call screen, tap Add Call . The system puts the active call on hold and displays the Contacts screen. You can dial the additional number from the contacts list or from the call log, the favorites list.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p38_img02` (page 38, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p38_img02.png`

### Concept

2. Follow the steps listed in the “Making an Outgoing Call” section for dialing a number using the various options. The system initiates an outgoing call for the selected number.

### Concept

3. In the new call screen, tap Merge. The system merges the 2 calls (one on hold and the new call) to create a

### Concept

conference call. The first call is activated before merging.

### Concept

To create a conference call by accepting a new incoming call:

### Concept

1. Accept a new incoming call as detailed in the “Accepting/Rejecting an Incoming Phone Call” section.

### Concept

2. In the new call screen, tap Merge. The system merges the 2 calls (one on hold and the new call) to create a conference call. The first call is activated before merging.

### Note

Note: You can view the list of participants in a conference call by taping the Participants icon.

### Note

Note: There can be maximum 5 participants in a conference call.

### Concept

Figure 21 Add Call to Conference

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p39_img00` (page 39, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p39_img00.png`

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Wireless Charger

### Concept

Wireless Phone Charger (WPC) is available in Tata vehicle to give an experience to charge your smart devices wirelessly. This refrains the anxiety of smartphone discharge during the drive. Popup indication appears on the screen to show the status of charging.

### Concept

Following screen is displayed when the phone is charged using the charging Pad.

### Concept

When no phone is placed on the charging pad, the charging on icon is hidden.

### Concept

When the phone is being charged using charging pad, wireless Charger icon pops up on the top right corner of the status bar.

### Concept

Figure 22 Wireless Charing On

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p40_img00` (page 40, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p40_img00.png`

### Concept

In case of charging error, the error charging icon is displayed on the top right corner of the status bar.

### Concept

Battery full charge pop appears on the system screen once the phone is fully charged.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Android Auto

### Concept

Android Auto is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Android smartphones from your vehicle infotainment system. You can use voice actions or simple arrangement of Google Maps, and other important phone functions to access the required functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

### Concept

The Android Auto feature requires the installation of the Android Auto Mobile App, which can be downloaded on your smartphone from Google Play Store.

### Note

Note: Applicable only for Android Smartphones with Android Version 10 and above

### Concept

• Make sure your phone is running Android 5.0 (Lollipop) and up. For best performance, Google recommend An- droid 6.0 (Marshmallow) and up.

### Concept

• Download Android Auto - Apps on Google Play from Google Play.

### Concept

• Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection.

### Note

Note: By default, Android Auto is configured in the infotainment system. Thereby, when you connect your Android Auto enabled smartphone with the infotainment

### Concept

system you will be prompted to select whether you would like to continue the phone connection for Android Auto.

### Note

Note: Android Auto is by default enabled on your vehicle.

### Concept

Connect - Wireless Android Auto

### Concept

1. Pair/connect your phone to the infotainment system using Bluetooth ® .

### Concept

2. Follow the prompts on the screen and on your phone to start.

### Concept

3. You will be asked to accept Terms before using the feature.

### Concept

Connect – Wired Android Auto

### Concept

1. Ensure your vehicle is in the parked condition and the Park Brake is applied.

### Concept

2. Connect your phone using USB cable to the Infotainment to start Android Auto

### Concept

3. Follow the prompts on the screen and on your phone to start.

### Note

Note: Your phone’s Bluetooth will be turned on automatically when wired Android Auto is connected to the car via USB.

### Concept

Android Auto APPLICATIONS

### Concept

Figure 24 Android Auto Projection

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p43_img00` (page 43, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p43_img00.png`

### Concept

Tap on Android Auto application from the App Launcher screen. Follow the instructions to get started.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p43_img01` (page 43, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p43_img01.png`

### Note

Note: If the connection with the infotainment system is lost, the app will get disconnected and infotainment system displays the home screen.

### Note

Note: Ensure you have enabled your Location in the Phone settings for using Android Auto Google Map navigation.

### Note

Note: Android Auto settings can be accessed from your phone only. Refer to your phone for settings details.

### Note

Note: For better usability of the Android Auto app, the Internet connectivity of phone must be good.

### Concept

You can access the Google Maps, communication functionalities (receives and make phone calls, receive, and send messages and so on) of your smartphone through the infotainment system. Even in the infotainment system, you just need to provide voice actions to control these functionalities, without removing your hand from the steering wheel.

### Concept

Any new message that you receive on your phone is displayed on the home screen and readout to you. You can either reply to the SMS with a default message like “I am Driving.

### Concept

You can use Google Assistant (voice recognition) so that your voice actions are recognized. To activate, tap the Mic icon (highlighted in the above figure) on the Android Auto Home screen.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p43_img02` (page 43, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p43_img02.png`

### Note

Note: Click the icon to go to the Android Auto Home screen from any other Android Auto screens.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Android Auto

### Concept

Access Google Maps using Android Auto

### Concept

To access Google Maps and its navigation support features from Android Auto on the infotainment system:

### Concept

1. Tap the icon on the Android Auto Home screen on the infotainment system. The Google Maps screen is displayed. You can now initiate and use the various features of Google Maps from the infotainment system, as you handle it from your Android smartphone.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p44_img00` (page 44, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p44_img00.png`

### Concept

Figure 25 Android Auto Google Map Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p44_img01` (page 44, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p44_img01.png`

### Concept

Handle Calls using Android Auto

### Concept

To handle calls or other communication related actions from Android Auto on the infotainment system:

### Concept

1. Tap the icon on the Android Auto Home screen on the infotainment system. The Dialer screen is displayed. You can now make calls, receive calls, or handle any other communication or other communication actions from the infotainment system, as you handle it from your Android smartphone.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p44_img02` (page 44, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p44_img02.png`

### Concept

1. On your display, select the app launcher . 2. Tap Android Auto 3. Select your favorite music app to browse and play music

### Concept

Apple CarPlay APPLICATIONS

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Apple iPhone from your vehicle infotainment system. You can use voice commands or the simple iPhone like interface on your infotainment system to operate your phone functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

### Note

Note: Applicable only for iPhones. Apple CarPlay is compatible from iPhone 5 and above versions. For more information, refer to

### Concept

https://www.apple.com/in/ios/carplay/

### Concept

Before you connect the iPhone to infotainment system to use Apple CarPlay, you need to perform some one-time configuration steps:

### Concept

1. Make sure you have iPhone 5 or up device, running on latest iOS.

### Concept

2. Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection.

### Note

Note: Apple CarPlay is by default enabled on your vehicle (if available).

### Concept

Connect – Wireless Apple CarPlay 1. Pair/connect your phone to the infotainment system using Bluetooth ® . 2. Follow the prompts on the screen and on your iPhone to start a wireless Apple CarPlay session. 3. You will be asked to accept Terms of Use before using the feature.

### Concept

Connect – Wired Apple CarPlay

### Concept

1. Connect your iPhone to the infotainment system, using the original Apple or Apple certified Lightning USB cable. On successful establishment of the connection, the infotainment system displays a popup or highlights the Apple CarPlay menu, if in focus in the home screen

### Concept

2. Tap on the popup/menu to launch the Apple CarPlay Home screen.

### Note

Note: If the connection with the infotainment system is lost, the app is disconnected, and the infotainment system Home screen is displayed.

### Note

Note: The settings of Apple CarPlay can be accessed from your iPhone only.

### Concept

APPLICATIONS Apple CarPlay

### Concept

You can access the Music, Message, communication functionalities (receives and make phone calls and so on) of your iPhone through the infotainment system. In the infotainment system, in addition to using the touch screen, control elements and SWC controls, you can just provide voice actions to control these functionalities, without removing your hand from the steering wheel.

### Concept

Figure 26 Apple CarPlay Home Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p46_img00` (page 46, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p46_img00.png`

### Concept

Say Hey Siri to activate Siri (voice recognition) so that your voice actions are recognized, tap and hold the Home icon on the Apple CarPlay Home screen. Once you are displayed with the waves, you can speak your voice action.

### Concept

Apple CarPlay will automatically get started in Connection. If Apple CarPlay does not activate automatically, you can access Apple CarPlay by:

### Concept

1. Tapping on Apple CarPlay icon.

### Concept

Handle Calls, Messages and Communication Actions

### Concept

To handle the various actions of your iPhone from Apple CarPlay on the infotainment system:

### Concept

1. To Handle Calls : Tap the Phone icon on the Apple CarPlay Home screen on the infotainment system. You can now make calls, receive calls, and view contacts.

### Concept

2. To Handle Messages : Tap the Messages icon. You can now read, send, and reply to received messages or handle other communication actions from the infotainment system, as you handle it from your iPhone.

### Concept

3. To handle Music : Tap the Music, Podcasts or Audiobooks icon. You can now access all your content from iTunes ® , Music app or other available third-party audio apps.

### Concept

4. To Return to the Infotainment System Home Screen: Tap the home icon. The system closes Apple CarPlay and displays the system home screen.

### Concept

Apple CarPlay APPLICATIONS

### Concept

5. You can click home icon on the left bar to go back to Home Screen on the infotainment system

### Note

Note: The other features in Apple CarPlay can be similarly accessed from your infotainment system.

### Concept

Figure 27 Apple CarPlay Screen with an Active Call

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p47_img00` (page 47, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p47_img00.png`

### Concept

When an Apple CarPlay session is active in the system and you access other system functions like, HVAC and Volume Control, the status of these functions will be displayed at the top of the Apple CarPlay screen.

### Concept

1. On your display, select the app launcher . 2. Tap Apple Carplay 3. Select your favorite music app to browse and play music

### Concept

Figure 28 Apple CarPlay Music Screen

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_007_p47_img01` (page 47, confidence 0.978)
  - File: `images/doc_007/p47_img01.png`

### Note

To setup Alexa as your voice assistant, you must sign into Amazon 1. Tap Alexa on the Application Screen 2. Go to https://amazon.com/us/code and enter the code displayed

### Note

Note : Your infotainment system must be connected to Wi-Fi to use this feature

### Note

Note : This feature is applicable based on vehicle variant.

### Note

Note: This feature is applicable only in vehicles which have inbuilt internet connectivity.

Figure 29 Amazon Sign in Screen

3. You will be signed in to use Alexa voice assistant.

### Concept

Sign in Using QR Code

### Concept

1. Open built in Camera of your phone 2. Point the camera towards QR Code 3. Follow the instructions displayed to Sign in

### Concept

To use Alexa, press Push to Talk button on the steering wheel or simply Say Alexa.

Figure 30 Using Alexa Screen

Alexa – Feature List

You can ask Alexa to do any number of things specific to your car:

1. Stream Music 2. Weather update 3. Navigation assistance 4. News and Information 5. Traffic Information

### Table 1

It oﬀers a comfortable resting place for the driver and co-driver arms during long drives, helping to reduce fatigue and provide a more relaxed driving experience.

### Concept

INTELLIGENT SPEED ASSISTANCE (ISA) Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) is a safety feature that adjusts the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) set speed based on detected speed limits from traﬃc signs boards and/or Map provided speed limit. lSA system ensures that vehicle speed does not exceed a safe or legal speed limit while ACC is active.

### Concept

Prerequisite for activation The following condition shall be satisﬁed to activate ISA

### Concept

This system does not guarantee safety or autonomous driving, so the driver should always pay close attention.

### Concept

How to use ISA feature

### Concept

• Driver can activate ISA feature from Infotainment by pressing the following button sequence. Go to Home page >> All App >> Settings >> Drive assist >> Traﬃc Sign Recognition and Speed Assist >> Intelligent Speed Assist.

### Concept

• When the ISA system detects that the current road speed limit is lower than the ACC set speed value, the driver will be notiﬁed by blinking below tell-tale indicator on the instrument cluster for 5 seconds.

### Procedure

• By observing the above mentioned tell-tale indicator blinking, the driver can press the "SET-" button (while tell-tale is blinking) on the steering wheel to adjust the ACC set speed to match the detected speed limit.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_009_p2_img00` (page 2, confidence 0.976)

### Concept

• When ACC Set Speed is adapted / adjusted to detected speed limit, Driver will get below pop up message for 5 sec duration: “ACC set speed changed”

#### Visual References

### Concept

• When ISA is in temporary failure state, below tell-tale indicator will be displayed along with a 5-second pop-up message informing the driver that "Intelligent speed assist system temporary available." • When ISA is in permanent failure state, below tell-tale indicator will be displayed along with a 5-second pop-up message informing the driver – “Intelligent speed assist system failure, please contact service center.”

### Concept

In case of damage to matte paint ﬁnish, whole area is required to be reworked as it is not possible to repair only the damage area. Extreme care is required as it is diﬃcult to restore quality after the repair. Always take your vehicle to Authorized workshop for repair.

### Procedure

• Avoid scrubbing or using abrasive tools like sponge, brush etc on the surface. These can scratch the matte paint and leave visible marks. • Do not wash your vehicle in direct sunlight or when the body is hot. This can cause soap or water to dry prematurely and leave water spots that are harder to remove from matte surfaces. • Do not park your vehicle prolonged in sunlight as this can cause UV fading. • Use tar remover to remove tar contaminates, do not apply too much pressure on the painted area. • While pressure washers are okay for rinsing, avoid using them too close to the paint surface, the high pressure can potentially lead to long-term damage. • The pressure should be under 2500 PSI and stand at minimum of ten inches. • Always wash from top to bottom to keep dirt from moving to clean areas • Gently scrub the surface with the wash pad, using back and forth motions (avoid circular motions to prevent swirl marks). • After washing, park the vehicle in shade or in a garage, it will help prevent water spots from forming on the matte paint surfaces which are more noticeable. • Use a dedicated microﬁber towel, chamois which is designed to absorb water without scratching the surface. • Gently wipe the water from the surface, do not rub it. • To preserve the ﬁnish and add a layer of protection against contaminants, apply matte speciﬁc sealants or protective coatings. • For wheels and hard to reach areas, use a soft brush to clean without damaging the matte ﬁnish. Avoid stiﬀ bristled brushes that may cause scratches.

### Concept

• It is important to ensure that the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) mode is active before utilizing the Intelligent Speed Assist (ISA) feature.

### Concept

1. The front-facing camera must be operational and free of obstructions. 2. Driver must ensure that both the ISA app and the Navigation app are updated to the latest version available in the Arcade app store. 3. Driver must ensure the Traﬃc Sign Recognition (TSR) system is active. 4. Driver must ensure that the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) system is active in order to utilize the ISA functionality. 5. Driver must ensure that there are no failures or degradation of functions related to the steering system, braking system, or any other critical systems.

### Warning

System limitations ISA feature subject to system limitation and unavailable or degrade performance or give false warning in following situations.

### Warning

1. For Speed limit signs with value lower than 30 Kmph, ISA will not reduce the ACC set Speed. However, Driver will be informed through Over speed warning and ISA prompt about the Over speeding. 2.

### Concept

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Power Steering Fluid Level

### Concept

The level of the power steering fluid should be between the MIN. and MAX. mark on the side of the power steering fluid con­ tainer. If the level falls below the MIN. mark, add recommended fluid.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p232_img00` (page 232, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p232_img00.png`

### Concept

In case of leakage or hard steering, please contact the nearest Authorized Service outlet.

### Concept

For location of Power steering fluid

### Concept

container, please refer Engine Com­ partment section. Windshield Washer Fluid Level

### Concept

Check that there is washer fluid in the tank. Refill it if necessary. Use a good quality windshield washer fluid, diluted with water as necessary.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p232_img04` (page 232, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p232_img04.png`

### Procedure

Let the engine cool down before • opening the cap. Wear eye and hand protection when opening the cap. Open the cap slowly half a turn to allow pressure to escape.

### Concept

Do not start the engine without oil in • the power steering system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p232_img01` (page 232, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p232_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not allow dirt into power steering • fluid reservoir during refilling or top up.

### Concept

Holding steering wheel at lock posi­ • tion (i.e >5sec) can damage /fail the power steering pump operation.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p232_img02` (page 232, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p232_img02.png`

### Concept

Do not run the vehicle with dry • power steering pump. Ensure the power steering fluid is available in the reservoir.

### Concept

For Oil/fluid specification and Quantity, please refer ‘Maintenance’ section.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p232_img03` (page 232, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p232_img03.png`

### Concept

Do not use detergent or any other • additive in the windshield washer reservoir. This can severely impair visibility when sprayed on the wind

text:
# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Driver Information System Image Description

### Note

Indicates the number of days/kilometers in which service is due. If service is overdue, it will display “0” km or “0” days and span­ ner symbol will blink at every ignition ON for few seconds. Never reset the display between service intervals otherwise this may result in to incorrect readings. Information is retained in the serv­ ice interval display even after the vehicle battery is discon­ nected. NOTE: This option is for indicative purpose only. Keep track of your odometer reading and follow the maintenance schedule.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p81_img00` (page 81, confidence 0.934)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p81_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_004_p81_img01` (page 81, confidence 0.934)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p81_img01.png`

### Concept

Current gear position indi­ cator (For MT)

### Note

Current gear engaged by the transmission shall be displayed on Driver Information System. NOTE: If “F” is displayed it means a ‘Fault’ condition. Contact the TATA MOTORS authorized service centre. In case of Manual Transmission, the gear number shall be dis­ played when the clutch is fully released.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p81_img02` (page 81, confidence 0.79)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p81_img02.png`

### Concept

Up or down arrow shall be displayed on DIS whenever a gear should be shifted up or down. No arrow shall be displayed when the selected gear is as per the vehicle dynamics.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p81_img03` (page 81, confidence 0.82)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p81_img03.png`

## Knowledge

### Concept

Instructions On How To Use The Puncture Repair Kit Safely

### Concept

Use product with original vehicle • ground tires only.

### Concept

Only use the Puncture repair Kit with • tubeless tires.

### Concept

If used for other than its intended pur­ • pose, the Puncture repair Kit may cause severe accident or injury due to the fact that compressed air can act as an explosive or propellant.

### Concept

Park your vehicle at the roadside so • that you do not obstruct the flow of traf­ fic and you are able to use the Punc­ ture repair Kit without being in danger.

### Concept

Engage the hand brake, even if you • have parked on a level road, to ensure that the vehicle will not move.

### Concept

Do not attempt to remove foreign ob­ • jects like nails or screws penetrating the tire. Leave them as they are.

### Concept

Leave the engine running while the • Puncture repair Kit is in use, but not if the vehicle is in an enclosed or poorly ventilated area.

### Concept

Never leave the Puncture repair Kit un­ • attended while in use.

### Concept

Do not keep the compressor operating • for more than 10 minutes otherwise there is a risk of it over-heating.

### Concept

Replace the sealant bottle with a new • one before the expiration date is reached (see bottle label). In case that the sealant is expired the functionality cannot be fully guaranteed. Only use original Puncture re-pair Kit bottles which are pressure resistant. How To Proceed In The Event Of Tyre Puncture

### Concept

You can temporarily repair a tire puncture in two steps.

### Warning

First pump the tire sealant and air into the tire (see Step 1). Immediately thereafter, drive a short distance (3-10 km / 2-6 miles) in order to distribute the sealant in the tire. After that, check the tire pressure and pump more air into the tire if necessary (see Step 2). Then you can proceed to drive with caution for a maximum distance of 200 km (120 miles) and at a maxi-mum speed of 80 km/h (50 mph).

### Concept

Inform all other users of the vehicle that the tire has been temporarily sealed with the Puncture repair Kit and make them aware of the special driving conditions to be observed.

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

The vehicle is equipped with DEF injection system and Selective Catalytic Reduc­ tion (SCR) to meet emission standards. DEF Storage

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p243_img00` (page 243, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p243_img00.png`

### Specification

DEF is a very stable product with a long shelf life. Stored at temperatures LOWER than 32°C, it has a shelf life of at least one year.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p243_img01` (page 243, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p243_img01.png`

### Concept

Preliminary Conditions

### Concept

Consumption of the additive DEF de- pends on the condition of vehicle use and is indicated on the instrument cluster.

### Specification

DEF freezes at temperatures lower than - 11°C. If the car stands for a long time at this temperature refilling could be difficult. For this reason, it is advised to park the vehicle in a garage and/or heated environ-ment and wait for the DEF to return to liq-uid state before topping up.

### Concept

Park the car on flat ground and stop • the engine by placing the ignition in the OFF position.

### Concept

DEF filler is located in the tailgate com­ •

### Procedure

partment below the tool kit tray. Open the tailgate and remove the tool kit tray and remove the cap from the DEF filler.

### Specification

DEF freezes at temperatures lower than -11°C.

### Concept

When working with DEF, it is important to know that:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p243_img02` (page 243, confidence 0.973)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p243_img02.png`

### Concept

Any containers or parts that comes • into contact with DEF must be DEF compatible (plastic or stainless steel). Copper, brass, aluminum,

### Concept

iron or non-stainless steel should be avoid-ed as they are subject to cor­ rosion by DEF.

### Concept

During filling, if DEF overflows / is • spilled, kindly ensure it is cleaned / wiped up completely by wet cloth & then by dry cloth also.

### Concept

Never fill DEF or diesel fuel into the wrong filling ports. This may result seri­ ous damage to Engine, Fuel system and Emission system components. In case of wrongly filled do not start the engine, contact TATA Motors Authorised Service Centre.

# IMPORTANT INFORMATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

• Before driving, read this Owner’s manual carefully and familiarize yourself with your vehicle. For your own safety and a longer ve­ hicle life, follow the instructions, ‘Warnings’ and ‘Notes’ in this manual. Ignoring them could result in damage to the or personal injury to you or others.

### Concept

• The Owner’s manual and other booklets are important documents and should always be kept in the vehicle. If you sell the vehicle, always pass on the documents to the new owner.

### Note

• This Owner's Manual describes all variants of the model and all standard/optional equipment of your vehicle available at the time of printing. Please note that your vehicle may not be equipped with all features described.

### Concept

• TATA MOTORS PASSENGER VEHICLES LIMITED reserves the right to introduce changes in the design, equipment and technical features without any obligation to install them on the vehicles previously sold. The equipment in your vehicle may therefore differ from that shown in the descriptions and illustrations.

### Concept

• Do not carry out any modification including fitment of non-genuine accessories on your vehicle. Safety, handling, performance and durability, may otherwise be adversely affected and may violate government regulations. TATA MOTORS PASSENGER VEHICLES LIMITED no liability for damage resulting from the modifications or use of non-genuine accessories.

### Concept

• All rights reserved.The information in this manual shall not be copied, translated or otherwise reproduced, in whole or inpart without written permission from TATA MOTORS.

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” po­ sition, this gauge indicates level of DEF left in the tank.

When DEF in tank is near to empty posi­ tion, DEF tell tale near to gauge will glow with subsequent text messages on LCD screen. To change screen over from IFE to DEF Gauge press mode button. text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Check for inflation and condition of your vehicle tyres periodically.

### Concept

Check the pressure in the tyres when they are cold.

### Concept

Keeping the tyres properly inflated gives you the best combination of riding comfort, handling, tyre life and better fuel efficiency.

### Concept

Over inflation of tyres makes the vehicle ride bumpy and harsh. Tyres are more prone to uneven wear and dam-age from road hazards.

### Concept

Under inflated tyres reduce your comfort in vehicle handling and are prone to fail­ ures due to high temperature. They also cause uneven wear and more fuel con­ sumption.

text:
# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Speedometer indicates the vehicle speed in km/h.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p77_img00` (page 77, confidence 0.989)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p77_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_004_p77_img01` (page 77, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p77_img01.png`

### Concept

Tachometer indicates engine speed in rev­ olutions per min (rpm).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p77_img02` (page 77, confidence 0.989)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p77_img02.png`

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in “ON” posi­ tion, fuel gauge gives an approximate in­ dication of the amount of fuel in the fuel tank. “F” stands for full and “E” stands for empty.

### Warning

When fuel in the tank is near to empty po­ sition, low fuel warning telltale turns Amber. Refill the tank as soon as possible.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p77_img04` (page 77, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p77_img04.png`
- Image: `doc_004_p77_img05` (page 77, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p77_img05.png`

### Procedure

Whenever you turn the ignition ON, the instrument cluster needles and gauges move to maximum value and return to ‘0’ position. This is a welcome strategy and a self-check feature.

### Concept

Never drive the vehicle with high engine ‘rpm’. This may cause severe engine damage.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p77_img03` (page 77, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p77_img03.png`

### Concept

Check the fuel level when the vehi­ • cle on a level road.

### Warning

The fuel level displayed can vary • when you drive on inclines, curves, brake and accelerate suddenly. This is due to the movement of fuel in the tank. The low fuel warning lamp may turn to ON or OFF earlier or later than usual.

## Tables

title: IMPORTANT INFORMATION
text:
# IMPORTANT INFORMATION

## Knowledge

### Warning

In this Owner’s Manual, you will find the text under the heading “WARNING” and “NOTE” which highlights important infor­ mation. Pay particular attention to these highlighted messages.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p9_img00` (page 9, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p9_img00.png`

### Concept

Safety consciousness not only ensures your safety and the safety of other road users, but it also helps to reduce the wear and tear on your vehicle.

### Concept

Safe driving depends on:

### Concept

How quickly you make decisions to • avoid an accident.

### Concept

Your ability to concentrate. •

### Concept

How well you can see and judge ob­ • jects.

### Concept

How well familiar you are with your ve­ • hicle controls and its capabilities.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p9_img02` (page 9, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p9_img02.png`

### Concept

Indicates additional information that will assist you in gaining the optimum ben­ efit and care for your vehicle.

### Concept

Indicates procedures or information that must be followed precisely in order to avoid the possibility of severe personal injury and serious damage to the vehi­ cle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p9_img01` (page 9, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p9_img01.png`

### Concept

Fatigue is a result of physical or mental exertion that impairs judgment. Driver fatigue may be due to inadequate sleep, extended work hours, strenuous work or non-work activities or combina­ tion of other factors. Take rest at regular intervals.

### Concept

Always take into account the road con­ • ditions, weather conditions, vehicle speed in order to prevent accidents.

### Concept

Turn ‘ON’ the side indicators at least • 30 meters before taking a turn or changing the lane.

### Concept

Decelerate to a safe speed before tak­ • ing turn. Do not apply brakes during cornering.

### Concept

When overtaking other vehicles, watch • out for the oncoming vehicle.

### Concept

Never drive under the influence of al­ • cohol or drugs.

### Concept

If your vehicle is equipped with info­ • tainment/navigation system, set and make changes to your travel route only when the vehicle is parked.

### Concept

Program radio presets with the vehicle • parked, and use your programmed presets to make radio use quicker and simpler.

### Concept

Driving Through Water

### Concept

Do not drive through flooded areas. Judge the depth of water before driving through it. Otherwise, water may enter the vehicle interior or the engine compartment.

### Concept

If at all the situation demands that you have to drive through water then;

### Concept

Keep engine in higher RPM and crawl • the vehicle in low gear.

### Concept

Flowing or rushing water creates • strong forces. Driving through flowing water could cause the vehicle to about trying to drive through flowing water.

### Concept

Lightly apply the brake pedal to dry the • liners until the brakes work normally once you are out of water.

### Concept

Driving on a Rainy Day

### Concept

Check wiper blades, lights and brakes • for proper functioning and condition.

### Concept

Check the tyre treads depth, the con­ • dition of the tread and tyre.

### Concept

Avoid harsh braking and sharp turns. It • may cause loss of control and lead to a skid.

### Concept

For slowing down, shift to lower gears • and brake gently.

### Concept

Keep lights ‘ON’ if visibility is poor. • Driving on Wet Roads

### Concept

On wet road or during light showers, “Aquaplaning” can occur. “Aquaplaning” is the loss of direct contact between the road surface and the vehicle’s tires due to a water film forming between them. Steering or braking the vehicle can be very difficult, and loss of control can occur.

### Concept

There is no hard and fast rule about aqua­ planing. The best advice is to slow down when the road is wet.

### Concept

Do not attempt to start the engine if ve­ hicle gets flooded due to water. Tow the vehicle to a safe place. Contact a near­ est TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p10_img00` (page 10, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p10_img00.png`

### Concept

Driving on Snowy Roads

### Concept

While driving in snow, it is advisable to use the snow chain on roads. Follow assembly and safety instruction provided by the snow chain manufacturers.

### Concept

Ensure that all lights are working and • windshield, window glasses are clean.

### Concept

Drive more slowly at night than in the • daytime, as the visual range is re­ stricted at night. Maintain a speed such that you can stop within illuminated distance of head lamps.

### Concept

Do not use the high beam unless in­ • evitable. It may dazzle the driver of the oncoming vehicle, thus causing an ac­ cident.

### Concept

Use head lamp main/dip beam to alert • other road users on turns/ cross roads.

### Concept

Use side indicators for lane change or • turning.

### Concept

Driving on Gradients

### Concept

When climbing gradient, the vehicle may begin to slow down and show a lack of power. If this happens, shift to a lower gear and apply power smoothly so that there is no loss of traction.

### Concept

When driving down a hill, the engine brak­ ing should be used by shifting into a lower gear. Do not drive in neutral gear or switch off the engine.

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a delayed reaction from the brakes when braking for the first time. You have to press the brake pedal more firmly. Maintain a greater distance from the ve­ hicle in front.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p11_img00` (page 11, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p11_img00.png`

### Concept

On long and steep gradients you must reduce the load on the brakes by shift­ ing early to a lower gear. This allows you to take advantage of the engine braking effect and helps avoid over­ heating of service brakes resulting in re­ duced braking efficiency.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p11_img01` (page 11, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p11_img01.png`

### Concept

Stopping distance progressively, in­ creases with vehicle speed. Maintain a sufficient distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead.

### Concept

For long distance driving, perform safety checks before starting a trip and take rest at certain intervals to prevent fatigue.

### Concept

This section of user manual describes your vehicle seat belt, airbag and Child re­ straints system. Please read and follow all these instructions carefully to minimize risk of severe injury or death.

### Concept

Seat belts are the primary restraints • system in the vehicle. All occupants, including the driver, should always wear their seat belts to minimize the risk of injury.

### Concept

Sit back and adjust (if equipped), the • seat. Make sure that your seat is ad­ justed to a good driving position and the back of the seat is upright.

### Concept

Buckling the Shoulder Seat Belt

### Concept

Grasp the tongue then slowly pull out • the seat belt over the shoulder and across the chest. When the seat belt is long enough to fit, insert the tongue into the lock buckle until you hear a “CLICK” which indicates that the seat belt is securely locked.

### Concept

Position the lap portion of seat belt • across your thighs, below your ab­ domen. To remove slack, pull up a bit on the shoulder seat belt. To loosen the lap portion seat belt if it is too tight, tilt the tongue and pull on the lap seat belt. A snug seat belt reduces the risk of sliding under the seat belt in a colli­ sion. Ensure that the seat belt running over the body (shoulder segment and lap segment) does not have any twist. Twisted seat belt may not offer effec­ tive protection when required.

### Concept

Releasing the Seat Belt

### Concept

To release the seat belt, push the red but­ ton on the lock buckle. The seat belt will automatically retract to its stowed position. If necessary, slide the tongue down the webbing to allow the seat belt to retract fully.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p13_img00` (page 13, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p13_img00.png`

### Concept

Fixed Rear Centre Lap Seat Belt

### Concept

When buckling, make sure you hear a click confirming that the tab is latched into the seat belt lock. To tighten it, pull the loose end through the buckle until the seat belt is comfortably adjusted around the pelvic bone (hips).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p13_img02` (page 13, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p13_img02.png`

### Concept

The above image is for reference pur­ pose only.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p13_img01` (page 13, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p13_img01.png`

### Concept

Each seating position and seat belt • assembly must be used by one oc­ cupant. It is not recommended to put a seat belt around a child, being carried on an occupant’s lap.

### Concept

Be careful not to damage or tamper • the seat belt webbing or hardware. Inspect the seat belt system period­ ically, checking for cuts, frays, or loose parts. A frayed or torn seat belt could rip apart in a collision and leave you with no protection.

### Concept

If the seat belt webbing or hardware • is damaged, get it replaced immedi­ ately at TATA Motors Authorized service centre.

### Concept

Do not insert any items such as • coins, clips, etc. into the seat belt buckles, and be careful not to spill liquids into these parts. If foreign materials get into a seat belt buckle, the seat belt will not work properly.

### Concept

Do not wear seat belts over hard, • sharp or fragile items in clothing, such as pens, keys, spectacles etc.

### Concept

Do not use any accessories on seat • belts or modify in any way the seat belt system. Devices claiming to im­ prove occupant comfort or reposi­ tioning the seat belt, can reduce the protection provided by the seat belt and increase the chance of serious injury in a collision.

### Concept

Seat Belts with Pre - Tensioner (if equipped)

### Concept

You can use pre-tensioner seat belts in the same manner as ordinary seat belts.

### Concept

The seat belt pre-tensioner system works in conjunction with the SUPPLEMENTARY RESTRAINTS SYSTEM (SRS-Airbags).

### Concept

In the event of a collision, as may be nec­ essary, pre-tensioner tightens the seat belt so that it fits the occupant’s body more snugly. When pre-tensioner activates, there could be some noise and release of smoke. This is normal and there are no health hazards or fire risk.

### Concept

If the vehicle has been involved in a colli­ sion, get it inspected immediately at au­ thorized TATA MOTORS SERVICE Center.

### Concept

Seat Belt with Load Limiter (if equipped)

### Concept

You can use the load limiter seat belts in the same manner as ordinary seat belts.

### Concept

The seat belt load limiter system works in conjunction with the SUPPLEMEN-TARY RESTRAINTS SYSTEM (SRS-Airbags).

### Concept

In the event of a collision, as may be nec­ essary, load limiter reduces the load on the rib cage region of the occupant.

### Concept

If the vehicle has been involved in a colli­ sion, get it inspected immediately at Au­ thorized TATA MOTORS SERVICE Center.

### Concept

Use of Seat Belts for Pregnant Woman

### Concept

In a collision, the pre-tensioner seat belt assembly mechanisms become hot dur­ ing activation. Do not touch the pre-ten­ sioner seat belt assemblies for several minutes after they have been activated.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p14_img00` (page 14, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p14_img00.png`

### Concept

Pregnant woman must wear a cor­ • rectly positioned seat belt. It is safer for mother as well as unborn child.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p14_img01` (page 14, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p14_img01.png`

### Concept

Pregnant woman should wear the • lap part of the seat belt across the pelvic bone (hips) and as snug across the hips as possible. Keep the seat belt low so that it does not come across the abdomen. That way the strong bones of the hips will take the force if there is a collision.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p14_img02` (page 14, confidence 0.965)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p14_img02.png`

### Warning

Seat Belt Warning Lamp

### Concept

For Driver For Front

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p15_img00` (page 15, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p15_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_004_p15_img01` (page 15, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p15_img01.png`

### Warning

The seat belt warning lamp reminds you to fasten the seat belt.

### Concept

If the driver does not fasten seat belt, • seat belt reminder lamp will blink and a buzzer will sound for pre-defined du­ ration until the driver’s seat belt is buckled.

### Concept

If front passenger seat is occupied by • adult and does not fasten seat belt, seat belt reminder lamp will blink and a buzzer will sound for pre-defined du­ ration until the front passenger seat belt is buckled.

### Concept

If this system is also provided for other • than Front row seats, applicable above warnings will appear until seat belts are buckled.

### Warning

If front passenger seat is occupied by • child, system may detect occupancy and warn with front passenger seat belt warning. It is not taken to mean child can occupy front passenger seat and use seat belt. Please refer CRS section for recommended seating po­ sition.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p15_img02` (page 15, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p15_img02.png`

### Concept

Using unauthorized after-market seat cover may affect function of occupant sensor. TATA motors does not recom­ mend any non-validated seat covers on seats.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Specification

24 X 7 ROAD ASSISTANCE

### Concept

It is our responsibility and our endeavor to ensure that you have our complete service backup, wherever and whenever you need the same. When you have a road network that spans wide area, the probability of a breakdown happening within hailing dis­ tance of a TATA MOTORS Authorized Workshop is very low.

### Concept

It is precisely for this reason, we have tied up with TVS AA, who will provide break­ down assistance including towing to the nearest TATA MOTORS Authorized Work­ shop through their Authorized Service Providers (ASP).

### Specification

The 24X7 On Road Assistance Program shall be automatically available to your ve­ hicle for the duration of Warranty period. The program shall also be available, if you avail the same post warranty.

### Concept

Response Time ** for the On Road As­ sistance Program

### Concept

** (The response time will depend on the location, terrain, traffic density and the time of the day.) Standard Procedure when Calling for on Road Assistance in case of a Breakdown:

### Concept

Dial the toll free help line number – • 1800 209 8282

### Concept

Identify your vehicle with the Vehicle • chassis number that is available in the Owner’s Manual.

### Concept

Explain your exact location with land­ • marks and tell us about the problem you face with the vehicle.

### Warning

Park your vehicle on the edge of the • road, open the bonnet and put on the hazard warning signal.

### Warning

Place the advance warning triangle • supplied with the vehicle approx. 3 m from the vehicle in the direction of on­ coming traffic. Within City Limits 60 minutes On State or Na­ tional Highways 90 minutes

title: EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE
text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Use only a battery of same rating & capac­ ity to jump start your vehicle. Position the booster battery close to your vehicle so that the jump leads will reach both batter­ ies.

### Concept

When using a battery of another vehicle, do not let the vehicles touch.

### Concept

Apply the parking brake firmly and keep the gearshift lever in neutral.

### Warning

Turn off all vehicle accessories, except those necessary for safety like hazard warning lamps.

### Concept

If your vehicle is equipped with Battery sensor, then do not connect your jump start cable lead directly on the Sensor sur­ face. Connect only on the negative cable surface as shown on the image. After jump start event, IAC function will be restored only when the Vehicle is parked in idle for 3-4 Hours.

### Concept

Make jump lead connections as follows:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p206_img00` (page 206, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p206_img00.png`

### Concept

Connect one end of the first jump lead • to the positive (+) terminal of the dis­ charged battery.

### Concept

Connect the other end to the positive • (+) terminal of the booster battery.

### Concept

Connect one end of the second jump • lead to the negative (–) terminal of the booster battery.

### Concept

Make the final connection (other end of • the negative terminal) to an unpainted, heavy metal part (i.e. engine mounting stud/nut) of the vehicle of discharged battery.

### Concept

Start the engine of the vehicle with the • discharged battery.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p206_img01` (page 206, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p206_img01.png`

### Concept

Before disconnecting the jumper ca­ • bles, let the engine run for several min­ utes.

### Concept

If the booster battery you are using is • fitted to another vehicle, start the en­ gine of the vehicle with the booster bat­ tery. Run the engine at moderate speed.

### Concept

Remove the jump leads in the exact • reverse order in which you connected them.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Make sure that vehicle is completely • stationary before you attempt to shift in reverse gear.

### Concept

Drive slowly on wet roads. •

### Concept

You can get extra braking from the en­ • gine by shifting to a lower gear. This can help you to maintain a safe speed and prevent your brakes from over­ heating specially while going down a hill. Tips for Obtaining Better Fuel Effi­ ciency

### Concept

Always maintain the specified tyre • pressure during fuel top-ups and also before a long trip. Vehicle running with low tyre pressure will consume more fuel than the one running with specified tyre pressure.

### Concept

Keep the vehicle clean. Get rid of the • not in use luggage/stuff lying in the boot etc.

### Concept

Regularly inspect your vehicle for any • leakages, worn out wires, rat bites etc.

### Concept

Always follow periodic & regular serv­ •

### Concept

ice schedule of the vehicle.

### Concept

Drive smart and smooth in an anticipa­ • tory manner. Select driving mode to suit your style.

### Concept

Do not accelerate excessively when • you are in lower gears (1 st or 2 nd ). Be gentle on the accelerator when you are in traffic. In lower gear, opening more throttle will shoot the engine RPM keeping the vehicle still at lower speeds which indirectly implies less distance with more fuel.

### Concept

Be in the maximum possible higher • gear at a given speed. This reduces the engine operating speeds which means the engine is running at lower rpm (Revolutions per Minute) for the same vehicle speed. Lesser the num­ ber of engine revolution lesser the fuel burned.

### Concept

Avoid harsh braking. •

### Concept

Maintain healthy driving habits & while • decelerating, do coasting in gear and not in neutral or with clutch pedal pressed.

### Concept

Consider using the car AC when you •

### Concept

really require. Consider using lower blower speeds rather than higher for cooling as at higher blower speeds it consumes more electric power which is ultimately drawn from engine by burning fuel.

### Concept

Avoid unnecessary extra electrical • loading on the car.

### Concept

Stop the engine wisely at traffic sig­ • nals. Switch ‘OFF’ the engine at the traffic signal only if the stoppage time is high (typically more than 30 sec).

### Concept

While driving on highways, drive with • windows closed. The more you open the windows the higher will be the re­ sistance to the vehicle at higher speeds which will reduce the fuel effi­ ciency.

### Concept

Do not over speed; follow the speed • limits. More the speed, higher the ex­ ternal resistance on the vehicle which will finally result into unnecessary con­ sumption of fuel.

## Knowledge

### Concept

PUNCTURE REPAIR KIT (if avail­ able)

### Specification

The Puncture repair Kit seals most tire punctures to restore temporarily mobility. Recommended use only for passenger car ground tires only and vehicle tire inflation pressure up to 300 kPa (3 bar, 43 psi). The system consists of a compressor and a sealant, and serves to effectively and con­ veniently seal punctures in car tires caused, for example, by nails or similar foreign objects with a diameter of up to ¼

### Concept

Depending on the type and extent of tire damage, some tires can only be partially sealed or not sealed at all. Loss of tire pressure can affect vehicle handling, lead­ ing to loss of vehicle control. Ob-serve the following rules when using the Puncture repair Kit:

### Warning

Drive with caution and avoid making • sudden steering or driving maneuvers , maneuvers, especially if the vehicle is heavily loaded or you are towing a trailer.

### Concept

The system will provide you with an • emergency temporary repair, enabling you to continue your journey to the next vehicle or tire dealer, or to drive a maximum distance of 200 km (120 miles).

### Concept

Do not exceed a maximum speed of • 80 km/h (50 mph).

### Concept

Keep the Puncture repair Kit out of the • reach of children.

### Concept

Once the Puncture repair Kit has been • used for a temporary tire repair, the functionality of the TPMS module (if

### Concept

applicable) shall be checked by an ex­ pert and replaced if necessary.

### Concept

These instructions provide a step-by-step explanation of how to use the Puncture re­ pair Kit to temporarily repair a tire punc­ ture.

### Concept

Please read the section on “How to pro­ ceed in the event of a tire puncture”.

### Concept

Compliance with these instructions is vital to ensure vehicle safety. Non-com­ pliance with these instructions means risking tire damage, which can affect vehicle handling and lead to loss of ve­ hicle control. This may result in serious injury or death. Inform all other users of the vehicle if standard items for dealing with a puncture (e.g. spare tire) have been replaced by the Puncture repair Kit.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p198_img00` (page 198, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p198_img00.png`

### Concept

Do not use the Puncture repair Kit if the tire has already been damaged as a re­ sult of being driven underinflated. Do not try to seal damage other than that located within the visible tread of the tire. Do not try to seal damage to the tire’s sidewall.
