# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

ON BOARD DIAGNOSTIC (OBD II) SYSTEM

### Concept

Diagnostic connector is located on RH side below the steering wheel.

### Concept

On board Diagnostics or OBD, is an auto­ motive term referring to a vehicle’s self-di­ agnostic and reporting capability. The OBD system allows continuous diagnosis of the components of the vehicle corre­ lated with emissions. This system warns the driver, by turning “ON” the Malfunction Indication lamp (MIL) on the instrument cluster, when a fault causes emission lev­ els to increase.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p239_img02` (page 239, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p239_img02.png`

### Concept

The OBD system also has a diagnostic connector that can be interfaced with ap­ propriate diagnostic tools, which makes it possible to read the fault codes stored in the Electronic Control Unit, together with a series of specific parameters for Engine operation and Diagnosis. This check can also be carried out by the traffic police.

### Concept

Use CR 2032 battery only.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_004/p239_img00.png`

### Concept

An inappropriately disposed battery can be harmful to the environment and human health. Dispose the battery ac­ cording to your local law(s) and regula­ tion.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND STOPPING (with­ out PEPS)

### Concept

Manual Transmission (MT)

### Concept

Make sure that parking brake is engaged and vehicle is in neutral gear.

### Concept

Press the clutch pedal fully and crank the engine. Do not press the accelerator pedal while starting the engine.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img00` (page 156, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img00.png`

### Concept

Release the key as soon as the engine starts. Repeat if engine does not start.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img02` (page 156, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img02.png`

### Concept

To start off, press the clutch pedal fully and shift into first gear.

### Concept

After releasing the parking brake, gradu­ ally release the clutch and slowly press the accelerator.

### Concept

Turn the key to ‘ACC’ position to switch off the engine. Before switching off the en­ gine, run the engine in idle condition for at least 30 seconds and then switch off. This will allow the engine oil to lubricate the tur­ bocharger, till its speed is fully reduced and also allow the unit to cool down.

### Concept

The Starter protection system fitted in this vehicle does not allow you to crank the engine until you fully press the

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img01` (page 156, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img01.png`

### Concept

The Starter protection system switches off the starter when it is continuously cranked for more than 10 secs. In such a case, get the key back to ‘OFF’ posi

### Concept

tion & wait for 30 secs.

### Concept

The engine emits poisonous exhaust gases such as carbon monoxide. Inhal­ ing these exhaust gases leads to poi­ soning. There is a risk of fatal injury. Therefore, never leave the engine run­ ning in enclosed spaces without suffi­ cient ventilation.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img03` (page 156, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img03.png`

### Concept

After starting, run the engine in idle speed for at least 30 seconds. Do not press accelerated pedal while starting the engine to avoid damage to tur­ bocharger.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img04` (page 156, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img04.png`

### Concept

When shifting or starting off, do not race the engine. Racing the engine can shorten engine life and affect smooth shifting.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img05` (page 156, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img05.png`

### Concept

A quick burst on the accelerator be­ • fore turning off the engine serves no practical purpose, it wastes fuel and can damage turbocharger.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p156_img06` (page 156, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p156_img06.png`

### Concept

Do not switch off the engine when it • is running at high speed. This will lead to premature turbocharger bearing wear.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

MAINTENANCE AND SERVICE

### Concept

Periodic maintenance is essential for en­ suring long trouble free performance.

### Concept

Have your vehicle serviced regularly from TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Cen­ tre.

### Concept

There is a large network of TATA MO­ TORS Authorized Service Centre to help you with their professional servicing ex­ pertise. Scheduled maintenance informa­ tion is provided which makes tracking routine service easy.

### Concept

The following checks can be carried out between the recommended scheduled maintenance services. Take help of our authorized service center for assistance.

### Concept

Engine coolant level •

### Concept

Brake/Clutch fluid level •

### Concept

Washer fluid level checking & topping • up

### Concept

Keep clothing away from moving • parts.

## Knowledge

Wheel change through spare wheel. •

### Concept

Arrangement of fuel. (Fuel cost will be • chargeable at actual cost).

Re-opening the vehicle in cases of key • lock out.

### Concept

Rectification of electrical problems re­ • lated to battery, fuses etc.

### Concept

On spot repairs for complaints re­ • pairable at site.

### Concept

Vehicle to vehicle towing or winching & • towing for non-accident cases up to the nearest TATA MOTORS authorized workshop. Towing charges at actual cost beyond the same to be paid to the ASP in cash. For accident cases, towing charges to be

borne by the customer.

24 X 7 On Road Assistance Program does not apply to

Toll or ferry charges paid by ASP in • reaching to the breakdown site to be settled with ASP in actuals in cash.

Cases involving accident, fire, theft, • vandalism, riots, lightening, earth­ quake, windstorm, hail, tsunami, un­ usual weather conditions, other acts of God, flood, etc.

Vehicles that are unattended, un-reg­ •

istered, impounded or abandoned.

### Concept

Breakdown/defects caused by misuse, • abuse, negligence, alterations or mod­ ifications made to the vehicle.

Lack of maintenance as per the main­ • tenance schedule as detailed in the owner’s manual.

### Concept

Cases involving racing, rallies, vehicle • testing or practice for such events.

Tachometer indicates engine speed in rev­ olutions per min (rpm).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p57_img02` (page 57, confidence 0.989)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p57_img02.png`

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in “ON” posi­ tion, fuel gauge gives an approximate in­ dication of the amount of fuel in the fuel tank. In indication window, “F” stands for full and “E” stands for empty.

### Warning

When fuel in the tank is near to empty po­ sition, low fuel warning telltale turns Amber. Refill the tank as soon as possible.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p57_img04` (page 57, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p57_img04.png`

### Procedure

Whenever you turn the ignition ON, the instrument cluster needles and gauges move to maximum value and return to ‘0’ position. This is a welcome strategy and a self-check feature.

### Concept

Never drive the vehicle with high engine rpm. This may cause severe engine damage.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Engine Oil Level Checking

### Concept

Warm up the engine to normal operating temperature.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p229_img02` (page 229, confidence 0.961)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p229_img02.png`

### Concept

Turn it ‘OFF’ and wait for 5 minutes for the oil to return to the oil pan. Be sure the ve­ hicle is on a level surface.

### Concept

Take out the dipstick, wipe it clean, and reinsert it fully. Pull it out again and exam­ ine the oil level. It should be between ‘MIN’ and ‘MAX’ level. If not, top up with recom­ mended engine oil.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p229_img01` (page 229, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p229_img01.png`

### Concept

For location of Engine oil filling cap and dip stick, please refer Engine Compart­ ment.

### Concept

Engine Oil Quality Monitoring Indicator

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a feature in the engine man­ agement system which will monitor the engine oil quality throughout the lifetime of the oil in the engine. This will ensure that an oil change is requested only when really necessary. Once the oil quality reaches a threshold, the engine management system will ask for oil change by lighting the above lamp. This lamp will be blinking for oil change re­ quest.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p229_img00` (page 229, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p229_img00.png`

### Concept

Depending on your driving conditions, the oil quality may get deteriorated sooner. For example, if you are driving predominantly in highway conditions without straining the engine excessively, the oil lamp indicating oil change may appear later than ex­ pected. Similarly, if you drive continuously and for a long time in city at low speeds with frequent cold starts and short jour­ neys, the engine management system may prompt you to change the oil sooner than had the car been used mainly in high­ ways.

### Concept

The oil consumption depends upon the driving style and the conditions under which the vehicle is used.

### Concept

Do not remove the filler cap when • the engine is running.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p229_img03` (page 229, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p229_img03.png`

### Concept

Do not add oil above the MAX. • mark. Oil level above the MAX. mark may cause engine damage.

## Tables

### Table 1

| The oil consumption depends upon the driving style and the conditions under which the vehicle is used. |
| --- |
| • Do not remove the filler cap when the engine is running. • Do not add oil above the MAX. mark. Oil level above the MAX. mark may cause engine damage. |
| • Under no circumstances oil change intervals should exceed 15,000 km or 12 Months, whichever occurs earlier. |
| The appearance of this blinking warning light or symbol is not related to the amount of oil in the engine, so if the light or symbol comes ON and blinking, never add / top up engine oil but contact the nearest TATA authorized service center to have oil change and reset. |
| Topping of the coolant should be done in the auxiliary tank only. |
| • Do not allow brake fluid to make contact with the skin or eyes. • Do not allow brake fluid to splash or spill on the painted surface as it will damage the paint. In case of spillage, wipe it off immediately. |
| In case of emergency, a large amount of water without engine coolant may be added in order to reach a vehicle serv- ice location. |

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Specification

The lamp blinks constantly to indicate that the DPF needs to eliminate the trapped pollu­ tants (particulate matter) through the re­ generation process, it therefore does not indicate a malfunction. The lamp remains off during the entire DPF regeneration and it lamps up only when driving conditions require the driver to be notified. To switch off the lamp, keep the car running until re­ generation is complete (ideally at 3 rd gear, 60 kmph with engine speed over 2000 rpm). The process normally takes about 20 minutes.

### Warning

Note: Failure to obey the correct proce­ dure for long distance when the DPF lamp comes ON can cause the warning lamp (MIL) to come ON. In that case, please contact nearest TATA authorized service center to restore correct DPF operation.

### Concept

EXHAUST AFTER TREATMENT SYSTEM

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p241_img00` (page 241, confidence 0.942)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p241_img00.png`

### Concept

Exhaust after treatment consists of below components:

### Concept

Diesel Oxidation Catalyst (DOC) 1.

### Concept

Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) 2.

### Concept

Selective Catalyst Reduction (SCR) 3.

### Concept

Various Sensors and Actuators. 4.

### Concept

The exhaust gas coming from the engine first passes through the DOC and then through DPF.

### Concept

DPF is a filter, which filters carbon soot in the exhaust gas. DOC and DPF contains precious metals which converts hydrocar­ bons, carbon monoxide etc. in the exhaust gas to harmless constituents.

### Concept

Additionally DPF also removes most of the carbon soot particles in the exhaust gas. The collected carbon soot in the DPF is re­ generated to clean the filter.

### Concept

In order to reduce the NOx levels even fur­ ther, SCR system is used. In SCR system, DEF is injected in the exhaust stream. With the help of injected ammonia in the DEF, NOx is converted into harmless con­

### Concept

In order to control exhaust emissions, this vehicle is equipped with SCR sys­ tem through which DEF (Diesel Exhaust Fluid) continuously flows. It is normal to have a noise from the SCR system dur­ ing vehicle operation or for about 20 to 30 seconds after engine is switched off.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p241_img01` (page 241, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p241_img01.png`

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Special Care for Tubeless Tyres

### Concept

While removing tyre from wheel rim • and mounting it back on wheel rim, take precautions not to damage tyre bead. Use tyre removal and assembly machines. Damage or cut on tyre bead may cause gradual loss of air and de­ flation of tyre.

### Concept

Do not scratch inside of tubeless tyre • with metallic or sharp object. Tubeless tyres are coated with impermeable layer of rubber from inside which holds the air inside the tyre. Removal of this layer due to scratching may cause gradual loss of air and deflation.

### Concept

If wheel rim gets damaged in service, • get the wheel rim repaired/ replaced immediately. Running the vehicle with damaged rim may cause deflation of tyre and subsequent dislodging of tyre from rim.

### Concept

Maintain recommended inflation pres­ • sure. Over-inflation, in particular, may cause puncture or bursting of tyre.

### Concept

REMOTE KEY BATTERY REPLACE­ MENT (for Flip key)

### Concept

Remote control key contains a battery, which is housed under the cover.

### Concept

If red LED on remote flashes for 5 times after operating any button on remote. It is recommended to replace battery at a TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

### Concept

You should, however, proceed as follows if you wish to replace the discharged bat­ tery yourself:

### Concept

Open the key blade. 1.

### Concept

Press off the battery cover with your 2. thumb or using a flat screwdriver at the points of the arrows.

### Concept

Remove the discharged battery from 3. the key by pressing the battery down­ wards at the point of the arrow.

### Concept

Life and wear pattern of tyres de­ • pends on various parameters like tyre pressure, wheel alignment, wheel balancing, tyre rotation, etc. It also largely depends on vehicle speed, load carried, usage, driving habits, road conditions, tyre quality, etc. In case fault is suspected to be due to poor quality of tyres, the same may be taken up with con­ cerned tyre manufacturer.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p237_img00` (page 237, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p237_img00.png`

### Concept

For steel rim, Red dot of tyre to be • matched with blue dot of rim while re-fitment.

### Concept

For alloy rim, Yellow dot of tyre to be • matched with valve of rim while re- fitment

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” po­ sition, this gauge indicates the engine coolant temperature.

### Concept

The indicator should be within the normal, acceptable temperature range i.e. be­ tween “H” and “C”. If the indicator ap­ proaches “H”, overheating is indicated by red progress bar.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p58_img02` (page 58, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p58_img02.png`

### Warning

If the coolant temperature is very high, the engine coolant temperature telltale flashes with an audio warning. In this case, stop the vehicle, switch ‘OFF’ the engine and allow it to cool down for some time. Con­ tact the nearest TATA MOTORS author­ ized service center immediately for rectification.

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” po­ sition, arrow in the gauge indicates level of DEF left in the tank.

### Concept

The Indicator should be within the accept­ able range. i.e., between “E” and “F”. When DEF in tank is near to empty posi­ tion, DEF telltale near to gauge will glow with subsequent Text alert on DIS Screen. If DEF level reaches to critically low level, then DEF Gauge will be replaced by the permanent text alert along with buzzer.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p58_img04` (page 58, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p58_img04.png`

### Concept

Check the fuel level when the vehi­ • cle is stationary on a level road.

The fuel level displayed can vary • when you drive on inclines, curves, brake and accelerate suddenly. This is due to the movement of fuel in the tank. The low fuel warning lamp may turn to ON or OFF earlier or later than usual.

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Press the start stop switch to switch off the engine. Before switching off the engine, run the engine in idle condition for at least 30 seconds and then switch off. This will allow the engine oil to lubricate the tur­ bocharger, till its speed is fully reduced and also allow the unit to cool down.

### Concept

To start off, press the clutch pedal fully and shift into first gear.

### Concept

After releasing the parking brake, gradu­ ally release the clutch and slowly press the accelerator.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p169_img03` (page 169, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p169_img03.png`

### Concept

The engine emits poisonous exhaust gases such as carbon monoxide. Inhal­ ing these exhaust gases leads to poi­ soning. There is a risk of fatal injury. Therefore, never leave the engine run­ ning in enclosed spaces without suffi­ cient ventilation.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p169_img00` (page 169, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p169_img00.png`

### Concept

After starting, run the engine in idle • speed for at least 30 seconds. Do not press accelerated pedal while starting the engine to avoid damage to turbocharger.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p169_img01` (page 169, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p169_img01.png`

### Warning

When vehicle is in ACC/IGN/RUN • mode and user does any door state transition including tailgate and if PEPS does not detect smart key in­ side the vehicle when last door in­ cluding tailgate is closed, then audio warning chime comes ON.

### Concept

A quick burst on the accelerator be­ • fore turning off the engine serves no practical purpose, it wastes fuel and can damage turbocharger.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p169_img02` (page 169, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p169_img02.png`

### Concept

Do not switch off the engine when it • is running at high speed. This will lead to premature turbocharger bearing wear.

### Concept

When shifting or starting off, do not race the engine. Racing the engine can shorten engine life and affect smooth shifting.

# ANTI-THEFT DEVICE IMMOBILIZER / PEPS

## Knowledge

### Concept

Immobilizer system is designed to pre-vent vehicle theft by electronically disabling the engine ignition system. The engine can be started only with vehicle’s original Immobi­ lizer ignition key which has an electronic identification programmed code.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p29_img00` (page 29, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p29_img00.png`

### Warning

Use only Flip key, the other should be kept in a safe location. Note down “key Tag no.” information (and keep it safe) which is required while getting new/spare keys. Remember that it is not possible to prepare new/spare keys without the “key Tag number.” Take pre­ caution about Flip key, as without Flip key vehicle cannot be started.

State Meaning / Function Of The State

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

Problem with key (Wrong key used to • start vehicle)

### Concept

Problem with Immobilizer system. Con­ • tact a TATA MOTORS Authorized Serv­ ice Centre.

### Concept

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Warning

Warning Lamps Color Indicator Remarks

### Concept

Front passenger Seat Belt Indicator Red

### Warning

The Front passenger seatbelt warning indicator turns ON when ignition is turned ON. If front passenger seat is occupied by adult, the warning lamp remains ON as long as the co-driver seatbelt is not fastened. If seatbelt remains unbuckled and vehicle goes above 15 kmph, then final audio warning will go on for 90 seconds. Note: Once the seatbelt is fastened the buzzer and warning lamp turns OFF. Seatbelt reminder remains OFF when reverse gear is engaged.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p93_img00` (page 93, confidence 0.952)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p93_img00.png`

### Warning

Speed limit warning indicator Amber

### Warning

This lamps comes on when ignition is switched ‘ON’ and goes ‘OFF’ after 4 Sec­ onds. When the vehicle speed cross 80 kmph, then speed limit warning indicator turns ‘ON’ along with audio chime for every 2 minute chime (Audible warning). If vehicle speed crosses 120 kmph, the speed limit warning indicator turns ‘ON’ along with an audio chime (audio warning) continuously, until the vehicle speed is above 120 kmph. If vehicle speed is between 80 kmph and 120 kmph, then the audio chime (audio warning) will become less frequent but the speed limit warning indicator will remain ‘ON’ continuously. # STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

STOPPING THE VEHICLE

### Concept

Turn the key to ‘ACC’ position to switch off the engine. Before switching off the en­ gine, run the engine in idle condition for at least 30 seconds and then switch off. This will allow the engine oil to lubricate the tur­ bocharger, till its speed is fully reduced and also allow the unit to cool down.

### Concept

Mechanical Parking Brake

### Concept

Mechanical parking brake acting on the rear wheels is provided on the vehicle.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_004/p173_img02.png`

Parking Brake Applied

A quick burst on the accelerator before turning off the engine serves absolutely no practical purpose, it wastes fuel and can damage turbocharger.

text:
# ANTI-LOCK BRAKING SYSTEM (ABS) (if equipped)

## Knowledge

### Concept

ABS regulates brake pres­ sure in such a way that the wheels do not lock when you brake. This allows you to continue steering the vehicle when braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p30_img00` (page 30, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p30_img00.png`

### Warning

The ABS warning lamp in the instrument cluster lights up when the ignition is switched on. It goes off after 2-3 seconds if system is healthy.

### Concept

In an emergency situation take your • foot off the accelerator and press the brake pedal fully. This allows the ABS to regulate braking for you and have steering control along with maximum possible braking.

### Concept

When ABS is active driver will feel • brake pedal pulsating and very low motor (ABS) activation noise from en­ gine compartment which is nor-mal during ABS braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p30_img02` (page 30, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p30_img02.png`

### Concept

If ABS is faulty, the wheels could • lock when braking. The steer ability and braking characteristics may be severely impaired. There is an in­ creased danger of skidding and ac­ cidents.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p30_img01` (page 30, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p30_img01.png`

### Concept

Drive on carefully. Have ABS • checked immediately at the TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Cen­ tre as soon as possible.

### Concept

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

can be selected. To reverse or park the ve­ hicle, move the shift lever to the R (Re­ verse) or P (Park) mode as required.

### Concept

‘+’ For Upshifting in Manual mode

### Concept

Push the gearshift lever to the “+” direction and release it. Every time the lever is op­ erated, upshifting takes place one step at a time in the order of 1 st > 2 nd > 3 rd > 4 th > 5 th > 6 th gear.

### Concept

‘−’ For Downshifting in Manual mode

### Concept

Pull the gearshift lever to the “–” direction and release it. Every time the lever is op­ erated, downshifting takes place in the or- der 6 th > 5 th > 4 th > 3 rd > 2 nd > 1 st gear.

### Concept

In Manual/sports mode, downshifts are made automatically when the vehicle slows down. 1 st gear is automatically se­ lected when the vehicle stops.

### Concept

In Manual/sports mode, when the engine rpm approaches the intended limits, up­ shift will be made automatically by varying the shift points.

title: CHILD RESTRAINT SYSTEM (CRS)
text:
# CHILD RESTRAINT SYSTEM (CRS)

## Knowledge

### Concept

TATA MOTORS strongly recommends the use of Child Restraint Systems (CRS) for all children up to age of 12 years and to be placed at recom-mended positions only. Children travel-ling without recommended CRS and seated at other positions may face serious injuries in case of a collision.

### Concept

CRS can be installed in the vehicle using seat belts and/or ISOFIX only (if equipped) or ISOFIX with Top Tether (if equipped).

### Concept

The harness system of CRS holds the child in place, and in a collision, acts to keep the child positioned in the seat and reduce the risk of injuries.

### Concept

All children below age of one year must al­ ways ride in a rear-facing infant CRS.

### Concept

Keep children above age of one year, in a forward-facing CRS with a harness until they reach the size or weight limit allowed by your CRS manufacturer.

### Concept

Once your child outgrows the forward-fac­ ing CRS, your child is ready for a booster seat.

### Concept

Selection and Installation of CRS

### Concept

Always select the CRS that complies with latest safety standards (AIS072 / ECE R44). The CRS are classified according to the child’s size, height and weight. Select the appropriate CRS for your child. Ensure that the child fits properly in the CRS and it is securely installed in the vehicle. For installation, please refer CRS manufac­ turer’s instruction manual.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p16_img00` (page 16, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p16_img00.png`

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

If you install a CRS in the rear seat, slide the front seat far enough forward so that the child’s feet do not touch the front seat­ back. This will help avoid injury to the child in the event of a collision.

After a collision, we recommend to get seat belts, seats, ISOFIX and top-tether anchorages (as may be applicable) inves­ tigated at TATA MOTORS Authorized serv­ ice center.

### Concept

If your vehicle is equipped with a front passenger airbag (PAB) and does not have PAB deactivation switch, do not in­ stall a rear-facing CRS in the front pas­ senger seat. If the PAB inflates, a child in a rear facing CRS could be seriously injured or killed.

- Image: `doc_004_p19_img00` (page 19, confidence 0.987)

### Concept

Children could be endangered in a col­ lision if their CRS is not properly se­ cured in the vehicle. Be sure to secure the child in the restraint system accord­ ing to the manufacturer’s instructions.

### Concept

Do not use an infant carrier or a child safety seat that “hooks” over a seat

back, it will not provide adequate pro­ tection in a collision.

A CRS in a closed vehicle can become very hot. To prevent burns, check the seating surface and buckles before placing your child in CRS.

### Concept

Do not leave unattended children in • your vehicle.

Do not install a booster seat or a • booster cushion with a seat belt that is slack or twisted.

### Concept

Do not put the safety seat belt under • your child’s arm or behind its back.

### Concept

Do not use pillows, books or towels • to boost your child’s height.

### Concept

Make sure that your children sit in • an upright position.

### Concept

Do not allow children to stand up or • kneel on either the rear or the front seats. An unrestrained child could suffer serious or fatal injuries during a collision.

### Concept

Do not leave any toys or other ob­ • jects loose in the CRS or on the seat while the vehicle is in motion.

### Concept

Each CRS should be used for one child only.

### Warning

When PAB deactivation switch (if pro­ vided) is turned ‘OFF’, make sure ‘PAB’ operational status lamp illuminates with ig­ nition ‘ON’, indicating that the passenger airbag is NOT operational. If the airbag SRS warning indicator in the instrument cluster illuminates continuously, it means that there is malfunction in the system. Re­ move the CRS from front passenger seat and contact your TATA MOTORS author­ ized service center.

### Concept

SUPPLEMENTARY RESTRAINT SYSTEM (SRS - Airbags) (if equipped)

### Concept

The airbag ‘SRS’ system comprises of the following components depending upon the provided safety features in vehicle.

### Concept

Seat belt Pre-tensioners •

### Concept

Seat belt with load limiters •

### Concept

Front Passenger Airbag •

### Concept

Side Airbags (if equipped) •

### Concept

Curtain Airbag (if equipped) •

### Concept

Airbag ‘SRS’ ECU (Electronic Control • Unit)

### Concept

SRS wiring harness •

### Concept

The System is active when ignition switch is in the “ON” position or the ignition mode is “ON”. Airbags are designed to inflate in severe collisions. In the event of a colli­ sion, the collision sensors will detect sig­ nals, and if the Airbag ECU judges that the signals represent a severe collision, will

### Concept

trigger the airbags. The inflated Airbags provide a cushion to the occupants. The Airbag inflates and deflates so quickly that you may not even realize that it has acti­ vated. The Airbag will neither hinder your view nor make it hurdle to exit the vehicle.

### Concept

Airbag inflation is virtually instantaneous and occurs with considerable force, ac­ companied by loud noise and smoke, which is normal. The inflated airbag, to­ gether with seat belts, limit the movement of an occupant, thereby reducing the risk of injury.

### Concept

When an airbag inflates, you may see some smoke-like particles. The particles are a normal by-product of the process that generates the non-toxic gas used for airbag inflation. These airborne particles may irritate the skin, eyes, nose, or throat. If you have skin or eye irritation, rinse the area with water. For nose or throat irrita­ tion, move to fresh air. Also sometimes the smoke can cause breathing problems, in such cases get fresh air promptly.

### Concept

After inflation, airbag provides a gradual cushioning effect for the occupant there­

### Concept

after deflates. It is not advisable to drive your vehicle after the airbags have been deployed. If you are involved in another collision, the airbags will not be in place to protect you.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p21_img00` (page 21, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p21_img00.png`

### Concept

The above images are for reference purpose only.

#### Visual References

### Concept

The driver airbag is mounted in the center of the steering wheel. The front passenger airbag is located inside the dashboard in front of the passenger seat. The vehicle fit­ ted with the airbags have suitable indica­ tions on steering wheel and on dash board. The word ‘AIRBAG’ is embossed on the airbag covers.

### Concept

Side airbags (if equipped) , are mounted in front row seats for outboard occupants only.

### Concept

Curtain airbags (if equipped), are mounted above the doors along the roof on both sides.

- Image: `doc_004_p22_img03` (page 22, confidence 0.982)

### Concept

Open your windows and doors as • soon as possible after collision to re­ duce prolonged exposure to the smoke and powder released by the inflating airbag.

- Image: `doc_004_p22_img00` (page 22, confidence 0.981)

- Image: `doc_004_p22_img01` (page 22, confidence 0.945)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p22_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not touch the airbag container’s • internal components immediately after an Airbag has inflated. The parts that come into contact with an inflating Airbag may be very hot.

### Concept

Always wash exposed skin areas • thoroughly with lukewarm water and mild soap.

### Concept

### Concept

Even in vehicles with Airbags, you • and your passengers must always wear the seat belts provided. In order to minimize the risk and sever­ ity of injury in the event of a collision.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p23_img00` (page 23, confidence 0.975)

### Concept

ALWAYS use seat belts and CRS – • during every trip and at all times. Even with airbags, you can be seri­ ously injured or killed in a collision if you are not wearing seat belt prop­ erly or not wearing seat belt when airbag inflates.

### Concept

You and your passengers should • never sit or lean unnecessarily close to the Airbags.

### Concept

Move your seat as far back as pos­ • sible from front Airbags, while still maintaining control of the vehicle.

### Concept

All occupants should sit upright with • the seatback in an upright position, centred on the seat cushion with their seat belt on, legs comfortably extended and their feet on the floor

### Concept

until the vehicle is parked and the engine is turned off.

### Concept

If an occupant is out of position dur­ • ing collision, the rapidly deploying Airbag may forcefully contact the occupant causing serious or fatal in­ juries.

### Concept

Do not allow the front passenger to • place their feet or legs on the dash­ board.

### Concept

The above images are for reference purpose only.

### Concept

Do not allow the passengers to lean • their heads or bodies onto doors or place objects between the doors and passengers when they are seated on seats equipped with side and/or curtain Airbags.

### Concept

Do not place or stick any item/s in • the vehicle, except at designated lo­ cations (such as utility bins, cup/bot­ tle holders, boot space etc). Loose items may act as a projectile during a collision and cause severe to fatal injuries.

### Concept

Please be aware that any unse­ • cured item in your vehicle, such as your pet, unsecured CRS or a lap­ top, can become a potential hazard in the event of a collision or sudden stop, causing injuries to occupants in the vehicle.

### Concept

Coat hooks (if provided), must be • used only for that purpose. Never hang other items on to those hooks. This could affect deployment of the Airbags, and may lead to severe to fatal injuries.

### Concept

ALWAYS contact your TATA MO­ • TORS authorized service center if the vehicle is damaged, even if airbag has not inflated.

### Concept

ALWAYS contact your TATA MO­ • TORS authorized service center if any part of an airbag module cover shows sign of cracking or damage.

### Concept

If your SRS malfunctions, the Airbag may not inflate properly during a colli­ sion thereby increasing risk of serious injury or death. If any of the following conditions occur, your SRS is malfunc­ tioning:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p25_img01` (page 25, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p25_img01.png`

### Warning

The SRS warning lamp does not • turn ‘ON’ when the ignition switch is placed in the ‘ON’ position for few seconds.

### Warning

The SRS warning lamp stays ‘ON’ • after illuminating.

### Warning

The SRS warning lamp comes • ‘ON’/stays ‘ON’ while the vehicle is in motion.

### Warning

The SRS warning lamp blinks when • the engine is running.

### Concept

We recommend the customer to imme­ diately visit TATA MOTORS authorized service center and get the SRS system inspected if any of the above conditions occur.

### Warning

Airbag Warning Sticker on Front Pas­ senger Sun Visor

### Warning

The Airbag Warning Symbol on sun visor reminds extreme hazards associated with the use of rearward-facing child restraint on front passenger seat during airbag de­ ployment.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p26_img01` (page 26, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p26_img01.png`

### Concept

It is not taken to mean child can occupy front passenger seat and use seat belt. Please refer CRS section for recom­ mended seating position for children.

### Concept

Airbag Deployment Conditions

### Concept

When front airbags should not deploy?

### Concept

Minor frontal collision: Seat belt (if worn) offers adequate occupant protection in low severity collisions. The airbags are trig­ gered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. Deployment of frontal airbags is not beneficial in low severity collisions.

### Concept

Side collision: During a side collision, oc­ cupants tend to move sideways. There­ fore, deploying frontal airbags in such situations will not benefit the occupants. Side airbags and side curtain airbags (if equipped) are specifically designed to re­ duce the injuries that can occur in side col­ lision.

### Concept

Never make any modifications to • your vehicle. The modifications car­ ried out, but not limited to the vehi­ cle frame, bumpers, front fenders, ride height, suspension, seat belts, interior trims, steering wheel (espe­ cially holders), are not acceptable. This will affect the intended perform­ ance of SRS system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p26_img00` (page 26, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p26_img00.png`

### Concept

Fitment of bull bars, seat covers on • seats with airbags etc, is strictly pro­ hibited, unless authorised by TATA MOTORS. This will affect the in­ tended performance of SRS sys­ tem.

### Concept

If you need to make any modifica­ • tions to accommodate any disability you may have, please contact your Authorized TATA MOTORS Dealer for necessary guidance.

### Concept

Do not tamper with SRS in any way. • This will lead to unexpected per­ formance of system and may cause serious injury or death.

### Concept

Never use a rearward facing child re­ straint on a seat protected by an active Airbag in front of it, Death or serious in­ jury to the child can occur.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p26_img02` (page 26, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p26_img02.png`

### Concept

Rear collision: During a rear collision, oc­ cupants tend to move (rearwards) away from frontal airbags. Therefore, deploying frontal airbags in such situations will not protect the occupant. Head restraints and seat belts provide occupant protection dur­ ing a rear collision.

### Concept

Rollovers collision: During a rollover col­ lision, unbelted occupants may float inside the passenger compartment. This will in­ crease the risk of injuries and may prove to be fatal. Wearing seat belts provide highly effective occupant protection during rollover collision. Front airbags, are not de­ signed to deploy in a rollover as frontal airbags cannot offer any protection in rollover collision.

### Concept

When front airbags/side airbags/side curtain airbags (if equipped) deploy with minor or no visible vehicle dam­ age?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. The extent of vehicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. In some extreme/rare condi­

### Concept

tions; of rough road driving, running into a curb or hitting other fixed objects; the airbags may deploy depending upon the severity of collision. In some of these con­ ditions, damage to the vehicle may be minor or not be readily visible.

### Concept

When front airbags/side airbags/side curtain airbags (if equipped) may not deploy, even with exterior visible vehi­ cle damage?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. The amount of visible vehicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. Some collisions can result in visible damage but with no airbag deployment, because the airbags would not have been needed or would not have provided protection even if they had deployed. Seat belts, if worn, offer ade­ quate occupant protection in such cases.

### Concept

CHILD LOCK (if equipped)

### Concept

Both the rear doors of the vehicle are pro­ vided with a child proof lock. Push the lock lever located on vertical face of the door downward before closing the door. The door which has been closed by activating the child lock cannot be opened from in­ side, it can be opened only from the out­ side.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER (DPF)

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF). DPF is a mechanical filter that physically traps particulate matter from diesel engine exhaust gas.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p240_img00` (page 240, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p240_img00.png`

### Concept

DPF traps the particulate matter in the fol­ lowing way:

### Concept

Filtration - Particulates / soot are col­ • lected in the inlet channel of the filter.

### Concept

Regeneration - When the filter chan­ • nels are filled up with soot, they are cleaned automatically by the engine management system. This process is known as DPF Regeneration and this will happen during normal running of the vehicle.

### Concept

DPF equipped in vehicle normally regen­ erates automatically which is controlled by engine management system.

### Concept

In certain specific driving conditions, DPF regeneration may not happen automati­ cally as the desired temperatures required to regenerate soot may not be achievable

### Warning

due to specific driving conditions. This in­ cludes prolonged driving at low vehicle speeds for considerable amount of time (driving in heavy city traffic), prolonged running of the engine in idle conditions etc. In such cases, a warning lamp as indi­ cated above will be illuminated in the in­ strument cluster indicating that soot regeneration is insufficient.

### Warning

This warning lamp switches ON constantly to indicate that the DPF needs to be re­ generated. This lamp does not indicate any malfunction.

### Warning

The warning lamp remains OFF during normal vehicle behavior and lights up only when driving condition requires the driver to be notified. When this lamp is ON, keep the car running ideally at 3 rd gear, 60km/hr with engine speed over 2000 rpm until re­ generation is completed and warning lamp goes OFF. The process normally takes about 20 minutes.

### Warning

If DPF regeneration process requested above is not fol­ lowed for a long distance and the vehicle is driven with warning lamp ON, it can cause MIL to be turned ON.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p240_img02` (page 240, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p240_img02.png`

### Concept

Once MIL is ON, please contact nearest TATA authorized service center.

### Concept

Service should connect the TATA MO­ TORS diagnostic tool and conduct DPF service regeneration as indicated in the di­ agnostic tool.

### Concept

Insufficient DPF regeneration resulting in the above lamps can also happen if the vehicle is driven with adultered diesel.

### Warning

Do not shut down engine till the warning lamp goes OFF.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p240_img01` (page 240, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p240_img01.png`

## Knowledge

### Concept

The more you look after the engine when it is new, the more satisfied you will be with its performance in the future.

### Concept

Avoid rapid acceleration and prolonged high speed running of the engine for the first 2,000 km.

### Concept

Do not exceed the following road speeds during running in period.

### Concept

Avoid heavy loads, e.g. driving at full throt­ tle, during this period. Change gears judi­ ciously.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Fuel consumption, engine, transmission, brake and tyre wear are mainly affected by below factors:

### Concept

Operating conditions of your vehicle •

### Concept

Your personal driving style • Operating Conditions

### Concept

Avoid frequent start and stop as these • increase fuel consumptions.

### Concept

Always make sure that the tyre pres­ • sures are correct.

### Concept

Do not carry any unnecessary weight. •

### Concept

Regularly, service your vehicle and ad­ • here to the recommended service maintenance schedule. Personal Driving Style

### Concept

Do not press the accelerator pedal • while starting the engine.

### Concept

Do not warm up the engine when the • vehicle is stationary.

### Concept

Always adapt your driving style to suit • the prevailing road, weather condi­ tions, and maintain a safe distance from the vehicle in front. Drive care­

### Concept

Avoid frequent, sudden acceleration • and braking.

### Concept

Select appropriate gear according to • varying speeds and load conditions.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p142_img00` (page 142, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p142_img00.png`

### Concept

Switch ‘OFF’ the engine in stationary • traffic or at signals.

### Concept

Keep an eye on the vehicle’s fuel con­ • sumption.

### Concept

Driving safety systems are merely aids • designed to assist driving. You are re­ sponsible for the distance to the vehi­ cle in front, for vehicle speed and anticipating braking in good time.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p142_img01` (page 142, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p142_img01.png`

### Concept

Recommended Fuel Economy Speeds (MT only)

### Concept

Good Driving Practices

### Concept

Slow down before shifting to a lower • gear. This will help avoiding revving of the engine causing damage (for MT).

### Concept

Avoid frequent brake application which • can cause overheating of brakes.

### Concept

Slow down the vehicle speed while • travelling in cross winds. This gives much better control over the vehicle.

### Concept

Avoid high speed when cornering or • turning.

### Concept

Press the clutch fully while shifting •

### Concept

Do not rest your foot on the clutch pedal while driving.

### Concept

You could lose control of your vehicle if you try to adjust the driver’s seat, head restraint, mirror, steering wheel and fas­ ten the seat belt while driving. There is

### Concept

a risk of an accident.

title: EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE
text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

When towing a break down vehicle, cer­ tain precautions and procedures must be taken to prevent damage to the vehicle and/or components. Failure to use stan­ dard towing precautionary measures when lifting or towing a break down vehicle could result in an unsafe operating condition.

### Concept

To ensure proper towing and to prevent accidental damage to your vehicle, take help of a TATA MOTORS authorized dealer or a commercial tow-truck service.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p207_img03` (page 207, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p207_img03.png`

### Concept

Do not disconnect the discharged bat­ tery from the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p207_img00` (page 207, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p207_img00.png`

### Concept

Never connect the jump lead directly to the negative (–) terminal of the dis­ charged battery. This may lead to an ex­ plosion.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p207_img01` (page 207, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p207_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not allow battery electrolyte to • come in contact with eyes, skin, fab­ rics or painted surfaces. The fluid contains acid which can cause in­ jury and severe damage. Wear pro­ tective apparel. Do not inhale any battery gases. Keep children away from batteries. In case if battery acid comes in contact with the skin, wash it off immediately with water and seek medical attention.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p207_img02` (page 207, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p207_img02.png`

### Concept

During charging and jump-starting, • explosive gases can escape from

### Concept

the battery. There is a risk of an ex­ plosion. Particularly avoid fire, open flames, creating sparks and smok­ ing. Ensure there is sufficient venti­ lation while charging and jump-starting. Do not lean over the battery.

### Concept

Make sure that the positive terminal • of a connected battery does not come into contact with vehicle parts. Never place metal objects or tools on a battery.

### Concept

It is important that you observe the • described order of the battery termi­ nals when connecting and discon­ necting a battery. If you are in doubt, seek assistance from qualified spe­ cialist workshop.

### Procedure

Never connect or disconnect the • battery terminals while the engine is running.

### Concept

Make sure that the parking brake is re­ leased; vehicle in neutral gear position and steering wheel is unlocked. The power steering functions only when en­ gine is running. Hence, during towing the steering efforts will be more.

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Your vehicle has power-assisted brakes.

### Concept

The distance needed to bring the vehicle to a halt increases with the speed of the vehicle. Start applying brake anticipating the distance and slow down gradually.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p158_img01` (page 158, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p158_img01.png`

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a de­ layed reaction from the brakes when brak­ ing for the first time. This may also occur after the vehicle has been washed.

### Concept

Brake performance may become poor and unpredictable if brakes are wet.

### Concept

After driving through water or washing the underside of the vehicle, test the brakes while driving at a slow speed to see if they have maintained their normal effective­ ness. If the brakes are less effective than normal, dry them by repeatedly applying the brakes while driving slowly until the brakes have regained their normal effec­ tiveness.

### Concept

Braking On Downhill Gradients

### Concept

On long and steep gradients, you must re­ duce the load on the brakes by shifting early to a lower gear. This allows you to take advantage of the engine braking ef­ fect and helps avoid overheating and ex­ cessive wear of the brakes. Automatic Transmission (if available)

### Concept

The Automatic transmission has 6 forward and one reverse gear. The individual gears are select automatically, depending on po­ sition of gear shift lever.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p158_img02` (page 158, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p158_img02.png`

### Concept

Never run the vehicle out of gear • and coast down a hill. This is ex­ tremely hazardous. Always run the vehicle in gear.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p158_img00` (page 158, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p158_img00.png`

### Concept

Slow down before shifting to a lower • gear. This will help avoid over- revving the engine, which can cause damage.

### Concept

Ensure the vehicle is completely • stopped before putting into reverse gear. It may cause damaged to the transmission.

### Concept

Never use the brake pedal as a • footrest.

### Concept

If you rest your foot on the brake • pedal while driving, the braking sys­ tem can overheat. This increases the stopping distance and can even cause the braking system to fail. There is a risk of an accident.

### Concept

Never press the brake pedal and • the accelerator pedal at the same time.

This will help avoid over- revving the engine, which can cause damage. • Ensure the vehicle is completely stopped before putting into reverse gear. It may cause damaged to the transmission. |
| --- |

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Parking Brake Released

### Concept

To release parking brake, hold the lever and pull the lever up slightly, press the knob with the help of middle and ring fin­ ger as shown in figure and release the parking brake.

- Image: `doc_004_p174_img01` (page 174, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p174_img01.png`

### Concept

Mechanical parking brake acting only on the rear wheels is provided on the vehicle.

### Procedure

To apply the parking brake, pull the lever up fully. The parking brakes tell-tale illumi­ nates on the instrument cluster. To release it, pull the lever up slightly, press the re­ lease knob and push the lever down. Park­ ing brakes tell-tale on the instrument cluster will turn ‘OFF’ when the lever is fully released. Vehicle Parking

### Concept

Park the vehicle in a safe place. •

### Concept

Apply the parking brake. •

### Concept

Engage the gear shift lever in Park (P) • mode.

### Concept

Ensure that all window glasses are • closed and all lamps are turned ‘OFF’.

### Concept

At night, put on the parking lights if re­ • quired.

### Concept

Remove the key from the vehicle and • lock the vehicle.

### Concept

Block the wheels and engaged in gear • if parked on a slope.

### Concept

Apply the parking brake properly before leaving the vehicle and release it before moving the vehicle.

### Concept

When parking on a downhill gradient, place the gear lever in ‘Reverse’ posi­ tion. While parking on uphill gradient, place the gear lever in the ‘1 st ’ position.

### Concept

Never leave children unsupervised in the parked vehicle. They could also op­ erate the vehicle’s equipment. There is a risk of an accident and injury.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

The distance guidelines will appear to be further from the vehicle than the actual dis­ tance.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p185_img00` (page 185, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p185_img00.png`

### Concept

Because of this, objects will appear to be closer than they actually are. In the same way, there will be a margin of error be­ tween the guidelines and the actual dis­ tance/course on the road.

### Concept

When Any Part Of The Vehicle Sags

title: ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY
text:
# ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY

## Knowledge

### Concept

TATA MOTORS PASSENGER VEHICLE LIMITED is committed to produce vehicles using environmentally sustainable technology. A number of features have been incorporated in TATA MOTORS passenger vehicles which have been designed to ensure environmental compatibility throughout the life cycle of the vehicle. We would like to inform you that your vehicle meets emission norms and this is being reg-ularly validated at the manufacturing stages.

### Concept

As a user you too can protect the environment by operating your vehicle in a proactive manner. A lot depends on your driving style and the way you maintain your vehicle. We have given a few tips for your guidance. Driving

### Concept

Avoid frequent and violent acceleration. •

### Concept

Do not carry any unnecessary weight in the vehicle as it over­ • loads the engine. Avoid using devices requiring high power consumption during slow city traffic condition.

### Concept

Monitor the vehicle’s fuel consumption regularly and if show­ • ing rising trend get the car immediately attended at the Com­ pany’s Authorised Service Outlets.

### Concept

Switch off the engine during long stops at traffic jams or sig­ • nals. If you need to keep the engine running, avoid unneces­ sary revving it up or stopping and starting.

### Concept

It is not necessary to rev up the engine before turning it off as • it unnecessarily burns the fuel.

### Concept

Shift to higher gears as soon as possible. Use each gear upto • 2/3rd of maximum engine speed.

### Concept

A chart indicating gear shifting speeds is given in this book. • Maintenance

### Concept

Ensure that recommended maintenance is carried out on the • vehicle regularly at the Authorised Service Outlets.

### Concept

As soon as you see any leakages of oil or fuel in the vehicle • we recommend to get it attended immediately.

### Concept

Use only recommended grades and specified quantity of lu­ • bricants.

### Concept

Get your vehicle checked for emission periodically by an au­ • thorised dealer.

### Concept

Ensure that fuel filter, oil filter and breather are checked peri­ • odically and replaced, if required, as recommended by TATA MOTORS.

### Concept

Do not pour used oils or coolants into the sewage drains, gar­ • den soil or open streams. Dispose the used filters and batter­ ies in compliance with the current legislation.

### Concept

Do not allow unauthorized person to tamper with engine set­ • tings or to carry modifications on the vehicle.

### Concept

Never allow the vehicle to run out of fuel. •

### Concept

Parts like brake liners, clutch discs should be vacuum • cleaned. Do not use compressed air for cleaning these parts which may spread dust in the atmosphere.

### Concept

While carrying out servicing or repairs of your vehicle, you should pay keen attention to some of the important engine aggregates and wiring harness which greatly affect emis­ sion. These components are:

### Concept

Fuel injection equipment- pump, rail, injectors, nozzles and 1. high-pressure pipes.

### Concept

Air Intake & Exhaust system, especially for leakages. 2.

### Concept

Cylinder head for valve leakage. 3.

### Concept

All filters such as air, oil and fuel filters (check periodically). 4.

### Concept

EGR Valve & Cooler 6.

### Concept

Electrical connections. 8.

### Concept

If the ‘Check Engine lamp’, ‘MIL’ , ‘SCR’ or ‘DPF’ lamp contin­ 9. uously glows, please take the vehicle to a TATA MOTORS Au­ thorized Dealer/Service Center.

### Concept

Exhaust After Treatment System parts. 10.

### Concept

EMS wiring harness i.e. electrical connections to all sensors 11. and actuators.

### Concept

This Owner’s manual contains further information on driving pre­ cautions and maintenance care leading to environment protec­ tion. Please familiarize yourself with these aspects before driving.

### Concept

### Concept

If the Brake pedal is repeatedly de­ pressed and released slowly with the shift Lever in R (Reverse) position, noise may be heard. This is a normal condition.

### Concept

Always depress the brake pedal fully, before and while shifting out of the P (Park) mode into another position. This is to avoid unintended motion of the ve­ hicle which could injure the passengers inside or around the vehicle.

### Concept

### Concept

Be ensure the vehicle is com-pletely • stopped before shifting into R (Re­ verse) or D (Drive).

### Concept

Always use the parking brake. Do • not depend on placing the transmis­ sion in P (Park) to keep the vehicle from moving.

### Concept

Optimum vehicle performance and • fuel economy is obtained by smoothly depressing and re-leasing the accelerator pedal.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

ENGINE PASSIVE START - CONDI­ TIONS

### Concept

Bring the smart key with you and sit in 1. the driver seat.

### Concept

Press the clutch pedal and then press 2. the start-stop switch.

### Concept

Green colour LED on start-stop switch 3. will turn ON.

### Concept

Once engine starts successfully, green 4. colour LED on start-stop switch will re­ main ON. Two Step Start

### Concept

Bring the smart key with you and sit in 1. the driver seat.

### Concept

Press the start-stop switch without 2. pressing clutch pedal.

### Concept

Amber colour LED on start-stop switch 3. turns ON.

### Concept

Engine will remain OFF and all electri­ 4. cal equipment and infotainment sys­ tem can be used. Steering is unlocked.

### Concept

Press the clutch pedal and then press 1. start-stop switch to start the engine.

### Concept

Green colour LED on start-stop switch 2. will turn ON.

### Concept

Once engine start successfully, green 3. colour LED on start-stop switch will re­ main ON. Three Step Start

### Concept

Bring the smart key with you and sit in 1. the driver seat.

### Concept

Press the start-stop switch without 2. pressing clutch pedal.

### Concept

Amber colour LED on start-stop switch 3. will turn ON.

### Concept

Limited display on instrument cluster 4. will be ON and steering will be un­ locked. Engine remain OFF.

### Concept

Press the start-stop switch without 1. pressing clutch pedal again.

### Concept

Green colour LED on start-stop switch 2. will turn ON.

### Concept

Engine will remain OFF and all elec-tri­ 3. cal equipment and infotainment sys­ tem can be used.

### Concept

Press the clutch pedal and then press 1. start-stop switch to start the engine.

### Concept

Green colour LED on start-stop switch 2. will turn ON.

### Concept

Once engine started successfully, 3. green colour LED on start-stop switch will remain ON.

For Corrosion protection of the metal surfaces. •

For decoration and identification. • Various Environmental Hazards Affecting Paints

Environmental hazards: destroy your vehicle’s finish.

Removal of medium scratches, orange peel, oxidation, dust nibs etc. & swirl marks from painted surface. •

TATA MOTORS has tied up with M/s Autokrom, M/s 3M & M/s Wurth for this world class treatment at affordable prices. This treatment is available in all authorized workshops. The Dealer Service Marketing Executive will explain to you the benefits and terms and con­ ditions of this treatment.

## Knowledge

### Concept

For fitment of cover,

#### Visual References

### Concept

Engage the front lugs first. •

### Concept

Slowly press from both side to engage • side lugs.

### Concept

Engage rear lugs and then tighten the • screws.

### Concept

In case of break down, we recommend that your vehicle be towed with the driving wheels off the ground or place the vehicle on a flatbed truck as shown.

### Concept

To avoid serious damage to automatic transaxle, limit the vehicle speed to 15 km/h (10 mph) and drive less than 1.5 k m (1 mile) when towing.

### Concept

Before towing, check the automatic transaxle fluid leak under your vehicle. If

### Concept

the automatic transaxle fluid is leaking, a flatbed equipment or towing dolly must be used.

### Concept

Never tow your vehicle with the front • wheels on the ground or four wheels on the ground (forward or back­ ward), as this may cause serious damage to the transmission.

- Image: `doc_004_p209_img01` (page 209, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p209_img01.png`

### Concept

When towing with the rear wheels • on the ground or on towing dollies, place the ignition switch in the ‘ACC’ or ‘ON’ position, and secure the steering wheel in the straight-ahead position with a rope or similar de­ vice.

## Knowledge

### Concept

Please ensure that the phone is com­ 1. patible to the charging standard “Qi”.

### Warning

If there is any metallic object between 2. smartphone and wireless charger pad, immediately remove smart phone and metallic object after it has completely cooled down. Once any metallic object is detected on wireless charger post charging it displays its warning mes­ sage on Infotainment unit, first remove smart phone then remove foreign ob­ ject from the charging pad and place the smart phone again on charging pad.

### Concept

In case of water/Liquid spillage on 3. charging pad, dry out the pad surface area properly & clean the ECU surface area by removing Anti-skid mat. Do not charge the smart phone until surface is completely dry.

### Concept

The Phone charging status is informa­ 4. tion by phone and not charger.

### Concept

Wireless charger works on principle of 5. magnetic induction, i.e. it converts electrical energy into magnetic energy

### Concept

to transfer energy from charging pad to phone. Please maintain safe distance from the charger most of the time as it may cause irritation to sensory organs or active implants if implemented in the body. Please consult medical specialist in case implant organ in the body of the user.

### Concept

Place the smart phone on the center of 6. the charging pad for effective charging with best results (refer Figure 1).

### Concept

It is recommended to turn on Engine 7. while charging phone on wireless charger to avoid vehicle battery drain.

### Concept

User shall clean charging pad/mat pe­ 8. riodically to avoid dust accumulation.

### Concept

It is recommended to keep Vehicle AC 9. at least 23 Deg Cel with Fan speed above 2 level as cool environment sup­ port efficient charging of the phone.

### Concept

It is recommended to keep mobile 10. phone at center of charging pad for ef­ fective charging. In case small phone kept at corner do not start charging or Foreign object detection message pop-up, please move phone to center

### Concept

1. If any metallic object such as coin/keys are located between wireless charging pad and phone back cover, the charging may get disrupted. Also, this may results in heat up of metallic objects.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Gear Shifting And Driving

### Concept

The gearshift pattern is as shown on the gear lever knob. Gear shifting should al­ ways be done with clutch pedal pressed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p170_img00` (page 170, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p170_img00.png`

### Concept

For engaging reverse gear, lift the latch and by keeping latch lifted, shift to reverse position.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p170_img01` (page 170, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p170_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_004_p170_img02` (page 170, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p170_img02.png`

### Concept

Gear recommendation is displayed • when the clutch pedal is in fully re­ leased position.

### Concept

If “F” is displayed in DIS of instru­ • ment cluster, it means ‘Fault’ condi­ tion. Contact the TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

### Concept

Press the clutch fully while shifting • the gear. The reverse gear should be engaged only when the vehicle is stationary. Wait for 5 seconds after declutching to ensure smooth engagement of the reverse gear.

### Concept

Do not press clutch pedal while driv­ • ing the vehicle or when stationary on a slope.

### Concept

Do not switch off the ignition while • driving.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p170_img03` (page 170, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p170_img03.png`

### Concept

If you switch off the ignition while • driving, safety-relevant functions are only available with limitations, or not at all. This could affect the power steering and the brake boosting ef­ fect. You will require considerably more effort to steer and brake. There is a risk of an accident.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Reverse Park Assist System Preven­ tive Maintenance/cleaning

### Concept

Regularly clean the Sensors and keep 1. them free from dust, ice, mud, water, chewing gum etc. for proper working of the system. Use a smooth cloth for cleaning.

### Concept

Do not use water at high pressure for 2. cleaning the sensor.

### Concept

Do not cover the sensors. This will in­ 3. terrupt park assist performance.

### Concept

Do not remove mud, snow on the sen­ 4. sors using stick or hard material. Use normal water and soft cloth.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p179_img00` (page 179, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p179_img00.png`

### Concept

Park Assist Malfunction Indications

### Concept

In case of Reverse park assist system malfunctions, the following screen may ap­ pear on the infotainment system.

### Concept

Reason for this fault may be

### Concept

Body Control Module Failure 1.

### Concept

Sensor Malfunction 2.

### Concept

Partner components such as Infotain­ 3. ment music system, Instrument Clus­ ter failure.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p179_img01` (page 179, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p179_img01.png`

### Concept

In low light conditions, the screen • may darken or image may appear faint.

### Concept

If the tire sizes are changed, the po­ • sition of the fixed guidelines dis­ played on the screen may change.

### Concept

In case of damage of the rear por­ • tion of the vehicle, Reverse Park As­ sist sensors position may change

### Concept

which causes wrong visual informa­ tion on display. In case of damage, make sure that, Reverse Park Assist sensors are fitted properly at the in­ tended location.

### Concept

In case of uneven road conditions or • up-hill or downhill conditions, do not depend on Reverse Park Assist aid.

### Concept

Do not apply any kind of force on • the reverse park assist sensors.

### Concept

Always use rear view mirrors along • with Reverse Park Assist for con­ firming safety of the rear and the surrounding conditions.

text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Screw the bottle clockwise firmly 4. against the slight resistance of the notches onto the sealing gasket of the bottle connector until it is screwed tight.

### Concept

Remove the valve cap from the dam­ 5. aged tire. Pull the protective cap off the end of the hose and screw the hose firmly onto the valve of the damaged tire. Make sure that the compressor switch is switched to “0” and the pres­ sure “air release” valve is closed.

### Concept

Insert power plug into the 12 volt 6. power socket connection.

### Concept

Start the engine (only if the vehicle is 7. outdoors or in a well ventilated area).

### Concept

Press compressor switch to “I”. 8.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p203_img02` (page 203, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p203_img02.png`

### Specification

Inflate the tire within about 10 minutes 9. to an inflation pressure of minimum 180 kPa, (1.8 bar, and 26 psi) and a maximum of 300 kPa (3 bar, 43 psi).

### Concept

Switch off the compressor briefly in 10. order to read the actual tire pressure from the pressure gauge.

### Concept

Leave the bottle seal intact. Screwing the bottle onto the bottle holder will pierce the seal of the bottle. Avoid skin contact with the sealant which contains natural rubber latex. Do not open pres­ sure “air release” valve. Please use pro­ tective glove for safety purpose.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p203_img00` (page 203, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p203_img00.png`

### Concept

Asphyxiation may occur if the engine is allowed to run in a non-ventilated or poorly ventilated area (e.g. inside a building)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p203_img01` (page 203, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p203_img01.png`

### Procedure

Check the sidewall of the tire prior to in­ flation. If there are any cracks, bumps or similar damage, do not attempt to in­ flate the tire. Do not stand directly be­ side the tire while the compressor is pumping. Watch the sidewall of the tire. If any cracks, bumps or similar damage appear, turn off the compressor and let the air out by means of the pressure “air release” valve. In this case, do not con­ tinue to use the tire.

### Specification

When pumping in the sealant through the tire valve, the pressure may rise up to 500 kPa (5 bar, 73 psi) but will drop again after about 30 seconds.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p203_img03` (page 203, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p203_img03.png`

### Warning

If heavy vibrations, unsteady steering behavior or noises should occur while driving, reduce your speed and drive with caution to a place where it is safe for you to stop the vehicle. Recheck the tire and its pressure. If the tire pressure is less than 130 kPa (1.3 bar, 19 psi) or if there are any visible cracks, bumps or similar damage on the side wall, do not continue to use the tire!

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p203_img04` (page 203, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p203_img04.png`

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Your vehicle has power assisted brakes.

### Concept

The distance needed to bring the vehicle to a halt increases with the speed of the vehicle. Start applying brake anticipating the distance and slow down gradually.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p171_img02` (page 171, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p171_img02.png`

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a de­ layed reaction from the brakes when brak­ ing for the first time. This may also occur after the vehicle has been washed.

### Concept

Brake performance may become poor and unpredictable if brakes are wet.

### Concept

After driving through water or washing the underside of the vehicle, test the brakes while driving at a slow speed to see if they have maintained their normal effective­ ness. If the brakes are less effective than normal, dry them by repeatedly applying the brakes while driving slowly until the brakes have regained their normal effec­ tiveness.

### Concept

Braking On Downhill Gradients

### Concept

On long and steep gradients, you must re­ duce the load on the brakes by shifting early to a lower gear. This allows you to

### Concept

You may notice a noise from transmis­ sion under certain circumstances. This noise is normal and is not an indication of a problem with your clutch or trans­ mission. This noise may be noticed when vehicle is idling in NEUTRAL con­ dition with the clutch engaged (clutch pedal released) or when the transmis­ sion is warm. It may also be heard while driving.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p171_img00` (page 171, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p171_img00.png`

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with Dual • Mass Flywheel (DMF), which plays important role in providing refined powertrain / driveline experience.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p171_img01` (page 171, confidence 0.975)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p171_img01.png`

### Concept

Driving at very low engine speed is • likely to stall the engine, especially when driven without any accelerator pedal inputs.

### Concept

Recommended Driving Precautions:

### Concept

Shift to lower gear as per gearshift • indicator (GSI) on cluster.

### Concept

To start-off (marching/ drive away), • always engage in first gear.

### Specification

While down shifting (from 3 rd to 2 nd • gear) at low engine RPM’s (below 1000 rpm) press accelerator pedal to provide required rpm.

### Concept

Never use the brake pedal as a • footrest.

### Concept

If you rest your foot on the brake • pedal while driving, the braking sys­ tem can overheat. This in-creases the stopping distance and can even cause the braking system to fail.

### Concept

There is a risk of an accident.

### Concept

Never press the brake pedal and • the accelerator pedal at the same time.

## Tables

### Table 1

| • Never use the brake pedal as a footrest. • If you rest your foot on the brake pedal while driving, the braking sys- tem can overheat. This in-creases the stopping distance and can even cause the braking system to fail. |
| --- |
| • Do not shift to lower gear on a slip- pery road surface in an at-tempt to increase the engine’s braking effect, the drive wheels could lose their grip. • There is an increased danger of skidding and accidents. |
| When descending on sharp gradients, NEVER turn the ignition key to the ‘OFF’ position. Emission control system damage may result. |
| A quick burst on the accelerator before turning off the engine serves absolutely no practical purpose, it wastes fuel and can damage turbocharger. |
| Do not switch the engine off when it is running at high speed. This will lead to premature turbocharger bearing wear. |
| Do not press the button, while applying parking brake. |
