### Concept

Your vehicle is subjected to many external influences such as climate, road condi­ tions, industrial pollution and proximity to the sea. These conditions demand regular care of the vehicle body. Dirt, insects, bird droppings, oil, grease, fuel and stone chip­ pings should be removed as soon as pos­ sible. Washing

### Concept

Following these tips while washing your vehicle.

### Concept

Always wash your vehicle in shade 1. and the surface is at room tempera­ ture.

### Concept

Wash with mild vehicle wash soap like 2. ‘Car Shampoo’ and use a soft bristle brush, sponge or soft cloth and rinse it frequently while washing to avoid scratches.

### Concept

To avoid scratches, please wear soft 3. gloves. Remove finger rings, nails, wrist watch while washing.

### Concept

To remove stubborn stains and con­ 4. taminants like tar, use turpentine or

### Concept

cleaners like ‘Stain remover’ which are safe for paint surfaces.

### Concept

Avoid substances like petrol, diesel, 5. kerosene, benzene, thinner, acids or other solvents that cause damage to paint.

### Concept

Dry your vehicle thoroughly to prevent 6. any damp spots.

### Concept

Rinse all surfaces thoroughly to pre­ 7. vent any traces of soap and other cleaners as this may lead to the forma­ tion of stains on the painted surface later.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p265_img00` (page 265, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p265_img00.png`

### Concept

After drying the vehicle, inspect it for chips and scratches that could allow corrosion to start. Apply touch up paint where nec­ essary. Cleaning of Carpets

### Concept

Vacuum clean the carpet regularly to re­ move dirt. Dirt will make the carpet wear out faster. Periodically, shampoo the car­ pet to keep it looking new.

### Concept

Use carpet cleaners (preferably foam type). Follow the instructions that come with the cleaner. Apply it with a sponge or soft brush. Keep the carpeting as dry as possible by not adding water to the foam.

### Concept

Avoid parking the car under trees • without proper cover, it will reduce the amount of bird droppings, tree sap and pollen contact on paint sur­ face. Regularly remove the twigs, leaves and vegetation near the windshield areas, to avoid water stagnation.

### Concept

Always close the sunroof while • washing the vehicle.

### Specification

Do not direct high pressure washer fluid/ water jets (Pressure above 0.5 bar) at electrical devices and connecter during washing. This is to prevent mal­ function / failure of electrical system due to water ingress.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p265_img01` (page 265, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p265_img01.png`

### Concept

Cleaning of Windows, Front and Rear Glasses

### Concept

Clean the windows inside and outside with commercially available glass cleaners.

### Concept

This will remove the haze that builds up on the inside of windows. Use a soft cloth or paper towels to clean all glass and plastic surfaces. Waxing

### Concept

Waxing and polishing is recommended to maintain the gloss and wet-look appear­ ance of your paint finish.

### Concept

Use good quality polish and wax for 1. your vehicle.

### Concept

Re-wax your vehicle when the water 2. does not slip off the surface but col­ lects over the surface in patches.

### Concept

Polishes and cleaners can restore shine to the painted surface that has oxidized and become dull. They normally contain mild abrasives and solvents that remove the top layer of the finish coat. Polish your ve­ hicle, if the finish does not regain its origi­ nal shine after using wax. Interior Fabric Cleaning Tips

### Concept

Stains should be treated immediately. 1. If left for a long time, they can leave a permanent mark.

### Concept

Cleaning the stains immediately is im­ 2. portant especially for stains, which contain artificial colors in the stain cre­ ating liquid or semisolid substance. The colorant may leave a stain if kept for longer time.

### Concept

Stain should not be removed by rub­ 3. bing. As far as possible, try to blot or lift the stain with cloth or plastic spatula and then clean the remaining stain with cloth or sponge.

### Concept

If the stain has dried, then gently brush 4. off the material and then press with

### Concept

damp cloth or sponge till it disappears.

### Concept

Do not use household detergents to 5. clean the fabric.

### Concept

Always use clean cotton cloth for 6. cleaning. Paint Care

### Concept

Following guidelines will help you to pro­ tect your vehicle from corrosion effectively.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p266_img01` (page 266, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p266_img01.png`

#### Visual References

### Concept

Avoid Spillage or Direct contact of Air freshener liquid/chemicals with painted plastic parts. These chemicals may cause damage to paint like blisters, peel off, wrinkles etc.

### Concept

In order to protect your vehicle from corro­ sion it is recommended that you wash your vehicle thoroughly and frequently in case:

### Concept

There is a heavy accumulation of dirt • and mud especially on the underbody.

### Concept

It is driven in areas having high atmos­ • pheric pollution due to smoke, soot, dust, iron dust and other chemical pol­ lutants.

### Concept

It is driven in coastal areas. •

### Concept

The underbody must be thoroughly • pressure washed after every three months.

### Concept

In addition to regularly washing your • car, the following precautions need to be taken. Periodic Inspection

### Concept

Regularly inspect your vehicle for any • damage in the paint film such as deep scratches and immediately get them repaired from an authorized service outlet, as these defects tend to accel­ erate corrosion.

### Concept

Inspect mud liners for damages. •

### Concept

Keep all drain holes clear from clog­ • ging. Proper Parking

### Concept

Always park your vehicle in shade to • protect it from harsh sunlight or in a well-ventilated garage so that there is no dampness on any part of the vehi­ cle. Wiper Care

### Concept

### Concept

The lamps comes on when ignition is switched ‘ON’ and goes ‘OFF’ in 3 sec­ onds. The lamps remains on continuously if there is any malfunction in ABS. Normal braking system will be operational without assistance of ABS. Contact the TATA MOTORS Authorized service center.

### Concept

Low Fuel indicator Amber

### Warning

Illuminates momentarily when ignition is switched ‘ON’. The symbol lights up continuously if fuel level in the tank is low. Fuel needs to be filled immediately. # ELECTRONIC BRAKE FORCE DIS­ TRIBUTION (EBD)

## Knowledge

### Concept

EBD monitors and controls the brake pressure on the rear wheels to improve driving sta­ bility while braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p31_img00` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p31_img00.png`

### Concept

EBD provides optimal braking pressure distribution between front and rear wheels to optimize braking distance and to ensure vehicle stability by means of lowering braking pressure increase at rear wheels.

### Concept

ADDITIONAL SAFETY FEATURES (as available)

### Concept

Cornering Stability Control (CSC)

### Concept

Corner stability Control supports / stabi­ lizes vehicle during partial braking on curves by reducing pressure at required inner wheel of the vehicle.

### Concept

This helps to reduce probability of vehicle over steering during cornering. OFF Road ABS

### Concept

Based on wheel speed information off road ABS helps to avoid wheel lock on un­ even surfaces like loose gravel, pot holes by reducing the stopping distance com­ pared to standard ABS. Electronic Traction Control (ETC)

### Concept

The Electronic Traction Control system function (ETC) is designed as a slip control system to prevent the driven wheels of a vehicle from excessive wheel slip. Roll Over Mitigation (ROM)

### Concept

The main feature of the Roll over Mitiga­ tion function is the detection of a rollover critical situation and to prevent the vehicle

### Concept

rollover. This is done by active brake inter­ ventions on selected wheels, thereby re­ ducing the forces that cause a roll-over situation. Brake Disc Wiping (BDW)

### Concept

Water on the brake disc leads to a delay in brake response time. The purpose of the function Brake Disc wiping is to re­ move moisture when driving in wet condi­ tions automatically. To get quick response form Brake and better deceleration. Electronic Brake Pre-fill (EBP)

### Concept

The Electronic Brake Prefill (EBP) function reduces the air gap of the brake pad and the brake disc. The function is triggered after a sudden release of the accelerator pedal due to an unexpected emergency brake situation. By actively pre-filling the brake-system the brake response time is reduced and results in a shorter stopping distance. Hydraulic Brake Assist (HBA)

### Concept

In a dangerous emergency situation, most drivers don’t use the full available perform­ ance of the brake system, because they

### Concept

If EBD is malfunctioning, the rear • wheels can lock, e.g. under full braking. This increases the risk of skidding and an accident.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p31_img01` (page 31, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p31_img01.png`

### Concept

You should therefore adapt your • driving style to the different handling characteristics. Have the brake sys­ tem checked immediately at a TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Cen­ tre as soon as possible.

### Concept

brake too soft. The HBA function detects the critical situation and builds up addi­ tional brake pressure to reduce the brak­ ing distance. Hydraulic Fading Compensation (HFC)

### Concept

In dangerous fading situations most driv­ ers operate the brake pedal with a small or regular braking force and they never reach to the maximum possible vehicle de­ celeration. The HFC function improve the stopping distance by eliminating required pressure build-up lag by the driver. Dynamic Wheel Torque by Brake (DWT-B)

### Concept

The main goal of the function is to improve the agility of a vehicle and to enable a more direct steering. This is mainly achieved by braking interventions at the inner wheels during turning. DWT-B re­ duces understeer tendency of the car and a higher curve speed can be achieved.

### Concept

Engine Drag Torque Control (EDTC)

### Concept

On slippery road conditions during in- gear Braking or Shift down of gear or sudden throttle release on a curve road.

### Concept

This causes high Engine drag on the driven wheel resulting into brake slip situ­ ations without any brake application.

### Concept

This makes vehicle highly under steerable. EDTC controls such brake slip on the driven wheels by increasing the engine torque to makes the vehicle stable and steerable. Hill Hold Control (HHC)

### Concept

Hill Hold Control is a comfort function. The main intend is to prevent the vehicle from rolling backwards while driving off up-hill on an inclined surface.

## Knowledge

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” po­ sition, this gauge indicates the engine coolant temperature.

If the coolant temperature reading is very high, the engine coolant temperature tell­ tale flashes with an audible buzzer. text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

STEERING LOCK AND IGNITION SWITCH (if available)

### Concept

The ignition switch has the following four positions:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p155_img00` (page 155, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p155_img00.png`

### Concept

LOCK - This is the normal parking posi­ tion. Key from lock can be removed in this position only.

### Concept

“LOCK” position prevents normal use of the steering wheel after the key is re­ moved.

### Procedure

To release the steering lock, insert the key and turn it clockwise to one of the other positions.

### Concept

ACC (for MT)- Accessories such as the in­ fotainment system can be operated, but the engine remains ‘OFF’. Steering gets unlocked.

### Concept

ACC (for AT)- Key rotation from ACC to lock position only happen when gear lever is in parking position.

### Concept

ON - This is the normal operating position. All electrical systems are ‘ON’.

### Concept

START - Turn the key further clockwise to the START position, (spring loaded) to start the engine. As soon as the engine starts, release the ignition key, which re­ turns to ON position. While cranking, all accessories will be momentarily ‘OFF’. Illuminated Key Ring (if available)

### Concept

When the vehicle is unlocked, the illumi­ nated key ring glows up. This helps to lo­ cate ignition switch in the dark.

### Concept

The engine can only be started • when the gearshift lever is in “N” po­ sition with the clutch pedal firmly pressed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p155_img01` (page 155, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p155_img01.png`

## Tables

### Table 1

| • The engine can only be started when the gearshift lever is in “N” po- sition with the clutch pedal firmly pressed. |
| --- |
| When shifting or starting off, do not race the engine. Racing the engine can shorten engine life and affect smooth shifting. |

Reverse Park Assist feature works on ultra sound echo technology, due to which per­ formance is not guaranteed in following scenarios:

### Concept

If the object has a sharp edge surface, • where surface may divert echoes from sensor reception.

### Concept

If object is mesh fence made up of thin • wires, where echoes can’t be given by the surface.

### Concept

Fast moving objects passes in the sen­ • sor field of detection, where echoes are not processed by the system.

### Concept

If object is made/covered by foam or • sponge or snow where ultrasonic sound signals are absorbed.

A key is an electronic access and authori­ zation system which is provided as a stan­ dard feature on your vehicle. Unlocking Principle

### Concept

The transponder which is built into the ig­ nition key carries a unique identification code. The vehicle unlocks when the code on the key matches with the code on the Engine Management System (EMS). In case of PEPS variant, Immobilizer function is provided by PEPS. Engine Starting

### Concept

When the key is inserted and the ignition is switched ‘ON’, all codes are communi­ cated within key, Immobilizer and EMS. The engine will start only if all the codes match. Loss of Keys

### Concept

If one of the key is lost, contact your near­ est TATA MOTORS authorized dealer im­ mediately.

### Concept

Do not turn ‘ON’ ignition switch by • using key with any type of metal wound around its grip or in contact with it. This may be detected as ab­ normal condition by immobilizer and prevent en-gine from starting.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

To start off, switch ON ignition switch and crank the engine, depress the brake pedal fully and release the parking brake. Press the shift lock button on the knob of gear selector lever and move the lever from Parking (P) mode to Drive (D) mode.

### Concept

Use Park (P) position when starting the engine or parking the vehicle. Apply the park­ ing brake whenever the vehicle is to be parked.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p159_img00` (page 159, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p159_img00.png`

### Concept

The selector lever must be engaged in Park (P) position only when the vehicle is stationary. DO not engage Parking Posi­ tion (P) in running condition.

### Concept

If engaged while the vehicle is in motion it may severely damage the transmission.

### Concept

Before leaving the driver’s seat, always make sure the shift lever is in the P (Park) position; then apply parking brake fully and shut the engine off. If this is not followed, Unexpected and sudden vehicle move­ ment can occur.

### Concept

This position puts the trans­ mission in reverse gear when engaged in stationary condition with brake pedal fully pressed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p159_img01` (page 159, confidence 1.0)

### Concept

The selector shall never be moved into re­ verse while driving forward.

### Concept

The transmission is in Neu­ tral position.

  - File: `images/doc_004/p159_img02.png`

### Concept

This position is for normal driving conditions for maxi­ mum efficiency and fuel economy. It should be used as often as possible.

This position allows the driver to switch to activate Manual mode to select gears like a manual gearbox.

### Concept

Pressing the shift lever towards left side while in Drive mode will put the transmis­ sion in Manual mode.

### Concept

The gear selector moves freely between the Manual (M) and Drive (D) positions. As soon as shifter is moved forward or back­ ward, the Manual (M) mode is activated.

### Concept

It is possible to shift from D mode to Man­ ual mode and vice versa at any time dur­ ing driving.

### Concept

To return back to Manual mode if it has been selected; move the selector lever to Drive mode (by tapping the lever towards right) and engage it again to M mode.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

REGENERATION PROCESS

### Concept

DPF is a mechanical filter that physically traps particulate matter from diesel engine exhaust gas.

### Concept

DPF traps the particulate matter in the fol­ lowing way:

### Concept

Filtration – Particulates / soot are col­ • lected in the inlet channel of the filter.

### Concept

Regeneration – When the filter chan­ • nels are filled up with soot, they are cleaned automatically by the engine management system. This process is known as DPF Regeneration and this will happen during normal running of the vehicle.

### Concept

In certain specific driving conditions, DPF regeneration may not happen automati­ cally as the desired temperatures required to regenerate soot many not be achievable due to specific driving conditions. This may happen in prolonged driving at low vehicle speeds for considerable amount of time (driving in heavy city traf­ fic), prolonged running of the engine in idle conditions, use of adulterated diesel etc.

### Warning

In such cases, a DPF warning lamp will be illuminated indicating that soot regenera­ tion is insufficient.

### Concept

Avoid parking of vehicle over inflam- mable materials, such as dry leaves; grass etc. as exhaust system is hot enough to initiate fire.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p242_img00` (page 242, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p242_img00.png`

### Concept

Ensure exhaust system is not • blocked and is free from obstruction.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p242_img01` (page 242, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p242_img01.png`

### Concept

Blockages in the exhaust can cre- • ate backpressure, low top speed, poor pick up, black smoke, car-bon build up and low mileage and can affect power output of the en-gine and the emission levels.

### Concept

The maximum sulphur content of the diesel fuel must not exceed 0.001% (10 parts per million). Fail-ure to comply with the standards may damage engine

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p242_img02` (page 242, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p242_img02.png`

### Concept

components and the exhaust after- treatment system.

### Concept

Please follow the steps below that will guide you to check and replace them.

### Concept

Apply parking brake. •

### Concept

Switch off all electrical accessories. •

### Concept

Turn the ignition key to the ‘LOCK’ po­ • sition.

In the fuse box, identify the defective • fuse from its melted wire.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

5. Hill Descent Control (HDC) (if avail­ able)

### Concept

While driving down on a hill slope, activate the HDC fea­ ture by pressing on the center console.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p189_img00` (page 189, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p189_img00.png`

### Concept

HDC provides a smooth and controlled hill descent by enabling the vehicle to control the speed of each wheel. The system will automatically apply the brakes to slow down to the desired vehicle speed. Cruise control +/-buttons or Brake and accelera­ tor pedal can adjust the speed to a com­ fortable level.

### Procedure

HDC interventions will be automatically disabled once the descent is complete and vehicle is on levelled road. Non-zero speed less than 35 kmph would be re­ quired to turn ON HDC. A speed greater than 40 kmph will end all active HDC con­ trol and switch HDC to standby mode. Once the vehicle speed is lower than the specified threshold of 40 kmph HDC be­ comes activated again whenever required (No press of HDC button is required).HDC is permanently switched off if the vehicle

### Concept

speed exceeds 60 kmph and Active state on HDC switch will go off automatically. HDC works in both Neutral and in Gear forward and reverse position.

### Concept

While driving down a hill, the engine brak­ ing should be used by shifting into a lower gear. Do not drive in neutral gear or switch off the engine.

### Concept

HDC cannot take account of road, weather, traffic and tyre conditions. You are always responsible for keeping con­ trol of the vehicle and for assessing whether the downhill gradient can be managed.

#### Visual References

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

Climbing Sharp Gradients on Loose Surfaces

### Concept

Start off smoothly in a suitable gear. Accel­ erate smoothly so that there is no loss of traction by over-revving of the engine.

### Concept

Choose a slope as smooth as possible and select the appropriate gear so that gear changing in the middle of the climb is not required.

### Concept

Changing gears in the middle of the climb can cause loss of momentum and engine stalling. Shifting to lower gear has to be done cautiously to avoid loss of traction.

### Concept

Under no conditions should the vehicle be moved diagonally across a hill. The dan­ ger is in loss of traction and sideways slip­ page, possibly resulting in toppling over. If unavoidable, choose as mild an angle as possible and keep the vehicle moving.

### Concept

If the wheels start to slip within few feet of the end of the climb, motion can be main­ tained by swinging the steered wheels left and right, thereby providing increased grip.

### Concept

If the vehicle stalls or losses headway

### Concept

while climbing a steep hill, make a quick shift to reverse and allow the vehicle to move back with the control of engine com­ pression. Descending Sharp Gradients

### Concept

Depending on the severity of the gradient, shift into appropriate gear. Use engine braking judiciously without over-revving the engine.

### Concept

Brake application under such situations should be done very.

### Concept

Do not shift to lower gear on a slip­ • pery road surface in an at-tempt to increase the engine’s braking effect, the drive wheels could lose their grip.

- Image: `doc_004_p172_img00` (page 172, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p172_img00.png`

### Concept

There is an increased danger of • skidding and accidents.

### Concept

When descending on sharp gradients, NEVER turn the ignition key to the ‘OFF’ position. Emission control system damage may result.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND STOPPING (PEPS) (if available)

### Concept

Engine Passive Start/stop

### Concept

Start/Stop switch is provided on the dash­ board towards the right side of steering wheel. Start / Stop Switch

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p166_img00` (page 166, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p166_img00.png`

### Concept

A Start Stop Switch (SSSW) or Push to Start Button is a main component of Pas­ sive (Engine) Start and Stop sys-tem. It is used to control ACC, IGN out-puts as well as to start and stop the engine.

### Concept

If smart key battery voltage is low or empty and vehicle is in OFF mode then to start the engine user needs to press start/stop button two times with interval of 2.5 sec. between two switch press after pressing the clutch pedal OR brake with valid smart key near Immobilizer antenna (located

### Concept

below front cup holder).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p166_img02` (page 166, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p166_img02.png`

### Concept

If vehicle engine is switched from ON to OFF and Start Stop button is pressed with clutch press within 5 sec, Engine gets cranked.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_004/p166_img03.png`

### Concept

If Smart key is inside the vehicle and • on pressing start stop switch, if start stop switch green LED blink for 10 sec. duration then rotate steering wheel and simultaneously press start stop switch again.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_004/p166_img01.png`

### Concept

If smart key is inside the vehicle and • on pressing start stop switch, if start stop switch green LED blinks more than 10 sec. duration then contact authorized TATA MOTORS dealer.

### Concept

If ESCL (Electronic Steering Col­ • umn Lock) is not unlocked properly, then vehicle doesn’t go into ACC mode.

### Concept

If ESCL (Electronic Steering Column Lock) is not unlocked properly, then En­ gine will not get cranked.

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

Pressing the unlock button (1) of remote will unlock all the Doors. One flash is com­ ing on side indicators. Approach Light

### Procedure

Press approach light button (2) once, low beam and positon lamp will turn ‘ON’. This

### Concept

feature helps to find and reach the parked vehicle or to reach home in dark/ cloudy condition after parking. Red LED will be flashing on the remote. To switch ‘OFF’ the approach lights, press and release the same button or it automatically turns ‘OFF’ after certain time.

#### Visual References

To unlatch the Tail gate, long press the ap­ proach light button (2) on remote for more than 2 sec.

  - File: `images/doc_004/p35_img01.png`

### Concept

Pressing the Lock button (3) once, remote locks all the doors of the vehicle. Folding Key Blade IN / OUT

### Concept

Press button (4) to flip out the key blade. For folding, press the button (4) and fold the key blade inside.

### Concept

Tail gate once unlatched will not get lock automatically with doors. It will get locked by slamming.

### Concept

Do not fold the key blade without press­ ing the button. Also, it should not be forced in any direction apart from fold­ ing direction to avoid damage to flip mechanism.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p35_img03` (page 35, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p35_img03.png`

### Concept

In vehicle, locked condition if lock button on remote key is pressed the turn indica­ tors of vehicle flashes for 4 times. Automatic Activation of Immobilizer

### Concept

If key is removed from ignition switch, the engine will be immobilized automatically even if you forget to lock the vehicle.

### Concept

For few variant, Ignition off is required to immobilize the vehicle. Auto Locking / Unlocking of Doors / Auto Relock

### Concept

Vehicle doors are automatically locked • when all doors are closed and the ve­ hicle speed crosses 10 kmph.

### Concept

When key is taken out all the doors get • automatically unlocked.

### Concept

For few variant, when ignition is turned • off all the doors get automatically un­ locked.

### Concept

Also, when unlocked with remote key and if no door is opened within 30 seconds, ve­ hicle doors get automatically locked.

### Concept

Anti-grab / Anti-scan Coding

### Concept

The remote control set of this security sys­ tem is protected against the use of devices called ‘scanners’ and ‘grabbers’ which can record and reproduce some types of re­ mote codes.

The func­ tion of the remote gets reinstated imme­ diately when the user stops pressing the push button of remote.

### Concept

Pressing the Lock button (1) once, remote locks all the doors of the vehicle. Approach Light

### Procedure

Press approach light button (2) once, low beam and position lamp will turn ‘ON’. This feature helps to find and reach the parked vehicle or to reach home in dark/ cloudy condition. To switch ‘OFF’ the approach lights, press and release the same button or it automatically turns ‘OFF’ after certain time. Tail Gate Opening

### Procedure

To open the Tail gate press the button (3) once on the smart key, Tail gate will un­ latch. Please refer section starting and driving for more information. Unlocking all Doors

### Concept

Pressing the unlock button (4) once, re­ mote will unlock all the Doors. Please refer section starting and driving for more infor­ mation.

### Concept

### Concept

Slide the knob (1) to unlatch the key. Pull the key blade (2) out.

Slot is provided below driver door han­ • dle.

Insert the key blade in slot and press. •

### Procedure

When vehicle is in OFF condition, if we press lock button and unlock button simul­ taneously, Force panic operation gets ac­ tivated. In this case, turn indicators of vehicle start flashing and horn will blow au­ tomatically. Force Panic Off Operation

### Concept

By pressing any button of smart key, Force panic operation gets deactivated. Vehicle Search

### Concept

In vehicle locked condition, if lock button on smart key is pressed, the turn indica­ tors of vehicle flashes 4 times. Automatic Activation Of Immobilizer

### Concept

If smart key is not found within the passen­ ger compartment, engine will be immobi­ lized and vehicle cannot start. Auto Locking / Unlocking Of Doors / Auto Relock

If another vehicle’s smart key is being 3.

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

at certain intervals to prevent fatigue. 2. Wet Mode

### Concept

On wet road or during light showers, “Aquaplaning” can occur. “Aquaplaning” is the loss of direct contact between the road surface and the vehicle’s tires due to a water film forming between them. Steering or braking the vehicle can be very difficult, and loss of control can occur.

### Concept

The best advice is to slow down when the road is wet.

### Concept

The wet mode is designed for driving in the rain. It is characterized by having bet­ ter traction and handling so you can effec­ tively and safely drive during these conditions.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p188_img00` (page 188, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p188_img00.png`

### Concept

Rough Road Mode optimizes the vehicle behavior for driving over rough road or other unyielding obstacles.

### Concept

Braking performance is also tuned to sup­ port Rough road surfaces as compared to other drive modes.

### Concept

System allows improved rough road per­ formance to be more easily accessible to all customers specially novice or inexperi­ enced user.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p188_img01` (page 188, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p188_img01.png`

### Concept

4. Electronic Stability Program (ESP)(if available)

### Concept

ESP monitors driving stability and traction.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p188_img02` (page 188, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p188_img02.png`

### Concept

If ESP detects that the vehicle is deviating from the direction desired by

### Concept

the driver, one or more wheels are braked to stabilize the vehicle. The engine output is also modified to keep the vehicle on the desired course within physical limits. ESP assists the driver when pulling away on wet or slippery roads. ESP can also stabi­ lize the vehicle during braking and accel­ eration. Activate the ESP feature by pressing on the center console.

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in wet road without braking, there may be a delayed reaction from the brakes when braking for the first time. You have to depress the brake pedal more firmly. Maintain a greater distance from the ve­ hicle in front.

### Concept

Cautiously drive the vehicle on a rough road or off the road. Otherwise, the tires and wheels may be damaged. After driving those areas, inspect the tires and wheels.

## Knowledge

### Concept

Switch the compressor off and check • the tire pressure again. If tire pressure is too high, deflate the tire to the spec­ ified pressure using the pressure “air release” valve.

#### Visual References

### Concept

Rest of the remaining sealant in the • hose might leak out when opening pressure “air release” valve or taking off the protective cap of the hose. Please use protective glove for safety purpose.

### Concept

Once you have inflated the tire to its • correct tire pressure, switch off the compressor, pull the plug out of the socket, unscrew the hose, fasten the tire valve cap and put back on the pro­

### Concept

tective cap of the hose.

### Concept

Leave the bottle in the holder and store • the Puncture repair Kit away safely in the vehicle trunk.

### Concept

19, 20. Drive to the nearest workshop to get the damaged tyre repaired and if the tyre repair is not possible, tyre should be removed from the car. Before the tire is re­ moved from the rim, inform your tire dealer that the tire contains sealant. Sealant de­ posits in a used hose may impair proper function of the Puncture repair Kit. Both the sealant bottle and the hose need to be replaced together after using the Puncture repair Kit.

### Concept

New sealant and replacement parts can be purchased from your authorized repair shop or dealer. Sealant bottles can be dis­ posed with house-hold waste.

### Concept

Compressor unit we can use for filling the air & checking the pressure of the normal tyre.

### Concept

After using the sealant you may drive no faster than 80 km/h (50 mph), and the damaged tire must be replaced as quickly as possible (with in a maximum driving distance of 200 km (120 miles)). You must not continue to drive if heavy vibrations, unsteady steering behavior or noises should occur while driving.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p205_img02` (page 205, confidence 0.987)

Remember that emergency roadside tire repair kits only provide temporary mobility. Regulation concerning tire re­ pair after usage of Puncture Repair Kit may differ from country to country. You should consult a tire specialist for ad­ vice.

#### Visual References

Before driving, ensure tire is adjusted to recommended inflation pressure as in­ dicated on vehicle placard. Monitor tire pressure until sealed tire is replaced. Proceed as described above from point 15 onwards.

# FULLY AUTOMATIC TEMPERA­ TURE CONTROL (FATC) (if avail­ able)

## Knowledge

### Concept

FATC system controls the inside tempera­ ture of the vehicle automatically and pro­ vides maximum passenger convenience regardless of outside weather conditions.

### Concept

Rear window demister switch 1.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p133_img02` (page 133, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p133_img02.png`

### Concept

Maximum defrost switch 2.

### Concept

Air distribution (mode) switch 3.

### Concept

Blower speed control down switch 4.

### Concept

Blower speed control up switch 5.

### Concept

Temperature control knob 6.

### Concept

Auto ‘ON’ selection switch 7.

### Concept

Fresh air / recirculation switch 8.

### Concept

AC compressor ‘ON / OFF’ switch 9.

### Concept

OFF mode switch 10. Display Unit

### Concept

FATC display is shown on infotainment display screen.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p133_img03` (page 133, confidence 0.989)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p133_img03.png`

### Concept

FATC functions can be controlled using both the FATC control panel and the touch screen display.

### Concept

Whenever the user presses any switch or turns the rotary knob, then the display unit will show the relevant Climate Information.

### Concept

Also, when the display is not in climate mode then climate information will be dis­ played on the all-time display provide on the bottom bar.

### Concept

Rear Window Demister Switch

### Concept

This switch operates rear win­ dow demister. The system will be deactivated after 15 min of continuous operation.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p133_img04` (page 133, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p133_img04.png`

### Concept

Maximum Defrost Switch

### Concept

This switch directs the main 1. airflow towards windscreen for faster defrosting. (It also overrides any mode selection you may have made).

When you turn off the button, the sys­ 2. tem returns to its default setting.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_004/p133_img05.png`

### Concept

### Concept

In AUTO mode, the FATC sys­ tem will regulate the mode auto­ matically. However, user override is possible with the use of MODE

### Concept

### Concept

Temperature Control Knob

### Concept

Turning the temperature control knob clockwise increases the temperature of the air. The desired temperature will be in­ creased by steps of 0.5ºC. User can select temperature range from 18ºC to 30ºC. Whereas the anti-clockwise direction de­ creases the temperature.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p134_img08` (page 134, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p134_img08.png`

### Concept

When you set the temperature to its lower limit (Lo) or its upper limit (Hi), the system runs at full cooling or heating only. It does­ n’t regulate the interior temperature.

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

The system automatically selects the 3. proper mix of conditioned and / or heated air that will, as quickly as pos­ sible, raise or lower the interior temper­ ature to your preference.

### Concept

When you set the temperature to its 4. lower limit (Lo) or its upper limit (Hi), the system runs at full cooling or heat­ ing only. It does not regulate the inte­ rior temperature.

### Concept

Semi-automatic Operation

### Concept

You can manually select various functions of the climate control system when it is in fully automatic mode. All other features re­ main automatically controlled. Making any manual selection causes the word ‘AUTO’ in the display to go OFF and overridden setting is displayed. System will remain in semiautomatic mode till ‘AUTO’ is re- pressed.

### Concept

Fresh Air / Recirculation Switch

### Concept

When the recirculation 1. switch or LED is switched ‘ON’, air from the vehicle’s interior is sent throughout the system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p135_img01` (page 135, confidence 1.0)

### Concept

When the recirculation switch is 2. switched ‘OFF’, air is brought in from outside of the vehicle (fresh mode). Whenever discomfort is felt, switch to fresh air mode.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_004_p135_img02` (page 135, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_004/p135_img02.png`

### Concept

The system should be used with recircula­ tion air mode for faster heat up and cool down, however keeping the system in re­ circulation mode, particularly with AC OFF, can cause the windows fog up.

### Concept

The outside air intakes for the climate control systems are at the base of wind­ screen. Keep this area clear from leaves and other debris.

### Procedure

Press the AC compressor ON/OFF button to turn the air conditioning ON or OFF. The AC icon will be activated on the display when the AC will be ON.

title: CHANGE PARK ASSIST DELAY TIMER
text:
# CHANGE PARK ASSIST DELAY TIMER

## Knowledge

### Concept

The system allows you to retain the Park Assist display screen even after the Reverse gear is disengaged. This feature is called as Park Assist Delay Timer.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p61_img00` (page 61, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p61_img00.png`

### Concept

When in a closed parking lot, you have to disen- gage and engage the Reverse gear multiple times for parking your vehicle within the availa- ble space. The Park Assist Delay Timer feature, when enabled, will retain the park assist screen for a pre-configured time even when the Re- verse gear is disengaged

### Concept

To change park assist delay timer:

### Concept

 In the Vehicle Setup screen, navigate to and select the Park Assist option. The system displays the Park Assist Setup screen.

### Concept

 Tap on Delay Timer and select the required timer option from 0 sec/5 sec/10 sec. When the Park Assist compo- nent is enabled next, the system retains the Park Assist display screen even after the Reverse gear is disen- gaged for the selected time period.

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to control lighting fea- tures like Approach Lamp and DRL if your vehicle is equipped with these features.

### Concept

If the vehicle is equipped with this feature, you can set the Approach Lamp illumination time period from the infotain- ment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p61_img01` (page 61, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p61_img01.png`

### Concept

When you approach your car in the dark, you can switch on the Approach Lamps (some exte- rior and interior lights of the vehicle) to identify your car as well as to find your way safely to it.

# SELECT AN AUDIO PRESET

## Knowledge

### Concept

④ Tap to change Audio Preset

### Concept

Table 18: Audio Preset and Equalizer

### Concept

The audio settings are common to all media sources.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p75_img00` (page 75, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p75_img00.png`

### Concept

SETTING BASS, MIDDLE AND TREBLE

### Concept

Bass: Increase or decrease the gain of low frequencies of au- dio sources.

### Concept

Middle: Increase or decrease the mid frequency of connected audio source.

### Concept

Treble: Increase or decrease the high frequencies of con- nected audio source.

### Concept

title: SYSTEM CARE AND MAINTENANCE
text:
# SYSTEM CARE AND MAINTENANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Please read and follow the safety guidelines listed in this section to avoid injury or property damage .

### Concept

GENERAL SAFETY GUIDELINES

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p9_img00` (page 9, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p9_img00.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system is a sophisticated elec- tronic device. Do not allow improper access of the infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p9_img01` (page 9, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p9_img01.png`

### Warning

Permanent hearing loss may occur if you play your music at loud volumes for prolonged dura- tion. Exercise caution when setting the volume of your infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p9_img02` (page 9, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p9_img02.png`

### Concept

Exposure of the infotainment system to water or excessive moisture can cause electric shocks, fire, or other damages.

### Concept

SAFETY GUIDELINES WHILE DRIVING

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p9_img03` (page 9, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p9_img03.png`

### Concept

Glance at the screen of the infotainment system only when necessary and safe to do so. If pro- longed viewing of the screen is necessary, park the vehicle at a safe location and engage the park brake.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p9_img04` (page 9, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p9_img04.png`

### Concept

Make certain that the volume level of the info- tainment system is set to a level that allows you to hear outside traffic and other warnings.

### Concept

Exert utmost care while handling the infotainment system, as partial or complete loss of the infotainment system functions due to intentional misuse is not covered under warranty. Some guidance for using or maintaining the system are listed below:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p9_img05` (page 9, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p9_img05.png`

### Concept

Parking under direct sunlight for prolonged du- ration can result in high temperatures inside your car, which can damage your infotainment system, if used. So, before using the system let the car interior to cool down.

### Concept

Do not open the infotainment system, as incor- rect handling can damage the system. Further, warranty is void, if seal is broken.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p10_img00` (page 10, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_001_p10_img01` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not replace the vehicle speakers or fit addi- tional speakers with aftermarket speakers. It may lead to the malfunctioning or even damage of the infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p10_img02` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img02.png`

### Concept

Do not apply sticky or strong alcohol based spray, lotion or liquid on the infotainment sys- tem while cleaning the vehicle dashboard. This may cause permanent damage to the system button functions, knob operations or the display screen. It may also lead to the deterioration of the system paint.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p10_img03` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img03.png`

### Concept

Usage of paint or color on the infotainment sys- tem can make the moving parts sticky and stop them from functioning correctly.

### Concept

Avoid addition of any accessories such as exter- nal amplifiers, which will lead to the modifica- tion of the standard factory wiring connections. As such unauthorized interconnections can re- sult in the malfunctioning of the infotainment system. Always contact the Tata Authorized Dealer for the changes to the vehicle or system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p10_img04` (page 10, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img04.png`
- Image: `doc_001_p10_img05` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img05.png`

### Concept

Ensure that any liquid does not enter the info- tainment system, as it will lead to the failure of radio. The warranty of the system will be void, if liquid ingress marks are observed inside the system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p10_img06` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img06.png`

### Concept

Do not use excessive force while handling the infotainment system, USB slot, AUX-In slot and so on. It might cause damage to the system or component.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p10_img07` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p10_img07.png`

### Concept

Avoid usage of hard or sharp objects like pen, key, USB stick etc. to touch the screen, as it can cause scratches on the screen surface.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p11_img00` (page 11, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p11_img00.png`

### Concept

Use a soft, clean and dry cleaning cloth to clean the touch screen surface. If required, use a lint- free cloth damped with a cleaning solution such as isopropyl alcohol, or an isopropyl alcohol and water solution ratio of 50:50. Be sure to follow the solvent manufacturer's precautions and di- rections.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p11_img01` (page 11, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p11_img01.png`

### Concept

Avoid spraying or spilling of cleaning solutions, perfumes, car fresheners, beverages, caustic chemicals or any liquids on the touch screen surface, as it can damage the screen or the info- tainment system.

### Concept

The warranty clauses applicable to the infotainment system are listed below:

### Concept

1. Warranty is applicable only in India.

### Concept

2. Warranty for the product is against defective materials and manufacturing faults for 36 months / 60,000 km (whichever comes earlier) from the date of the first sale of vehicle. 3. Display and touch panel, if applicable to your system, are covered for 12 months from the date of the first sale of vehicle. 4. Warranty is expressly not applicable under the following conditions:

### Concept

a. Where the product has been dismantled, re-

### Concept

paired, altered, modified or damaged due to user negligence and misuse b. The serial number of the product been re-

### Concept

moved, defaced or altered. c. Warranty void sticker is removed or tam- pered d. Improper usage such as wrong electrical

### Concept

supply / voltage setting causing damage to the equipment e. Tampered, serviced or repaired by any

### Concept

agency not authorized by Tata Motors Lim- ited

# MANAGE PAIRED DEVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

 Refer to the user manual of your phone to verify whether all instructions for reset, connection and pair- ing have been followed.

### Concept

 Re-initiate Bluetooth pairing search or connection re- quest either from the phone or the infotainment system.

### Concept

 Pairing search enables faster pairing or connection be- tween the devices.

### Concept

 If the above steps do not help, start the pairing process from the beginning.

### Concept

If the pairing is still unsuccessful, try clearing the paired de- vices list from the Bluetooth settings of your phone and reset your phone, if required. Do the same on the infotainment sys- tem, if necessary. Even after following the troubleshooting steps you are unable to pair the devices, any one of the fol- lowing conditions might be true for your phone:

### Concept

 Compatibility with 3rd party phones depends on the Bluetooth standards, Bluetooth versions, OS version and applications deployed on the phone by its manufac- turer. So, the Bluetooth functions on your phone may not support pairing of devices or is not compatible with the infotainment system due to the differences in Blue- tooth software versions.

### Concept

 It is recommended that you update the firmware of your phone when you receive a message from the phone manufacturer prompting you to upgrade, as these up- grades are meant to provide the latest and more defect free software to you.

### Concept

 Generally Bluetooth SIG certified phones are known to work reliably with the infotainment system. Please check if your phone complies with the Bluetooth stand- ards.

### Concept

The infotainment system allows you to perform following op- erations for the paired devices:

### Concept

 View the list of devices paired to the system

### Concept

 Connect to a paired device

### Concept

 Disconnect an already paired device

### Concept

 Delete paired device(s)

### Concept

In the Bluetooth options, navigate to and select Paired Device List. The system displays the list of devices that are paired with the system.

title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
text:
# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)

## Knowledge

### Concept

Infotainment system and will be able to play compatible video files. It is to be noted that this behavior might vary from phone to phone based your phone specific implementation.

### Concept

From what all the Media sources I can play video?

### Concept

You can play video only from USB.

### Concept

Can I See / Play audio / Video / pictures from my smartphone when connected through USB port?

### Concept

Yes. However you have to enable your phone in Mass Storage Class mode just after connection to Car USB port. This behav- ior might vary based on smartphone which you are using.

### Concept

What are the supported video and audio codecs?

### Concept

The supported video and audio codecs are as follows:

### Concept

 Video Codecs: H.264 (BP, MP and HP up to AVC Level 3.2), MPEG4 (Simple and Advanced Simple Profile - All Levels)

### Concept

 Audio Codecs - Profile Supported: MP3, AAC

### Concept

 Container File: AVI, MP4

### Concept

I am unable to connect my Phone to the infotainment system using a USB cable however, I am able to connect through Bluetooth. Can you please help me with a solution?

### Concept

The USB cable that you are using to connect the Phone with the infotainment system might not be compatible with your Phone. Please use only the USB cable provided by the Phone Manufacturer.

### Concept

I am unable to connect to Android Auto. I have followed all steps specified. What could be the cause of the problem?

### Concept

If the connection between the Android Auto application and the infotainment system fails, this problem could arise. The connection will fail due to one of the following reasons:

### Concept

 Bluetooth connection was unsuccessful or connection was lost

### Concept

 If the infotainment system date and time does not match with the Phone data and time settings.

text:
# VOICE COMMAND GUIDELINES

## Knowledge

### Concept

 When similar sounding contact names/song names are spoken, the system will display a list of options match- ing the spoken name. You can choose the required op- tion from the list by calling out the corresponding line number or touching the required option on the screen.

### Concept

 Only speak the commands that are listed in the “Voice Recognition Commands” section.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p64_img00` (page 64, confidence 0.965)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p64_img00.png`

### Concept

The infotainment system also displays the voice recognition commands. You can se- lect and view the required command de- tails from within the Voice screen.

### Concept

 Speak the commands and names in a neutral English accent for best results.

### Concept

 Do not take long pauses (greater than 1 second) while speaking the words in a command. Speak the words of the command at a constant rate.

### Concept

 Avoid varying your pitch and volume while speaking the commands. Speak clearly and loudly at a reasonable speed.

### Concept

 Ensure that there is no noise disturbance when you speak the commands like, other passengers in the ve- hicle are talking or there is lot of wind noise. Disturb- ance from external sound sources may result in poor voice recognition.

### Concept

 Always face forward while speaking your commands as the voice recognition quality is best in this orientation.

### Concept

Figure 31: Voice Command List

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p65_img00` (page 65, confidence 0.97)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p65_img00.png`

### Concept

Feature Command System Action

### Concept

Cancel Cancels the currently active Voice Recognition session.

### Concept

Removes the digits in the number that was spoken earlier. For example: If you speak a phone number and wants to delete a digit in it, you can speak the Remove command.

### Concept

Feature Command System Action

### Concept

Corrects the digits in the number that was spoken earlier. For example, if you speak a phone number and wants to correct a digit in it, you can speak the Correct command.

### Concept

Special Characters: #: Hash / Pound Or +: Plus Or *:Star Or

### Concept

Uses the spoken special character as the response. These commands are mainly used while responding to an Interactive Voice Response (IVR).

### Concept

Prompts you to say the number to be dialed. After you say the required number, repeats the number to confirm it. Once you confirm the number by saying Dial again, dials the specified number.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p66_img00` (page 66, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p66_img00.png`

### Concept

You can delete or correct the digits in the number by saying the com- mands “Remove” or “Correction”. Dial <number> Dials the number specified with the command.

### Concept

Feature Command System Action

### Concept

You can say the number by saying each digit separately. For example to dial the number 9876543210, say, Dial nine eight seven six five four three two one zero

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p67_img00` (page 67, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p67_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_001_p67_img01` (page 67, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p67_img01.png`

### Concept

You can also say the number by saying the digits in groups of two or three. For example, to dial the number 022333267510, say Dial zero, double two, triple three, twenty six, seventy five, ten.

### Concept

Prompts you to say the contact name from the Contact list that must be dialed.

### Concept

After you say the contact name, the system dials the contact.

### Concept

Dials the specified contact name from the Contact list.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p67_img02` (page 67, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p67_img02.png`

### Concept

You can also say the category of the contact number like Mobile, Home, Work or Other along with the contact name. For example, to dial to the mobile number of the contact Amitabh Sharma, you can say Call Amitabh Sharma Mobile or Call Amitabh Mobile.

### Concept

Feature Command System Action

### Concept

The system may take some time to fetch the specified contact from the phone book contacts list.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p68_img00` (page 68, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p68_img00.png`

### Concept

Redial Re-dials the last number that was dialed.

### Concept

### Concept

title: ANDROID AUTO CONFIGURATION
text:
# ANDROID AUTO CONFIGURATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

Android Auto is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Android smartphones from your vehicle infotain- ment system. You can use voice actions or simple arrange- ment of Google Maps, Google Play Music and other important phone functions to access the required functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

### Concept

The Android Auto feature requires the installation of the An- droid Auto Mobile App, which can be downloaded on your smartphone from Google Play Store.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p85_img00` (page 85, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p85_img00.png`

### Concept

Android smartphones with android version 5.0 (Lollipop) or greater supports the Android Auto app. For best performance, Google recom- mends Android version 6.0 (Marshmallow) or above. For more information, refer to

### Concept

https://support.google.com/androidauto/an- swer/6348190?hl=en

### Concept

Before you connect the Android Auto app on your smartphone with the infotainment system, you need to perform the some one-time configuration steps:

### Concept

 Make sure your phone is running Android 5.0 (Lollipop) and up. For best performance, Google recommend An- droid 6.0 (Marshmallow) and up.

### Concept

 Download the Android Auto app from Google Play.

### Concept

 Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection

### Concept

Android Auto is by default enabled on your vehi- cle. (if available)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p85_img01` (page 85, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p85_img01.png`

### Concept

 For your safety, ensure your vehicle is ON and in the parked condition and the Park Brake is engaged.

### Concept

 Connect your phone to your car using a USB cable.

### Concept

 Your phone might ask you to download or update cer- tain apps, like Google Maps.

### Concept

 Review the Safety Information and Android Auto permis- sions to access your apps.

### Concept

 Turn on notifications for Android Auto. For the best ex- perience, we recommend accepting all requests.

### Concept

Your phone’s Bluetooth will be turned on auto- matically when Android Auto is connected to the car via USB.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p86_img00` (page 86, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p86_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_001_p86_img01` (page 86, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p86_img01.png`

### Concept

### Concept

On your car display, select Android Auto . Follow the in- structions to get started.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_001/p86_img02.png`
- Image: `doc_001_p86_img03` (page 86, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p86_img03.png`

If the connection with the infotainment system is lost, the app will get disconnected and info- tainment system displays the Home screen.

text:
# TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS FOR PAIRING DEVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

 The system will take you into Phone Setup, navigate to Pair New Device row and tap to initiate pairing process.

### Concept

 The system searches and displays a list for nearby Blue- tooth Devices, tap or select your device name to pro- ceed.

### Concept

 On selection, the system initiates the pairing by prompt- ing a confirmation message for passcode matching on both devices.

### Concept

 On confirmation, the pairing is successful and you can use Phone features as per your need, the system dis- plays your device name in the Paired Devices screen and in QAD.

### Concept

When the pairing is initiated, the currently con- nected device(s) must be temporarily discon- nected. The system will prompt you with a con- firmation message for disconnecting the con- nected paired devices.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p45_img00` (page 45, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p45_img00.png`

### Concept

GUIDELINES FOR PAIRING DEVICES

### Concept

Some of the guidelines for successfully pairing and connect- ing your phone with the infotainment system are:

### Concept

 Ensure that Bluetooth feature is switched ON in your phone for successful pairing or auto-reconnection with the infotainment system.

### Concept

 Ensure that the phone and the infotainment system are set to be visible to one another (refer to the Bluetooth Setup settings of your phone and infotainment system).

### Concept

 Ensure that your phone is not in Battery Saver or Air- plane mode.

### Concept

 Ensure that the phone and infotainment system are in proximity.

### Concept

 Ensure that your phone book contacts do not have spe- cial characters or blanks before their name. If there are such Contacts, please rename them.

### Concept

If you are unable to pair your phone with the infotainment sys- tem even after following the guidelines, try the following trou- bleshooting steps:

# CONNEXTNEXT INFOTAINMENT SYSTEM USER’S MANUAL

## Knowledge

### Concept

Welcome to the ConnectNext Infotainment System User's Manual. The infotainment system in your vehicle provides you with state of the art in-car entertainment to enhance your driving experience.

### Concept

Before using the infotainment system for the first time, please ensure that you read this manual carefully. The manual will familiar- ize you with the infotainment system of your car and its functionalities. It also contains instructions on how to use the infotainment system in a safe and effective manner.

### Concept

We insist that all service and maintenance of the infotainment system of your car must be done only at authorized Tata Service Centers. Incorrect installation or servicing can cause permanent damage to the system. If you have any further questions about the infotainment system, please get in touch with the nearest Tata Dealership. We will be happy to answer your queries and value your feedback.

### Concept

We wish you a safe and connected drive!

## Knowledge

### Concept

INTRODUCING CONNECTNEXT INFOTAINMENT SYSTEM

### Concept

The ConnectNext infotainment system provides you with a bundle of high-end functionalities to:

### Concept

### Concept

 Handle certain vehicle feature controls

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

 4 channel audio output

### Concept

 AM and FM Tuner bands with 20 memories each

### Concept

 USB, iPod, AUX and Bluetooth ® Audio multimedia sup- port (if available)

### Concept

 Bluetooth ® connectivity for simultaneous pairing with up to 10 devices, hands free calling, phonebook access and set favourite contacts capability.

### Concept

### Concept

 Climate Control from infotainment system

### Concept

 Voice Assistance to operate your infotainment system functionality using voice commands

### Concept

 Android Auto™ and Apple CarPlay™ compatibility for smartphone control using infotainment system (if avail- able)

### Concept

 DriveNext for real-time driving behavior analysis

### Concept

 Display OFF feature for distraction free night drive

### Concept

 Speed Dependent Volume Control

### Concept

 Infotainment controls from steering Wheel and island mounted button panel

### Concept

Some of the vehicle are not standard in every vehicle variant. Features that are unavailable in the vehicle cannot be controlled using the info- tainment system. Please refer to the Owner’s Manual of your vehicle or check with your vehi- cle dealer to confirm the list of features availa- ble in your vehicle.

# CARPLAY CONFIGURATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is a projection technology, which allows you to operate your Apple iPhone from your vehicle infotainment sys- tem. You can use voice commands or the simple iPhone like interface on your infotainment system to operate your phone functionalities. It is designed to minimize distraction while driving.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_001_p87_img00` (page 87, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_001/p87_img00.png`

### Concept

Apple CarPlay is compatible from iPhone 5 and up. For more information, refer to

### Concept

https://www.apple.com/in/ios/carplay/

### Concept

Before you connect the iPhone to infotainment system to use CarPlay, you need to perform the some one-time configuration steps:

### Concept

 Make sure you have iPhone 5 or up device, running on latetst iOS.

### Concept

 Make sure your phone has a strong and fast network connection

### Concept

 Connect your phone to your car using a USB cable.

### Concept

 Make sure that CarPlay isn't restricted. Go to Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions, tap Al- lowed Apps and make sure that CarPlay is enabled.

title: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
text:
# FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)

## Knowledge

### Concept

How do I initiate/ start Android Auto/CarPlay in the infotain- ment system?

### Concept

Please refer to Android Auto and Apple CarPlay sections for details.

### Concept

To use Android Auto/CarPlay, do we have any specific Smartphone/iPhone version requirements?

### Concept

For Android Auto the required specification is, Android smartphones with android version 5.0 or greater. For CarPlay the requirement is, iPhone 5 and above versions.

### Concept

Can I use my phone while I have connected to the infotain- ment system for Android Auto and I am currently using its functionalities?

### Concept

Yes, you can use your phone, while connected to the infotain- ment system for Android Auto and the application is currently in use.

### Concept

Where can I get the list of apps that are compatible with An- droid Auto/Car Play?

### Concept

 Apps compatible with Android Auto: From Android Auto Browse menu-> More Apps option.

### Concept

 Apps compatible with CarPlay: Listed on the CarPlay app Home screen.

### Concept

How do I use Google Voice Recognition while Android Auto is connected and running on the infotainment system?

### Concept

You can enable OK Google using any one of the following ways:

### Concept

 To activate OK Google (voice recognition) so that your voice actions are recognized, press the mike icon.

### Concept

 You can also enable OK Google by doing a Long Press on the Voice command Steering Wheel control element.

### Concept

Can Android Auto and CarPlay be used simultaneously?

### Concept

No, Android Auto and CarPlay cannot be used simultaneously from the infotainment system. You need to disconnect one app before connecting and using the other.

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

During phone charging, the wireless 3. charger and phone may become warm. In this case, charging will stop due to phone’s internal protection func­ tion. Charging may resume after phone cools down.

### Concept

Please do not put any liquid (e.g. 4. water, cold drink, and sanitizer), dust particles or flammable object on anti- skid mat.

### Concept

Do not cover the wireless charger with 5. a cloth or other object while charging. It may heat up the device and reduce the charging efficiency.

### Concept

Do not disassemble, modify or remove 6. the wireless charger. Also do not apply force or impact to the wireless charger. Information

### Concept

Small noise may be heard when a 1. smart phone which does not support wireless charging or any foreign object is placed on the charging pad. This small sound is due to the vehicle dis­ cerning compatibility of the object placed on the charging pad. It does not

### Concept

affect the vehicle performance or the smartphone in any way.

### Concept

For certain cellular phones with their 2. own protection, the wireless charging speed may decrease and the wireless changing may stop.

### Concept

When the interior temperature of the 3. wireless charger rises above a set temperature, the wireless charging will cease / stop to charging function. After the interior temperature drops below set threshold, the wireless charging function will resume.

### Concept

Wireless charging will stop when the 4. vehicle is Ignition OFF.

### Concept

Wireless charging will stop when the 5. smartphone is not in complete contact with the wireless charging pad.

### Concept

When charging certain smart phones, 6. the charging full message on head unit may not display when the smart phone is fully charged. It depends on smart phone manufacturer characteristics/ configurations.

### Concept

Smartphone of some manufacturers 7. may display messages on weak cur­

### Concept

rent. This is due to particular charac­ teristic of smartphone and does not imply a malfunction on wireless charger.

### Concept

Smaller smartphone users (ex. IPhone 8. 8) may face intermittent charging is­ sues due to its smaller size. (To avoid this, place the smartphone at center of the charging pad). Small mobile phones may not be able to charge in any/ every position as kept on charging pad.

### Concept

The wireless charger may not operate 9. correctly when the vehicle is near a TV tower, electric power plant, gas station, large display, airport, or other facility that generates strong magnetic field radio waves or electrical disturbance / noise.

### Concept

If FOD is message pop-up then after 10. lifting the phone FOD message may disappear or remains till metal object is also removed. This depend of wire­ less charging support feature of smart phone.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

Service Intervals In

### Concept

Km (kilometer) Or Months Whichever

### Procedure

I: Inspect ( Check, Clean, Correct, Top Up, Adjust, Repair, Replace As Necessary) T: Tightening Torque R: Replace

### Procedure

Check condition of rubber bushes/parts in lower control arms, front and rear coil spring seats, front & rear bump stop- pers, anti-roll bar links, rear twist beam, rubber boots/dust cover/bellow in rack & pinion, steering and suspension ball joints, steering column. ### Concept

In case of break down, we recommend that your vehicle be towed with the driving wheels off the ground or place the vehicle on a flatbed truck as shown.

To avoid serious damage to automatic transaxle, limit the vehicle speed to 15 km/h (10 mph) and drive less than 1.5 k m (1 mile) when towing.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

tyre damage, some tyres can only be partially sealed or not sealed at all.

### Concept

Loss of tyre pressure can affect vehicle • handling and vehicle control.

### Warning

Drive with caution and avoid making • sudden steering or driving maneuvers, especially if the vehicle is heavily loaded or you are towing a trailer.

### Concept

The system will provide you with an • emergency temporary repair, enabling you to continue your journey to the next vehicle or tyre dealer, or to drive a maximum distance of 200 Kms.

### Concept

Do not exceed a maximum speed of • 80 km/h.

### Concept

Keep the Puncture repair Kit out of the • reach of children.

### Concept

If used for other than its intended pur­ • pose, the tyre puncture repair Kit may cause severe accident or injury due to the fact that compressed air can act as an explosive or propellant.

### Concept

Park your vehicle at the roadside so • that you do not obstruct the flow of traf­ fic and you are able to use the Punc­

### Concept

ture repair Kit without being in danger.

### Concept

Engage the hand brake, even if you • have parked on a level road, to ensure that the vehicle will not move.

### Concept

Do not attempt to remove foreign ob­ • jects like nails or screws penetrating the tyre leave them as it is.

### Concept

Always ensure the vehicle engine is • running during the tyre puncture re- pair kit is in use, but not if the vehicle is in an enclosed or poorly ventilated area.

### Concept

Never leave the tyre puncture repair kit • unattended while in use.

### Concept

Do not keep the compressor operating • for more than 10 minutes other-wise there is a risk of it overheating.

### Concept

Replace the sealant bottle with a new • one before the expiry date is reached (see bottle label). In case that the sealant is expired the functionality can­ not be fully guaranteed. Only use orig­ inal tyre puncture repair kit bottles which are pressure resistant.

### Concept

Do not use the Puncture repair Kit if the tyre has already been damaged as a re­ sult of being driven underinflated. Do not try to seal damage other than that located within the visible tread of the tyre. Do not try to seal damage to the tyre’s sidewall.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p269_img00` (page 269, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p269_img00.png`

text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Use only a battery of same rating & capac­ ity to jump start your vehicle. Position the booster battery close to your vehicle so that the jump leads will reach both batter­ ies.

### Concept

When using a battery of another vehicle, do not let the vehicles touch.

### Concept

Apply the parking brake firmly and keep the gearshift lever in neutral.

### Warning

Turn off all vehicle accessories, except those necessary for safety like hazard warning lamps.

### Concept

If your vehicle is equipped with Battery sensor, then do not connect your jump start cable lead directly on the Sensor sur­ face. Connect only on the negative cable surface as shown on the image. After jump start event, IAC function will be restored only when the Vehicle is parked in idle for 3-4 Hours.

### Concept

Make jump lead connections as follows:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p276_img00` (page 276, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p276_img00.png`

### Concept

Connect one end of the first jump lead • to the positive (+) terminal of the dis­ charged battery.

### Concept

Connect the other end to the positive • (+) terminal of the booster battery.

### Concept

Connect one end of the second jump • lead to the negative (–) terminal of the booster battery.

### Concept

Make the final connection (other end of • the negative terminal) to an unpainted, heavy metal part (i.e. engine mounting stud/nut) of the vehicle of discharged battery.

### Concept

Start the engine of the vehicle with the • discharged battery.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p276_img01` (page 276, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p276_img01.png`

### Concept

Before disconnecting the jumper ca­ • bles, let the engine run for several min­ utes.

### Concept

If the booster battery you are using is • fitted to another vehicle, start the en­ gine of the vehicle with the booster bat­ tery. Run the engine at moderate speed.

### Concept

Remove the jump leads in the exact • reverse order in which you connected them.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

unpredictable if brakes are wet.

### Concept

After driving through water or washing the underside of the vehicle, test the brakes while driving at a slow speed to see if they have maintained their normal effective­ ness. If the brakes are less effective than normal, dry them by repeatedly applying the brakes while driving slowly until the brakes have regained their normal effec­ tiveness. Braking on Downhill Gradients

### Concept

On long and steep gradients, you must re­ duce the load on the brakes by shifting early to a lower gear. This allows you to take advantage of the engine braking ef­ fect and helps avoid overheating and ex­ cessive wear of the brakes.

### Concept

Mechanical Parking Brake

Mechanical parking brake acting on the rear wheels is provided on the vehicle.

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Concept

Engine Passive Start/stop

### Concept

Start/Stop switch is provided on the dash- board towards the right side of steering wheel. Start / Stop Switch

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p230_img00` (page 230, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p230_img00.png`

### Concept

A Start Stop Switch (SSSW) or Push to Start Button is a main component of Pas- sive (Engine) Start and Stop system. It is used to control ACC, IGN outputs as well as to start and stop the engine.

### Concept

If smart key battery voltage is low or empty and vehicle is in OFF mode then to start the engine user needs to press start/stop button two times with interval of 2.5 sec. between two switch press after pressing the clutch pedal OR brake with valid smart key near Immobilizer antenna (located

### Concept

below front cup holder).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p230_img02` (page 230, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p230_img02.png`

### Concept

If vehicle engine is switched from ON to OFF and Start Stop button is pressed with clutch press within 5 sec, Engine gets cranked.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p230_img03` (page 230, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p230_img03.png`

• If Smart key is inside the vehicle and on pressing start stop switch, if start stop switch green LED blink for 10 sec. duration then rotate steering wheel and simultaneously press start stop switch again.

  - File: `images/doc_003/p230_img01.png`

### Concept

• If smart key is inside the vehicle and on pressing start stop switch, if start stop switch green LED blinks more than 10 sec. duration then contact authorized TATA MOTORS dealer.

### Concept

• If ESCL (Electronic Steering Col- umn Lock) is not unlocked properly, then vehicle doesn’t go into ACC mode.

### Concept
