title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

When Any Part Of The Vehicle Sags

### Concept

When any part of the vehicle sags due to the number of passengers or the distribu­ tion of the load, there is a margin of error between the fixed guide lines on the screen and the actual distance/course on the road.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p256_img00` (page 256, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p256_img00.png`

### Concept

When Approaching Three-dimensional Objects

### Concept

The distance guidelines are displayed ac­ cording to flat surfaced objects (such as the road). It is not possible to determine the position of three-dimensional objects

### Concept

(such as vehicles) using the distance guidelines. When approaching a three-di­ mensional object.

### Concept

a. Distance Guidelines

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p256_img01` (page 256, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p256_img01.png`

### Concept

Visually check the surroundings and the area behind the vehicle. On the screen, it appears that a truck is parked at point B. However, in reality if you back up to point A, you will hit the truck. On the screen, it appears that A is closest and C is furthest away. However, in reality, the distance to A and C is the same, and B is farther than A and C.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p256_img02` (page 256, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p256_img02.png`

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

The following preconditions should be maintained for the whole duration on the update.

### Concept

Vehicle Battery voltage should be within 10-16 Volts.

### Concept

If the vehicle battery is low (Not EV ve­ • hicle battery) then the update is not possible, wait for on-board charging to charge the vehicle battery or visit the service center.

### Concept

Ignition on is not vehicle cranked state. • To put the vehicle in Ignition ON, press the Start/Stop button twice without pressing on the brake.

### Concept

Vehicle in stand-still condition. (Vehicle speed = 0 and Engine RPM = 0.)

### Concept

The vehicle should not be in cranked • state. The vehicle should also be sta­ tionary in a safe location.

### Concept

Gear Position should be Neutral.

### Concept

Put the vehicle in Neutral gear posi­ • tion.

### Concept

Park Brake should be enabled.

### Concept

Enable the park brake. Accelerator • Pedal Position should not be pressed (0%).

### Concept

Do not place your feet on the acceler­ • ator.

### Concept

The vehicle should not be in a charging state. (Only for EV)

### Concept

Vehicle should not be in charging. •

### Concept

To Open– Pull the lever to open the glove box flap.

The luggage cover can be lifted. •

### Concept

Front Seat Back Pockets (if equipped)

### Note

Rear pockets are provided behind the front seats for keeping small magazines /Note­ book etc.

The coat hook cannot restrain • heavy objects or items.

### Concept

Do not hang objects on coat hooks • which can obstruct the curtain airbag deployment during impact.

### Concept

Never hang hard, sharp-edged or • fragile objects on the coat hook.

### Concept

Do not use these hooks for securing luggage like using nets etc.

### Concept

The Climate Control regulates the temperature inside the vehicle and filter the dust particles in cabin based on the user set temperature settings.

### Concept

The air is distributed through the vents in the passenger compartment as shown below:

- Image: `doc_003_p203_img00` (page 203, confidence 0.983)

### Concept

Centre Air Vents ( Front)

### Concept

Centre air vents are provided on dash- board. Air flow and its direction can be ad- justed with the help of knob provided on respective vent.

title: IMPORTANT INFORMATION
text:
# IMPORTANT INFORMATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

Safety consciousness not only ensures your safety and the safety of other road users, but it also helps to reduce the wear and tear on your vehicle.

### Concept

Safe Driving Depends On:

### Concept

• How quickly you make decisions to avoid an accident.

### Concept

• Your ability to concentrate.

### Concept

• How well you can see and judge ob- jects.

### Concept

• How well familiar you are with your ve- hicle controls and its capabilities. Safety Tips

### Concept

• Always take into account the road con- ditions, weather conditions, vehicle speed in order to prevent accidents.

### Concept

• Turn ‘ON’ the side indicators at least 30 meters before taking a turn or changing the lane.

### Concept

• Decelerate to a safe speed before tak- ing turn. Do not apply brakes during cornering.

### Concept

• When overtaking other vehicles, watch out for the oncoming vehicle.

### Concept

• Never drive under the influence of al- cohol or drugs.

### Concept

• If your vehicle is equipped with info- tainment/ navigation system, set and make changes to your travel route only when the vehicle is parked.

### Concept

• Program radio presets with the vehicle parked, and use your programmed presets to make radio use quicker and simpler.

### Concept

• If your car gets flooded and has soaked carpeting or water on the floor- ing, you should not try to start the en- gine, we recommend to kindly contact TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre. While Handling Hot Parts

### Concept

• Never remove the coolant cap when the engine is hot. The engine coolant is under high pressure and could splash on to skin/eyes causing severe burns.

### Concept

• Stay rod becomes hot enough after ve-

### Concept

hicle running, be careful while using it. Touch only rubber part available on stay rod.

### Concept

• Never touch engine exhaust after ve- hicle running as it will cause severe in- jury.

### Concept

• Do not touch tyre and wheel rim when it is hot after a long journey it may cause burn injury.

### Concept

Vehicle In Water Logged Condition Vehicle In Flood Vehicle In Fire

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p10_img00` (page 10, confidence 0.996)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p10_img01` (page 10, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p10_img04` (page 10, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img04.png`

### Concept

If your vehicle gets flooded wait for water level to recede

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p10_img02` (page 10, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img02.png`

### Concept

Once the water is receded, ap- proach the vehicle, open all doors and let the water inside the vehicle get drained completely

### Procedure

• Remove floor carpet and open the rubber/plastic gourmet provided on floor board, stepney space for water to recede from interior flooring of the

### Concept

vehicle completely. • Push your vehicle to safe place do not try to start the vehicle

### Concept

If the vehicle is submerged in water, we recommend to kindly contact TATA MO- TORS Authorised Service Center.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p10_img03` (page 10, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img03.png`

### Concept

• Do not modify your vehicle.

### Concept

• Do not install high wattage bulbs, non-genuine lamps, horns

### Concept

• Do not modify suspension, wheels, tyres

### Concept

• Before driving through water logged areas ensure that water is below tailpipe level • Unseen pot holes could damage under surface of the vehicle •

### Concept

Drive slowly and maintain constant ac- celeration After passing the water logged area ensure to press brakes intermittently to dry the brake disc

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p10_img06` (page 10, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img06.png`

### Concept

• Do not drive through heavy water logged area

### Concept

Water may enter into vehicle interior and engine compartment which may damage electrical, electronic circuits and cause hydrostatic lock of en- gine. Battery may get damaged or short circuited

### Concept

Stick to manufacturer recom- mended parts. Safety matters

### Concept

Avoid tampering with the wiring har- ness, it can lead to short circuits.

### Concept

• Be cautious with retrofitted CNG kits. Improper installation can cause leaks or fire hazards.

### Concept

In case of vehicle fire, immediately evacuate vehicle and contact local fire tender responder. They possess proper training and equipment to safely extinguish vehicle fire. Contact nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Center for further assistance.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p10_img05` (page 10, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p10_img05.png`

### Concept

ehicle Cyber Attack Modern vehicles are equipped with inter- net connectivity for navigation, entertain- ment and diagnostics, making them vulnerable to cyber attacks. Vehicles collect and stores personal data, which can be targeted by hackers. Cyber attacks can compromise infotain- ment system, brakes, steering and engine control, leading to severe cyber risk

### Concept

ehicle Cyber Security

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p11_img00` (page 11, confidence 0.998)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p11_img00.png`

### Concept

• Refrain from connecting the vehicle to public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks.

### Concept

Ensure your vehicle is physically se- cured by locking doors and parking in safe areas to prevent from unautho- rized access.

### Concept

Never leave your keys in the car, even if you are nearby.

### Concept

Do not store or carry inflammable materials in the vehicle

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p11_img01` (page 11, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p11_img01.png`

### Concept

• Keep your vehicle updated with latest software versions. • Pay attention to any security alerts or notifications and follow the guidelines. • Disable the bluetooth of the car where not required and vehicle is not in use. • Keep infotainment app’s login creden- tials private & do not share it with anyone.

### Concept

Your vehicle is provided with good seating comfort. To make your journey more safe and enjoyable we recommend you to fol- low below warnings and cautions.

### Concept

Front Passenger Seat

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p12_img01` (page 12, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p12_img01.png`

### Concept

Applicable for Hatchback/SUV

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p12_img03` (page 12, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p12_img03.png`

### Concept

• Do not adjust seat while driving / ve- hicle is moving. Doing so could re- sult in loss of control, and an accident causing death, serious in- jury, or property damage.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p12_img00` (page 12, confidence 0.981)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p12_img00.png`

### Concept

• Always sit as far back as possible from the steering wheel while main- taining comfortable control of the vehicle. Fitment of seat covers on driver seat with airbags is strictly prohibited.

### Concept

• Do not keep any sitting cushion on seats. This may result in serious or fatal injury in the event of accident.

### Concept

• After adjusting the seat make sure it is securely locked by pushing it for- ward and backwards without using

### Concept

lock release lever. Sudden or unex- pected movement of the driver’s seat could cause to lose control of the vehicle resulting in an accident.

### Concept

• All passengers must be seated in seats and restrained with seat belt properly while riding in vehicle

### Concept

• If there are occupants in the rear seats, be careful while adjusting the front seat position.

### Concept

Never ride in a vehicle with a front seat ‐ back fully reclined. This may lead to serious injuries. Fitment of seat cov- ers on front passenger seat with airbags is strictly prohibited.

### Concept

The rear seatback must be securely latched. If not, passengers and objects

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p12_img02` (page 12, confidence 0.976)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p12_img02.png`

### Concept

could thrown forward resulting in seri- ous injury in the event of a sudden stop or collision. Luggage and other objects in boot should be kept flat. If large, heavy, or piled they must be secured properly. No passenger should ride in the boot area or sit or lie on folded seat- backs while the vehicle is in motion.

### Concept

Under no circumstances should ob- jects be piled higher than the seat- backs. Failure to follow these warnings could result in serious in- jury in the event of a sudden stop or collision. Ensure that objects are se- curely fastened.

### Concept

Storing items against seatback or in any other way interfering with proper locking of a seatback could result in serious or fatal injury in a sudden stop or collision After reset- ting the seatback to its seating posi- tion make sure it is securely latched

### Procedure

Adjust the head restraint so that it is as close to the head as possible and the cen- ter of the head restraint supports the back of the head at eye level.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p13_img02` (page 13, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p13_img02.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p13_img04` (page 13, confidence 0.962)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p13_img04.png`

### Procedure

Adjust the head restraint so that it is as close to the head as possible and the cen- ter of the head restraint supports the back of the head at eye level.

### Concept

by pushing it forward and back- wards

### Concept

Your hands might cut or injured by the sharp edges of the seats mechanism during looking for small objects trapped under the seats or between the seat and the center console.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p13_img00` (page 13, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p13_img00.png`

### Concept

Do not drive the vehicle without the seat head restraints. Head restraints are in- tended to help reduce injuries during an accident.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p13_img01` (page 13, confidence 0.939)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p13_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p13_img03` (page 13, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p13_img03.png`

### Concept

This section describes your Vehicle’s Seat belts, Airbags and Child restraints system. Please read and follow all these instruc- tions carefully to minimize risk of severe injury or death.

### Concept

Seat belts are the primary restraints system in the vehicle. All occupants, including the driver, should always wear seat belts. Your vehicle is equipped with three point seat belts for all occupants.

### Concept

Sit back and adjust the driver seat. Make sure that your seat is adjusted to a good driving position and the back of the seat is upright.

### Concept

Buckling of Seat Belt

### Concept

• Grasp the tongue then slowly pull out the seat belt over the shoulder and across the chest. When the seat belt is long enough to fit, insert the tongue into the lock buckle until you hear a “CLICK” which indicates that the seat- belt is securely locked. (Refer “IN- SERT TO LOCK” image)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p14_img00` (page 14, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p14_img00.png`

### Concept

• Position the lap portion of seat belt across your pelvic bone, below your abdomen. To remove slack, pull up a bit on the shoulder seat belt. To loosen the lap portion seat belt if it is too tight,

### Concept

• Ensure that the seat belt webbing is straight and not twisted. Twisted seat- belts may not work properly in case of collision.

### Concept

Releasing the Seat Belt

### Concept

To release the seat belt, push the red but- ton on the lock buckle (refer “PRESS TO UNLOCK” image). Ensure to hold seat belt during unlocking and release it slowly to- wards the seat belt mounting. The seat belt will automatically retract to its stowed position. If necessary, slide the tongue down the webbing to allow the seat belt to retract fully.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p14_img01` (page 14, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p14_img01.png`

### Concept

Due to retractor reversal action if you leave the seat belt from the unlock po-

### Concept

tilt the tongue and pull on the lap seat belt. A snug seat belt reduces the risk of sliding under the seat belt in a colli- sion. Ensure that the seat belt running over the body (shoulder segment and lap segment) does not have any twist. Twisted seat belt may not offer effec- tive protection when required.

### Concept

Seat Belt Height Adjustments (if equip- ped)

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

SERVICE INSTRUCTIONS

### Concept

The TATA HARRIER has been manufactured to give you eco­ nomical and trouble free performance. To achieve this, please fol­ low the instructions as stated.

### Concept

Your vehicle is entitled to three free services (labour only). The free service coupons are attached to the sales invoice. Please present these coupons to the servicing dealer while availing free services.

### Concept

1st free service - At 1,000 - 2,000 kms. OR 2 months, whichever is earlier.

### Concept

2nd free service - At 7,000 - 8,000 kms. OR 6 months, whichever is earlier.

### Concept

3rd free service - At 14,500 - 15,500 kms. OR 12 months, whichever is earlier.

### Concept

All services other than free services are chargeable.

### Concept

Servicing of the vehicle can be done at any TATA MOTORS Au­ thorised Dealer Workshop or TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre (TASC).

### Concept

Warranty claims can be settled by any TATA MOTORS Authorised Dealer Workshop or TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre (TASC).

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Engine Oil Level Checking

### Concept

Warm up the engine to normal operating temperature.

### Concept

Turn it ‘OFF’ and wait for 5 minutes for the oil to return to the oil pan. Be sure the ve­ hicle is on a level surface.

### Concept

Take out the dipstick, wipe it clean, and reinsert it fully. Pull it out again and exam­ ine the oil level. It should be between ‘MIN’ and ‘MAX’ level. If not, top up with recom­ mended engine oil. Engine oil dipstick

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p307_img01` (page 307, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p307_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p307_img02` (page 307, confidence 1.0)

- Image: `doc_003_p307_img03` (page 307, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p307_img03.png`

### Concept

For location of Engine oil filling cap and dip stick, please refer Engine Compart­ ment.

### Concept

Engine Oil Quality Monitoring Indicator

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a feature in the engine man­ agement system which will monitor the engine oil quality throughout the lifetime of the oil in the engine. This will ensure that an oil change is requested only when really necessary. Once the oil quality reaches a threshold, the engine management system will ask for oil change by lighting the above lamp. This lamp will be blinking for oil change re­ quest.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p307_img00` (page 307, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p307_img00.png`

### Concept

Depending on your driving conditions, the oil quality may get deteriorated sooner. For example, if you are driving predominantly in highway conditions without straining the engine excessively, the oil lamp indicating oil change may appear later than ex­ pected. Similarly, if you drive continuously and for a long time in city at low speeds with frequent cold starts and short jour­ neys, the engine management system may prompt you to change the oil sooner than had the car been used mainly in high­ ways.

### Concept

The oil consumption depends upon the driving style and the conditions under which the vehicle is used.

### Concept

Do not remove the filler cap when • the engine is running.

### Concept

Do not add oil above the MAX. • mark. Oil level above the MAX. mark may cause engine damage.

text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

How to Proceed In The Event Of a Tyre Puncture in Two Steps

### Warning

First pump the tyre sealant and air into the tyre (see Step 1).Immediately there-after, drive a short distance (3-10 km) in order to distribute the seal-ant in the tyre. After that check the tyre pressure and pump more air into the tyre if necessary (see Step 2). Then you can proceed to drive with caution for a maximum distance of 200 kms and at a maximum speed of 80 km/h. Step 1: Pumping the Tyre Sealant and Air into the Tyre

### Procedure

 Take out the hose and power plug with cable out of the tyre puncture re- pair kit casing. Remove the white cap of T-type connector of Sealant Bottle.  Connect the hose pipe of the com- pressor with T-type connector of seal- ant bottle. Ensure it is tightly Fitted.  Avoid skin contact with the sealant which contains natural rubber latex. Do not open pressure "air release" valve. Use enclosed protective gloves.

### Procedure

 Install sealant Bottle by rotating clock- wise firmly against the bottle holding grooves on the compressor. Remove the white cap of the hose pipe of the sealant bottle.  Insert power plug into the 12 volt power socket connection.  Start the vehicle in idling (only if the vehicle is outdoors or in a well venti- lated area).  Press compressor switch to ON Im- portant: When pumping in the sealant through the tyre valve, the pressure may rise up to 500 KPa (5 bar. 73 psi) but will drop again after about 30 sec- onds.  Inflate the tyre to an inflation pressure of minimum 180kPa, (1.8 bar/26 psi) and a maximum of 300kPa (3 bar/43 psi).  Remove the sealant bottle from the compressor grooves & tight the white caps on the hose pipe of the sealant bottle as well as T -type connector of the sealant bottle. This avoids unex- pected leakage of sealant residue and Lock it.

### Concept

 Make sure the puncture repair kit stored safely, but it’s still easily acces- sible, in the vehicle.  The compressor will be needed again when you check the tyre pressure.

### Concept

 Ensure pump should not be ON for more than 10 min as it may heat up and stop working.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p272_img00` (page 272, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p272_img00.png`

### Procedure

 Check the sidewall of the tyre prior to inflation. If there are any cracks, bumps or similar damage, do not attempt to inflate the tyre. Do not stand directly beside the tyre while the compressor is pumping. Watch the sidewall of the tyre. If any cracks, bumps or similar damage appear, turn off the compressor and let the air out by means of the pressure “air release” valve. In this case, do not continue to use the tyre.

### Concept

Your vehicle is subjected to many external influences such as climate, road condi- tions, industrial pollution and proximity to the sea. These conditions demand regular care of the vehicle body. Dirt, insects, bird droppings, oil, grease, fuel and stone chip- pings should be removed as soon as pos- sible. Washing

### Concept

Following these tips while washing your vehicle. 1. Always wash your vehicle in shade and ensure surface is at room temper- ature.

### Concept

2. Wash with mild vehicle wash soap like ‘Car Shampoo’ and use a soft bristle brush, sponge or soft cloth and rinse it frequently while washing to avoid scratches.

### Concept

3. When cleaning ensure that drain holes of lower door panels and rocker panel are free from mud, slug etc to make way for entrapped water inside it to avoid corrosion.

### Concept

4. To avoid scratches, please wear soft gloves. Remove finger rings, nails, wrist watch while washing.

### Concept

5. To remove stubborn stains and con- taminants like tar, use turpentine or cleaners like ‘Stain remover’ which are safe for paint surfaces.

### Concept

6. Avoid substances like petrol, diesel, kerosene, benzene, thinner, acids or other solvents that cause damage to vehicle interior, exterior and paint.

### Concept

7. Dry your vehicle thoroughly to prevent any damp spots.

### Concept

8. Rinse all surfaces thoroughly to pre- vent any traces of soap and other cleaners as this may lead to the forma- tion of stains on the painted surface later.

### Concept

9. During washing of the vehicle, do not apply water jet OR pressure water from pipe directly on any rubber mate- rial or Seal surface. This is to avoid damage to Rubber sealing parts in the sunroof system or in the vehicle. The damage to the sunroof sealing or any other seal in the vehicle will cause

### Concept

10. It is recommended to use dry low pres- sure air for cleaning the engine com- partment. Do not use pressurized water

### Concept

After drying the vehicle, inspect it for chips and scratches that could allow corrosion to start. Apply touch up paint where nec­ essary. Cleaning of Carpets

### Concept

Vacuum clean the carpet regularly to re­ move dirt. Dirt will make the carpet wear out faster. Periodically, shampoo the car­ pet to keep it looking new.

### Concept

Use carpet cleaners (preferably foam type). Follow the instructions that come with the cleaner. Apply it with a sponge or soft brush. Keep the carpeting as dry as possible by not adding water to the foam.

### Concept

Cleaning of Windows, Front and Rear Glasses

### Concept

Clean the windows inside and outside with commercially available glass cleaners.

### Concept

This will remove the haze that builds up on the inside of windows. Use a soft cloth or paper towels to clean all glass and plastic surfaces. Waxing

### Concept

### Concept

Polishes and cleaners can restore shine to the painted surface that has oxidized and become dull. They normally contain mild abrasives and solvents that remove the top layer of the finish coat. Polish your ve­ hicle, if the finish does not regain its origi­ nal shine after using wax. Interior Fabric Cleaning Tips

### Concept

Stains should be treated immediately. 1. If left for a long time, they can leave a permanent mark.

### Concept

### Concept

Stain should not be removed by rub­ 3. bing. As far as possible, try to blot or lift the stain with cloth or plastic spatula and then clean the remaining stain with cloth or sponge.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Warning

 If heavy vibrations, unsteady steer- ing behavior or noises should oc- cur while driving, reduce your speed and drive with caution to a place where it is safe for you to stop the vehicle. Recheck the tyre and its pressure. If the tyre pres- sure is less than 130kPa (1.3bar, 19 psi) or if there are any visible cracks, bumps or similar damage on the side wall, do not continue to use the tyre.  After using the sealant you may drive no faster than 80 km/h and the damaged tyre must be re- placed as quickly as possible (within a maximum driving distance of 200 km.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p274_img00` (page 274, confidence 0.989)

### Procedure

 Remove the puncture repair kit from the luggage area.  Insert the power plug into the 12V power socket connection and start the vehicle in idling. 

### Procedure

Remove the plug from the tyre valve and screw the inflator hose into the tyre valve Press the switch to “I” present on the inflator and the motor will start to in- flate.

### Procedure

 As specified pressure is achieved then switch to “0” present on the inflator and compressor will turn off.  Check the tyre pressure again. If tyre pressure is too high, deflate the tyre to the specified pressure using the pres- sure “air release” valve.

### Concept

 Remove the inflator hose from the tyre valve and plug the tyre valve safely.

### Specification

 Remove the power plug 12V from the power socket and assemble it properly and keep the unit in luggage space again for next use.

Remember that emergency road-side tyre repair kits only provide temporary mobility. You should consult a tyre specialist for advice.

title: PRO- ELECTRONIC STABILITY GRAM (ESP) (if equipped)
text:
# PRO- ELECTRONIC STABILITY GRAM (ESP) (if equipped)

## Knowledge

### Concept

ELECTRONIC BRAKE FORCE DIS- TRIBUTION (EBD)

### Concept

EBD monitors and controls

### Concept

the brake pressure on the rear wheels to improve driv- ing stability while braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p32_img00` (page 32, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p32_img00.png`

### Concept

EBD provides optimal braking pressure distribution between front and rear wheels to optimize braking distance and to ensure vehicle stability by means of lowering braking pressure increase at rear wheels.

### Concept

ESP monitors driving sta-

### Concept

bility and traction. If ESP detects that the vehicle is deviating from the direc- tion desired by the driver, one or more wheels are braked to stabilize the vehicle. The engine output is also modified to keep the vehicle on the desired course within physical limits. ESP assists the driver when pulling away on wet or slippery roads. ESP can also stabilize the vehicle during braking and acceleration.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p32_img02` (page 32, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p32_img02.png`

### Concept

Cornering Stability Control (CSC)

### Concept

Corner stability Control supports / stabi- lizes vehicle during partial braking on curves by reducing pressure at required inner wheel of the vehicle.

### Concept

This helps to reduce probability of vehicle over steering during cornering.

### Concept

Based on wheel speed information off road ABS helps to avoid wheel lock on un- even surfaces like loose gravel, pot holes

### Concept

by reducing the stopping distance com- pared to standard ABS.

### Concept

Electronic Traction Control (ETC)

### Concept

The Electronic Traction Control system function (ETC) is designed as a slip control system to prevent the driven wheels of a vehicle from excessive wheel slip.

### Concept

Roll Over Mitigation (ROM)

### Concept

The main feature of the Roll over Mitiga- tion function is the detection of a rollover critical situation and to prevent the vehicle rollover. This is done by active brake inter- ventions on selected wheels, thereby re- ducing the forces that cause a roll-over situation.

### Concept

Brake Disc Wiping (BDW)

### Concept

Water on the brake disc leads to a delay in brake response time. The purpose of the function Brake Disc wiping is to re- move moisture when driving in wet condi- tions automatically. To get quick response form Brake and better deceleration.

### Concept

Electronic Brake Pre-fill (EBP)

### Concept

The Electronic Brake Prefill (EBP) function reduces the air gap of the brake pad and

### Concept

• If EBD is malfunctioning, the rear wheels can lock, e.g. under full braking. This increases the risk of skidding and an accident.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p32_img01` (page 32, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p32_img01.png`

### Concept

• You should therefore adapt your driving style to the different handling characteristics. Have the brake sys- tem checked immediately at a TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Cen- tre as soon as possible.

### Concept

Dynamic Wheel Torque by Brake (DWT- B)

### Concept

The main goal of the function is to improve the agility of a vehicle and to enable a more direct steering. This is mainly achieved by braking interventions at the inner wheels during turning. DWT-B re- duces understeer tendency of the car and a higher curve speed can be achieved.

### Concept

Engine Drag Torque Control (EDTC)

### Concept

On slippery road conditions during in- gear Braking or Shift down of gear or sudden throttle release on a curve road.

### Concept

This causes high Engine drag on the driven wheel resulting into brake slip situ- ations without any brake application.

### Concept

This makes vehicle highly under steerable. EDTC controls such brake slip on the driven wheels by increasing the engine torque to makes the vehicle stable and steerable.

### Concept

Hill Hold Control (HHC)

### Concept

Hill Hold Control is a comfort function. The main intend is to prevent the vehicle from rolling backwards while driving off up-hill

### Concept

on an inclined surface.

### Concept

Driver Doze Off Alert (DDOA) (if equip-

### Concept

• Many road accidents are due to micro sleep activity of the driver.

### Concept

• Driver Doze Off Alert feature monitors the behavior of the driver on a contin- uous basis & detects patterns of a drowsy driver

### Warning

• In case drowsiness is detected, audio/visual warning would be dis- played on the instrument panel cluster.

### Concept

• Driver steering behavior along with the overall trip duration, time of the day, drive monotony are considered to de- tect a sleepy driver.

### Warning

• The function helps in accident reduc- tion by giving prompt warning to the driver to stay alert or take a break.

### Concept

• The function will reset once there is a driver change detected or sufficient break time has elapsed.

### Concept

• No additional H/W such as driver fac- ing camera is required.

### Concept

the brake disc. The function is triggered after a sudden release of the accelerator pedal due to an unexpected emergency brake situation. By actively pre-filling the brake-system the brake response time is reduced and results in a shorter stopping distance.

### Concept

Hydraulic Brake Assist (HBA)

### Concept

In a dangerous emergency situation, most drivers don’t use the full available perform- ance of the brake system, because they brake too soft. The HBA function detects the critical situation and builds up addi- tional brake pressure to reduce the brak- ing distance.

### Concept

Hydraulic Fading Compensation (HFC)

### Concept

In dangerous fading situations most driv- ers operate the brake pedal with a small or regular braking force and they never reach to the maximum possible vehicle de- celeration. The HFC function improve the stopping distance by eliminating required pressure build-up lag by the driver.

### Concept

Panic Brake Alert (PBA) (if equipped)

### Warning

• Panic brake alert warns surrounding vehicles when emergency or heavy braking takes place. The function will trigger Hazard lamps automatically, which will act as an immediate warning to vehicles directly behind and nearby.

### Concept

• PBA is an immediate and urgent warn- ing to all vehicles around thus improv- ing their response time to unforeseen braking situations

### Warning

• PBA can help reduce accidents through effective warning to surround- ing traffic during emergency Braking

### Concept

• With PBA, surrounding drivers and ve- hicles have more time to respond against slowdown vehicles

### Concept

• Reducing the amount and degree of injuries caused by rear end collisions that occur during heavy braking.

### Warning

• PBA provides additional warning to im- prove road safety.

### Concept

After Impact Braking (AIB) (if equipped)

### Concept

• In the event of primary collision there are chances that vehicle can no longer be safely controlled. Accident analysis has shown that an active brake inter- vention would mitigate the effect of the subsequent collisions.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p34_img00` (page 34, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p34_img00.png`

### Concept

• After impact braking system is acti- vated automatically and brakes the car in a safe manner to mitigate secondary collision.

### Warning

• Hazard & brake lights are triggered to intimate surrounding users of an emer- gency situation. Warning lights will

### Concept

continue flashing after vehicle comes to a standstill.

### Concept

• In case vehicle is fitted with Automated Parking Brake, it will be auto engaged.

### Concept

• The driver can override the system by depressing the brake/acc pedal if there is a risk of being hit by following traffic.

### Concept

• The basic assumption is that the brake system is intact after the primary im- pact.

### Concept

• Mitigate impact/severity of subsequent collisions.

text:
# POWER OPERATED TAILGATE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Option - IV (Mechanical/Service Tail­ gate Opening)

### Concept

Incase if Tailgate got stuck and is unable to operate. Owner needs to contact the near by authorized service center or get in contact with the customer support.

### Concept

Closing the Tailgate

### Concept

Pull down the tailgate slowly and Push it to Close. Make sure that the Tailgate is se­ curely locked.

### Procedure

The Power Operated Tailgate has capabil­ ity to automatically open and close when the trigger is provided by the user. It con­ sist of a motor which will drive the tailgate to open or close. A hazard flashes and buzzer indicate the customer while open­ ing and closing of power tailgate.

### Procedure

To open, close or stop the tailgate auto­ matically one of the triggers from the fol­ lowing will be used

### Concept

PEPS UID (Key fob) 1.

### Concept

PEPS Tailgate Switch 2.

### Concept

Tailgate Fascia Switch 3.

### Concept

Tail gate Kick Sensor [hands free ac­ 4. cess]

### Concept

Tailgate Closure Switch (Inside Tail­ 5. gate, Close Only)

### Concept

Tail gate can’t be locked using mechan­ ical key/ flip key/ smart key. It can be locked by slamming it.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p48_img00` (page 48, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p48_img00.png`

### Procedure

To open and close tailgate press the 1. button. If button is long pressed for 3 seconds then the tailgate will open or close. To open/close the tailgate with this method vehicle is required to be in standby, accessory delay or awake mode.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p49_img00` (page 49, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p49_img00.png`

### Procedure

To stop the tailgate while opening and 2. closing is in progress, short press tail­ gate button. Automatic tailgate will stop in open or close position and will work only when PEPS key is near to vehicle vicinity and this feature is enabled from

### Concept

infotainment. 2. PEPS Tailgate Switch (Outside Tail- gate) (if equipped)

### Procedure

To open and close tailgate, press the 1. outside tailgate switch. To open /close the tailgate with this method vehicle is required to be in standby, accessory delay or awake, ignition or run (vehicle speed is less than 5 kmph) vehicle condition.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p49_img01` (page 49, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p49_img01.png`

### Procedure

To stop the tailgate while opening and 2. closing is in progress, press outside tailgate switch. Automatic tailgate will stop in open or close position and will

### Concept

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Warning

Gauge Information Note/Warning

### Warning

When fuel in the tank is near to empty position, low fuel warning telltale turns Amber. Refill the tank as soon as possible. At every key in and Ignition ON, Fuel Gauge Bar move to F and come back to E position. This is wel­ come strategy.

### Concept

earlier or delayed than usual.

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in “ON” position, this • gauge gives an approximate indication of the amount of fuel in the fuel tank and it takes few seconds to stabilize after the ignition is turned ON.

### Warning

WARNING: When Cluster detect Low Fuel level, It blinks last fuel bar with 1Hz frequency and Fuel tank symbol is con­ tinue ON state. If there is any fault in the system, Low fuel warning symbol shall blink. Take your vehicle to the nearest TATA MOTORS authorized service station.

### Warning

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” position, this gauge indicates the engine coolant temperature. The indicator should be within normal, acceptable temperature range i.e., between “H” and “C”. If the indicator approaches “H”, overheating is indicated by red LED bar in case of 4”. The RED bar and High Coolant temp warning telltale indicates overheating that may damage the engine. Continuing to drive the vehicle when engine over­ heating is indicated can result in severe engine dam­ age or fire.

### Concept

If the coolant temperature reading is very high, • The Engine coolant temperature telltale flashes with an audible buzzer.

### Concept

In this case, stop the vehicle, switch ‘OFF’ the • engine and cool it down for some time. Contact a nearest TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre immediately for rectification.

### Note

Note : At every key in and Ignition ON, Temperature Gauge moves to H and returns to C position for 10” Cluster.

title: MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES
text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Warning

due to specific driving conditions. This in­ cludes prolonged driving at low vehicle speeds for considerable amount of time (driving in heavy city traffic), prolonged running of the engine in idle conditions etc. In such cases, a warning lamp as indi­ cated above will be illuminated in the in­ strument cluster indicating that soot regeneration is insufficient.

### Warning

This warning lamp switches ON constantly to indicate that the DPF needs to be re­ generated. This lamp does not indicate any malfunction.

### Warning

The warning lamp remains OFF during normal vehicle behavior and lights up only when driving condition requires the driver to be notified. When this lamp is ON, keep the car running ideally at 3 rd gear, 60km/hr with engine speed over 2000 rpm until re­ generation is completed and warning lamp goes OFF. The process normally takes about 20 minutes.

### Warning

If DPF regeneration process requested above is not fol­ lowed for a long distance and the vehicle is driven with warning lamp ON, it can cause MIL to be turned ON.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p318_img01` (page 318, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p318_img01.png`

### Concept

Once MIL is ON, please contact nearest TATA MOTORS authorized service center.

### Concept

Service should connect the TATA MO­ TORS diagnostic tool and conduct DPF service regeneration as indicated in the di­ agnostic tool.

### Concept

Insufficient DPF regeneration resulting in the above lamps can also happen if the vehicle is driven with adultered diesel.

### Specification

The lamp blinks constantly to indicate that the DPF needs to eliminate the trapped pollu­ tants (particulate matter) through the re­ generation process, it therefore does not indicate a malfunction. The lamp remains off during the entire DPF regeneration and it lamps up only when driving conditions require the driver to be notified. To switch off the lamp, keep the car running until re­ generation is complete (ideally at 3 rd gear, 60 kmph with engine speed over 2000 rpm). The process normally takes about 20 minutes.

### Warning

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Whenever the vehicle is to be parked, Press the Park (P) button on the gear shifter, as well as apply the parking brake.

### Concept

The gear shifter must be engaged in Park (P) position only when the vehicle is sta­ tionary. Do not engage Parking Position (P) in running condition. If engaged while the vehicle is in motion it may severely damage the transmission.

### Concept

Before leaving the driver’s seat, always make sure the shifter is in the P (Park) po­ sition; then apply parking brake fully and shut the engine off. If this is not followed, Unexpected and sudden vehicle move­ ment can occur.

### Concept

Shift from P to any gear R/N/D is possible only with foot brake & plunger is pressed on the selector lever.

### Concept

This position puts the transmission in re­ verse gear when engaged in stationary condition with Plunger press on the selec­

### Concept

tor lever & foot brake pedal is fully pressed and selector lever movement in upward di­ rection. The selector lever shall never be moved into reverse while driving forward.

### Concept

To put the transmission in Neutral position from R or D foot brake & plunger press on the selector lever is required. It enables the engine to start and operate without driving the vehicle.

### Concept

This position is for normal driving condi­ tions for maximum efficiency and fuel economy. To move to Drive position the selector lever should be moved to down­ ward direction. Ensure the Plunger is pressed on the selector lever to Shift the gear from D to N. Also to Shift from D to R with foot brake & plunger press on the se­ lector lever are required.

### Concept

Transmission Control Unit may dis­ • allow incorrect manual shift com­ mand by user and a message ‘Driver Control Shift denied’ is dis­ played on Instrument Cluster.

### Concept

The first few shifts on a new vehicle, • maybe somewhat abrupt after TCU replacement or software updation. This is normal condition. Shifting se­ quence will get adjusted after few shift cycle by TCU (Transmission Control Unit).

### Warning

In the event that the transmission • develops a fault, a warning mes­ sage may be displayed on the In­ strument cluster & only limited gears may become available. You should seek qualified assistance immedi

### Concept

Procedure for filling DEF in DEF tank

### Concept

• Ensure vehicle is parked in plain sur- face in no load condition (vehicle sh- ould be empty without passengers or luggage)

### Concept

• Ensure ignition is in OFF position (remove key from barrel, if provided)

### Concept

• Wait for 6 minutes after ignition OFF.

### Concept

• Fill DEF as required. Total DEF Qu- antity inside the DEF tank should never be more than 15 litres. Only TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre will be able to correctly dete- rmine the quantity of DEF available inside the tank.

### Warning

Low DEF Level Warning Messages

### Concept

These messages will be indicated when DEF level is low. This can happen when vehicle runs without filling DEF in spite of message to fill DEF.

### Warning

• First warning message will be indi- cated at approximately in between 1500 – 2400 km before emptying of DEF tank at the current DEF consump- tion rate. “DEF LEVEL LOW, REFILL SOON” message will be indicated at this warning level.

### Warning

• If “DEF level low, Refill Soon “Warning message appears in the cluster, it indi- cates that DEF needs to be topped up. In case you are refilling the DEF you- rself, fill only maximum 7.0 litres • Wait for 6 minutes after filling DEF. • Turn ON the ignition and wait till DEF level gets updated in instrument clus- ter. Start the vehicle. • If still problem persist contact nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre immediately.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p324_img02` (page 324, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p324_img02.png`

### Concept

1. In absence of DEF level low warni- ng, refilling is not recommended. 2. Do not overfill the DEF/urea, over- filling may result in system/compo- nent failure.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

STEERING LOCK AND IGNITION SWITCH (if equipped)

### Concept

The ignition switch has the following four positions:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p229_img02` (page 229, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p229_img02.png`

### Concept

LOCK - This is the normal parking posi­ tion. Key from lock can be removed in this position only.

### Concept

“LOCK” position prevents normal use of the steering wheel after the key is re­ moved.

### Procedure

To release the steering lock, insert the key and turn it clockwise to one of the other positions.

### Concept

ACC - Accessories such as the infotain­ ment system can be operated, but the en­ gine remains ‘OFF’. Steering gets unlocked.

### Concept

ON - This is the normal operating position. All electrical systems are ‘ON’.

### Concept

START - Turn the key further clockwise to the START position, (spring loaded) to start the engine. As soon as the engine starts, release the ignition key, which re­ turns to ON position. While cranking, all accessories will be momentarily ‘OFF’. Illuminated Key Ring (if equipped)

### Concept

When the vehicle is unlocked, the illumi­ nated key ring glows up. This helps to lo­ cate ignition switch in the dark.

### Concept

When adjusting the steering wheel, make sure that:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p229_img00` (page 229, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p229_img00.png`

### Concept

You can operate control pedals • without any obstacles.

### Concept

You can see all the displays in the • instrument cluster clearly.

### Concept

Before starting off, make sure that • the steering wheel position is locked.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p229_img01` (page 229, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p229_img01.png`

### Concept

Never unlock or adjust the steering • wheel while the vehicle is in motion.

### Concept

A key is an electronic access and authori­ zation system which is provided as a stan­ dard feature on your vehicle. Unlocking Principle

### Concept

The transponder which is built into the ig­ nition key carries a unique identification code. The vehicle unlocks when the code on the key matches with the code on the Engine Management System (EMS). In case of PEPS variant, Immobilizer function is provided by PEPS. Engine Starting

### Concept

When the key is inserted and the ignition is switched ‘ON’, all codes are communi­ cated within key, Immobilizer and EMS. The engine will start only if all the codes match. Loss of Keys

### Concept

If one of the key is lost, contact your near­ est TATA MOTORS authorized dealer im­ mediately.

### Concept

Do not turn ‘ON’ ignition switch by • using key with any type of metal wound around its grip or in contact with it. This may be detected as ab­ normal condition by immobilizer and prevent engine from starting.

the Immobilizer indicator lamp on the instrument cluster is glowing. In this condition the vehicle will not start and the vehicle’s battery will also be drained due to frequent cranking.

To switch ‘OFF’ the approach lights, press and release the same button or it automatically turns ‘OFF’ after certain time. Tail Gate Opening

### Procedure

To open the Tail gate press the button (3) once on the smart key, Tail gate will un­ latch. Please refer section starting and driving for more information. Unlocking all Doors

Slot is provided below driver door han­ • dle.

### Concept

By pressing any button of smart key, Force panic operation gets deactivated. Vehicle Search

### Concept

In vehicle locked condition, if lock button on smart key is pressed, the turn indica­ tors of vehicle flashes 4 times. Automatic Activation Of Immobilizer

### Concept

If smart key is not found within the passen­ ger compartment, engine will be immobi­ lized and vehicle cannot start. Auto Locking / Unlocking Of Doors / Auto Relock

In PEPS variants, door will get unlocked when ignition is OFF by pressing Start Stop switch.

Anti-grab / Anti-scan Coding

### Concept

### Concept

Don’t operate Unlock button of remote • in the vicinity of your vehicle, as it could lead to an unintentional unlock­ ing your vehicle.

### Concept

For battery, replacement procedure • refer ‘MAINTENANCE’ section.

### Concept

Do not remove the battery connection • of the vehicle while the vehicle has been locked by remote. Smart Key Precautions

### Concept

If smart key is close to radio transmitter 1. such as radio station or an airport which can interfere with normal opera­ tion of the transmitter.

### Concept

### Concept

If another vehicle’s smart key is being 3.

operated close to your vehicle, signal will fluctuate.

### Concept

when all doors are closed and the ve­ hicle speed crosses 10 kmph.

When key is taken out all the doors get • automatically unlocked.

### Concept

The remote control set of this security sys­ tem is protected against the use of devices called ‘scanners’ and ‘grabbers’ which can record and reproduce some types of re­ mote codes.

### Concept

In case any button of the key is acciden­ tally pressed for more than 20 seconds, the remote stops functioning till the time the button is pressed. The LED on the Remote also stops glowing. The func­ tion of the remote gets reinstated imme­ diately when the user stops pressing

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Please ensure that the phone is com­ 1. patible to the charging standard “Qi”.

### Warning

If there is any metallic object between 2. smartphone and wireless charger pad, immediately remove smart phone and metallic object after it has completely cooled down. Once any metallic object is detected on wireless charger post charging it displays its warning mes­ sage on Infotainment unit, first remove smart phone then remove foreign ob­ ject from the charging pad and place the smart phone again on charging pad.

### Concept

In case of water/Liquid spillage on 3.

### Concept

charging pad, dry out the pad surface area properly & clean the ECU surface area by removing Anti-skid mat. Do not charge the smart phone until surface is completely dry.

### Concept

The Phone charging status is informa­ 4. tion by phone and not charger.

### Concept

Wireless charger works on principle of 5. magnetic induction, i.e. it converts electrical energy into magnetic energy to transfer energy from charging pad to phone. Please maintain safe distance from the charger most of the time as it may cause irritation to sensory organs or active implants if implemented in the body. Please consult medical specialist in case implant organ in the body of the user.

### Concept

Place the smart phone on the center of 6. the charging pad for effective charging with best results (refer Figure 1).

### Concept

It is recommended to turn on Engine 7. while charging phone on wireless charger to avoid vehicle battery drain.

### Concept

User shall clean charging pad/mat pe­ 8. riodically to avoid dust accumulation.

### Concept

It is recommended to keep Vehicle AC 9. at least 23 Deg Cel with Fan speed above 2 level as cool environment sup­ port efficient charging of the phone.

### Concept

It is recommended to keep mobile 10. phone at center of charging pad for ef­ fective charging. In case small phone kept at corner do not start charging or foreign object detection message pop- up, please move phone to center of pad.

### Concept

Always use TATA MOTORS PASSEN­ 11. GER VEHICLES LIMITED approved charging pad for efficient charging.

### Specification

Do not use metallic smart phone cov­ 1. ers as it would halt the wireless charg­ ing function. The wireless charging may not function properly when there is a heavy & thick (more than 1 mm thick) accessory cover on the smart phone.

### Concept

Do not place smart phone up-side 2. down (screen face) on charging pad or do not misalign mobile phone on charging pad in such case smartphone

### Concept

1. If any metallic object such as coin/keys are located between wireless charging pad and phone back cover, the charging may get disrupted. Also, this may results in heat up of metallic objects.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_003/p144_img00.png`

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

To start off, press the clutch pedal fully and shift into first gear.

### Concept

After releasing the parking brake, gradu­ ally release the clutch and slowly press the accelerator.

### Concept

Turn the key to ‘ACC’ position to switch off the engine. Before switching off the en­ gine, run the engine in idle condition for at least 30 seconds and then switch off. This will allow the engine oil to lubricate the tur­ bocharger, till its speed is fully reduced and also allow the unit to cool down.

### Concept

Gear Shifting and Driving

### Concept

The gearshift pattern is as shown on the gear lever knob. Gear shifting should al­ ways be done with clutch pedal pressed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p233_img04` (page 233, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p233_img04.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p233_img05` (page 233, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p233_img05.png`

### Concept

tion & wait for 30 secs.

### Concept

The vehicle emits poisonous exhaust gases such as carbon monoxide. Inhal­ ing these exhaust gases leads to poi­ soning. There is a risk of fatal injury. Therefore, Never leave the vehicle run­ ning in enclosed spaces without suffi­ cient ventilation.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p233_img00` (page 233, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p233_img00.png`

### Concept

After starting, run the engine in idle speed for at least 30 seconds. Do not press accelerated pedal while starting the engine to avoid damage to tur­ bocharger.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p233_img01` (page 233, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p233_img01.png`

### Concept

When shifting or starting off, do not race the engine. Racing the engine can shorten engine life and affect smooth shifting.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p233_img02` (page 233, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p233_img02.png`

### Concept

A quick burst on the accelerator be­ • fore turning off the engine serves no practical purpose, it wastes fuel and can damage turbocharger.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p233_img03` (page 233, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p233_img03.png`

### Concept

Do not switch off the engine when it • is running at high speed. This will lead to premature turbocharger bearing wear.

### Concept

Gear recommendation is displayed • when the clutch pedal is in fully re­ leased position.

### Concept

If “F” is displayed in DIS of instru­ • ment cluster, it means ‘Fault’ condi­ tion. Contact a TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

This behavior is absolutely normal, the oil change is intended to keep your engine at peak efficiency, and replacing used oil with fresh oil is normal maintenance and not a malfunction.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p308_img04` (page 308, confidence 0.955)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p308_img04.png`

### Concept

As soon as this lamp is blinking, the oil should be changed as per oil change / servicing procedure. Please contact near­ est TATA MOTORS authorized service center immediately.

### Concept

Once the oil is changed as per the normal oil change / servicing procedure, the oil quality should be reset using TATA MO­ TORS diagnostic tool. The vehicle should never be run again after an oil change without resetting oil quality using TATA MOTORS diagnostic tool.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p308_img01` (page 308, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p308_img01.png`

### Concept

If the vehicle is continuously driven ignor­

### Concept

ing this lamp, MIL, in addition to the above lamp, will be turned ON. Depending on the distance driven without oil change and oil quality reset, the engine will go into a soft or strong performance reduction mode.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p308_img02` (page 308, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p308_img02.png`

### Concept

Brake/clutch Fluid Level

### Concept

Pull the notch and release the top cover.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p308_img03` (page 308, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p308_img03.png`

Under no circumstances oil change • intervals should exceed 15,000 km or 12 Months, whichever occurs earlier.

### Warning

The appearance of this blinking warning light or symbol is not related to the amount of oil in the engine, so if the light or symbol comes ON and blinking, never add / top up engine oil but contact the nearest TATA MOTORS authori s ed service cent re to have oil change and reset.

### Concept

Regularly clean the sensors and keep 1. them free from dust, ice, mud, water, chewing gum etc. for proper working of the system. Use a smooth cloth for cleaning.

### Concept

Do not use water at high pressure for 2. cleaning the sensor.

### Concept

Do not cover the sensors. This will in­ 3. terrupt park assist performance.

### Concept

Do not remove mud, snow on the sen­ 4. sors using stick or hard material. Use normal water and soft cloth. Park Assist Malfunction Indications

### Concept

### Concept

Reason for this fault may be

### Concept

Body Control Module Failure 1.

### Concept

### Concept

Partner components such as Infotain­ 3. ment music system, Instrument Clus­ ter failure

### Concept

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

ON BOARD DIAGNOSTIC (OBD II) SYSTEM

### Concept

Diagnostic connector is located on RH side below the steering wheel.

### Concept

On board Diagnostics or OBD, is an auto­ motive term referring to a vehicle’s self-di­ agnostic and reporting capability. The OBD system allows continuous diagnosis of the components of the vehicle corre­ lated with emissions. This system warns the driver, by turning “ON” the Malfunction Indication lamp (MIL) on the instrument cluster, when a fault causes emission lev­ els to increase.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p317_img00` (page 317, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p317_img00.png`

### Concept

The OBD system also has a diagnostic connector that can be interfaced with ap­ propriate diagnostic tools, which makes it possible to read the fault codes stored in the Electronic Control Unit, together with a series of specific parameters for Engine operation and Diagnosis. This check can also be carried out by the traffic police.

### Concept

DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER (DPF)

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF). DPF is a mechanical filter that physically traps particulate matter from diesel engine exhaust gas.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p317_img01` (page 317, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p317_img01.png`

### Concept

DPF traps the particulate matter in the fol­ lowing way:

### Concept

Filtration - Particulates / soot are col­ • lected in the inlet channel of the filter.

### Concept

Regeneration - When the filter chan­ • nels are filled up with soot, they are cleaned automatically by the engine management system. This process is known as DPF Regeneration and this will happen during normal running of the vehicle.

### Concept

DPF equipped in vehicle normally regen­ erates automatically which is controlled by engine management system.

### Concept

In certain specific driving conditions, DPF regeneration may not happen automati­ cally as the desired temperatures required to regenerate soot may not be achievable

# ANTI-THEFT DEVICE IMMOBILIZER/PEPS

## Knowledge

### Concept

Immobilizer system is designed to prevent vehicle theft by elec- tronically disabling the engine ignition system. The engine can be started only with vehicle’s original Immobilizer ignition key which has an electronic identification programmed code.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p30_img00` (page 30, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p30_img00.png`

### Note

Use only Flip key, the other should be kept in a safe location. Note down “key Tag no.” information (and keep it safe) which is required while getting new/spare keys. Remember that it is not possible to prepare new/spare keys without the “key Tag number.” Take precaution about Flip key, as without Flip key vehicle cannot be started.

### Concept

Immobilizer Lamp Status

### Concept

Meaning / Func- tion of the State

### Concept

Ignition OFF Blinking Locked

### Concept

Vehicle Immobi- lized and awaiting electronic key

### Concept

Ignition ON OFF Unlocked

### Concept

Normal condition and ready to start the vehicle

### Concept

Ignition ON ON Locked

### Concept

Problem with key (Wrong key used to start vehicle)

### Concept

Problem with Immobilizer system. Con- tact a TATA MOTORS Au- thorized Serv- ice Centre.

### Concept

Ignition ON Blinking Unlocked

### Concept

Contact a TATA MOTORS Author- ized Service Cen- tre immediately.

## Tables

### Table 1

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ignition ON | OFF | Unlocked | Normal condition and ready to start the vehicle |

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Climbing Sharp Gradients on Loose Surfaces

### Concept

Start off smoothly in a suitable gear. Accel­ erate smoothly so that there is no loss of traction by over-revving of the engine.

### Concept

Choose a slope as smooth as possible and select the appropriate gear so that gear changing in the middle of the climb is not required.

### Concept

Changing gears in the middle of the climb can cause loss of momentum and engine stalling. Shifting to lower gear has to be done cautiously to avoid loss of traction.

### Concept

Under no conditions should the vehicle be moved diagonally across a hill. The dan­ ger is in loss of traction and sideways slip­ page, possibly resulting in toppling over. If unavoidable, choose as mild an angle as possible and keep the vehicle moving.

### Concept

If the wheels start to slip within few feet of the end of the climb, motion can be main­ tained by swinging the steered wheels left and right, thereby providing increased grip.

### Concept

If the vehicle stalls or losses headway

### Concept

while climbing a steep hill, make a quick shift to reverse and allow the vehicle to move back with the control of engine com­ pression. Descending Sharp Gradients

### Concept

Depending on the severity of the gradient, shift into appropriate gear. Use engine braking judiciously without over-revving the engine.

### Concept

Brake application under such situations should be done very.

### Concept

Your vehicle has power assisted brakes.

### Concept

The distance needed to bring the vehicle to a halt increases with the speed of the vehicle. Start applying brake anticipating the distance and slow down gradually.

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a de­ layed reaction from the brakes when brak­ ing for the first time. This may also occur after the vehicle has been washed.

### Concept

Brake performance may become poor and

### Concept

When descending on sharp gradients, NEVER turn the ignition key to the ‘OFF’ position. Emission control system damage may result.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p238_img00` (page 238, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p238_img00.png`

Never use the brake pedal as a • footrest.

#### Visual References

### Concept

If you rest your foot on the brake • pedal while driving, the braking sys­ tem can overheat. This increases the stopping distance and can even cause the braking system to fail. There is a risk of an accident.

### Concept

Never press the brake pedal and • the accelerator pedal at the same time.

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

ADVANCED DRIVER ASSISTANCE SYSTEMS (ADAS) (if equipped)

### Concept

The Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) provides the alerts and controls to improve the overall safety of vehicle and increases the driver comfort.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p162_img00` (page 162, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p162_img00.png`

### Concept

Limitations of Advanced Driver Assis­ tance System

### Concept

There might be degraded/no/unexpected functionality of ADAS for following cases:

### Concept

There is adverse environmental condi­ • tions such as heavy snow, heavy rain, etc.

### Concept

The ADAS sensors are • covered/blocked with snow, dirt, mud, etc.

### Concept

There is splash on ADAS sensors due • to water logging on the road.

### Concept

The temperature around the ADAS • sensors is too high or too low.

### Concept

A trailer, carrier or other attachment is • installed in your vehicle.

### Concept

The bumper around the radars is cov­ • ered with objects such as a stickers, guards, paint, bike rack etc.

### Concept

The area around the radars is im­ • pacted, damaged or the radars are out

### Concept

Windshield area around the ADAS • camera is damaged or camera is out of position.

### Concept

Your vehicle height is low due to heavy • loads, abnormal tyre pressure (tyre pressure is low, uneven) or a tyre is damaged, etc.

### Concept

The road contains multiple metallic • components (for example, metallic bridges, metal construction poles etc).

### Concept

The vehicle drives on a curved road. •

### Concept

The vehicle severely vibrates while • driving on bumpy/uneven paths.

### Concept

When the ADAS sensors are blocked • by other vehicles, walls or parking-lot pillars.

### Concept

The vehicle is driven through a toll­ • gate.

### Concept

Driving on a road where trees or grass • are overgrown.

### Concept

Driving in areas where the sensor does • not detect another vehicle or structure (like bullock cart, horse cart etc) for an extended period of time.

### Concept

ADAS is only an aid system, it is • NOT a substitute for the driver’s at­ tention. The driver must always re­ main in control of the vehicle, observe the surroundings and drive safely.

### Concept

ADAS system is assist system for • driver for comfort driving. The driver should observe surroundings envi­ ronment obstacles in vehicle path and judge distance of vehicle from obstacle and apply enough braking. Driver should also observe traffic signs on road, lane marking always and act accordingly.

### Concept

The correct operation of the ADAS • sensors will be compromised if they

### Concept

are misaligned due to accident dam­ age at the windshield/bumper area of the vehicle.

title: ENVIRONMENT PROTECTION
text:
# ENVIRONMENT PROTECTION

## Knowledge

### Concept

TATA MOTORS PASSENGER VEHICLE LIMITED is committed to produce vehicles using environmentally sustainable technol­ ogy. A number of features have been incorporated in TATA MO­ TORS passenger vehicles which have been designed to ensure environmental compatibility throughout the life cycle of the vehi­ cle. We would like to inform you that your vehicle meets emission norms and this is being regularly validated at the manufacturing stages.

### Concept

As a user you too can protect the environment by operating your vehicle in a proactive manner. A lot depends on your driving style and the way you maintain your vehicle. We have given a few tips for your guidance. Driving

### Concept

Avoid frequent and violent acceleration. •

### Concept

Do not carry any unnecessary weight in the vehicle as it over­ • loads the engine. Avoid using devices requiring high power consumption during slow city traffic condition.

### Concept

Monitor the vehicle’s fuel consumption regularly and if show­ • ing rising trend get the car immediately attended at the Com­ pany’s Authorised Service Outlets.

### Concept

Switch off the engine during long stops at traffic jams or sig­ • nals. If you need to keep the engine running, avoid unneces­ sary revving it up or stopping and starting.

### Concept

It is not necessary to rev up the engine before turning it off as •

### Concept

it unnecessarily burns the fuel.

### Concept

Shift to higher gears as soon as possible. Use each gear upto • 2/3rd of maximum engine speed.

### Concept

A chart indicating gear shifting speeds is given in this book. • Maintenance

### Concept

Ensure that recommended maintenance is carried out on the • vehicle regularly at the Authorised Service Outlets.

### Concept

As soon as you see any leakages of oil or fuel in the vehicle • we recommend to get it attended immediately.

### Concept

Use only recommended grades and specified quantity of lu­ • bricants.

### Concept

Get your vehicle checked for emission periodically by an au­ • thorised dealer.

### Concept

Ensure that fuel filter, oil filter and breather are checked peri­ • odically and replaced, if required, as recommended by TATA MOTORS.

### Concept

Do not pour used oils or coolants into the sewage drains, gar­ • den soil or open streams. Dispose the used filters and batter­ ies in compliance with the current legislation.

### Concept

Do not allow unauthorized person to tamper with engine set­ • tings or to carry modifications on the vehicle.

### Concept

Never allow the vehicle to run out of fuel. •

### Concept

Parts like brake liners, clutch discs should be vacuum • cleaned. Do not use compressed air for cleaning these parts

### Concept

which may spread dust in the atmosphere.

### Concept

While carrying out servicing or repairs of your vehicle, you should pay keen attention to some of the important engine aggregates and wiring harness which greatly affect emis­ sion. These components are:

### Concept

Fuel injection equipment- pump, rail, injectors, nozzles and 1. high-pressure pipes.

### Concept

Air Intake & Exhaust system, especially for leakages. 2.

### Concept

Cylinder head for valve leakage. 3.

### Concept

All filters such as air, oil and fuel filters (check periodically). 4.

### Concept

EGR Valve & Cooler 6.

### Concept

Electrical connections. 8.

### Concept

If the ‘Check Engine lamp’, ‘MIL’ , ‘SCR’ or ‘DPF’ lamp contin­ 9. uously glows, please take the vehicle to a TATA MOTORS Au­ thorized Dealer/Service Center.

### Concept

Exhaust After Treatment System parts. 10.

### Concept

EMS wiring harness i.e. electrical connections to all sensors 11. and actuators.

### Concept

This Owner’s manual contains further information on driving pre­ cautions and maintenance care leading to environment protec­ tion. Please familiarize yourself with these aspects before driving.

### Concept

We WARRANT each TATA MOTORS PASSENGER VEHICLE and parts thereof manufactured by us to be free from defect in material and workmanship subject to the following terms and conditions:

### Concept

This warranty shall be for a period of 3 years from the date of sale of the car or a mileage of 1, 00,000 Kms whichever occurs 1. earlier .

### Concept

Our obligation under this warranty shall be limited to repairing or replacing, free of charge, such parts of the car which, in our 2. opinion, are defective, on the car being brought to us or to our dealers within the period. The parts so repaired or replaced shall also be warranted for quality and workmanship but such warranty shall be co-terminus with this original warranty.

### Concept

Any part which is found to be defective and is replaced by us under the warranty shall be our property. 3.

### Concept

## Knowledge

### Concept

Speedometer The Speedometer Indicates the actual vehicle speed in km/h

### Concept

### Concept

This is welcome strategy and self-check feature •

### Concept

Tachometer Tachometer indicates the engine speed in revolu­ tions per minute.

### Concept

Whenever engine is accelerated beyond safe • RPM, tachometer Bar Indication turns RED. In such case, reduce the engine RPM immediately.

### Concept

Never drive the vehicle with engine in high RPM. • This may cause severe engine damage.

title: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
text:
# TECHNICAL INFORMATION

## Knowledge

### Concept

Normal grade BS VI compliant diesel conforming to IS1460:2017 or equivalent is recommended to be used as fuel.

### Concept

Do not use premium diesel available in the market like extra pre­ mium / Turbojet etc.

### Concept

Recommended Fuel Specifications

### Concept

Parameter Unit BS VI Cetane Number (min) CN 51 Sulphur content mg/kg 10 Lubricity (HFRR) micron 460

### Concept

Never use alcohol or mix diesel with alcohol based fuels in­ cluding kerosene etc. It will damage the engine, fuel system and other related systems. If accidentally done so, do not start the vehicle. Contact TATA MOTORS dealer.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p337_img00` (page 337, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p337_img00.png`

### Concept

During cold weather conditions/freezing weather, diesel fuel thickens due to formation of paraffin layer. This results in diffi­ culty of engine starting as there will be interruption of fuel sup­ ply to engine.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p337_img01` (page 337, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p337_img01.png`

### Concept

It is advised to use locally available diesel fuel appropriate for the cold temperature conditions which are available at the fill­ ing stations during winter season. Please check with your fuel retailer for further details.

### Concept

It is recommended to maintain minimum of 10 liters of fuel in the fuel tank. Driving the vehicle till the fuel tank is empty is not advised. Always check fuel level before planning your journey.

- Image: `doc_003_p337_img02` (page 337, confidence 0.984)

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Lamp Condensation / Fogging Con­ dition

### Concept

Condensation is a natural phenomenon in Lamp. This occurs mainly because of at­ mospheric condition/weather change. Dur­ ing normal condensation, thin film of mist is visible on the inside surface of the exte­ rior lens. Generally, this condition is con­ sidered normal and will be eliminated by turning on the respective lamp with engine running or during normal driving condi­ tions. By doing this if the condensation has begun to clear after the drying time it indi­ cates that the lamp sealing has NOT been breached and will eventually clear. The lamp must NOT be replaced.

### Concept

High-pressure washer jet direct on • vent system of lamp are not recom­ mended, there might be possibility

### Concept

of water ingress causing for heavy fogging.
