# 7. Curtain Airbag LH

## Knowledge

### Concept

Supplementary Restraint System (SRS - Airbags)

### Concept

The SRS [Supplemental Restraint system] is designed to provide protection to occupants in case of collision or sudden impact, when crash is detected, the SRS airbag system deploys airbags to help reduce the risk of injury to the occupant. It works in conjunction with seat belts.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p17_img00` (page 17, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p17_img00.png`

### Concept

There are 7 airbags provided in your car:

### Concept

2. Driver Knee Airbag (if equipped)

### Concept

3. Front Passenger Airbag

### Concept

6. Curtain Airbag RH

### Concept

The driver airbag is mounted in the centre of the steering wheel. Driver Knee airbag (if equipped) is mounted behind the dash- board panel below steering wheel. The front passenger airbag is located inside the dashboard in front of the passenger seat. The airbags have suitable indications on steering wheel and on dash board.

### Concept

Side airbags are mounted in front row seats.

### Concept

Curtain airbags are mounted above the doors along the roof on both sides.

### Concept

The word ‘AIRBAG’ is marked at adjacent locations of respective airbags.

### Concept

The ‘SRS’ system also comprises of the following components depending upon the provided safety features in vehicle.

### Concept

• Seat belt Pre-tensioners

### Concept

• Seat belt with load limiters

### Concept

• Airbag ‘SRS’ ECU (Electronic Control Unit)

### Concept

• SRS wiring harness

### Concept

The System is active when ignition switch is in the “ON” position or the ignition mode is “ON”. Airbags are designed to inflate in collisions when required.

### Concept

In the event of a collision, the collision sen- sors will detect signals, and if the Airbag ECU judges that the signals represent a severe collision, will trigger the airbags. The inflated Airbags provide a cushion to the occupants. The Airbag inflates and de- flates so quickly that you may not even re- alize that it has activated. The Airbag will neither hinder your view nor make it hurdle

### Concept

to exit the vehicle.

### Concept

Airbag inflation is virtually instantaneous and occurs with considerable force, ac- companied by loud noise and smoke, which is normal. The inflated airbag, to- gether with seat belts, limit the movement of an occupant, thereby reducing the risk of injury.

### Concept

When an airbag inflates, you may see some smoke-like particles. The particles are a normal by-product of the process that generates the non-toxic gas used for airbag inflation. These airborne particles may irritate the skin, eyes, nose, or throat. If you have skin or eye irritation, rinse the area with water. For nose or throat irrita- tion, move to fresh air. Also sometimes the smoke can cause breathing problems, in such cases get fresh air promptly.

### Concept

After inflation, airbag provides a gradual cushioning effect for the occupant there- after deflates. It is not advisable to drive your vehicle after the airbags have been deployed. If you are involved in another collision, the airbags will not be in place to protect you.

### Concept

• Open your windows and doors as soon as possible after collision to re- duce prolonged exposure to the smoke and powder released by the inflating Airbag.

### Concept

• Even in vehicle with airbags, you and your passengers must always wear the seat belts provided. In order to minimize the risk and sever- ity of injury in the event of a collision.

### Concept

### Concept

This switch can be operated by using me- chanical key / Key with remote / smart key as per vehicle variants. Refer “Keys” sec- tion in this Manual.

### Warning

Airbag Warning Sticker on Front Pas- senger Sun Visor

### Warning

The Airbag Warning Symbol on sun visor reminds of the extreme hazards associ- ated with the use of a rearward-facing child restraint on front passenger seat dur- ing airbag deployment. It does not mean that a child cannot occupy front passenger seat and use seat belt. Please refer CRS section for recommended seating position for children.

If any of the following conditions occur, your SRS is malfunc- tioning: • The SRS warning lamp does not turn ‘ON’ when the ignition switch is placed in the ‘ON’ position for few seconds.

### Concept

• Never make any modifications to your vehicle. The modifications car- ried out, but not limited to the vehi- cle frame, bumpers, front fenders, ride height, suspension, seat belts, interior trims, steering wheel (espe- cially holders), are not acceptable. This will affect the intended perform- ance of SRS.

### Concept

• If you need to make any modifica- tions to accommodate any disability you may have, please contact your Authorized TATA MOTORS Dealer for necessary guidance.

### Concept

• Do not tamper with SRS in any way. This will lead to unexpected per- formance of system and may cause serious injury or death.

### Concept

Airbags Deployment Conditions

### Concept

When front airbags should not deploy?

### Concept

Minor frontal collision: Seat belt (if worn) offers adequate occupant protection in low severity collisions. The airbags are trig- gered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. Deployment of frontal airbags is not beneficial in low severity collisions.

### Concept

Side collision: During a side collision, oc- cupants tend to move sideways. There- fore, deploying frontal airbags in such situations will not benefit the occupants. Side airbags and side curtain airbags are specifically designed to reduce the injuries that can occur in side collision.

### Concept

Rear collision: During a rear collision, oc- cupants tend to move (rearwards) away from frontal airbags. Therefore, deploying

### Concept

frontal airbags in such situations will not protect the occupant. Head restraints and seat belts provide occupant protection dur- ing a rear collision.

### Concept

Rollovers collision: During a rollover col- lision, unbelted occupants may float inside the passenger compartment. This will in- crease the risk of injuries and may prove to be fatal. Wearing seat belts provide highly effective occupant protection during rollover collision. Front airbags, are not de- signed to deploy in a rollover as frontal airbags cannot offer any protection in rollover collision.

### Concept

When front airbags/side airbags/side curtain airbags may not deploy with minor or no visible vehicle damage?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. The extent of vehicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. In some extreme/rare condi- tions of rough road driving, running into a curb or hitting other fixed objects the airbags may deploy depending upon the severity of collision. In some of these con-

### Concept

ditions, damage to the vehicle may be minor or not be readily visible.

### Concept

When front airbags/side airbags/side curtain airbags may not deploy, even with exterior visible vehicle damage?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. The amount of visible vehicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. Some collisions can result in visible damage but with no airbag deployment, because the airbags would not have been needed or would not have provided protection even if they had deployed. Seat belts, if worn, offer ade- quate occupant protection in such cases. Children on Board

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Make sure that vehicle is completely • stationary before you attempt to shift in reverse gear.

### Concept

Drive slowly on wet roads. •

### Concept

You can get extra braking from the en­ • gine by shifting to a lower gear. This can help you to maintain a safe speed and prevent your brakes from over­ heating specially while going down a hill. Tips for Obtaining Better Fuel Effi­ ciency

### Concept

Always maintain the specified tyre • pressure during fuel top-ups and also before a long trip. Vehicle running with low tyre pressure will consume more fuel than the one running with specified tyre pressure.

### Concept

Keep the vehicle clean. Get rid of the • not in use luggage/stuff lying in the boot etc.

### Concept

Regularly inspect your vehicle for any • leakages, worn out wires, rat bites etc.

### Concept

Always follow periodic & regular serv­ •

### Concept

ice schedule of the vehicle.

### Concept

Drive smart and smooth in an anticipa­ • tory manner. Select driving mode to suit your style.

### Concept

Do not accelerate excessively when • you are in lower gears (1 st or 2 nd ). Be gentle on the accelerator when you are in traffic. In lower gear, opening more throttle will shoot the engine RPM keeping the vehicle still at lower speeds which indirectly implies less distance with more fuel.

### Concept

Be in the maximum possible higher • gear at a given speed. This reduces the engine operating speeds which means the engine is running at lower rpm (Revolutions per Minute) for the same vehicle speed. Lesser the num­ ber of engine revolution lesser the fuel burned.

### Concept

Avoid harsh braking. •

### Concept

Maintain healthy driving habits & while • decelerating, do coasting in gear and not in neutral or with clutch pedal pressed.

### Concept

Consider using the car AC when you •

### Concept

really require. Consider using lower blower speeds rather than higher for cooling as at higher blower speeds it consumes more electric power which is ultimately drawn from engine by burning fuel.

### Concept

Avoid unnecessary extra electrical • loading on the car.

### Concept

Stop the engine wisely at traffic sig­ • nals. Switch ‘OFF’ the engine at the traffic signal only if the stoppage time is high (typically more than 30 sec).

### Concept

While driving on highways, drive with • windows closed. The more you open the windows the higher will be the re­ sistance to the vehicle at higher speeds which will reduce the fuel effi­ ciency.

### Concept

Do not over speed; follow the speed • limits. More the speed, higher the ex­ ternal resistance on the vehicle which will finally result into unnecessary con­ sumption of fuel.

# kg C, D, E X IL IL X

## Knowledge

### Concept

A CRS in a closed vehicle can become very hot. To prevent burns, check the seating surface and buckles before placing your child in CRS.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p28_img00` (page 28, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p28_img00.png`

### Concept

• Do not modify CRS in any way.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p28_img01` (page 28, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p28_img01.png`

### Concept

• Do not install a booster seat or a booster cushion with only the lap strap of the seat belt or a seat belt that is slack or twisted.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p28_img02` (page 28, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p28_img02.png`

### Concept

• Do not leave any toys or other ob- jects loose in the CRS or on the seat while the vehicle is in motion.

### Concept

IL: The seat is suitable for the ISOFIX child seats with “Semi-Universal” approval.

### Concept

IUF: The seat is suitable for forward facing child seats and is permitted for use in this weight category.

### Concept

X: The seat is not equipped for the ISOFIX system.

### Concept

*Rear outboard seating positions are suitable for ISO/R3, Class C CRS.

### Concept

Recommended CRS Positions (CRS That Can Be Used With

### Specification

### Specification

### Concept

After a collision, we recommend to get seat belts, seats, ISOFIX and top-tether anchorages (as may be applicable) inves- tigated at TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

### Concept

Each CRS should be used for one child only.

### Concept

Passenger airbag can be turned OFF manually through switch provided on side face of the dashboard at front passenger side. Visual signal of passenger airbag ON or OFF is indicated on the roof console.

### Concept

When passenger airbag is ON, a rearward facing child seat shall not be installed on the front passenger seat.

### Concept

When passenger airbag is OFF, a forward or rearward facing child seat can be in- stalled on the front passenger seat.

### Concept

While installing a rearward facing child seat on the front passenger seat, passen- ger airbag must be OFF.

### Concept

Refer images in PAB Switch section.

### Concept

Child lock are provided on both rear doors. It is used for safety of a child.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p29_img01` (page 29, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p29_img01.png`

### Concept

Child safety lever to be used for safety of

### Concept

child for preventing them to open rear door while seating in passenger seat to avoid accident while vehicle is moving.

### Concept

Both the rear doors of the vehicle are pro- vided with a child proof lock. Push the lock lever (located on vertical face of the door) downward before closing the door. The door which has been locked by activating the child lock cannot be opened from in- side. It can be opened only from the out- side.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p29_img02` (page 29, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p29_img02.png`

### Warning

If the airbag SRS warning indicator in the instrument cluster illuminates con- tinuously, it means that there is mal- function in the system. Remove the CRS from front passenger seat and contact your TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p29_img00` (page 29, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p29_img00.png`

### Concept

Lift the lock lever upward to deactivate the childproof lock when not required.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Specification

When pumping in the sealant through the tyre valve, the pressure may rise up to 500 kPa (5 bar/73 psi) but will drop again after about 30 seconds.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p273_img00` (page 273, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p273_img00.png`

### Concept

Need to drain fluid from tyre before repair.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p273_img01` (page 273, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p273_img01.png`

### Concept

Step 2: Checking The Tyre Pressure

### Specification

Once a tyre inflation pressure of at least 180kPa (1.8 bar/26 psi) has been reached. Switch the compressor to “0” in order to read the actual tyre pressure from the pressure gauge.

### Concept

Pull the power plug from the 12 volt power socket connection.

### Concept

 Slowly unscrew the hose from the tyre valve (sealant residues may escape from the hose) and put the protective cap back onto the hose.

### Concept

 Leave the bottle in the holder. This avoids unexpected leakage of sealant residue.

### Concept

 Make sure the Puncture repair Kit, the cap of the bottle and the orange cap are stored safely, but are still easily accessible, in the vehicle.

### Concept

 The kit will be needed again when you check the tyre pressure.

### Concept

 Start and drive for about 3-10 km so that the sealant can seal the damaged area. Do not drive for more than 10 min and not faster than 80 km/h.

### Procedure

 Stop the vehicle after driving about 3- 10 km. Check and where necessary, adjust the pressure of the damaged tyre. Remove the protective cap from the end of the hose. Screw the hose firmly onto the valve of the damaged tyre. Read the tyre pressure from the pressure gauge.

### Specification

 If the pressure of the sealant-filled tyre is 130kPa (1.3 bar/19 psi) or more, it must now be adjusted to the pressure specified for your vehicle

### Concept

(Refer tyre pressure sticker pasted on driver door side).

### Concept

 Inflate the tyre to the specified pres- sure using the pressure “air release” valve. Rest of the remaining sealant in the hose might leak out when opening pressure “air release” valve or taking off the protective cap of the hose. Please use protective glove for safety purpose.

### Concept

 Once you have inflated the tyre to its correct tyre pressure, switch off the compressor, pull the plug out of the socket, unscrew the hose, fasten the tyre valve cap and put back on the protective cap of the hose.

### Concept

 Leave the bottle in the holder and store the Puncture repair Kit away safely in the vehicle trunk

### Concept

 Drive to the nearest workshop to get the damaged tyre repaired and if the tyre repair is not possible it should be removed from the car. Before the tyre is removed from the rim, inform your tyre dealer that the tyre contains seal- ant.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Fuel consumption, engine, transmission, brake and tyre wear are mainly affected by below factors:

### Concept

Operating conditions of your vehicle •

### Concept

Your personal driving style • Operating Conditions

### Concept

Avoid frequent start and stop as these • increase fuel consumptions.

### Concept

Always make sure that the tyre pres­ • sures are correct.

### Concept

Do not carry any unnecessary weight. •

### Concept

Regularly, service your vehicle and ad­ • here to the recommended service maintenance schedule. Personal Driving Style

### Concept

Do not press the accelerator pedal • while starting the engine.

### Concept

Do not warm up the engine when the • vehicle is stationary.

### Concept

Always adapt your driving style to suit • the prevailing road, weather condi­ tions, and maintain a safe distance from the vehicle in front. Drive care­

### Concept

Avoid frequent, sudden acceleration • and braking.

### Concept

Select appropriate gear according to • varying speeds and load conditions.

  - File: `images/doc_003/p212_img00.png`

Switch ‘OFF’ the engine in stationary • traffic or at signals.

### Concept

Keep an eye on the vehicle’s fuel con­ • sumption.

### Concept

Driving safety systems are merely aids • designed to assist driving. You are re­ sponsible for the distance to the vehi­ cle in front, for vehicle speed and anticipating braking in good time.

Slow down before shifting to a lower • gear. This will help avoiding revving of the engine causing damage (for MT).

Avoid frequent brake application which • can cause overheating of brakes.

### Concept

Slow down the vehicle speed while • travelling in cross winds. This gives much better control over the vehicle.

### Concept

Avoid high speed when cornering or • turning.

### Concept

Press the clutch fully while shifting •

### Concept

### Concept

AEB will not work under following con­ • ditions:

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

III. When target vehicle or object ahead is not detected anymore.

### Concept

IV. When user presses and releases brake pedal.

For some special obstacles like barri­ • cades, cows and other animals, there is a possibility that FCW warning and Braking may not be given.

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

The driver has to follow warnings and • instructions before use of FCW-AEB system to avoid serious injury or death.

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

FCW-AEB system should never be • tested by driving toward a person or object or animal. This may result in se­ rious injury or loss of life.

### Warning

### Warning

FCW-AEB system works by predicting • the path and direction of travel of ob­ stacles. In certain complex environ­ ment situations or sensors misaligned. The system may provide false warning or braking or may not provide warning or braking for front object.

### Concept

During AEB collision the passengers • can experience great discomfort and high jerk while the system applies maximum possible brake to avoid/mit­ igate the collision. This can cause minor to medium level injuries to the passenger. It is advisable that to avoid major injuries the passengers should always wear seatbelt.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Park Assist System Limitations

### Concept

Park Assist system is not a collision avoid­ ing system. It is solely the driver’s respon­ sibility to park the vehicle safely.

### Concept

Park Assist feature works on ultra sound echo technology, due to which perform­ ance is not guaranteed in following sce­ narios:

### Concept

If the object has a sharp edge surface, • where surface may divert echoes from

### Concept

If object is mesh fence made up of thin • wires, where echoes can’t be given by the surface.

### Concept

Fast moving objects passes in the sen­ • sor field of detection, where echoes are not processed by the system.

### Concept

If object is made/covered by foam or • sponge or snow where ultrasonic sound signals are absorbed.

### Warning

Objects close to the rear bumper can • go undetected by the Park Assist field of detection. Driver should use ex­ treme caution while parking the vehi­ cle.

### Concept

If height of the bumper is changed due • to alteration to the suspension or other causes.

### Concept

If the sensor areas are extremely hot • from direct sunlight or cold due to freezing weather.

### Concept

If Sensors are covered by a hand, • sticker, accessory, etc.

### Concept

If ultrasonic noise is present around • Vehicle due to heavy rain, wind other

### Concept

vehicle sensors, horn, engine, air brak­ ing system (large vehicles), Exhaust Fans, Wireless transmitters or mobile phones.

### Concept

If the vehicle speed exceeds 10 km/h, • the system will not warn you even though objects are detected, error message ‘Vehicle Speed is high, drive slowly!’ will appear.

### Concept

Driving on uneven road surfaces e.g. • Gravel, unpaved roads, Artificial Speed Breakers, or gradient.

### Concept

Poles of square/rectangle cross sec­ • tion might not be detected at vehicle edge.

### Concept

If trailer is connected. •

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

When towing a break down vehicle, cer­ tain precautions and procedures must be taken to prevent damage to the vehicle and/or components. Failure to use stan­ dard towing precautionary measures when lifting or towing a break down vehicle could result in an unsafe operating condition.

### Concept

To ensure proper towing and to prevent accidental damage to your vehicle, take help of a TATA MOTORS authorized dealer or a commercial tow-truck service.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p277_img03` (page 277, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p277_img03.png`

### Concept

Do not disconnect the discharged bat­ tery from the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p277_img00` (page 277, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p277_img00.png`

### Concept

Never connect the jump lead directly to the negative (–) terminal of the dis­ charged battery. This may lead to an ex­ plosion.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p277_img01` (page 277, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p277_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not allow battery electrolyte to • come in contact with eyes, skin, fab­ rics or painted surfaces. The fluid contains acid which can cause in­ jury and severe damage. Wear pro­ tective apparel. Do not inhale any battery gases. Keep children away from batteries. In case if battery acid comes in contact with the skin, wash it off immediately with water and seek medical attention.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p277_img02` (page 277, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p277_img02.png`

### Concept

During charging and jump-starting, • explosive gases can escape from

### Concept

the battery. There is a risk of an ex­ plosion. Particularly avoid fire, open flames, creating sparks and smok­ ing. Ensure there is sufficient venti­ lation while charging and jump-starting. Do not lean over the battery.

### Concept

Make sure that the positive terminal • of a connected battery does not come into contact with vehicle parts. Never place metal objects or tools on a battery.

### Concept

It is important that you observe the • described order of the battery termi­ nals when connecting and discon­ necting a battery. If you are in doubt, seek assistance from qualified spe­ cialist workshop.

### Procedure

Never connect or disconnect the • battery terminals while the engine is running.

### Concept

Make sure that the parking brake is re­ leased ; vehicle in neutral gear position and steering wheel is unlocked. The power steering functions only when en­ gine is running. Hence, during towing the steering efforts will be more.

title: MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES
text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

EXHAUST AFTER TREATMENT SYSTEM

### Concept

Exhaust after treatment consists of below components:

### Concept

Diesel Oxidation Catalyst (DOC) 1.

### Concept

Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) 2.

### Concept

Selective Catalyst Reduction (SCR) 3.

### Concept

Various Sensors and Actuators. 4.

### Concept

The exhaust gas coming from the engine first passes through the DOC and then through DPF.

### Concept

DPF is a filter, which filters carbon soot in the exhaust gas. DOC and DPF contains precious metals which converts hydrocar­ bons, carbon monoxide etc. in the exhaust gas to harmless constituents.

### Concept

Additionally DPF also removes most of the carbon soot particles in the exhaust gas. The collected carbon soot in the DPF is re­ generated to clean the filter.

### Concept

In order to reduce the NOx levels even fur­ ther, SCR system is used. In SCR system, DEF is injected in the exhaust stream. With the help of injected ammonia in the DEF, NOx is converted into harmless con­

### Concept

Avoid parking of vehicle over inflamma­ ble materials, such as dry leaves; grass etc. as exhaust system is hot enough to initiate fire.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p319_img00` (page 319, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p319_img00.png`

### Concept

Ensure exhaust system is not • blocked and is free from obstruction.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p319_img01` (page 319, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p319_img01.png`

### Concept

Blockages in the exhaust can create • backpressure, low top speed, poor pick up, black smoke, carbon buildup and low mileage and can af­ fect power output of the engine and thee mission levels.

### Concept

The maximum sulphur content of the diesel fuel must not exceed 0.001% (10 parts per million). Failure to comply with the standards may damage engine components and the exhaust after- treatment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p319_img02` (page 319, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p319_img02.png`

### Concept

In order to control exhaust emissions, this vehicle is equipped with SCR sys­ tem through which DEF (Diesel Exhaust Fluid) continuously flows. It is normal to have a noise from the SCR system dur­ ing vehicle operation or for about 20 to 30 seconds after engine is switched off.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p319_img03` (page 319, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p319_img03.png`

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Following precautions are to be taken when temporary spare wheel is fitted on the vehicle (if provided)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p265_img00` (page 265, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p265_img00.png`

### Concept

IN CASE of FLAT TYRE

### Concept

Reduce vehicle speed gradually, Avoid • sudden steering movement or braking.

### Concept

Pay attention to the traffic conditions • as you do so.

### Warning

Switch on the hazard warning lamps. •

### Concept

Stop the vehicle on solid, non-slippery • and level ground, as far away as pos­ sible from traffic.

### Concept

Use the Jack on level, hard ground. • Avoid changing the wheel on uphill and downhill slopes. Chock the wheels, if the deflated wheel needs to be changed on slope / ghat area.

### Concept

If possible, bring the front wheels into • the straight-ahead position.

### Concept

Secure the vehicle against rolling • away.

### Concept

Set the parking brake firmly and shift • into “R” (Reverse) gear on level ground and while vehicle is in downhill posi­ tion.

### Concept

When the vehicle is in uphill position, • shift the gear in first gear.

### Concept

• Drive the shortest possible dis- tances. The temporary spare wheel should be exchanged for a normal wheel as soon as possible. The temporary spare wheel is de-signed for a short period of use only.

### Concept

• “80 km/h” or “50 mph” is the maxi- mum speed you are permit-ted to drive with this tyre.

### Concept

• Never drive faster than 80 km/h (50 mph). Do not accelerate quickly, brake suddenly or drive at high speed through bends

### Concept

• After fitting the temporary spare wheel, the tyre pressure must be checked as soon as possible.

### Specification

• Recommended tyre pressure is 33 psi (2.3 bar) for temporary spare wheel.

### Concept

Snow chains cannot be used on the • temporary spare wheel.

### Concept

Never use more than one temporary • spare wheel.

### Concept

Do not drive through an automatic • car wash.

### Concept

Never use a temporary spare tyre if • it is damaged or worn down to the tread wear indicators.

### Concept

The ground clearance of your vehi­ • cle may be reduced. Take care when parking next to curb.

### Concept

The temporary spare should not be • installed on the front axle if the ve­ hicle must be driven in snow or on ice.

### Concept

Do not tow whilst the temporary • spare wheel is installed.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Switch off the engine. •

### Warning

Keep advance warning triangle at a • suitable distance behind the vehicle as an indication of breakdown.

### Concept

Close all the doors. •

### Concept

Remove the center hub cap/wheel cover in case of steel wheel rim (if equipped).

### Concept

Loosen the nuts (as indicated) on the wheel in diagonal sequence. Do not un­ screw the nuts completely before jacking the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p266_img01` (page 266, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p266_img01.png`

### Concept

If you drive with a flat tyre, there is a risk of the following hazards:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p266_img00` (page 266, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p266_img00.png`

### Concept

A flat tyre affects the ability to steer • or brake the vehicle.

### Concept

You could lose control of the vehi­ • cle.

### Concept

Continued driving with a flat tyre will • permanently damage the tyre and cause excessive heat buildup and possibly a fire. There is a risk of an accident.

### Concept

The jack is designed only to raise • and hold the vehicle for a short time while a wheel is being changed. It is not suited for performing mainte­ nance work under the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p266_img02` (page 266, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p266_img02.png`

### Concept

Use the jack on level, hard ground. • Avoid changing the wheel on uphill and downhill slopes. Chock the wheels, if the deflated wheel needs to be changed on slope / ghat area.

### Concept

Before raising the vehicle, secure it • from rolling away by applying the parking brake.

### Concept

Shift the gear into ‘R’ (reverse) on • level ground and while vehicle is in downhill position, and shift the gear in first gear when vehicle is in uphill position.

### Concept

Do not use wooden blocks or similar • objects as a jack underlay.

### Concept

Do not place your hands and feet or • lie under the raised vehicle when it

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Specification

24 X 7 ROADSIDE ASSISTANCE

### Concept

It is our responsibility and our endeavor to ensure that you have our complete service backup, wherever and whenever you need the same. When you have a road network that spans wide area, the probability of a breakdown happening within hailing dis­ tance of a TATA MOTORS Authorized Workshop is very low.

### Concept

It is precisely for this reason, we have tied up with TVS Auto Assist and Allianz serv­ ice provider, who will provide on- road services for repairable breakdown assis­ tance including towing to the nearest TATA MOTORS Authorized Workshop and am­ bulance for injured passenger to nearest hospital through their Authorized Service Providers (ASP).

### Specification

The 24X7 On Roadside Assistance Pro­ gram shall be automatically available to your vehicle for the duration of Warranty period (3+1 Years). The program shall also be available, if you avail the same post warranty.

Explain your exact location with land­ • marks and tell us about the problem you face with the vehicle.

Park your vehicle on the edge of the • road, open the bonnet and put on the hazard warning signal.

Place the advance warning triangle • supplied with the vehicle approx. 3 m from the vehicle in the direction of on­ coming traffic.

### Concept

RESS (REMOTE ENGINE START STOP) (if equipped)

### Concept

The remote engine start stop feature im- proves the user experience and comfort by providing the remote engine start stop from the mobile app.

### Concept

Using this feature, user can remotely ac- cess the vehicle through connected car application (IRA) and start the pre condi- tioning (engine and AC ON/OFF).

### Concept

In the ignition OFF condition user can 1. start the vehicle remotely using mobile application.

### Concept

In the mobile app, user need to set 2. timer value (set timer) for that specific time vehicle is turned ON.

### Concept

Based on the user’s set timer value ve­ 3. hicle engine will be on and based on set temperature FATC will start the AC in auto mode with the requested tem­ perature.

### Concept

Remote engine start command turns 4. ON engine and remote AC.

### Concept

User can also send remote stop com­ 5.

### Procedure

mand through app in order to kill set timer and turn OFF engine.

Failure Conditions/Time Killer

### Concept

Remote based start stop will be failed if

### Concept

The vehicle is in ignition ON state. •

### Concept

Any of the door/bonnet/tailgate is left • opened.

### Concept

The battery voltage of the vehicle is • below Threshold value.

### Concept

The steering of the vehicle is in un­ • locked state.

### Concept

The vehicle speed is NOT zero and the • low fuel level indication is ON.

### Concept

The accelerator/clutch brake pedal is • already ENGAGED.

### Concept

Vehicle is NOT in neutral gear. •

### Concept

Hand Brake is not fully engaged or • electronic park brake not engaged.

### Concept

All doors should be locked including • tailgate and bonnet.

### Concept

• Low fuel level indication should be in OFF state.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

DIESEL EXHAUST FLUID (DEF)

### Concept

The vehicle is equipped with DEF injection system and Se­ lective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) to meet emission standards. DEF Storage

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p322_img00` (page 322, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p322_img00.png`

### Specification

DEF is a very stable product with a long shelf life. Stored at temperatures LOWER than 32°C, it has a shelf life of at least one year.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p322_img01` (page 322, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p322_img01.png`

### Concept

Preliminary Conditions

### Concept

Consumption of the additive DEF depends on the condition of vehicle use and is indi­ cated on the instrument cluster.

### Specification

DEF freezes at temperatures lower than - 11°C. If the car stands for a long time at this temperature refilling could be difficult. For this reason, it is advised to park the vehicle in a garage and/or heated environ­ ment and wait for the DEF to return to liq­ uid state before topping up.

### Concept

Park the car on flat ground and stop • the engine by placing the ignition in the OFF position.

### Procedure

DEF filler is located in the tailgate com­ • partment below the tool kit tray. Open the tailgate and remove the tool kit tray

### Concept

and remove the cap from the DEF filler.

DEF freezes at temperatures lower than -11°C.

## Knowledge

### Warning

In situations where there is water on • the road, there may be false detections and false warning and braking may be given. Lane Departure Warning (LDW)

### Warning

LDW is a safety feature which helps the driver to keep the vehicle in the lane by providing warning to the user when vehicle departs lane without driver intention.

### Concept

Prerequisite for activation

### Concept

The following condition shall be satisfied to activate LDW

### Concept

Front Camera should be fault free and 1. blockage free.

### Concept

Front windshield should be clean. 2.

### Concept

Vehicle speed is more than 60kmph. 3.

### Concept

Driver steering wheel inputs are within 4. operating limits for the function.

### Concept

Lane markings are properly detected 5. and a lane is properly recognized.

### Concept

Turn Indicator of the side of departure 6. is OFF.

### Concept

LDW is default ON at start of vehicle

### Concept

User can turn OFF LDW feature. 1.

### Concept

User can turn ON LDW feature. 2.

### Concept

In infotainment system user interface, press the following button sequence to reach LDW user settings page

### Concept

Go to Home page >> All App >> Settings >> Driver Assistance >> Drive assist

### Concept

Lane Recognition (When LDW ON and No Lane Recognition)

### Concept

When no lanes are detected and LDW feature is ON. Driver will get Tell Tale on Instrument cluster in white color. If feature is not work­ ing because of any reason it may go to standby state. In that case also this tell- tale will be shown in white color. In this scenario try cleaning windshield area where camera is mounted and give an ig­ nition cycle. If the feature still does not work after driving above 60kmph, visit service center.

When the Vehicle de­ parts to one side of the lane without giving turn indicator and is very close to the lane edge, the visual warning for lane departure of respective side will be in red color on cluster along with Tell Tale & audio LDW warning will not be given if turn indicator of the particular side is ON.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

REGENERATION PROCESS

### Concept

DPF is a mechanical filter that physically traps particulate matter from diesel engine exhaust gas.

### Concept

DPF traps the particulate matter in the fol­ lowing way:

### Concept

Filtration – Particulates / soot are col­ • lected in the inlet channel of the filter.

### Concept

Regeneration – When the filter chan­ • nels are filled up with soot, they are cleaned automatically by the engine management system. This process is known as DPF Regeneration and this will happen during normal running of the vehicle.

### Concept

In certain specific driving conditions, DPF regeneration may not happen automati­ cally as the desired temperatures required to regenerate soot many not be achievable due to specific driving conditions. This may happen in prolonged driving at low vehicle speeds for considerable amount of time (driving in heavy city traffic), pro­ longed running of the engine in idle condi­ tions, use of adulterated diesel etc.

### Warning

In such cases, a DPF warning lamp will be illuminated indicating that soot regenera­ tion is insufficient. PARK DPF Regeneration Procedure (if equipped)

### Concept

This procedure enables DPF regeneration strat­ egy on vehicle through vehicle infotainment sys­ tem.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p320_img00` (page 320, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p320_img00.png`

### Concept

PARK DPF regeneration is only possible when the DPF tell-tale appears in the in­ strument cluster.

### Concept

Follow the below steps to perform DPF Regeneration through Infotainment sys­ tem.

### Concept

Park the vehicle safely in a well venti­ 1. lated levelled open space and free of any flammable material in vicinity. Do not park vehicle in enclosed place, above grass (especially dry grass/leaves/ cellulose materials etc.) while doing DPF regeneration.

### Specification

Ensure adequate fuel availability 2. (10.0L minimum) and keep the bonnet

### Concept

Shift the gear lever to Neutral in engine 3. running condition and apply the park­ ing brake.

### Concept

Do not press Accelerator/ Brake/ 4. Clutch pedal during the Park DPF re­ generation procedure.

### Concept

Do not park vehicle close to any • flammable material during DPF re­ generation process to avoid fire in­ cidents.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p320_img01` (page 320, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p320_img01.png`

### Concept

Do not touch, keep away yourself • and kids from exhaust system to avoid burns/injury.

### Procedure

DPF Regeneration process will not start if CHECK ENGINE LAMP or MIL tale- tale is ON in the cluster. Take your ve­ hicle to an authorised TATA dealer for assistance. While DPF regeneration is ON do not press the accelerator, brake, clutch pedals or change the gear from

### Concept

APB Malfunction Indicator

### Concept

Both the APB malfunction lamp and park­ ing brake lamp glow in cluster for 3 secs during ignition ON then disappears. If any abnormality is there in the system the mal­ function indicator stays continuously ON.

### Concept

In the case of any fault in the ESP system, this lamp may or may not appear.

Parking brake lamp does not illuminate if the APB is not engaged except the 3 secs during the ignition ON.

### Concept

In the case of any failure in the service brake or during any other emergency situ­ ations APB switch can be applied in vehi­ cle running condition. text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Your vehicle has fuse boxes at two loca­ tions.

### Concept

The vehicles electrical circuits have fuses to protect the wiring from short circuits or sustained overload.

### Concept

Engine Compartment Fuse Box 1.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p280_img00` (page 280, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p280_img00.png`

### Concept

Cabin Compartment Fuse Box 2.

### Concept

Checking and Replacing Fuses

### Concept

If any electrical unit in your vehicle is not functioning, check the fuses first.

### Procedure

Please follow the steps below that will guide you to check and replace them.

### Concept

Apply parking brake. •

### Concept

Switch off all electrical accessories. •

### Concept

Turn the ignition key to the ‘LOCK’ po­ • sition.

### Concept

In the fuse box, identify the defective • fuse from its melted wire.

### Concept

Remove the blown fuse by “fuse • puller”. The fuse puller and spare fuses are provided in the engine compart­ ment fuse box.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p280_img01` (page 280, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p280_img01.png`

### Concept

Engine compartment fuse box

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p280_img02` (page 280, confidence 0.997)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p280_img02.png`

### Concept

Blown fuses must be replaced with • fuses of same rating, which you can recognize by color and value.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p280_img03` (page 280, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p280_img03.png`

### Concept

Ensure that all other fuses are pressed • firmly in position.

### Concept

If a newly inserted fuse also blows, • have the cause traced and rectified at nearest TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre immediately.

### Concept

Always ensure that the spare fuses are replenished.

### Concept

As the camera is, IP protected, do not • detach, disassemble or modify in any manner from the actual position. This will show required visual information in display.

### Procedure

Do not use camera when tailgate is • open. If tailgate is open, visual infor­ mation may not be the actual rear view of the vehicle & system will warn with message ‘Tail Gate Open, Please close.

### Concept

When the camera is operated under • fluorescent lights, sodium light or mer­ cury light etc., illuminated areas on the lens may appear to flicker in the dis­ play.

### Concept

Do not attach any advertisement or • styling or any kind of stickers on top of camera. If this happens, camera can­ not provide you the visual image and may damage camera.

### Concept

Do not add any accessory, which will • obstruct camera field of view.

### Concept

Due to environmental reasons, dust, 1. mud or fog may accumulate on the camera lens. So regularly clean the camera lens.

### Concept

Use water to clean the camera lens. 2. Do not use extreme cold or hot water. Rapid changes in temperature may brittle the camera lens. Do not apply High Pressure water for cleaning.

### Concept

Wipe the camera lens with soft cloth. 3.

### Concept

Do not use hard cloth or material to 4. wipe the camera lens. This will cause scratches on the camera, and leads to deteriorated visual image on the dis­ play.

### Concept

Do not apply organic solvent, car wax, 5. window cleaner or glass coat to clean the camera. If this is applied, wipe it off as soon as possible.

### Concept

Do not apply heavy force on lens, 6. while cleaning.

### Concept

Do not remove mud, snow on the cam­ 7. era lens using stick or hard material. Use normal water and soft cloth.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

• Message “ENGINE STOP TANK EMPTY” will be displayed once DEF tank is empty.

### Concept

Once the engine is stopped with this mes- sage, it will not be possible to restart the engine without filling DEF.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p325_img01` (page 325, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p325_img01.png`

### Concept

DEF Level Messages in case of SCR System Fault These messages will be indicated when there is any problem in the SCR system and SCR system fault is displayed. • Depending on the distance, the vehicle can run before emptying of DEF tank at the current DEF consumption rate. “SCR SYSTEM FAULT, ENGINE STOPS IN XXX KM” message will be indicated.

### Warning

If the vehicle is run without rectifying the SCR system (through TATA MOTORS service center), warning message will con-tinue with corresponding distance gradually reducing to 0 km. After this, engine will not start in the next ignition cycle. The vehicle has to be brought to TATA MOTORS service center for rectification. DEF Level Messages in case of Poor Quality DEF • In case of use of poor quality of DEF, message “DEF QUALITY LOW, EN- GINE STOPS IN XXX KM” will appear. In such cases, currently filled DEF has to be drained completely and proper good quality DEF needs to be filled until DEF tank is full.

### Concept

Please refer to DEF filling procedure for filling DEF.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p325_img02` (page 325, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p325_img02.png`

### Concept

• On further driving the vehicle without filling DEF, message “ENGINE WILL NOT RESTART IN NEXT KEY ON” will appear.

#### Visual References

If ’Fault’ is displayed in the Gear number position, take your vehicle to TATA MOTORS Author­ ized Service Centre to get it repaired.

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Driver Information System Image Description

### Concept

Service reminder is the feature to give the prior and overdue information about service of the vehicle to the user for proper vehicle maintenance. There are two types of service reminder i) By Kms ii) By days I. By Kms The service reminder shall come at every 15000 kms and it shall be popup before 500kms of due (i.e. 15000-500=14500km) and it shall be subtracted from the distance travelled. II. By Days The service reminder shall come at every 365 days and it shall be popup before 30 days of due time (i.e. 365-30=335 days) and it shall be subtracted from the days crossed. III. By Kms overdue The service reminder overdue shall come if the due km is crossed and it shall be displayed in every IGN ON and it shall be minimized in the TFT (i.e. 15000-15050=50km) IV. By days overdue The service reminder overdue shall come if the due days is crossed and it shall be displayed in every IGN ON and it shall be minimized in the TFT (i.e. 365-400=35 days).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p80_img00` (page 80, confidence 0.953)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p80_img00.png`

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Severe conditions are as below -

### Concept

A: Repeatedly driving short distance of less than 7 km. B: Extensive low speed driving for long distances. C: Driving on rough, dusty, muddy, unpaved, gravelled or salt-spread roads. D: Frequently driving in heavy traffic areas and in stop and go conditions. E: Driving only on uphill, downhill, or mountain roads. F: Vehicle towing, driving for petrol car, taxi, or other commercial use. G: Frequently driving under high speed and acceleration.

### Procedure

Item Interval Condition A B C D E F Engine oil and oil filter Replace every 7500 Km R R R R R R Check and adjust wheel alignment Inspect every 7500 km I I I I I I Sunroof- Guide rails and drain holes Inspect every 7500 km I I I I I I

### Note

NOTE • In Free service, labor charges are free, any parts and consumables will be chargeable. • Filters, Fluid, Consumables, Grease, Components, wheel alignment Wheel Balancing and weights etc. will be replaced on chargeable basis. • Check the coolant level and top up as required, replace if it is contaminated /discolored or there is sludge formation. • Periodic maintenance schedule is for reference. TMPV reserves the rights to change the Periodic Maintenance Schedule. • For cleaning the engine compartment, it is recommended to use dry low pressure air. Do not use pressurized water. • DEF is a consumable item, refill or replacement is not based on service intervals. The consumption of DEF can vary depending on driving style, and road and weather conditions. • Tyre pressure to be checked every 15 days. • Check the coolant level and top up as required, replace if it is contaminated /discolored or there is sludge formation • In case of emergency, a large amount of water without engine coolant may be added in order to reach a vehicle service location.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Check for inflation and condition of your vehicle tyres periodically.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p312_img00` (page 312, confidence 0.954)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p312_img00.png`

### Concept

Check the pressure in the tyres when they are cold.

### Concept

Keeping the tyres properly inflated gives you the best combination of riding comfort, handling, tyre life and better fuel efficiency.

### Concept

Over inflation of tyres makes the vehicle ride bumpy and harsh. Tyres are more prone to uneven wear and dam-age from road hazards.

### Concept

Under inflated tyres reduce your comfort in vehicle handling and are prone to fail­ ures due to high temperature. They also cause uneven wear and more fuel con­ sumption.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p312_img01` (page 312, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p312_img01.png`

### Concept

The battery contains sulphuric acid • (electrolyte) which is poisonous and highly corrosive in nature. Getting electrolyte in your eyes or on the skin can cause severe burns. Wear protective clothing and a face shield or have a skilled technician to do the battery maintenance.

### Concept

pressure Uniform wear

### Concept

Excessive center tread

### Concept

Every time you check inflation pressure, you should also examine tyres for un­ even wear, damage and trapping of for­ eign objects in the treads and wear.

Adaptive Cruise Control (if equipped)

### Concept

Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) is a com­ fort feature that allows a vehicle’s cruise control system to adapt the host vehicle’s speed automatically even in traffic condi­ tions. Feature detects vehicles, which are in the host vehicle’s path. If slower moving vehicle is detected the ACC system will slow down the host vehicle speed and maintain appropriate distance from the tar­ get vehicle. If the system detects that the forward vehicle is no longer present in the host vehicle’s path, the system will accel­ erate the vehicle back to its set cruise con­ trol speed.

### Concept

The feature identifies the nature of traffic and distance from other vehicles and help to adjust the speed and distance of the host vehicle according to vehicle moving in front.

### Concept

ACC is drive assist feature and it will • not avoid collision.

### Concept

BSD-LCA may not function properly, • under the following situations:

### Concept

The speed of the other vehicle is • very fast that it passes by your ve­ hicle in a very short time.

### Concept

Your vehicle changes lane without • giving turn indicators.

### Concept

When your vehicle overtakes other • vehicle and relative speed between the two vehicles is low.

When your vehicle is braking. •

### Concept

### Concept

hicle in the next lane.

The function may recognize a ve­ • hicle in the same lane.

### Concept

BSD-LCA may not operate properly • when driving on a slope. The function may not detect the vehicle in the next lane.

### Concept

When User Engages ACC at a speed • higher than 30kpmh, then that speed will be set as ACC speed and vehicle will cruise at that speed if no obstacle is present in the path.

### Concept

If ACC is ON/Engaged and User Acti­ • vates the Hill Descent Control (HDC) function by pressing the HDC button, then ACC will be OFF/Standby. If HDC is already activated and user tries to activate the ACC, then ACC won’t be active. HDC function has always higher priority than ACC.

### Concept

Overtake Assist Control (OAC): During • the Follow Control mode, if the driver has will to overtake the target vehicle, OAC function will help to overtake the target vehicle by enhancing the accel­ eration smoothly. For OAC activation, Turn indicator must be ON and mini­ mum host vehicle speed should by 20kph.

### Concept

Active Cruise Mode – If there is no vehi­ cle in the path of subject vehicle, then it will cruise at a speed equal to ACC set speed.

### Concept

Active Follow Mode – If there is a vehicle in the path of the subject vehicle, then it will maintain a distance from the target ve­ hicle equivalent to the distance set by the user.

### Concept

Stop - Hold Mode – If the preceding vehi­ cle is stopped then host vehicle will also stop. If the preceding vehicle moves then host vehicle will also move without user in­ tervention. Now after 5 sec of stop mode to restart ACC user intervention is required irrespective of preceding vehicle. User can exist from stop hold mode by double pressing ACC resume/Cancel button. # DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Warning

Warning Lamps Color Indicator Remarks

### Concept

One of these symbols comes ‘ON’ when the turn indicators is switched ‘ON’. Turn signal lamps can be operated only when the Ignition supply is ‘ON’ and by using the turn indicator switch on the combi-switch. The direction indicator arrow on Instrument Cluster flashes along with external indicator lights as selected. Both telltales shall blink simultaneously when Hazard switch is pressed irre­ spective of Ignition ON and the Tick-Tock sound shall be given when any one or both the telltales are ON.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p107_img00` (page 107, confidence 0.943)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p107_img00.png`

### Concept

This symbol comes ‘ON’ when the headlamp high beam is switched ‘ON’ and High beam was flashed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p107_img01` (page 107, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p107_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_003_p107_img02` (page 107, confidence 0.928)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p107_img02.png`

### Concept

Low Engine Oil Pressure Indicator Red

### Warning

When the Ignition is turned ‘ON’, this symbol lights up and goes ‘OFF’ as soon as the required engine oil pressure is developed after starting the en­ gine. Warning : If the low oil pressure indicator does not glow or remains ‘ON’ with the ‘IGN’ ‘ON’ and engine is running, it indicates a fault in the electrical circuit / lubrica­ tion system. Take your car to a TATA Authorized Service Centre.

### Warning

Battery charging/ Engine warning Red

### Note

This symbol lights up when the ‘IGN’ is turned ‘ON’ and should go ‘OFF’ after the engine starts. Note: If it remains ‘ON’ while the engine is running, it indicates that the battery is not getting charged. Switch off all unnecessary electrical equipment and get the problem attended at TATA authorized Service center.

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

After detecting low beam from oncom­ • ing vehicle, HBA may give flash from low beam to high beam and again low beam due to any other light sources present around or due to camera de­ tection performance.

### Concept

If HBA detects the light sources of on­ • coming vehicle only for short period, HBA can stay in high beam without switching low beam.

### Concept

In the case that obviously appeared • light sources of oncoming vehicle over the guardrail are detected, HBA may switch high beam to low beam.

### Concept

In the city or in a light source area such • as traffic sign, electronic sign board, building light, streetlight, HBA may switch high beam to low beam.

### Concept

HBA shall not operate at daytime even • though High Beam is on by the auto light sensor.

### Concept

HBA will operate in following weather • conditions:

### Concept

The normal nighttime environment •

### Concept

in which the light of the front vehi­ cle is detected by the naked eye. Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) and Over-speed Limit Alert.

### Concept

Traffic Sign recognition (TSR) is a feature by which a vehicle is able to recognize the traffic signs available on the road.

### Concept

Over-speed alert system will alert driver when vehicle speed is more than detected speed limit sign on the road.

### Concept

Prerequisite for Activation

### Concept

Front camera should be fault and blockage free

### Concept

Front windshield should be clean

### Concept

Vehicle speed is above 0 km/h

### Concept

TSR shall be default ON at the start of ve­ hicle.

### Concept

User can turn TSR feature ON from In­ 1. fotainment setting menu.

### Concept

User can turn TSR feature OFF from 2. Infotainment setting menu.

### Concept

User Settings - Over-speed limit alert

### Concept

TSR and Over-speed limit alert should be

### Concept

default ON at the start of vehicle.

### Concept

User can turn Over-speed limit alert 1. feature ON from infotainment setting menu.

### Concept

User can turn Over-speed limit alert 2. feature OFF from infotainment setting menu.

### Warning

User can update warning settings for 3. ex No warning, Only Visual, Audio and Visual

### Concept

User can update threshold settings for 4. ex 0 Kpmh, 3Kmph, 5 Kmph, 10 Kmph

### Concept

TSR should be always ON to use Over- speed limit alert feature.

nition/Engine ON condition. Always ensure parking brake is released and parking brake warning lamp is OFF before start of the drive. If this is not possible use the vehi­ cle with extreme precaution until you reach service center.

text:
# SYSTEM ANTI-LOCK BRAKING (ABS)

## Knowledge

### Concept

pressure in such a way that the wheels do not lock when you brake. This allows you to continue steering the vehicle when braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p31_img00` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p31_img00.png`

### Warning

The ABS warning lamp in the instrument cluster lights up when the ignition is switched on. It goes off after 2-3 seconds if system is healthy.

### Concept

• In case of emergency braking, press the brake pedal fully. This allows the ABS to regulate braking force and maintain directional control of vehicle.

### Concept

• When ABS is active driver may feel brake pedal pulsating and very low (ABS) motor activation noise from en- gine compartment which is normal dur- ing braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p31_img02` (page 31, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p31_img02.png`

### Concept

• If ABS is faulty, the wheels could lock when braking. The steer ability and braking characteristics may be severely impaired. There is an in- creased danger of skidding and ac- cidents.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p31_img01` (page 31, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p31_img01.png`

### Concept

• Drive on carefully. Have ABS checked immediately at the TATA- MOTORS Authorized Service Cen- tre as soon as possible.

### Concept

• ABS may not shorten the distance in all situation.

### Concept

• ABS system will have the effect of increased stopping distance due to conditions such as gravel, pot holes, slippery surfaces, wet road, ground covered with snow etc.

### Concept

• Travelling on bad road, panic brak- ing brake pedal may become hard, this is due to ABS system taking control. ABS will not compensate forbad road, weather conditions and poor driving judgment. Always drive

### Concept

carefully in adverse weather and traffic conditions.

### Concept

• Always keep safe distance and ad- here to speed limits.

| • If EBD is malfunctioning, the rear wheels can lock, e.g. under full braking. ### Concept

Park Assist System is an electronic park­ ing aid that assist you to park vehicle safely when in reverse gear mode. It also provides front part assist (if equipped) if your vehicle speed is below 10Kmph and Front part assist option is enabled through infotainment screen.

### Concept

It provides audio, visual information through vehicle infotainment system. Se­ lect this feature in infotainment display to see any obstacle behind/front of the vehi­ cle.

# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

For alloy wheel rims with spare wheel of steel wheel rim (if equipped)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p314_img00` (page 314, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p314_img00.png`

### Concept

Incorrect wheel alignment causes exces­ sive and uneven tyre wear. Check wheel alignment at specified intervals. Wheel Balancing

### Concept

Wheels of your vehicle are balanced for better ride comfort and longer tyre life. Bal­ ancing needs to be done whenever tyre is removed from rim.

### Concept

Special Care for Tubeless Tyres

### Concept

While removing tyre from wheel rim • and mounting it back on wheel rim, take precautions not to damage tyre bead. Use tyre removal and assembly machines. Damage or cut on tyre bead may cause gradual loss of air and de­ flation of tyre.

### Concept

Do not scratch inside of tubeless tyre • with metallic or sharp object. Tubeless tyres are coated with impermeable layer of rubber from inside which holds the air inside the tyre. Removal of this layer due to scratching may cause gradual loss of air and deflation.

### Concept

If wheel rim gets damaged in service, • get the wheel rim repaired/ replaced immediately. Running the vehicle with damaged rim may cause deflation of tyre and subsequent dislodging of tyre from rim.

### Concept

Maintain recommended inflation pres­ • sure. Over-inflation, in particular, may cause puncture or bursting of tyre.

### Concept

If the vehicle vibrates abnormally on a smooth road, have the wheel balanced done immediately.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p314_img01` (page 314, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p314_img01.png`

### Concept

While driving in snow, it is advisable • to use the snow chain on roads. Fol­ low assembly and safety instruction provided by the snow chain manu­ facturers.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p314_img02` (page 314, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p314_img02.png`

### Concept

Please refer service schedule for • wheel alignment.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Ventilated Seats (if equipped)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p221_img00` (page 221, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p221_img00.png`

### Concept

To start ventilation, press the ventilation button. It’s has 3 ventilation adjustment in decreasing order and LED glows for each press. To stop the ventilation, long press the ventilation button for few seconds.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p221_img01` (page 221, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p221_img01.png`

### Concept

Default setting is highest speed on first press.

### Concept

The ventilated seat by default is set to OFF whenever the engine START/STOP button is turned ON.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p221_img02` (page 221, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p221_img02.png`

### Concept

To protect ventilated seats

### Concept

Use the air ventilation seat ONLY • when the vehicle HVAC system is ON.

### Concept

Never use alcohol based liquids to • clean the Seats as it may damage the leatherette material.

### Concept

Avoid spillage of liquids on the venti­ • lated seats surface this may lead to blockage of air path/ holes ventilated seat system and may not function properly.

### Concept

Do not add seat covers, as it will not • allow ventilated seats to function prop­ erly.

### Concept

Do not keep plastic covers of seat as it •

### Concept

is, as it will not allow ventilated seats to function properly. Lumbar Support (if equipped)

### Concept

Continuous (Multiple adjusting position) lumbar support is provided on driver and front passenger seat to give you comfort while driving. It is adjusted by the lever provided on the side of the seat backrest.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p221_img03` (page 221, confidence 0.988)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p221_img03.png`

### Concept

Do not apply excessive force on venti­ lation button as it may get damaged. Button operates with slight finger force as they are electronically controlled.

text:
# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

>> Driver Assistance >> Drive assist

### Warning

Warning Behavior (When FCW and AEB Both OFF)

### Concept

When both FCW and AEB are disabled, the system does not respond to collision risks and the following tell- tale appears on the instrument cluster panel.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p165_img00` (page 165, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p165_img00.png`

### Warning

Warning Behavior (When Only FCW is ON)

### Warning

When Only FCW is ON, the system gives only one level of warning. The driver is alerted to the risk of an imminent collision by visual and audible warning which may

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p165_img01` (page 165, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p165_img01.png`

### Concept

be accompanied by a short brake pulse.

### Warning

Warning Behavior (When FCW and AEB Both ON)

### Warning

When both FCW and AEB are ON, the system gives two level of warning along with brake intervention as described below.

### Warning

1st Warning - The driver is alerted to the risk of an imminent collision by visual and audible warning which may be accompa­ nied by a short brake pulse.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p165_img02` (page 165, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p165_img02.png`

### Warning

2nd Warning - If the driver does not take action or the driver braking force is not enough to mitigate collision, system issues the second level of visual and audible warning and applies emergency braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_003_p165_img03` (page 165, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_003/p165_img03.png`

### Concept

After the vehicle has come to a complete halt post emergency braking, the system holds the vehicle stationary for around 2 seconds. After these 2 seconds it is driver responsibility to control the vehicle and to prevent it from moving forward or creep­ ing.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

VEHICLE PARKING FOR LONG DU- RATION

### Concept

(Non - Use maintenance)

### Concept

If you want to park your vehicle at one place for long duration, following care is to be taken:

### Concept

1. Park the vehicle in covered, dry and if possible well-ventilated premises. En- gage a gear.

### Concept

2. Remove the battery terminal cables (first remove the cable from the nega- tive terminal). Ensure that battery is fully charged.

### Concept

3. Block the wheel or engage in the gear mode.

### Concept

4. Clean and protect the painted parts using protective wax.

### Concept

5. Clean and protect the shiny metal parts using commercially available special compounds.

### Concept

6. Sprinkle talcum powder on the rubber windscreen wiper and lift them off the glass.

### Concept

7. Wiper blade lifting sequence during cleaning / replacing, first lift front pas-

### Concept

senger side wiper blade, then driver side blade.

### Concept

8. Slightly open the windows.

### Concept

9. Cover the vehicle with a cloth or perfo- rated plastic sheet. Do not use sheets of imperforated plastic as they do not allow moisture on the vehicle body to evaporate.

### Specification

10. Inflate the tyres to 0.5 bar above the normal specified pressure and check it at regular intervals.

### Concept

11. Check the battery charge every six weeks.

### Concept

12. Do not drain the engine cooling sys- tem.

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

• ASA is enabled through driver assist settings. • Adaptive Cruise Control is active and not overridden by driver accelerator pedal input. • All prerequisites of ACC are met. • Standard lane markings are detected clearly on any one side. • Lane markings on both sides are clearly visible. • Lane width is as per standard road building norms applicable to the coun- try (typically 2.5-4.5 metres) • The vehicle position is stable, entirely within lane boundaries and the lane is recognized by the system. • Turn indicators are OFF. • Steering wheel position should be sta- ble and not to be turned suddenly. • Vehicle speed should be within 30 to 165 kmph. • No malfunctions of Adaptive Steering Assist & Electronic Stability Control systems

### Concept

Once activated, the system can continue operation when lane markings are de- tected on only one side, or if lane mark- ings are not detected on either side but a preceding vehicle is being followed. User Settings

### Concept

Adaptive Steering Assist can be selected from the driver assist settings from Info- tainment screen. Follow the following sequence: Go to Home page » All Apps » Settings » Driver Assist Following the Preceding Vehicle Path

### Concept

Once activated, the system can follow the path of a preceding vehicle (excluding 2- wheeled vehicles such as bicycles, mo- torcycles, scooters etc.) and continue of- fering assistance even when lane mark- ing detection is not clear, when the follow- ing conditions are met:

### Concept

• Vehicle speed is lower than 75 km/hr (once activated, this mode of control

### Concept

shall be released when the vehicle speed exceeds 80 km/hr). • Distance between driven vehicle and preceding vehicle is within 50 meters (once activated, this mode of control shall be released when the distance exceeds 70 meters). • The preceding vehicle’s path has not deviated too much with respect to driven vehicle, or with respect to the path predicted for the preceding vehi- cle by the system. System Limitation Scenarios

### Concept

ASA system is subject to system limita- tions and may be unavailable or degraded performance or give false warnings in fol- lowing situations.

### Concept

• Inclement weather (rain, snow, fog, dust, haze, mist etc.) • Camera blockage (direct sunlight or headlamp glare on camera, mud/ dirt/moisture/stickers/debris on wind- shield surface in front of camera etc.) • Low ambient light (headlamps of driven vehicle/ tail lamps of preceding

Avoid heavy loads, e.g. driving at full throttle, during this period. Change gears judiciously. IMPORTANT INFORMATION Vehicle in Water Logged Condition

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p14_img00` (page 14, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p14_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p14_img01` (page 14, confidence 0.814)
