### Concept

Before driving through water - logged areas, ensure that the water level is below the air - intake snorkel entry. Unseen potholes could damage under surface of the vehicle. • Drive slowly and maintain constant acceleration. • After passing the water logged area ensure to press brakes intermittently to dry the brake disc.

### Concept

• Do not drive through heavily water - logged areas. • Water may enter the engine throu - gh the air - intake snorkel, which can cause serious engine damage. • Battery may get damaged or short circuited.

### Warning

WARNING • If your vehicle gets flooded wait for water level to recede. • Once the water has receded, ap- proach the vehicle, open all doors, and let the water inside the vehicle get drained completely. • Remove floor carpet and open the rubber/plastic gourmet provided on floor board, stepney space for wa- ter to recede from interior flooring of the vehicle completely. • Push your vehicle to safe place do not try to start the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p14_img03` (page 14, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p14_img03.png`

### Concept

• The resonator drain plug should be opened and any accumulated wat- er drained during every scheduled service. • If the vehicle is submerged in wat- er, we recommend to kindly conta- ct TATA MOTORS Authorised Ser- vice Centre.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p14_img02` (page 14, confidence 0.941)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p14_img02.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p14_img04` (page 14, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p14_img04.png`

### Concept

In case of vehicle fire, immediately evac- uate vehicle and contact local fire tender responder. They possess proper training and equipment to safely extinguish vehi- cle fire. Contact nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre for further as- sistance.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p15_img00` (page 15, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p15_img00.png`

### Warning

WARNING • Do not modify your vehicle. • Do not install high-wattage bulbs, non-genuine lamps, or horns. • Do not modify suspension, wheels,

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p15_img01` (page 15, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p15_img01.png`

### Concept

tyres. • Stick to manufacturer recom- mended parts. Safety matters. • Avoid tampering with the wiring harness, it can lead to short cir- cuits. • Be cautious with retrofitted CNG kits. Improper installation can cause leaks or fire hazards.

### Concept

Do not store or carry inflammable ma- terials in the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p15_img02` (page 15, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p15_img02.png`

### Concept

Vehicle Cyber Attack

### Concept

Modern vehicles are equipped with inter- net connectivity for navigation, entertain- ment, and diagnostics, making them vul- nerable to Cyber Attacks. Vehicles collect and store personal data, which can be targeted by hackers. Cyber Attacks can compromise infotain- ment system, brakes, steering, and en- gine control, leading to severe cyber risk

### Concept

Vehicle Cyber Security

### Concept

• Refrain from connecting the vehicle to public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks. • Ensure your vehicle is physically se- cured by locking doors and parking in safe areas to prevent from unauthor- ised access. • Never leave your keys in the car, even if you are nearby. • Keep your vehicle updated with latest software versions. • Pay attention to any security alerts or notifications and follow the guidelines.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p15_img03` (page 15, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p15_img03.png`

### Concept

• Disable the bluetooth of the car where not required and vehicle is not in use.

### Concept

• Keep infotainment app’s login creden- tials private & do not share it with an- yone.

### Concept

• Safety consciousness not only en- sures your safety and the safety of other road users, but it also helps to reduce the wear and tear on your ve- hicle.

### Concept

• How quickly you make decisions to avoid an accident.

### Concept

• Your ability to concentrate.

### Concept

• How well you can see and judge ob- jects.

### Concept

• How well familiar you are with your ve- hicle controls and its capabilities.

### Concept

• Turn ‘ON’ the side indicators at least 30 meters before taking a turn or changing the lane.

### Concept

• Decelerate to a safe speed before tak- ing turn. Do not apply brakes during cornering.

### Concept

• When overtaking other vehicles, watch out for the oncoming vehicle.

### Concept

• Never drive under the influence of al- cohol or drugs.

### Concept

• If your vehicle is equipped with info- tainment/navigation system, set and make changes to your travel route only when the vehicle is parked.

### Concept

• Program radio presets with the vehicle parked, and use your programmed presets to make radio use quicker and simpler.

### Concept

• If your car gets flooded and has soaked carpeting or water on the flooring, you should not try to start the engine, we recommend to kindly con- tact TATA MOTORS Authorised Ser- vice Centre.

### Concept

• While re-fuelling, switch OFF the en- gine and avoid the usage of mobile phone.

### Concept

Do not remove the labels attached at different places on your vehicle, they include safety instructions or vehicle specifications.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p17_img00` (page 17, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p17_img00.png`

### Concept

While Handling Hot Parts

### Concept

• Never remove the coolant cap when the engine is hot. The engine coolant is under high pressure and could splash on to skin/eyes causing severe burns.

### Concept

• Stay rod becomes hot enough after vehicle running, be careful while using it. Touch only rubber part available on stay rod.

### Concept

• Never touch engine exhaust after ve- hicle running as it will cause severe in- jury.

### Concept

• Do not touch tyre and wheel rim when it is hot after a long journey it may cause burn injury.

### Concept

Your vehicle is provided with good seating comfort. To make your journey more safe and enjoyable we recommend you to fol- low below warnings and cautions.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p18_img04` (page 18, confidence 0.833)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p18_img04.png`

### Concept

Front Passenger Seat

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p18_img00` (page 18, confidence 0.994)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p18_img00.png`

### Concept

Never ride in a vehicle with a front seat ‐ back fully reclined. This may lead to serious injuries. Fitment of seat co- vers on front passenger seat with air- bags is strictly prohibited.

### Concept

The rear seatback must be securely latched. If not, passengers and ob- jects could be thrown forward resulting in serious injury in the event of a sud- den stop or collision. Luggage and other objects in the boot should be kept flat. If large, heavy, or piled they must be secured properly. No passen- ger should ride in the boot area or sit or lie on folded seatbacks while the vehicle is in motion.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p18_img01` (page 18, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p18_img01.png`

### Concept

Applicable for Hatchback/SUV

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p18_img02` (page 18, confidence 0.994)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p18_img02.png`

### Concept

• Under no circumstances should ob- jects be piled higher than the seat- backs. Failure to follow these warn- ings could result in serious injury in the event of a sudden stop or colli- sion. Ensure that objects are se- curely fastened.

### Concept

• Do not adjust seat while driving/ve- hicle is moving. Doing so could re- sult in loss of control, and an acci- dent causing death, serious injury, or property damage.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p18_img03` (page 18, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p18_img03.png`

### Concept

• Always sit as far back as possible from the steering wheel while main- taining comfortable control of the vehicle. Fitment of seat covers on driver seat with airbags is strictly prohibited.

### Concept

• Do not keep any sitting cushion on the seat. This may result in serious or fatal injury in the event of an ac- cident.

### Concept

• After adjusting the seat make sure it is securely locked by pushing it forward and backward without us- ing the lock release lever. Sudden or unexpected movement of the driver ’ s seat could cause to lose control of the vehicle resulting in an accident.

### Concept

• All passengers must be seated in seats and restrained with seat belts properly while riding in vehicle.

### Concept

• If there are occupants in the rear seats, be careful while adjusting the front seat position.

### Concept

• Storing items against seatback or in any other way interfering with the proper locking of a seatback could result in serious or fatal injury in a sudden stop or collision After reset- ting the seatback to its seating po- sition make sure it is securely latched by pushing it forward and backward.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p19_img00` (page 19, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p19_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p19_img05` (page 19, confidence 0.999)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p19_img05.png`

### Concept

Head Restraint Front Seat

### Procedure

Adjust the head restraint so that it is as close to the head as possible and center of the head restraint supports the back of the head at eye level.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p19_img01` (page 19, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p19_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p19_img02` (page 19, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p19_img02.png`

### Concept

Do not drive the vehicle without the seat head restraints. Head restraints are intended to help reduce injuries during an accident.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p19_img03` (page 19, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p19_img03.png`

### Procedure

Adjust the head restraint so that it is as close to the head as possible and the cen- ter of the head restraint supports the back of the head at eye level.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p19_img04` (page 19, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p19_img04.png`

### Concept

Your hands might cut or injured by the sharp edges of the seat mechanism during looking for small objects trapped under the seats or between the seat and the center console.

### Concept

This section describes your Vehicle’s Seat belts, Please read and follow all these instructions carefully to minimize risk of severe injury or death.

### Concept

• Seat belts are the primary restraint system in the vehicle. All occupants, including the driver, should always wear seat belts. Your vehicle is equipped with three point seat belts for all occupants.

### Concept

• Sit back and adjust the driver seat. Make sure that your seat is adjusted to a good driving position and the back of the seat is upright.

### Concept

Buckling the Seat Belt

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p20_img00` (page 20, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p20_img00.png`

### Concept

• Grasp the tongue then slowly pull out the seat belt over the shoulder and across the chest. When the seat belt is long enough to fit, insert the tongue into the lock buckle until you hear a “CLICK” which indicates that the seat- belt is securely locked. (Refer to “IN- SERT TO LOCK” image)

### Concept

• Position the lap portion of the seat belt across your pelvic bone, below your abdomen. To remove slack, pull up a bit on the shoulder seat belt. To

### Concept

loosen the lap portion seat belt if it is too tight, tilt the tongue and pull on the lap seat belt. A snug seat belt reduces the risk of sliding under the seat belt in a collision. Ensure that the seat belt running over the body (shoulder seg- ment and lap segment) does not have any twist. Twisted seat belt may not offer effective protection when re- quired.

### Concept

• Ensure that the seat belt webbing is straight and not twisted. Twisted seat belts may not work properly in case of collision.

### Note

NOTE It is not advised by TATA MOTORS to remove the mini tongue from small buckle, located at rear middle seat.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p20_img01` (page 20, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p20_img01.png`

### Concept

Releasing the Seat Belt

### Concept

To release the seat belt, push the red but- ton on the lock buckle (refer “PRESS TO UNLOCK” image). Ensure to hold seat belt during unlocking and release it slowly towards the seat belt mounting. The seat belt will automatically retract to its stowed position. If necessary, slide the tongue down the webbing to allow the seat belt to retract fully.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p21_img00` (page 21, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p21_img00.png`

### Concept

Due to retractor reversal action if you leave the seat belt from the unlock po- sition it may hit you or parts like glass in the way which may cause injury to you or damage to the vehicle.

### Concept

• Each seating position and seat belt assembly must be used by one oc- cupant.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p21_img01` (page 21, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p21_img01.png`

### Concept

• Be careful not to damage or tamper the seat belt webbing or hardware. Inspect the seat belt system period- ically, checking for cuts, frays, or

### Concept

loose parts. A frayed or torn seatbelt could rip apart in a collision and leave you with no protection.

### Concept

• If the seat belt webbing or hardware is damaged, get it replaced immedi- ately at TATA MOTORS Authorised service centre.

### Concept

• Do not insert any items such as coins, clips, etc. into the seat belt buckles, and be careful not to spill liquids into these parts. If foreign materials get into a seat belt buckle, the seat belt will not work properly.

### Concept

• Do not wear seat belts over hard, sharp, or fragile items in clothing, such as pens, keys, spectacles, etc.

### Concept

• Do not use any accessories on seat belts or modify in any way the seat- belt system. Devices claiming to im- prove occupant comfort or reposi- tioning the seat belt, can reduce the protection provided by the seat belt and increase the chance of serious injury in a collision.

### Concept

Seat Belt Height Adjustments

### Concept

If a seat belt height adjuster is provided, the occupant should adjust it so that the shoulder belt is centered across the mid- dle of the shoulder, provides proper over- lap, stays away from the neck and face, and does not slip off the shoulder.

Procedure for filling DEF in DEF tank

### Concept

• Ensure vehicle is parked in plain sur- face in no load condition (vehicle should be empty without passengers or luggage)

### Concept

• Ensure ignition is in OFF position (re- move key from barrel, if provided)

### Concept

• Wait for 6 minutes after ignition off.

### Concept

### Warning

• If “DEF level low, Refill Soon “Warning message appears in the cluster, it in- dicates that DEF needs to be topped up. In case you are refilling the DEF yourself, fill only maximum 7.0 litres

### Concept

• Wait for 6 minutes after filling DEF.

### Concept

• Turn ON the ignition and wait till DEF level gets updated in instrument clus- ter. Start the vehicle.

### Concept

• If still problem persist contact nearest Authorised Tata dealer immediately.

### Concept

### Concept

These messages will be indicated when DEF level is low. This can happen when vehicle runs without filling DEF in spite of message to fill DEF.

• First warning message will be indi- cated at approximately in between 1500 – 2400 km before emptying of DEF tank at the current DEF con- sumption rate. “DEF LEVEL LOW, REFILL SOON” message will be indi- cated at this warning level.

title: INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES
text:
# INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Do’s And Don’ts. Do’s • All doors should be locked including tailgate and bonnet.

### Concept

• Low fuel level indication should be in OFF state.

### Concept

• Park brake should be fully engaged and gear position should be in neutral state.

### Concept

• Vehicle should be at rest position.

### Concept

• Don’t trigger command immediately af- ter vehicle lock wait for 15 sec.

### Concept

• Don’t park vehicle on higher slope plane this may cause RESS Fail.

### Concept

• Don’t trigger command back to back provide some delay.

### Concept

• Don’t trigger command immediately if command fails in previous cycle.

### Concept

REMOTE AC CONTROL (RAC) (if equipped)

### Concept

The remote AC feature improves the user experience and comfort by providing the remote climate control from the mobile App. Using this feature, the user can remotely access the vehicle using the connected car smartphone app and start the pre- conditioning (AC ON/OFF) before reach- ing the vehicle.

### Concept

Operating Conditions

### Procedure

1. In the Ignition OFF condition user can turn ON the AC from outside the vehi- cle using mobile App. 2. In the mobile App user need to pro- vide the set timer value (Set Timer) and set temperature value (set temp) before giving the remote AC request. 3. Based on the user’s set temperature FATC will start the climate control in auto mode with the requested temper- ature once the engine is ON remotely.

### Concept

Failure Conditions / Time Killer

### Concept

• Ignition/Engine is ON manually before sending the command through mobile App.

### Concept

• The battery voltage of the vehicle is below or above Threshold value.

### Concept

• AC is ON before sending the com- mand through mobile App.

### Concept

• Hand Brake is not fully engaged or electronic park brake not engaged.

### Concept

• Any of the door/bonnet/tailgate is left opened.

### Concept

• The steering of the vehicle is in un- locked state.

### Concept

• The vehicle speed is NOT zero and the low fuel level indication is ON.

### Concept

• The accelerator/clutch/brake pedal is already ENGAGED.

### Concept

• Vehicle is NOT in neutral gear.

### Concept

DIGITAL DISPLAY (10.25” INCH) (if equipped )

### Note

Note: All instrument cluster images are for reference only and may vary depending on your vehicle model.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p103_img00` (page 103, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p103_img00.png`

### Warning

Gauge Information Note / Warning

### Concept

Speedometer The Speedometer Indicates the actual vehicle speed in km/h

### Concept

• At every key IN and Ignition ON, the speedometer Bar moves to MAX and return to ‘0’ position. • This is welcome strategy and self-check feature.

### Concept

Odometer Odometer Indicates distance travelled by ve- hicle.

### Concept

• The odometer reading does not return to 0 when max- imum value is reached, the display will freeze to maxi- mum value.

### Concept

Tachometer Tachometer indicates the engine speed in revolutions per minute.

### Warning

Warning: • Whenever engine is accelerated beyond safe RPM, ta- chometer Bar Indication turns RED. In such case, re- duce the engine RPM immediately. • Never drive the vehicle with engine in high RPM. This may cause severe engine damage. Note: At every key in and Ignition ON, tachometer moves to MAX and return to ‘0’ position. This is a welcome strategy and a self-check feature. In Engine running condition if the Tachometer is not show- ing the RPM, take your vehicle to TATA MOTORS Author- ised Service Centre .

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in “ON” position, fuel gauge gives an approximate indication of the amount of fuel in the fuel tank. “F” stands for full and “E” stands for Empty.

### Warning

• On inclines, curves, during braking and sudden accel- eration due to the movement of fuel in the tank, the fuel level display may fluctuate or the low fuel level warning lamp may turns ON/OFF earlier or delayed than usual.

### Warning

Gauge Information Note / Warning

### Warning

When fuel in the tank is near to empty posi- tion, low fuel warning telltale turns Amber. Refill the tank as soon as possible. At every key in and Ignition ON, Fuel Gauge Bar move to F and come back to E position. This is welcome strategy.

### Warning

• When the ignition switch is in “ON” position, this gauge gives an approximate indication of the amount of fuel in the fuel tank and it takes few sec- onds to stabilize after the ignition is turned ON. Warning: When Cluster detect Low Fuel level, It blinks last fuel bar with 1Hz frequency and Fuel tank symbol is con- tinue ON state. If there is any fault in the system, Low fuel warning symbol shall blink. Take your vehicle to the nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre .

### Warning

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” posi- tion, this gauge indicates the engine coolant temperature. The indicator should be within normal, ac- ceptable temperature range i.e., between “H” and “C”. If the indicator approaches “H”, over- heating is indicated by red LED bar in case of 4”. The RED bar and High Coolant temp warning telltale indicates overheating that may dam- age the engine.

### Note

• If the coolant temperature reading is very high, The Engine coolant temperature telltale flashes with an audible buzzer. • In this case, stop the vehicle, switch ‘OFF’ the en- gine and cool it down for some time. Contact a nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Cen- tre immediately for rectification. Note: At every key in and Ignition ON, Temperature Gauge moves to H and return to C position for 10” Cluster. This is welcome strategy and self-check feature.

### Warning

Gauge Information Note / Warning

### Concept

Continuing to drive the vehicle when engine overheating is indicated can result in severe engine damage or fire.

### Warning

Warning: Never remove the radiator pressure cap from the radia- tor when the engine is hot. Do not restart the engine until the problem has been duly attended.

### Concept

Instantaneous Fuel Economy

### Concept

Updates display “Instantaneous Fuel con- sumption” at regular time interval in bar graph.

### Concept

Maintain INST FE bar graph above 15 km/l to achieve better fuel economy.

### Concept

Trip Meter A: Trip A Indicates distance traveled by vehicle since last reset within the range of 0 km to 9999.9 km with the resolution of 0.1 km. Trip Meter B: Trip B Indicates distance traveled by vehicle since last reset within the range of 0 km to 9999.9 km with the resolution of 0.1 km.

### Concept

Trip A can be RESET to 0 by pressing Set switch when display is in a TRIP A mode. Trip B can be RESET to 0 by pressing Set switch when display is in a TRIP A mode.

title: EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN
text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

## Knowledge

### Concept

How to Proceed In The Event Of a Tyre Puncture in Two Steps

### Warning

First pump the tyre sealant and air into the tyre (see Step 1).Immediately there-after, drive a short distance (3-10 km) in order to distribute the sealant in the tyre. After that check the tyre pressure and pump more air into the tyre if necessary (see Step 2). Then you can proceed to drive with caution for a maximum distance of 200 kms. Step 1: Pumping the Tyre Sealant and Air into the Tyre

### Procedure

• Take out the hose and power plug with cable out of the tyre puncture repair kit casing. Remove the white cap of T-type connector of Sealant Bottle. • Connect the hose pipe of the compres- sor with T-type connector of sealant bot- tle. Ensure it is tightly Fitted. • Avoid skin contact with the sealant which contains natural rubber latex. Do not open pressure "air release" valve. Use enclosed protective gloves.

### Procedure

• Install sealant Bottle by rotating clock- wise firmly against the bottle holding grooves on the compressor. Remove the white cap of the hose pipe of the sealant bottle. • Insert power plug into the 12 volt power socket connection. • Start the vehicle in idling (only if the ve- hicle is outdoors or in a well ventilated area). • Press compressor switch to ON Im- portant: When pumping in the sealant through the tyre valve, the pressure may rise up to 500 KPa (5 bar. 73 psi) but will drop again after about 30 sec- onds. • Inflate the tyre to an inflation pressure of minimum 180kPa, (1.8 bar/26 psi) and a maximum of 300kPa (3 bar/43psi). • Remove the sealant bottle from the compressor grooves & tight the white caps on the hose pipe of the sealant bottle as well as T -type connector of the sealant bottle. This avoids unexpected leakage of sealant residue and Lock it.

### Concept

• Make sure the puncture repair kit stored safely, but it’s still easily accessible, in the vehicle. • The compressor will be needed again when you check the tyre pressure

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p338_img00` (page 338, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p338_img00.png`

### Concept

• Ensure pump should not be ON for more than 10 min as it may heat up and stop working.

### Procedure

• Check the sidewall of the tyre prior to inflation. If there are any cracks, bumps or similar damage, do not at- tempt to inflate the tyre. Do not stand directly beside the tyre while the compressor is pumping. Watch the sidewall of the tyre. If any cracks, bumps or similar damage appear, turn off the compressor and let the air out by means of the pressure “air release” valve. In this case, do not continue to use the tyre.

text:
# INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

POWER SUNROOF (if equipped)

### Concept

It brings natural light and fresh air into passenger compartment. The cabin be- comes more illuminated and bright which gives pleasant feeling while driving and makes driving experience more enjoyable and relaxed.

### Concept

Sunroof allows air to flow evenly from the roof which is quieter and less intrusive than wind blowing through a side window.

### Concept

Sunroof can be operated by Electrical Switch, Voice Command and by Rain De- tection / Vehicle Lock.

### Concept

Power Sunroof Switch

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p288_img01` (page 288, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p288_img01.png`

### Procedure

Power sunroof switch is mounted in over- head console near the roof lamp. This switch is used to open, close, tilt up / down the sunroof as required. Condition to operate sunroof ignition / vehicle ON. 1. Push the knob away from the wind shield to open the sunroof. It has two detents. • 1st detent: First click (Express op- eration) only sunshade will get open. • 2nd detent: Second Click (Sun shade and Sunroof both will get open) 2. Push the knob towards the windshield to close the sunroof. It has two de- tents. • 1st detent: First click (Express op- eration) (only sunroof will get close). • 2nd detent: Second Click (Sunroof and sunshade will get closed). 3. Press at the centre of the knob for tilt up / down function.

text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

• User can change/set the time gap in active and standby mode by pressing ACC time gap switch.

### Concept

• When User presses ACC OFF button from Steering wheel, this turns ACC OFF.

### Concept

• When User Engages ACC at a speed lower than 30kmph and more than 7 kmph, then ACC speed will be set as 30kmph and vehicle speed will in- crease to 30kmph if there is no obsta- cle present in the path.

### Concept

• When User Engages ACC at a speed higher than 30kpmh, then that speed will be set as ACC speed and vehicle will cruise at that speed if no obstacle is present in the path.

### Concept

• If ACC is ON/Engaged and User Acti- vates the Hill Descent Control (HDC) function by pressing the HDC button, then ACC will be OFF/Standby. If HDC is already activated and user tries to activate the ACC, then ACC won’t be active. HDC function has al- ways higher priority than ACC.

### Concept

• Overtake Assist Control (OAC): Dur- ing the Follow Control mode, if the driver wants to overtake the target ve- hicle, OAC function will help to over- take the target vehicle by enhancing the acceleration smoothly. For OAC activation, Turn indicator must be ON and minimum host vehicle speed should be 20kmph.

### Concept

Active Cruise Mode – If there is no vehi- cle in the path of subject vehicle, then it will cruise at a speed equal to ACC set speed.

### Concept

Active Follow Mode – If there is a vehicle in the path of the subject vehicle, then it will maintain a distance from the target ve- hicle equivalent to the distance set by the user.

### Concept

# INFOTAINMENT SYSTEM DISPLAY

## Knowledge

### Concept

INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES

### Concept

The size and type of the infotainment system display screen may vary de- pending on the specific variant of your vehicle.

### Concept

Master / Force Reset Process

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p297_img01` (page 297, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p297_img01.png`

### Concept

If your infotainment system touch screen becomes unresponsive or shows some unusual behaviour, then you can restart it to potentially resolve the issue. Follow

### Concept

some basic steps given below and you can restart the system. To restart the infotainment system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p297_img02` (page 297, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p297_img02.png`

### Concept

1. Park the vehicle. 2. Hold the Steering wheel Mute button (long press) for more than 10 secs and then release the button as soon as the display goes blank. 3. The step above will trigger the info- tainment system restart procedure. Wait until the system restarts.

### Concept

4. When you hold the Steering wheel Mute button for more than 15 sec, sys- tem aborts restart process and display turns ON.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p297_img03` (page 297, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p297_img03.png`

### Concept

• It is preferable to do one Ignition OFF to ON cycle after Mas- ter/Force reset to synchronize ve- hicle settings with the TATA Info- tainment System.

### Concept

• If the reboot does not work or mas- ter/force resets are required on a weekly or daily basis, vehicle shall be taken to dealership. There, the dealer can update your firmware or inspect the system for hard- ware problems.

### Concept

• Force/Master reset keeps the stored data, such as call history, text message information, and previously paired phones as it is.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND CARE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Special Care for Tubeless Tyres

### Concept

• When you remove the tyre and install it back on the rim, take precautions not to damage tyre bead. Use tyre re- moval and assembly machines. Dam- age or cut on tyre bead may cause gradual loss of air and deflation of tyres.

### Concept

• Do not scratch the inner surface of tubeless tyre with metallic or sharp ob- jects. Tubeless tyres are coated with impermeable layer of rubber from the inner surface which holds the air in the tyre. Removal of this layer due to scratching may cause gradual loss of air and deflation.

### Concept

• If wheel rim gets damaged in service, get the wheel rim repaired/ replaced immediately. Running the vehicle with damaged rim may cause deflation of tyre and subsequent dislodging of tyre from rim.

### Concept

• Keep the recommended inflation pres- sure. Over-inflation, in particular, may cause puncture or bursting of tyres.

### Concept

Life and wear pattern of tyres de- pends on various parameters like tyre pressure, wheel alignment, wheel balancing, tyre rotation, etc. It also largely depends on vehicle speed, load carried, usage, driving habits, road conditions, tyre quality, etc.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p398_img00` (page 398, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p398_img00.png`

### Concept

In case fault is suspected to be due to poor quality of tyres, the same may be taken up with concerned tyre man- ufacture

### Concept

Summer tyres have a tread designed to provide superior performance on dry pavement. However, the performance of these tyres will be substantially reduced in wet conditions. If you operate your vehicle on wet roads, use all season tyres for all four wheels. Special Winter Equipment

### Concept

It is recommended that the following items be carried in the vehicle during winter:

### Concept

• A scraper and stiff-bristled brush to re- move ice and snow from the windows and wiper blades. • A shovel to dig the vehicle out of snow drifts. • Extra windshield-washer fluid to refill the reservoir tank.

Avoid stiff bris- tled brushes that may cause scratches.

In case of damage to matte paint fin- ish, whole area is required to be re- worked as it is not possible to repair only the damage area. Extreme care is required as it is difficult to restore quality after the repair. Always take your vehicle to Authorized workshop for repair.

text:
# 16. Dynamic Braking Support (DBS)

## Knowledge

### Concept

• The Safety of the vehicles always lies in the hands of the driver, never rely on the HBA feature to prevent accidents.

### Concept

12. Hydraulic Fading Compensation (HFC)

### Concept

In dangerous fading situations, most driv- ers operate the brake pedal with a small or regular braking force and they never reach to the maximum possible vehicle deceleration. The moment temperature rises, the HFC system automatically com- pensates for this by increasing the hy- draulic pressure in relation to the force ap- plied to the pedal. The HFC function im- prove the stopping distance by eliminat- ing require pressure build-up lag by the driver.

### Concept

• The HFC feature is provided to as- sist the driver in cases of emer- gency the capabilities of an HFC

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p43_img00` (page 43, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p43_img00.png`

### Concept

equipped vehicle must never be ex- ploited in a reckless or dangerous manner. • The Safety of the vehicles always lies in the hands of the driver, never rely on the HFC feature to prevent accidents. 13. Dynamic Wheel Torque by Brake (DWT-B)

### Concept

The main goal of the function is to im- prove the agility of a vehicle and to enable a more direct steering. This is mainly achieved by braking interventions at the inner wheels during turning. DWT-B re- duces understeer tendency of the car and a higher curve speed can be achieved. 14. Engine Drag Torque Control (EDTC)

### Concept

On slippery road conditions during in- gear Braking or Shift down of gear or sud- den throttle release causes high Engine drag on the driven wheel resulting into brake slip situations without any brake ap- plication.

### Concept

This makes vehicle highly under steera- ble. EDTC controls such brake slip on the driven wheels by increasing the engine torque to makes the vehicle stable and steerable.

### Concept

15. Panic Brake Alert (PBA)

### Warning

Panic brake alert warns vehicles ap- proaching from behind when emergency or heavy braking takes place. The func- tion will trigger Hazard lamps automati- cally, which will act as an immediate warning to vehicles directly behind and nearby. PBA is an immediate and urgent warning to all vehicles around thus im- proving their response time to unforeseen braking situations.

### Concept

Dynamic Braking support feature makes use of the data from the forward facing ve- hicle sensors to detect a crash imminent scenario, and if the driver doesn’t brake hard enough to avoid a crash, the brake control system supplements the braking by driver.

### Concept

• The HFC feature is provided to as- sist the driver in cases of emer- gency the capabilities of an HFC equipped vehicle must never be ex- ploited in a reckless or dangerous manner. • The Safety of the vehicles always lies in the hands of the driver, never rely on the HFC feature to prevent accidents. 17. After Impact Braking (AIB)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p44_img00` (page 44, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p44_img00.png`

### Warning

In the event of primary collision there are chances that vehicle can no longer be safely controlled. Accident analysis has shown that an active brake intervention would mitigate the effect of the subse- quent collisions. After impact braking sys- tem is activated automatically and brakes the car in a safe manner to mitigate sec- ondary collision. Hazard & brake lights are triggered to intimate surrounding us- ers of an emergency situation. Warning lights will continue flashing after vehicle

### Concept

comes to a standstill. The driver can over- ride the system by depressing the brake/acc pedal if there is a risk of being hit by following traffic.

#### Visual References

The basic assumption for the AIB to work is that the brake system is intact after the primary impact.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Warning

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p231_img00` (page 231, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p231_img00.png`

### Concept

Park Assist System Limitations

### Concept

The Reverse Park Assist system is not a collision ‑ avoidance system. It is solely the driver’s responsibility to park the vehicle safely. The Reverse Park Assist feature operates using ultrasonic echo technology; there- fore, its performance is not guaranteed under the following conditions:

### Concept

• If an object has a sharp ‑ edged sur- face or a surface that causes ultra- sonic echoes to disperse, the object may not be detected properly. • If an object is a mesh fence or is made of thin wires that cannot suffi- ciently reflect ultrasonic echoes, de- tection may be limited. • Fast ‑ moving objects passing through the sensor’s detection field may not be detected because the system may not process the ultrasonic echoes in time. • If an object is made of or covered with foam, sponge, snow, ice, mud, dirt, slush, frost, or water droplets (for ex- ample, after washing the vehicle or during rain), ultrasonic signals may be absorbed or distorted, resulting in reduced detection performance. • If the sensor surface or the area around the sensor is covered by a hand, sticker, accessory, protective film, or aftermarket coating, the sys- tem may not operate properly.

### Warning

• Objects close to the rear bumper may not be detected, depending on the limits of the detection field. Drivers should always exercise caution while parking.

### Concept

• Detection performance may be af- fected if the vehicle’s ride height changes due to heavy cargo or load, incorrect tire pressure, suspension modifications, or other vehicle altera- tions.

### Concept

title: 24 X 7 ROADSIDE ASSISTANCE Dear Customer,
text:
# 24 X 7 ROADSIDE ASSISTANCE Dear Customer,

## Knowledge

### Concept

EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

### Concept

It is our responsibility and our endeavour to ensure that you have our complete ser- vice backup if ever, wherever and when- ever you need the same. When you have a road network that spans wide area, the probability of a breakdown happening within hailing distance of a TATA MO- TORS Authorised Workshop is very low.

### Concept

It is precisely for this reason, we have tied up with TVS Auto Assist and Allianz ser- vice provider, who will provide on-road services for repairable breakdown assis- tance including towing to the nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Workshop and ambulance for injured passenger to nearest hospital through their Authorised Service Providers (ASP).

### Specification

The 24X7 Roadside Assistance Program shall be automatically available to your vehicle for the duration of Warranty pe- riod. The program shall also be available, if you avail the same post warranty.

### Concept

Standard Procedure When Calling For Roadside Assistance In Case Of a Breakdown

### Concept

• Dial the toll free help line number – 1800 209 8282

### Concept

• Identify your vehicle with the Vehicle chassis number that is available in the Owner’s Manual.

### Concept

• Explain your exact location with land- marks and tell us about the problem you face with the vehicle.

### Warning

• Park your vehicle on the edge of the road, open the bonnet and put on the hazard warning signal.

### Warning

title: SUPPLEMENTARY RESTRAINT SYSTEM (SRS - AIRBAGS)
text:
# SUPPLEMENTARY RESTRAINT SYSTEM (SRS - AIRBAGS)

## Knowledge

### Concept

The SRS [Supplementary Restraint system] is designed to provide protection to occu- pants in case of collision or sudden impact, when a crash is detected, the SRS airbag system deploys airbags to help reduce the risk of injury to the occupant. It works in conjunction with seat belts.

### Concept

There are 7 airbags provided in your car :

### Concept

1. Diver Knee Airbag (if equipped) 2. Driver Airbag 3. Front Passenger Airbag 4. Side Airbag LH 5. Side Airbag RH 6. Curtain Airbag LH 7. Curtain Airbag RH The driver airbag is mounted in the centre of the steering wheel. Driver Knee airbag (if equipped) is mounted behind the dash- board panel below steering wheel. The front passenger airbag is located inside the dashboard in front of the passenger seat. The airbags have suitable indica- tions on steering wheel and on dash- board. Side airbags are mounted in front-row seats. Curtain airbags are mounted above the doors along the roof on both sides. The word ‘AIRBAG’ is marked at adjacent locations of respective airbags.

### Concept

The ‘SRS’ system also comprises the fol- lowing components depending upon the provided safety features in vehicle.

### Concept

• Seat belt Pre-tensioners

### Concept

• Seat belt with load limiters

### Concept

• Airbag ‘SRS’ ECU (Electronic Control Unit)

### Concept

• SRS wiring harness

### Warning

• SRS Warning lamp The System is active when ignition switch is in the “ON” position or the ignition mode is “ON”. Airbags are designed to inflate in collisions when required. In the event of a collision, the collision sensors will detect signals, and if the Air- bag ECU judges that the signals repre- sent a severe collision, will trigger the air- bags. The inflated Airbags provide a cushion to the occupants. The Airbag in- flates and deflates so quickly that you may not even realize that it has activated. The Airbag will neither hinder your view nor make it hurdle to exit the vehicle.

### Concept

Airbag inflation is virtually instantaneous and occurs with considerable force, ac- companied by loud noise and smoke, which is normal. The inflated airbag, to- gether with seat belts, limits the move- ment of an occupant, thereby reducing the risk of injury. When an airbag inflates, you may see some smoke-like particles. The particles are a normal by-product of the process that generates the non-toxic gas used for airbag inflation. These airborne particles may irritate the skin, eyes, nose, or throat. If you have skin or eye irritation, rinse the area with water. For nose or throat irrita- tion, move to fresh air. Also sometimes the smoke can cause breathing problems, in such cases get fresh air promptly.

### Concept

It is not advisable to drive your vehicle af- ter the airbags have been deployed. If you are involved in another collision, the air- bags will not be in place to protect you.

### Concept

• Even in vehicles with airbags, all the occupants must always wear the seat belts provided. In order to min- imize the risk and severity of injury in the event of a collision.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p25_img00` (page 25, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p25_img00.png`

### Concept

• If an occupant is out of position dur- ing collision, the rapidly deploying Airbag may forcefully contact the oc- cupant causing serious or fatal inju- ries.

### Concept

• Open your windows and doors as soon as possible after a collision to reduce prolonged exposure to the smoke and powder released by the inflating Airbag. • Do not touch the Airbag container’s internal components immediately after an Airbag has inflated. The parts that come into contact with an inflating Airbag may be very hot. • Always wash exposed skin areas thoroughly with lukewarm water and mild soap.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p25_img01` (page 25, confidence 0.996)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p25_img01.png`

### Concept

• Always use seat belts and CRS at all times. Even with airbags, you can be seriously injured or killed in a col- lision if you are not wearing seat belt properly or not wearing seat belt when airbag inflates.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p26_img00` (page 26, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p26_img00.png`

### Concept

• All occupants should never sit or lean unnecessarily close to the Air- bags.

### Concept

• Move your seat as far back as pos- sible from front Airbags, while still maintaining control of the vehicle.

### Concept

• All occupants should sit upright with the seatback in an upright position, centered on the seat cushion with their seat belt on, legs comfortably extended and their feet on the floor until the vehicle is parked and en- gine is turned off.

### Concept

• Do not allow the front passenger to place their feet or legs on the dash- board.

### Concept

Passenger Airbag (PAB) Switch

### Concept

The passenger airbag switch is used to activate and de-activate the passenger airbag in the vehicle.

### Concept

The switch is located on the left side of the dashboard and can be accessed once the co-driver side door is opened.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p26_img01` (page 26, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p26_img01.png`

### Concept

When an adult is seated in the front pas- senger seat, ensure that PAB switch is turned to ‘ON’ position. This will ensure that the passenger airbag is operational in the event of a collision.

### Concept

If rearward facing child seat needs to be installed on front passenger seat to carry the child then ensure PAB switch is turned OFF. This will ensure that the passenger airbag will remain de-activated in the event of a collision .

### Concept

This switch can be operated by using me- chanical key / Key with remote / smart key as per vehicle variants. For more details refer “Keys” section in this Manual.

### Concept

Passenger Airbag (PAB) Indicator

### Concept

The passenger airbag indicator is pro- vided to notify an occupant, whether pas- senger airbag is activated (ON) or deac- tivated (OFF) in vehicle.

### Concept

The PAB indicator is positioned on the roof, close to the roof lamp.

### Concept

When the PAB switch is turned to ‘ON’ position to activate the airbag, ‘ON symbol & text’ will illuminate in amber color. PAB Indicator OFF:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p27_img02` (page 27, confidence 0.961)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img02.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p27_img05` (page 27, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img05.png`

### Concept

When the PAB switch is turned to ‘OFF’ position to deactivate the airbag, the ‘OFF symbol & text’ will illuminate in amber color.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p27_img06` (page 27, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img06.png`

### Concept

Wrong Seating Positions

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p27_img00` (page 27, confidence 0.962)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p27_img01` (page 27, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p27_img03` (page 27, confidence 0.792)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img03.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p27_img04` (page 27, confidence 0.477)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p27_img04.png`

### Concept

• Never place your arm over the air- bag as a deploying airbag can result in serious arm fractures or other in- juries.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p28_img00` (page 28, confidence 0.876)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p28_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p28_img01` (page 28, confidence 0.943)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p28_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p28_img03` (page 28, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p28_img03.png`

### Concept

• Do not allow the passengers to lean their heads or bodies onto doors or place objects between the doors and passengers when they are seated on seats equipped with side and/or curtain Airbags.

### Concept

• Do not place or stick any items in the vehicle, except at designated lo- cations (such as utility bins, cup/bottle holders, boot space, etc.). Loose items may act as a pro- jectile during a collision and cause severe to fatal injuries. • Please be aware that any unse- cured item in your vehicle, such as your pet, unsecured CRS, or a lap- top, can become a potential hazard in the event of a collision or sudden stop, causing injuries to occupants in the vehicle. • Coat hooks (if equipped) must be used only for that purpose. Never hang other items onto those hooks. This could affect deployment of the Airbags and may lead to severe to fatal injuries. • Always contact your TATA MO- TORS Authorised Service Centre if the vehicle is damaged, even if air- bag has not inflated or if any part of an airbag module cover shows signs of cracking or damage.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p28_img02` (page 28, confidence 0.943)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p28_img02.png`

### Concept

If your SRS malfunctions, the Airbag may not inflate properly during a colli- sion thereby increasing risk of serious injury or death. If any of the following conditions occur, your SRS is malfunc- tioning:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p29_img00` (page 29, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p29_img00.png`

### Warning

• The SRS warning lamp does not turn ‘ON’ when the ignition switch is placed in the ‘ON’ position for few seconds.

### Warning

• The SRS warning lamp stays ‘ON’ after illuminating.

### Warning

• The SRS warning lamp comes ‘ON’/stays ‘ON’ while the vehicle is in motion.

### Warning

• The SRS warning lamp blinks when the vehicle is running. We recommend to immediately visit TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre and get the SRS system in- spected if any of the above conditions occur.

### Concept

• Never make any modifications to your vehicle. The modifications car- ried out, but not limited to the vehicle frame, bumpers, front fenders, ride height, suspension, seat belts, inte- rior trims, and steering wheel (espe- cially holders), are not acceptable. This will affect the intended perfor- mance of SRS.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p29_img01` (page 29, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p29_img01.png`

### Concept

• Fitment of bull bars, seat covers on seats with airbags, etc., is strictly prohibited.

### Concept

• If you need to make any modifica- tions to accommodate any disability you may have, please contact your TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre for necessary guidance.

### Concept

• Do not tamper with SRS in any way. This will lead to unexpected perfor- mance of system and may cause serious injury or death.

### Warning

Airbag Warning Sticker on Front Passenger Sun Visor

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p29_img02` (page 29, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p29_img02.png`

### Warning

The Airbag Warning Symbol on sun visor reminds of the extreme hazards associ- ated with the use of a rearward-facing child restraint on front passenger seat during airbag deployment. It does not mean that a child cannot occupy front passenger seat and use seat belt. Please refer CRS section for recommended seat- ing positions for children.

### Concept

Never use a rearward-facing child re- straint on a seat protected by an ac- tive Airbag in front of it, Death or seri- ous injury to the child can occur.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p30_img00` (page 30, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p30_img00.png`

### Concept

Airbags Deployment Conditions

### Concept

When front airbags should not be de- ployed?

### Concept

Minor frontal collision : Seat belt (if worn) offers adequate occupant protec- tion in low-severity collisions. The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. De- ployment of frontal airbags is not benefi- cial in low severity collisions.

### Concept

Side collision : During a side collision, oc- cupants tend to move sideways. There- fore, deploying frontal airbags in such sit- uations will not benefit the occupants. Side airbags and side curtain airbags (if equipped) are specifically designed to re- duce the injuries that can occur in side collision.

### Concept

Rear collision: During a rear collision, occupants tend to move (rearwards) away from frontal airbags. Therefore, de- ploying frontal airbags in such situations will not protect the occupant. Head re- straints and seat belts provide occupant protection during a rear collision. Rollover collision: During a rollover col- lision, unbelted occupants may float in- side the passenger compartment. This will increase the risk of injuries and may prove to be fatal. Wearing seat belts pro- vides highly effective occupant protection during a rollover collision. Front airbags are not designed to deploy in a rollover as frontal airbags cannot offer any protection in rollover collision.

### Concept

When front airbags/side airbags/side curtain airbags (if equipped) deploy with minor or no visible vehicle dam- age? The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. The extent of vehicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. In some extreme/rare condi- tions; of rough road driving, running into a

### Concept

curb, or hitting other fixed objects; the air- bags may deploy depending upon the se- verity of a collision. In some of these con- ditions, damage to the vehicle may be mi- nor or not be readily visible.

### Concept

When front airbags/side airbags/side curtain airbags (if equipped) may not deploy, even with exterior visible vehi- cle damage?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. The amount of visible vehicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. Some collisions can result in visible damage but with no airbag deployment, because the airbags would not have been needed or would not have provided protection even if they had deployed. Seat belts, if worn, offer ade- quate occupant protection in such cases.

### Concept

• Do not leave unattended children in your vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p31_img00` (page 31, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p31_img00.png`

### Concept

• During reversing and parking, en- sure that children are far away from the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p31_img01` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p31_img01.png`

### Concept

• Do not put the safety seat belt under your child’s arm or behind its back.

### Concept

• Do not use pillows, books, or towels to boost your child’s height.

### Concept

• Do not allow children to stand up or kneel on either the rear or the front seats. An unrestrained child could suffer serious or fatal injuries during a collision.

### Concept

• Do not install a booster seat or a booster cushion with a seat belt that is slack or twisted.

### Concept

Child Restraint System (CRS)

### Specification

TATA MOTORS strongly recommends the use of Child Restraint Systems (CRS) for all children up to 36 Kg and to be placed at recommended positions only (Refer CRS Position table in this section).

### Concept

CRS can be installed in the vehicle using seat belts and/or ISOFIX with support leg (if equipped) or ISOFIX with Top Tether (if equipped). These ISOFIX attachment points are located on rear outboard seat- ing locations which enables quick and safe child seat engagement.

### Concept

ISOFIX with mounting eyelets

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p31_img02` (page 31, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p31_img02.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p31_img03` (page 31, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p31_img03.png`

### Concept

Top Tether mounting anchorages are lo- cated at backside of rear outboard seats. The harness system of CRS holds the child in place, and in a collision, acts to keep the child positioned in the seat and reduce the risk of injuries.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p32_img00` (page 32, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p32_img00.png`

### Concept

Keep children in a forward-facing or rear- ward facing CRS with a harness until they reach the size or age or weight limit rec- ommended by your CRS manufacturer.

### Concept

Selection and Installation of CRS

### Concept

Always select the CRS that complies with the latest safety standards (AIS 072 / ECE R44 / ECE R129). The CRS are classified according to the child’s size, height, and weight. Select the appropriate CRS for your child. Ensure that the child fits properly in the CRS and it is securely in- stalled in the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p32_img01` (page 32, confidence 0.96)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p32_img01.png`

### Concept

While installing the child seats always ad- here to the directions in this Owner’s Man- ual as well as those provided by the child seat’s manufacturer.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p32_img02` (page 32, confidence 0.96)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p32_img02.png`

### Specification

TATA MOTORS recommends Joie i- Spin Safe i-Size child seats for up to 18 Kg children. These seats are available at TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Cen- tre .

### Concept

TATA MOTORS recommends to keep the highlighted device in close condi- tion while using Joie i-Spin Safe child seat in car.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p33_img00` (page 33, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p33_img00.png`

### Concept

Installing the Child Seat on Front Pas- senger Seats

### Concept

• Adjust the front passenger seat for- ward or backward as per requirement, so that there could not be any contact between front passenger seat & child seat or child present behind it.

### Concept

• If required, adjust the front passenger seat height to its suitable position.

### Concept

• While installing child seat on front pas- senger seating position, adjust the buckle to its suitable position of rota- tion.

### Specification

• While installing forward-facing child seat for 15 to 18kg children on front passenger seating position, adjust the front passenger seat to its rear most position. Installing the Child Seat on Rear Pas- senger Seats

### Concept

• If required, adjust the front seat so that there could not be any contact be- tween front seat & child seat or child present behind front seat.

### Concept

• While installing child seats, rear seat head restraints must be removed & kept at safe location to reinstall it whenever adult passenger is sitting at that position.

### Concept

• While installing child seats on rear outboard seating position, adjust their respective buckles to its required po- sition of rotation.

### Concept

Never try pinching of any part of your body intentionally to activate the Auto- matic reversal function. The Automatic reversal function may not work if something gets stuck just before the sunroof fully closes.

### Concept

Even though the sunroof can be operated when the ignition key is in the ON position (the vehicle is not running), operating the sunroof repeatedly with the vehicle turned off will run down the battery. Operate the sunroof while the vehicle is running. When a desired sunroof operation is com- pleted, release the switch. If you keep pressing the switch, it could cause a mal- function. Especially in winter, never oper- ate the sunroof if moving areas are iced. Wait until the areas are de-iced. Make sure head, hands, arms or any other body parts or objects are out of the

### Concept

way before operating the sunroof. Body parts or objects may get pinched causing injuries or vehicle damage.

### Concept

Never deliberately use your body parts to test the automatic reversal function. The sunroof glass may reverse direction, but there is a risk of injury.

### Concept

Dust accumulated between the sunroof and roof panel can make noise or cause any damage. Open the sunroof and re- move dust regularly using a clean cloth.

### Concept

Do not sit on the top of the sunroof. It may cause injury or vehicle damage.

### Concept

Do not allow passengers to lean out of an open sunroof whilst the vehicle is in mo- tion. Injuries may occur from objects such as tree branches.

### Concept

Safety of the vehicle occupants must be observed at all times. Do not allow limbs to be placed in the moving path of the sunroof at any time, injury may occur.

text:
# ANTI-THEFT DEVICE IMMOBI- LIZER

## Knowledge

### Concept

Immobilizer system is designed to prevent vehicle theft by electronically disabling the vehicle ignition system. The vehicle can be started only with vehicle’s original Immobilizer ignition key which has an electronic identification programmed code.

### Note

Use only one key, the other should be kept in a safe location. Note down “key Tag no.” information (and keep it safe) which is required while getting new/spare keys. Remember that it is not possible to prepare new/spare keys without the “key Tag number.” Take precaution about key, as without key vehicle cannot be started.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p48_img00` (page 48, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p48_img00.png`

### Concept

Immobilizer Lamp Status

### Concept

Vehicle State Meaning / Function Of The State

### Concept

Vehicle Immobilized and awaiting electronic key.

### Concept

Normal condition and ready to start the ve- hicle.

### Concept

• Problem with key (wrong key used to start vehicle)

### Concept

• Problem with Immobilizer system. Contact TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre.

### Concept

ON Blinking Unlocked

### Concept

Contact TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre immediately.

### Concept

A key is an electronic access and author- ization system available as a standard feature with your vehicle.

### Concept

The transponder in the ignition key carries a Unique Identification Code (UID). The vehicle unlocks when the code on the key matches with the code on the Engine Management System (EMS). In case of PEPS variant, Immobilizer function is pro- vided by PEPS ECU.

### Concept

When the key is inserted and the ignition is switched to ‘ON’, all codes are commu- nicated within key, Immobilizer, and EMS. The engine will start only if all the codes match.

### Concept

If one of the keys is lost, Contact the TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Cen- tre immediately.

### Concept

• Do not turn ‘ON’ ignition switch by using key with any type of metal wound around its grip or in contact with it. This may be detected as ab- normal condition by immobilizer and prevent vehicle from starting.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p49_img00` (page 49, confidence 0.989)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p49_img00.png`

### Concept

• Do not leave the key in high tem- perature areas. The transponder in it will behave abnormally when re- used.

### Concept

• Do not try to start the vehicle when the Immobilizer indicator lamp on the instrument cluster is glowing. In this condition, the vehicle will not start and the vehicle’s battery will also be drained due to frequent cranking.

Lamp Condensation / Fogging Condi- tion

### Concept

Condensation is a natural phenomenon in Lamp. This occurs mainly because of at- mospheric condition/weather change. During normal condensation, thin film of mist is visible on the inside surface of the exterior lens. Generally, this condition is considered normal and will be eliminated by turning on the respective lamp with en- gine running or during normal driving con- ditions. By doing this if the condensation has begun to clear after the drying time it indicates that the lamp sealing has NOT been breached and will eventually clear. The lamp must NOT be replaced.

ACC SET+: This button is used to increase the Set speed. If user presses button for short duration, then set speed will increase by 1kmph and for long press set speed will increase by 10kmph. ACC SET–: This button is used to decrease the Set speed. If user presses button for short duration, then set speed will decrease by 1kmph and for long press set speed will decrease by 10kmph. ACC Time Gap: This button is used to set the desired dis- tance between the host vehi- cle and the target vehicle. Pre-requisites for Activation

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_005/p237_img00.png`

### Concept

Front ADAS features uses front radar and front windshield camera, as shown in above image.

### Warning

1. Forward Collision Warning and Au- tomatic Emergency Braking (FCW & AEB) Forward Collision Warning System warns the driver by providing audio and visual warning when there is a possibil- ity of collision with the preceding 4

### Concept

wheelers, cyclists or pedestrians de- tected ahead. Automatic Emergency Braking system avoids accident or miti- gates collision impact by applying brake whenever driver applied brake is not sufficient or not applied.

### Concept

Prerequisite for Activation

### Concept

The following conditions shall be satisfied for FCW and AEB to activate. 1. Front camera and front radar are fault/blockage free. 2. Front windshield should be clean. 3. Front bumper should be clean. 4. Vehicle speed should be 7-180 kmph approximately. 5. Vehicle shall be in Drive or Neutral Mode. 6. Steering wheel position should be sta- ble and not to be turned suddenly. 7. No other system failures or degrada- tion of functions related to AEB sys- tems like Braking system, Steering system etc.

### Concept

When vehicle is at standstill user can se- lect FCW-AEB features settings from in- fotainment as below:

### Concept

Go to Home page >> All App >> Settings

### Concept

>> Driver Assistance >> Drive assist.

### Concept

1. User can turn OFF FCW-AEB feature.

### Concept

2. User can turn ON only FCW or both FCW and AEB.

### Procedure

3. Select FCW sensitivity (low, medium and high) to adjust the distance at which collision warnings are provided:

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

• High - FCW is provided at a higher than normal distance to collision risk

### Warning

• The distance to empty value is an estimate of the available driving dis- tance. • If low fuel warning comes, fill the fuel immediately regardless the value of displayed DTE. • If vehicle is not on level ground or negative of battery has been disturbed, the DTE function may not operate correctly.

### Concept

• DTE indicates approximate distance (km) that the vehicle can travel with available & usable fuel in tank and the driving pattern. • This value may differ from the actual driving distance. • Refuel’ shall be displayed which indicates that it’s the time to take your vehicle to the nearest petrol pump to fill the fuel.

Once 0.5 km distance is covered, Average Fuel Economy A shall be displayed.

title: EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN
text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

## Knowledge

### Concept

Guidelines (Do’s & Don’ts)

### Concept

When towing a break down vehicle, cer- tain precautions and procedures must be taken to prevent damage to the vehicle and/or components. Failure to use stand- ard towing precautionary measures when lifting or towing a break down vehicle could result in an unsafe operating condi- tion.

### Concept

To correctly tow and prevent accidental damage to your vehicle, take help of a TATA Motors Authorised Service Centre or a commercial tow-truck service.

### Concept

Make sure that the parking brake is re- leased; Vehicle is in neutral and steer- ing wheel is unlocked. The power steering functions only when vehicle is running. Hence, during towing the steering efforts will be more.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p343_img00` (page 343, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p343_img00.png`

### Concept

• Do not get under your vehicle after it has been lifted by a tow truck.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p343_img01` (page 343, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p343_img01.png`

### Concept

• For towing a vehicle, the best way is to use a wrecker. Alternatively use a rigid tow bar.

### Warning

• Switch ‘ON’ the hazard warning in- dicators of both the vehicles to warn other road users.

### Concept

• Limit the speed to 20-30 km/h.

### Concept

• In case of brake failure, use the parking brake to control the vehicle.

### Concept

• Fasten the tow rope or tow bar at the towing eyes. Otherwise, the ve- hicle could be damaged.

### Concept

• When towing, pull away slowly and smoothly. If the tractive power is too high, the vehicles could be dam- aged.

### Concept

• Unscrew the screws (1) & (2) with the help of screw driver which is pro- vided in Tool kit.

### Concept

• For removal of cover, pull the rear side down.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p343_img02` (page 343, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p343_img02.png`

# INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Warning

Warning for Voice Command

### Concept

• Speak the commands / Instructions in a neutral English accent for best re- sults.

### Concept

• Do not take long pauses (greater than 1 second) while speaking the words in a command. Speak the words of the command at a constant rate. • Avoid varying your pitch and volume while speaking the commands. Speak clearly and loudly at a reasonable speed. • Ensure that there is no noise disturb- ance when you speak the commands like, other passengers in the vehicle are talking or there is lot of wind noise. Disturbance from external sound sources may result in poor voice recognition. • Always face forward while speaking your commands as the voice recogni- tion quality is best in this orientation.

### Concept

Sunroof Closure on Auto Detection of Rain / Vehicle Lock

### Concept

For User Convenience / Protection of ve- hicle, sunroof will automatically close un- der following conditions:

### Procedure

• Rain Detection: When sunroof is open and rain is detected (based on Wiper speed being slow/high upon rain), then Sunroof will close automatically • Vehicle Locking: The sunroof will close automatically when ignition is off and vehicle is locked from out through driver door manual key or by remote key.

### Concept

Combi Switch should be in auto mode to close sunroof with rain sensor.

If the sunroof senses any obstacle while it is closing then it will reverse its direction and opens the sunroof so that trapped ob- ject will get released easily. The auto re- verse function may not work if very thin or soft object is caught between the sunroof assemblies. # STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Manual Activation (Linked to Wind- shield Washers):

### Concept

• When the front windshield washer is ac- tivated, the front camera cleaning noz- zle operates simultaneously. • When the rear windshield washer is ac- tivated, the rear camera cleaning nozzle operates simultaneously.

### Concept

When the front or rear camera clean- ing nozzle is activated, the cleaning process can be viewed on the infotain- ment screen. To see it, select Sur- round View, tap the 2D icon, and choose the Front or Rear Camera view.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p228_img01` (page 228, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p228_img01.png`

### Concept

When the front windshield washer is de- activated, the water flow stops and the nozzle automatically retracts to its original position without any user action.

### Concept

• Always use clean water or manufac- turer-approved washer fluids for optimal performance. • Activate the system regularly to ensure clear visibility and keep the lens clean. • Regularly check that the nozzle moves in/out smoothly and that the spray pat- tern works properly.

### Concept

• Avoid pulling, twisting, or tampering with the nozzle head. • Do not use harsh chemicals, solvents, or unapproved detergents—they may cause damage. • Never disassemble or modify the nozzle assembly. • Do not use sharp objects to clean or un- clog the nozzle slit, as this could lead to damage.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p228_img02` (page 228, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p228_img02.png`

### Concept

Dry mud on a camera lens requires several cleaning cycles for complete removal. Gentle repetition ensures clarity without damaging the lens sur- face.

### Concept

• If the nozzle slits are blocked, gently wipe the nozzle head using a soft cloth and clean water.

#### Visual References

### Concept

Manual SZM Calibration.

### Concept

Whenever a seat stuck issue is reported (e.g., seat not going to its desired loca- tion), perform manual re-calibration of the Seat Zone Module (SZM) by following these steps:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p186_img01` (page 186, confidence 0.96)

### Concept

1. Long press the primary movement switches (Height, Slide, and Recline) in any of the directions (e.g., Height Up/Down, Slide Fore/Aft, Recline / In- cline).

### Concept

2. Continue pressing (> 5 Secs) until the seat reaches the hardened (end) po- sition in each direction. Follow this process for every direction (i.e. slide, height, recline).

### Concept

3. This process recalibrates the internal position counters of the SZM and can restore proper seat movement func- tionality.

### Concept

4. After Recalibration please check whether the seat is stopping at de- sired softends.

### Concept

Always perform these actions from outside the vehicle to avoid injury, es- pecially during movement in tight spaces or toward rear stops.

### Concept

In case of some issue during Installation the device will try to reinstall the update automatically. If the re installation also fails the device will try to go back to the previous version (rollback).

### Concept

If the rollback fails or the update is inter- rupted then the ECU being updated will not function, to resolve this contact the nearest service centre. If the update was for a non-critical ECU the user will be no- tified to contact the nearest service centre and then safely drive the vehicle to it.

### Concept

The following preconditions should be maintained for the whole duration on the update.

### Concept

Vehicle Battery voltage should be within 10-16 Volts.

### Concept

• If the vehicle battery is low (Not EV ve- hicle battery) then the update is not possible, wait for on-board charging to charge the vehicle battery or visit the service centre.

### Concept

• Ignition on is not vehicle cranked state. To put the vehicle in Ignition ON, press the Start/Stop button twice without pressing on the brake.

### Concept

Vehicle in stand-still condition. (Vehicle speed = 0 and Engine RPM = 0.)

### Concept

• The vehicle should not be in cranked state. The vehicle should also be sta- tionary in a safe location.

### Concept

Gear Position should be Neutral.

### Concept

• Put the vehicle in Neutral gear posi- tion. • Park Brake should be enabled. • Enable the park brake. Accelerator Pedal Position should not be pressed (0%). • Do not place your feet on the acceler- ator.

### Concept

The vehicle should not be in a charging state. (Only for EV)

### Concept

• Vehicle should not be in charging.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

• Do not use the high beam unless in- evitable. It may dazzle the driver of the oncoming vehicle, thus causing an accident.

### Concept

• Use headlamp main/dip beam to alert other road users on turns/ cross roads etc.

### Concept

• Use side indicators for lane change or turning. Driving on Gradients

### Concept

When climbing gradient, the vehicle may begin to slow down and show a lack of power. If this happens, shift to a lower gear and apply power smoothly so that there is no loss of traction.

### Concept

When driving down a hill, the engine brak- ing should be used by shifting into a lower gear. Do not drive in neutral gear or switch off the engine.

### Concept

Depending on the severity of the gradient, shift into appropriate gear. Use engine braking judiciously without over-revving

### Concept

the engine. Brake gently in such situa- tions.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p169_img00` (page 169, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p169_img00.png`

### Concept

On long and steep gradients you must reduce the load on the brakes by tak- ing your foot off the accelerator pedal. This allows you to take advantage of regenerative braking effect and helps avoid overheating of service brakes resulting in reduced braking efficiency.

### Concept

Stopping distance progressively, in- creases with vehicle speed. Maintain a sufficient distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead.

### Concept

For long distance driving, perform safety checks before starting a trip and take rest at certain intervals to prevent fatigue.

### Concept

Driving in Heat and Cold Weather

### Specification

The heating and cooling on the car uses energy from the battery. Set temperatures to a comfortable 24°C - 26°C with Auto mode and Econ activated, and see the

### Concept

comfort as well as the range go up signif- icantly.

### Specification

# 2. Active return control

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Concept

To release the steering lock, put the key in the slot and turn it clockwise to one click (ACC).

### Concept

ACC Accessories such as the infotainment system can be operated, but the engine remains ‘OFF’. Steering gets unlocked.

### Concept

ON This is the normal operating position. All electrical systems are ‘ON’.

### Concept

START Turn the key further clockwise to the START position, (spring loaded) to start the engine. As soon as the engine starts, release the ignition key, which returns to ON position. While cranking, all accesso-ries will be momentarily ‘OFF’.

### Concept

Illuminated Key Ring (if equipped)

### Concept

When the vehicle is unlocked, the illumi-nated key ring glows. This helps to locate ignition switch in the dark.

### Concept

Electric Power Assisted Steering (EPAS)

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with electric power assisted steering system. The EPAS system makes steering the vehicle easier with less effort.

### Concept

In EPAS system, the steering effort be- comes heavier as the vehicle speed in- creases and becomes lighter as the vehi- cle speed decreases for better control of the vehicle at different vehicle speeds.

### Concept

If the vehicle is ‘OFF’ or if the EPAS sys- tem becomes inoperative, the vehicle still can be steered with more steering effort however ignition switch should be in ON position else steering wheel will get locked.

### Concept

This EPAS system is available with the following assist features

### Concept

1. Speed sensitive assist control

### Concept

switch is OFF/ON. The ignition switch has the following four positions: LOCK This is the normal parking position. Key from lock can be removed in this position only. “LOCK” position prevents normal use of the steering wheel after the key is re- moved.
