Force Panic ON Operation

### Procedure

When vehicle is in OFF condition, if we press lock button and unlock button sim- ultaneously, Force panic operation gets activated. In this case, turn indicators of vehicle start flashing and horn will blow automatically.

### Concept

Force Panic OFF Operation

### Concept

Press Lock/Unlock of smart key to deacti- vate force panic operation gets deacti- vated.

### Concept

• Don’t operate Unlock button of re- mote in the vicinity of your vehicle, as it could lead to an unintentional unlocking your vehicle.

### Concept

• For battery, replacement proce- dure refer ‘MAINTENANCE’ sec- tion.

### Concept

• Do not remove the battery connec- tion of the vehicle while the vehicle has been locked by remote.

### Concept

Smart Key Precautions

### Concept

1. If smart key is close to radio transmit- ter such as radio station or an airport which can interfere with normal oper- ation of the transmitter.

### Concept

2. If smart key is near a mobile two way radio system or a cellular phone, then it will not work properly.

### Concept

3. If another vehicle’s smart key is being operated close to your vehicle, signal will fluctuate.

### Concept

Keep smart key away from electro- magnetic materials that blocks electro- magnetic waves to the key surface. In case any button of the key is acci- dentally pressed for more than 20 sec- onds, the remote stops functioning till the time the button is pressed. The LED on the remote also stops glowing. The function of the remote gets rein- stated immediately when the user stops pressing the push button of re- mote.

### Procedure

### Concept

Option 2 - Door Locking / Unlocking using Door Handle Switch (DHS) (if equipped)

### Concept

To lock/unlock all the doors without oper- ating smart key button/key blade. Press the door handle switch (DHS) provided on the driver door to lock/unlock all the four doors except tailgate.

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

2. Lower the bonnet close to the bumper, then let it drop down.

### Concept

Ensure that the bonnet is properly locked before driving or it can fly up unexpectedly during driving.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p62_img00` (page 62, confidence 0.992)

### Procedure

1. To open the fuel flap, gently press on fuel flap.

### Note

NOTE For mechanical / flip key (without smart key), to open the fuel flap. Make sure the smart key should be in au- thentication range and the vehicle is in unlock condition. Then gently press the fuel flap.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p62_img01` (page 62, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p62_img01.png`

### Concept

2. Once the release is triggered, the fuel flap should pop open slightly, then pull it fully open by hand.

### Procedure

3. To open the fuel cap by turning it in counter clockwise for fuel filling. 4. For closing, turn the fuel cap clock- wise. 5. After refuelling, simply push the fuel flap back into its closed position until it locks.

### Concept

• Fuel vapor is extremely hazardous. Always switch ‘OFF’ the engine be- fore refueling and never refill near sparks or open flames. Do not use

### Concept

cell phone when you fill fuel.

### Concept

• Do not continue adding fuel after the automatic shut ‘OFF’ function is operated if it is equipped on the fuel station. Overfilling the fuel tank could damage the fuel system.

### Note

NOTE • To fill up the fuel, the Engine must be stopped by turning OFF the Ig- nition Key/Start-Stop button. If the Engine is in Idle Stop Start (ISS) mode, it may restart automatically while filling the fuel. • Remove the fuel filler cap slowly, and wait for any hissing to stop. The fuel may be under pressure and may spray out. • If fuel cap needs replacement, make sure that it is replaced by a genuine cap at the TATA MO- TORS Authorised Service Centre.

# MAINTENANCE AND CARE

## Knowledge

### Note

NOTE • In Free service, labor charges are free, any parts and consumables will be chargeable. • Filters, Fluid, Consumables, Grease, Components, wheel alignment Wheel Balancing and weights etc. will be replaced on chargeable basis. • Check the coolant level and top up as required, replace if it is contaminated /discolored or there is sludge formation. • Periodic maintenance schedule is for reference. TMPV reserves the rights to change the Periodic Maintenance Schedule. • For cleaning the engine compartment, it is recommended to use dry low pressure air. Do not use pressurized water. • DEF is a consumable item, refill or replacement is not based on service intervals. Automatic Transmission with Mono- stable Shifter (if equipped)

#### Visual References

### Concept

Automatic Transmission offers four Gear positions in the Gear shifter: 1. Park Mode (P) 2. Reverse Mode (R) 3. Neutral Mode (N) 4. Drive Mode (D)

### Procedure

• Start the ignition to ON position. • Press the brake pedal, bring the gear shifter to Neutral position. Check “N” is displayed on cluster or ensure the Park mode is ‘ON’ on the shifter, check ‘P’ is displayed on Instrument cluster. • Now start the vehicle, release the parking brake. • Based on requirement select the drive mode “D” or reverse mode “R”. • Slowly release the brake pedal and vehicle will start moving.

### Concept

• Press the brake pedal regardless of gear position. • Vehicle will come to halt. • Bring the gear shifter from drive mode “D” to Neutral mode “N” or Parking mode “P”.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND CARE

## Knowledge

### Concept

• Avoid parking the car under trees without proper cover, it will reduce the amount of bird droppings, tree sap and pollen contact on paint surface. Regularly remove the twigs, leaves and vegetation near the windshield areas, to avoid wa- ter stagnation.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p427_img00` (page 427, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p427_img00.png`

### Concept

• Always close the sunroof while washing the vehicle.

### Specification

Do not direct high pressure washer fluid/ water jets (Pressure above 0.5 bar) at electrical devices and con- necter during washing. This is to pre- vent malfunction/failure of electrical system due to water ingress.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p427_img01` (page 427, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p427_img01.png`

### Concept

After drying the vehicle, inspect it for chips and scratches that could allow corrosion

### Concept

to start. Apply touch up paint where nec- essary. Cleaning of Carpets

### Concept

Vacuum clean the carpet regularly to re- move dirt. Dirt will make the carpet wear out faster. Periodically, shampoo the car- pet to keep it looking new. Use carpet cleaners (preferably foam type). Follow the instructions that come with the cleaner. Apply it with a sponge or soft brush. Keep the carpeting as dry as possible by not adding water to the foam.

### Concept

Avoid wiping of painted surface in dry condition as it may leave scratches on the painted surface.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p427_img02` (page 427, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p427_img02.png`

### Concept

Cleaning of Windows, Front and Rear Glasses

### Concept

Clean the windows inside and outside with commercially available glass clean- ers.

### Concept

This will remove the haze that builds up on the inside of windows. Use a soft cloth or paper towels to clean all glass and plastic surfaces. Waxing Waxing and polishing are recom- mended to maintain the gloss and wet- look appearance of your paint finish. 1. Use good quality polish and wax for your vehicle. 2. Re-wax your vehicle when the water does not slip off the surface but col- lects over the surface in patches. Polishing

### Concept

Polishes and cleaners can restore shine to the painted surface that has oxidized and become dull. They normally contain mild abrasives and solvents that remove the top layer of the finish coat. Polish your vehicle, if the finish does not regain its original shine after using wax.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

## Knowledge

### Concept

JUMP STARTING YOUR CAR Use only a battery of same rating & ca- pacity to jump start your vehicle. Position the booster battery close to your vehicle so that the jump leads will reach both bat- teries.

### Concept

When using a battery of another vehicle, do not let the vehicles touch. Apply the parking brake firmly and keep the gear- shift lever in neutral.

### Warning

Turn off all vehicle accessories, except those necessary for safety like hazard warning lamps.

### Concept

If your vehicle is equipped with Battery sensor, then do not connect your jump start cable lead directly on the Sensor sur- face. Connect only on the negative cable surface as shown on the image. After jump start event, IAC function will be re- stored only when the Vehicle is parked in idle for 3-4 Hours.

### Concept

(For Diesel & Petrol)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p341_img00` (page 341, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p341_img00.png`

### Concept

Make jump lead connections as follows:

### Concept

• Connect one end of the first jump lead to the positive (+) terminal of the dis- charged battery.

### Concept

• Connect the other end to the positive (+) terminal of the booster battery.

### Concept

• Connect one end of the second jump lead to the negative (–) terminal of the booster battery.

### Concept

• Make the final connection (other end of the negative terminal) to an un- painted, heavy metal part (i.e. engine mounting stud/nut) of the vehicle of discharged battery.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p341_img01` (page 341, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p341_img01.png`

### Concept

• Start the engine of the vehicle with the discharged battery.

### Concept

• Before disconnecting the jumper ca- bles, let the engine run for several minutes.

title: 4. Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) (if equipped)
text:
# 4. Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) (if equipped)

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Concept

Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) is a safety feature that adjusts the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) set speed based on detected speed lim- its from traffic signs boards and/or Map provided speed limit. lSA sys- tem ensures that vehicle speed does not exceed a safe or legal speed limit while ACC is active. Prerequisite for activation

### Concept

The following conditions shall be satisfied to activate ISA: 1. The front-facing camera must be op- erational and free of obstructions. 2. Driver must ensure that both the ISA app and the Navigation app are up- dated to the latest version available in the Arcade app store. 3. Driver must ensure the Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) system is active.

### Concept

4. Driver must ensure that the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) system is ac- tive in order to utilize the ISA func- tionality. 5. Driver must ensure that there are no failures or degradation of functions related to the steering system, brak- ing system, or any other critical sys- tems.

### Note

NOTE This system does not guarantee safety or autonomous driving, so the driver should always pay close atten- tion. How to use ISA feature

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p251_img00` (page 251, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p251_img00.png`

### Concept

The ISA feature can be activated from in- fotainment by pressing the following se- quence:

### Concept

• Go to Home page >> All App >> Set- tings >> Drive assist >> Traffic Sign Recognition and Speed Assist >> In- telligent Speed Assist. • It is important to ensure that the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) mode

### Concept

is active before utilizing the Intelligent Speed Assist (ISA) fea- ture.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p251_img01` (page 251, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p251_img01.png`

### Concept

• When the ISA system detects that the current road speed limit is lower than the ACC set speed value, the driver will be notified by blinking this tell-tale indicator on the instrument cluster for 5 seconds.

### Procedure

• By observing the above mentioned tell-tale indicator blinking, the driver can press the "SET-" button (while tell-tale is blinking) on the steering wheel to adjust the ACC set speed to match the detected speed limit.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

• Plan your tour in advance, check for road conditions, kms to be covered in a day, halting destination, fuel station, food station, hospitals and roadside assistance in case of emergency.

### Concept

• Always ensure all occupants wear seat belt.

### Concept

• Follow speed limits and adjust your speed according to road conditions.

### Concept

• Keep safe following distance from the vehicle in front of you.

### Concept

• Obey traffic rules and sign at all times.

### Concept

• Avoid distractions like mobile phone, texting while driving.

### Concept

• Check your mirror frequently and be aware of surrounding.

### Concept

• Never drive under the influence of al- cohol or drugs.

### Concept

• Avoid aggressive driving behaviour like tailgating or excessive over speeding.

### Concept

• Regularly maintain your vehicle to en- sure good working condition.

### Concept

• Take adequate break and rest every after 200 kms.

### Concept

• Check tyre pressure, coolant, oil indi- cation, any leakage under the vehicle regularly during travelling.

### Concept

• Use horn, light and indicators as per condition.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p167_img00` (page 167, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p167_img00.png`

### Concept

We strongly advise you not to drive in late hours/sleep hours to avoid fatality because body response is slow to re- spond to any situation in this time pe- riod.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p167_img01` (page 167, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p167_img01.png`

### Concept

Remember, safe driving is crucial for your safety and safety of others on the road, drive responsibly following above driving tip may help is good and enjoyable travelling experience.

### Concept

Driving Through Flooded Water

### Concept

Water may enter the vehicle interior and engine compartment which could damage engine, electronic & electrical systems. Judge the depth of water before driving through it. If at all the situation demands that you have to drive through water then;

### Concept

• Keep engine in higher RPM and crawl the vehicle in low gear.

### Concept

• Flowing or rushing water creates strong forces. Driving through flowing water could cause the vehicle to flow in water.

### Concept

• Lightly apply the brake pedal to dry the liners until the brakes work nor- mally once you are out of water.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p167_img02` (page 167, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p167_img02.png`

### Concept

Do not attempt to start the engine if ve- hicle gets flooded due to water. Tow the vehicle to a safe place. Contact a nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

## Knowledge

### Specification

When pumping in the sealant through the tyre valve, the pressure may rise up to 500 kPa (5 bar/73 psi) but will drop again after about 30 seconds.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p339_img00` (page 339, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p339_img00.png`

### Concept

Need to drain fluid from tyre before re- pair.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p339_img01` (page 339, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p339_img01.png`

### Concept

Step 2: Checking The Tyre Pressure

### Specification

• Once a tyre inflation pressure of at least 180kPa (1.8 bar/26 psi) has been reached. Switch the compressor to “0” in order to read the actual tyre pressure from the pressure gauge. Pull the power plug from the 12 volt power socket con- nection. • Slowly unscrew the hose from the tyre valve (sealant residues may escape from the hose) and put the protective cap back onto the hose. • Leave the bottle in the holder. This avoids unexpected leakage of sealant residue.

### Procedure

• Make sure the Puncture repair Kit, the cap of the bottle and the orange cap are stored safely, but are still easily acces- sible, in the vehicle. • The kit will be needed again when you check the tyre pressure. • Start and drive for about 3-10 km so that the sealant can seal the damaged area. Do not drive for more than 10 min and not faster than 80 km/h. • Stop the vehicle after driving about 3- 10 km. Check and where necessary, adjust the pressure of the damaged tyre. Re- move the protective cap from the end of the hose. Screw the hose firmly onto the valve of the damaged tyre. Read the tyre pressure from the pressure gauge. • If the pressure of the sealant-filled tyre is 130kPa (1.3 bar/19 psi) or more, it must now be adjusted to the pressure specified for your vehicle (Refer tyre pressure sticker pasted on driver door side). • Inflate the tyre to the specified pressure using the pressure “air release” valve. Rest of the remaining sealant in the

### Concept

hose might leak out when opening pres- sure “air release” valve or taking off the protective cap of the hose. Please use protective glove for safety purpose. • Once you have inflated the tyre to its correct tyre pressure, switch off the compressor, pull the plug out of the socket, unscrew the hose, fasten the tyre valve cap and put back on the pro- tective cap of the hose. • Leave the bottle in the holder and store the Puncture repair Kit away safely in the vehicle trunk • Drive to the nearest workshop to get the damaged tyre repaired and if the tyre re- pair is not possible it should be removed from the car. Before the tyre is removed from the rim, inform your tyre dealer that the tyre contains sealant.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p339_img02` (page 339, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p339_img02.png`

### Warning

• If heavy vibrations, unsteady steer- ing behavior or noises should occur while driving, reduce your speed and drive with caution to a place where it is safe for you to stop the vehicle.

text:
# 10. Blind Spot Detection - Lane Change Alert (BSD-LCA)

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Warning

BSD-LCA detects moving objects present in the adjacent lanes and warns if there are moving objects present in blind spots of the host vehicle or there is a high speed closing vehicle in adjacent lanes. Warning to the driver is given in stages.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p268_img00` (page 268, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p268_img00.png`

### Concept

Prerequisite for activation

### Concept

The following condition shall be satisfied to activate BSD-LCA 1. Rear Corner Radars and other related systems are fault free. 2. For AT/AMT/DCT vehicle (if equipped) the gear engaged shall be in Drive (D) or Neutral (N) Mode. 3. Vehicle speed is above 20 kmph ap- proximately. User Settings

### Procedure

1. BSD-LCA will be default ON during start of vehicle i.e. on every Ignition ON the BSD-LCA feature will be ena- bled even if previously disabled. 2. User can turn ON/OFF BSD-LCA fea- ture using infotainment screen. In infotainment system user interface, press the following button sequence to reach BSD-LCA user settings page Go to Home page >> All App >> Settings >>Driver Assistance >> Drive assist.

### Concept

5. When charging certain smart phones, the charging full message on head unit may not display when the smart phone is fully charged. It depends on smart phone manufac- turer. 6. Smartphone of some manufacturers may display messages on weak cur- rent. This is due to particular charac- teristic of smartphone and does not imply a malfunction on wireless charger. Smaller smartphone users (ex. IPhone) may face intermittent charging issues due to its smaller size. (To avoid this, place the smartphone at center of the charging pad). Small mobile phones may not be able to charge in every position on charging pad. 7. The wireless charger may not oper- ate correctly when the vehicle is near a TV tower, electric power plant, gas station, large display, airport, or other facility that generates strong radio waves or electrical noise.

The infotainment system displays no warning message/ indication in this mode. This mode represents that the charging function is halted and not functional. The charging function could halt because of below reasons like: 1. Phone is not properly aligned with the charging pad or not positioned cor- rectly on pad wireless charger in standby mode. 2. Phone is kept in upside down position wireless charger in standby mode. 3. Phone is fully charged, and phone does not demand power wireless charger in standby mode. Smart Phone Charging ON Mode

Lane Keep Assist (LKA) equipped with Lane Departure Warning (LDW) It is a safety feature which helps the driver to keep the vehicle in the lane by provid- ing warning and steering inputs to the user when vehicle departs the lane with- out driver’s intention. Whenever vehicle moves towards lane edge, driver is alerted with LDW and LKA brings the vehicle back into the lane. Prerequisite for activation

### Concept

The following conditions shall be satisfied to activate LKA-LDW

### Concept

• Front Camera is fault/ blockage free.

### Concept

• Front windshield should be clean.

### Concept

• Vehicle speed is more than 60Kmph.

### Concept

• Vehicle shall be in Drive mode

### Concept

• Steering wheel position should be sta- ble and not to be turned suddenly.

### Concept

• Lane markings are properly detected and a lane is properly recognized.

### Concept

• Turn Indicator of the side of departure is OFF.

### Concept

• In case turn signal is given, LKA will resume after few sec when Turn sig- nal is turned OFF.

### Concept

• No other system failures or malfunc- tion related to Steering system.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

• If you rest your foot on the brake pe- dal while driving, the braking sys- tem can overheat and cause fading of brake pads. This increases the stopping distance and can even cause the braking system to fail. There is a risk of an accident.

### Concept

• Never press the brake pedal and the accelerator pedal at the same time.

### Concept

After you drive through water or if you wash the underside of the vehicle, test the brakes at slow speeds to see if the brakes work fine. If the brakes are less effective than normal, dry them by repeatedly ap- plying the brakes at slow speeds until the brakes have regained their normal effec- tiveness.

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a de- layed reaction from the brakes when you brake for the first time. This may also oc- cur after the vehicle has been washed. Brake performance may become poor and unpredictable if brakes are wet.

### Concept

Braking on Downhill Gradients

### Concept

On long and steep gradients, you must re- duce the load on the brakes by shifting early to a lower gear. This allows you to take advantage of the engine braking ef- fect and helps avoid overheating and ex- cessive wear of the brakes.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p176_img00` (page 176, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p176_img00.png`

### Concept

• Do not shift to lower gear on a slip- pery road surface in an attempt to increase the engine’s braking ef- fect, the drive wheels could lose their grip.

### Concept

• There is an increased danger of skidding and accidents.

### Concept

Check traffic conditions before doing the above activity.

# INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Fresh Air / Recirculation

### Concept

1. When the recirculation switch is turned ON, air from the vehicle’s interior is sent throughout the system. 2. When the recirculation switch is turned OFF, air from outside enters in to the cabin (fresh mode). Whenever discomfort is felt, switch to fresh air mode. 3. Recirculation can be turned ON/OFF from FATC control panel.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p282_img00` (page 282, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p282_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p282_img04` (page 282, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p282_img04.png`

### Concept

The outside air intakes for the climate control systems are at the base of windscreen. Keep this area clear from leaves and other debris.

### Concept

### Concept

## Knowledge

### Concept

Lateral Sunshade Curtain (if equipped)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p318_img00` (page 318, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p318_img00.png`

### Concept

The purpose of sunshade is to prevent discomfort caused by direct sunlight com- ing into the vehicle. Sunshade operating procedure

### Concept

• Pull Up: Lift the sunshade fabric by us- ing pull handle (2) and engage the pull bar onto both the hooks (1) simultane- ously. After engagement, move the pull handle in downward direction.

### Concept

• Pull Down: Hold the pull handle (2) and remove the pull bar from both the hooks (1) by raising it slightly. Slowly pull down the sunshade fabric and place it over the door trim.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p318_img01` (page 318, confidence 0.997)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p318_img01.png`

### Concept

• Do not hang any other objects ex- cept the shade curtain on the hooks.

### Concept

• Always ensure that the sunshade pull bar is engaged in both the hooks at the same time. There is a risk of fabric damage, if it is en- gaged in only one hook.

### Concept

• Sunshade to be opened and closed by using pull handle only.

### Concept

• Do not hold or fold the stiffener rods on the sunshade.

### Concept

• Sunshade fabric may get damaged due to head rested on it/contact with any pointed item like orna- ments, nails etc/pulling of cloth/ fabric abruptly.

### Concept

• When window is open, avoid using sunshade to prevent any risk of damage to sunshade fabric. Risk of fabric damage is higher, especially in vehicle running conditions.

### Concept

• Sunshade to be operated only from inside the car in door closed condi- tion.

#### Visual References

  - File: `images/doc_005/p252_img00.png`

### Concept

• When ISA is in tem- porary failure state, this tell-tale indicator will be displayed along with a 5-second pop-up mes- sage informing the driver that "Intelli- gent speed assist system temporary available."

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p252_img01` (page 252, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p252_img01.png`

### Concept

• When ISA is in per- manent failure state, this tell-tale indicator will be displayed along with a 5-second pop-up mes- sage informing the driver – “Intelli- gent speed assist system failure, please contact service center.” System limitations

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p252_img02` (page 252, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p252_img02.png`

### Warning

ISA feature subject to system limitation and unavailable or degrade performance or give false warning in following situa- tions. 1. For Speed limit signs with value lower than 30 Kmph, ISA will not re- duce the ACC set Speed. However, Driver will be informed through Over speed warning and ISA prompt about the Over speeding. 2. The final functionality of the ISA sys- tem depends on the availability of map data and/or Traffic Sign Recog- nition (TSR). 3. TSR Limitations: The Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) feature relies on a

### Concept

camera sensor and has certain limi- tations, including the inability to de- tect three-digit speed limit signs, multi-stacked speed limit signs, and signboards that are not installed ac- cording to VINNA conventions (e.g., a white background with numbers in black and red outer circle) or that are incorrectly placed or signboards out- side the camera's field of view. 4. MAP Data Limitation: The ISA sys- tem relies on up-to-date map data to determine speed limits. Inaccuracies or delays in map data updates can lead to the system displaying incor- rect speed limit information. 5. ISA system will not work in some sit- uation where speed sign boards are present but the MAP data does not provide speed limit information. 6. Inclement weather (rain, snow, fog, dust, haze, mist etc.) 7. Camera blockage (direct sunlight or headlamp glare on camera, mud/ dirt/moisture/ stickers/ debris on windshield surface in front of camera etc.)

text:
# 3. Seat and ORVM Memory Recall Operation

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Concept

I. To store seat and ORVM position in M1 button:

### Procedure

Press the SET button, and within 5 seconds (or until the SET button LED lights up), press the M1 button to save the seat and ORVM positions at M1. II. To store seat and ORVM position in

### Procedure

Press the SET button, and within 5 seconds (or until the SET button LED lights up), press the M2 button to save the seat and ORVM positions to M2. III. To store seat and ORVM position in

### Procedure

Press the SET button, and within 5 seconds (or while the SET button LED is illuminated), press the M3 but- ton to store the seat and ORVM po- sitions at M3.

### Concept

• When the Seat and ORVM position is stored, user can see pop up for re- spective Memory Button on IPC and a

### Concept

chime sounds to confirm the settings have been stored.

### Concept

• The seat and ORVM memory storage function operates in the Ignition OFF (Awake, Accessory, and Accessory Delay), Ignition ON, and Run power modes.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p188_img00` (page 188, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p188_img00.png`

### Concept

• Any existing Seat and ORVM Posi- tion are over-written when storing a new memory position.

### Concept

• While storing Seat and ORVM Posi- tion, if the vehicle speed increased by 5 km/h, the ongoing store opera- tion will not be cancelled.

### Concept

• User can Store the seat position be- tween Pre stop to hard Stop of seat travel track.

### Concept

• To recall the Stored Seat and ORVM Position, Press M1/M2/M3 as per user choice.

### Concept

• After Pressing M1/M2/M3 seat and ORVM will automatically adjust to pre- viously stored seat and ORVM posi- tion. • When the M1/M2/M3 position is re- called, user can see pop up for re- spective Memory Button on IPC and a chime sounds to confirm the settings have been recalled. • Seat and ORVM memory store func- tion work in Ignition OFF (Awake, Ac- cessory, and Accessory Delay), Igni- tion ON and Run power modes.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p188_img01` (page 188, confidence 0.997)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p188_img01.png`

### Concept

• When the vehicle speed > 6 kmph (±1kmph), to recall the stored seat position, long press M1/M2/M3.

### Concept

• If user wants to recall seat position stored beyond Pre stop, then Seat will travel till Pre stop position.

### Concept

• If the speed of the vehicle is> 6kmph (±1kmph), & switch M1/M2/M3 is one touch/short pressed, memory seat position will not be recalled.

title: 4. Unlocking All Doors
text:
# 4. Unlocking All Doors

## Knowledge

### Concept

Pressing the unlock button (4) of remote will unlock all the doors. One flash is com- ing on side indicators. Manual Operation of Central Door Locking / Unlocking

### Concept

All doors can be locked / unlocked oper- ating driver door using either key blade from outside or knob from inside. Flip Key Features Vehicle Search

### Concept

In vehicle, locked condition if lock button on remote key is pressed the turn indica- tors of vehicle flashes for 4 times. Automatic Activation of Immobilizer

### Concept

If key is removed from ignition switch, the engine will be immobilized automatically even if you forget to lock the vehicle. For few variants, Ignition off is required to immobilize the vehicle. Auto Locking / Unlocking of Doors / Auto Unlock

### Concept

Vehicle doors are automatically locked

### Concept

• When all doors are closed and the ve- hicle speed crosses 13 km/h.

### Concept

• When key is taken out all the doors get automatically unlocked.

### Concept

• For few variants, when ignition is turned off all the doors get automati- cally unlocked.

### Concept

• When unlocked with remote key and if no door is opened within 30 seconds, vehicle doors get automatically locked. Anti-grab / Anti-scan Coding

### Concept

The remote control set of this security system is protected against the use of de- vices called ‘scanners’ and ‘grabbers’ which can record and reproduce some types of remote codes.

### Concept

Force Panic ON Operation

### Procedure

When vehicle is in OFF condition, if we press lock button and unlock button sim- ultaneously, Force panic operation gets activated. In this case, turn indicators of vehicle start flashing and horn will blow automatically.

### Concept

Force Panic OFF Operation

### Concept

Press Lock/Unlock of smart key to deacti- vate force panic operation gets deacti- vated.

### Concept

Don’t operate unlock push-button of re- mote while in the vicinity of your vehicle, as it could lead to an unintentional unlock- ing of vehicle. Don’t use discharged bat- teries in remote, as it could damage the remote. For battery replacement proce- dure refer maintenance section. Don’t re- move the battery connection of the vehi- cle while the vehicle has been locked by remote.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p52_img00` (page 52, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p52_img00.png`

### Concept

In case any button of the key is acci- dentally pressed for more than 20 seconds, the remote stops functioning till the time the button is pressed. The LED on the Remote also stops glow- ing. The function of the remote gets reinstated immediately when the user stops pressing the push button of re- mote.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Driving on a Wet Road

### Concept

• Check wiper blades, lights and brakes for proper functioning. • Check the tyre condition visually, tyre treads depth, cut mark, worn out etc. • Avoid harsh braking and sharp turns. It may cause loss of control and lead to a skid. • For slowing down, shift to lower gears and brake gently. • Keep lights ‘ON’ if visibility is poor.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p168_img00` (page 168, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p168_img00.png`

### Concept

On wet roads or during light showers, “Aquaplaning” can occur. “Aquaplan- ing” is the loss of direct contact be- tween the road surface and the vehi- cle’s tyres due to a water film forming between them Steering or braking the vehicle can be very difficult, and loss of control can occur. There is no hard and fast rule about aquaplaning. The best advice is to slow down when the road is wet.

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a delayed reaction from the brakes when braking for the first time. You have to press the brake pedal more firmly. Maintain a greater distance from the vehicle in front.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p168_img01` (page 168, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p168_img01.png`

### Concept

Driving on Snow roads

### Concept

While driving on snow, it is advisable to use the snow chain on roads. Follow as- sembly and safety instruction provided by the snow chain manufacturers.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p168_img02` (page 168, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p168_img02.png`

### Specification

• Wet ice (0°C and freezing rain), snow or ice can be slick and very hard to drive on. The vehicle will have much less traction or “grip” un- der these conditions. Try to avoid driving on wet ice.

### Warning

• Whatever the conditions, drive with caution. Accelerate and slow down with care. If accelerating too fast, the drive wheels will lose even more

### Concept

• Allow more stopping distance under these conditions. Braking should be started sooner than on dry pave- ment.

### Concept

• Allow greater following distances on slippery roads.

### Concept

• Watch for slippery spots (glare ice). These may appear on an otherwise clear road in shaded areas. If a patch of ice is seen ahead, brake before reaching it. Try not to brake while on the ice, and avoid any sud- den steering maneuvers.

### Concept

• Do not use cruise control on slip- pery roads .

### Concept

• Ensure that all lights are working and windshield, window glasses are clean.

### Concept

• Drive more slowly at night than in the daytime, as the visual range is restricted at night. Maintain a speed

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Procedure

1. Press the clutch/brake pedal and then press start/stop button to start the ve- hicle. 2. Green colour LED on start/stop button will turn ON. 3. Once vehicle starts successfully, green colour LED on start/stop switch will remain ON.

### Concept

Three Step Start Step 1

### Procedure

1. Have the smart key with you and sit on the driver’s seat. 2. Press the start/stop button without pressing clutch pedal. 3. Amber colour LED on start/stop button will turn ON. 4. Limited information will be displayed on instrument cluster. Engine remains OFF. (In MT and AT variants, Steering is unlocked).

### Procedure

1. Press the start/stop button without pressing clutch pedal again. 2. Green colour LED on start/stop button will turn ON. 3. Vehicle will remain OFF but all electri- cal equipment and infotainment sys- tem can be used. Step 3

### Concept

1. Press the clutch pedal and then press start/stop button to start the vehicle. 2. Green colour LED on start/stop button remains ON. 3. Once the vehicle is started success- fully, the green colour LED on start/stop button stays ON. (In AT var- iants, transmission gets unlocked) Engine Passive Stop Condition Single Press Stop

### Concept

• Press the start/stop button with or without brake.

### Concept

• ACC and IGN turns OFF.

### Concept

• LED on start/stop switch turns OFF.

### Concept

Single Long Press Stop

### Concept

• Press the start/stop button for more than three seconds.

### Concept

• IGN returns OFF, ACC remains ON.

### Concept

• Amber colour LED on start/stop switch turns ON.

### Warning

When vehicle is in OFF mode, if user tries to lock the vehicle from outside by pressing any door handle switch and if PEPS detects that the smart key is left inside the vehicle, an audio warning/ chime is sounded and door will not get locked.

### Concept

For AT variants, transmission lock/un- lock mechanism may or may not be applicable to your vehicle. For such variants steering lock is provided .

# 2. Tail Gate Unlatch

## Knowledge

### Concept

Vehicle Alarm & Security

### Concept

To prevent automobile thefts, the anti- theft system makes use of an anti-theft alarm (ATA). On detection of any unau- thorised access, the BCM triggers the horn (acoustic alarm) and flashes the turn indicators.

### Concept

Smart Key (PEPS) (if equipped)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p53_img00` (page 53, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p53_img00.png`

### Procedure

Keep the smart key with user to perform the passive access. It is used for locking, unlocking, and starting the vehicle. 1. Locking all doors 2. Tail Gate unlatch / Power Operated Tailgate Open and Close (if equipped) 3. Approach Light 4. Unlocking all doors

### Concept

1. Locking All Doors

### Procedure

Press the lock button once (1) to lock all the doors of the vehicle. Successful lock will be indicated by two flashes of turn sig- nal indicators. If lock button is pressed on the key with the any door open, locking- unlocking takes place with audible warn- ing indicators do not flash.

### Concept

Press the tail gate opening button once (2) to unlock the tailgate with in authenti- cation range of Smart key i.e. 1 to 1.5 me- ters.

### Procedure

Power operated Tailgate Open and Close (if equipped)

### Procedure

To open and close tailgate press the but- ton. If button is long pressed for 3 sec- onds then the tailgate will open or close. 3. Approach Light (if equipped)

## Knowledge

### Concept

• If the booster battery you are using is fitted to another vehicle, start the en- gine of the vehicle with the booster battery. Run the engine at moderate speed.

### Concept

• Remove the jump leads in the exact reverse order in which you connected them.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p342_img00` (page 342, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p342_img00.png`

### Concept

Do not disconnect the discharged bat- tery from the vehicle.

### Concept

• Do not connect the jump lead di- rectly to the negative (–) terminal of the discharged battery. This may lead to an explosion.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p342_img01` (page 342, confidence 0.99)

### Concept

### Concept

### Concept

• Make sure that the positive terminal of a connected battery does not come into contact with vehicle parts. Never place metal objects or tools on a battery.

### Concept

• It is important that you observe the described order of the battery termi- nals when connecting and discon- necting a battery. If you are in doubt, seek assistance from quali- fied specialist workshop.

### Procedure

• Do not connect or disconnect the

### Concept

battery terminals while the engine is running.

### Procedure

Do’s • Use only authorized Battery sensor. • Use only authorized Battery. • Always disconnect the Battery sensor output for any service on vehicle. Don’t Do not remove the Battery sensor if it is not necessary. • Do not mallet/hammer the Battery sensor to fix on Battery Pole. • Do not place the Battery sensor on Positive Pole. • Do not remove the Battery Sensor connector.

title: MAINTENANCE AND CARE
text:
# MAINTENANCE AND CARE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Interior Fabric Cleaning Tips

### Concept

1. Stains should be treated immediately. If left for a long time, they can leave a permanent mark. 2. Cleaning the stains immediately is im- portant especially for stains, which contain artificial colors in the stain cre- ating liquid or semisolid substances. The colorant may leave a stain if kept for longer time. 3. Stain should not be removed by rub- bing. As far as possible, try to blot or lift the stain with cloth or plastic spat- ula and then clean the remaining stain with cloth or sponge. 4. If the stain has dried, then gently brush off the material and then press with damp cloth or sponge till it disap- pears. 5. Do not use household detergents to clean the fabric. 6. Always use clean cotton cloth for cleaning.

### Concept

Following guidelines will help you to pro- tect your vehicle from corrosion effec- tively.

### Concept

Avoid Spillage or Direct contact of Air freshener liquid/chemicals with painted and coated plastic parts. These chemicals may cause damage to paint/coat surface like blisters, peel off, wrinkles etc.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p428_img00` (page 428, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p428_img00.png`

### Concept

In order to protect your vehicle from cor- rosion it is recommended that you wash your vehicle thoroughly and frequently in case:

### Concept

• There is a heavy accumulation of dirt and mud especially on the underbody.

### Concept

• It is driven in areas having high atmos- pheric pollution due to smoke, soot, dust, iron dust and other chemical pol- lutants.

### Concept

• It is driven in coastal areas.

### Concept

• The underbody must be thoroughly pressure washed after every three months.

### Concept

• In addition to regularly washing your car, the following precautions need to be taken. Periodic Inspection

### Concept

• Regularly inspect your vehicle for any damage in the paint film such as deep scratches and immediately get them repaired from an authorised service outlet, as these defects tend to accel- erate corrosion.

### Concept

• Inspect mud liners for damages.

### Concept

• Keep all drain holes clear from clog- ging. Wiper Care

### Concept

• To prevent damage to the wipers or windshield, do not operate the wipers when the windshield is dry.

### Concept

• To prevent damage to the wiper arms and other components, do not attempt to move the wipers manually.

### Concept

Conditions for refilling: Vehicle should be parked on a flat road surface. Switch OFF the Engine and ignition should be in OFF position.

### Concept

After DEF refilling through Nozzle OR container, in case of DEF is spills out during refilling. Spill out DEF need to be swapped out with help of cotton or same mean.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p408_img01` (page 408, confidence 0.991)

### Concept

DEF Quantity Refilling

### Warning

Total DEF Quantity inside the DEF tank should never be more than 15 litres. Only Tata Dealer will be able to correctly deter- mine the quantity of DEF available inside the tank. If “DEF level low, Refill Soon” Warning message appears in the cluster, it indi- cates that DEF needs to be topped up. In case you are refilling the DEF yourself, fill only maximum 7.0 litres.

You can fill up at any DEF Distributor/Re- tailer.

• Insert the DEF nozzle in the filler, start refilling and stop refilling at the first shut-off (the shut-off indicates that the DEF tank is full). Do not proceed with the refilling, to prevent spillage of DEF.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Seat Ventilation (if equipped)

### Concept

To start ventilation, press button once.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p192_img00` (page 192, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p192_img00.png`

### Concept

It has 3 ventilation adjustments in de- creasing order and LED glows for each press. To stop the ventilation long press the button for few seconds.

### Concept

Default setting is highest speed on first press.

### Concept

The ventilated seat by default is set to OFF whenever the vehicle START/STOP button is turned on.

### Concept

Do not apply excessive force on ven- tilation button as it may get damaged. Button operates with slight finger force as they are electronically controlled.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p192_img02` (page 192, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p192_img02.png`

### Concept

To protect ventilated seats-

### Concept

• Use the air ventilation seat ONLY when the vehicle HVAC system is on.

### Concept

• Never use liquids like alcohol, high viscosity oils or other to spill on ventilated seats.

### Concept

• Avoid spillage of liquids on the ven- tilated seats surface this may lead to blockage of ventilated seat sys- tem and may not function properly.

### Concept

• Do not add seat covers, as it will not allow ventilated seats to func- tion properly.

### Concept

• Do not keep plastic covers of seat as it is, as it will not allow ventilated seats to function properly.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p192_img01` (page 192, confidence 0.964)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p192_img01.png`
- Image: `doc_005_p192_img03` (page 192, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p192_img03.png`

### Concept

Ventilated seats to be vacuum cleaned regularly as there are chances of air vent hole blockage af- ter usage.

title: REGENERATION PROCESS
text:
# REGENERATION PROCESS

## Knowledge

### Concept

MAINTENANCE AND CARE

### Concept

DPF is a mechanical filter that physically traps particulate matter from diesel engine exhaust gas. DPF traps the particulate matter in the fol- lowing way:

### Concept

• Filtration – Particulates/soot are col- lected in the inlet channel of the filter.

### Concept

• Regeneration – When the filter chan- nels are filled up with soot, they are cleaned automatically by the engine management system. This process is known as DPF Regeneration and this will happen during normal running of the vehicle. In certain specific driving conditions, DPF regeneration may not happen automati- cally as the desired temperatures required to regenerate soot many not be achieva- ble due to specific driving conditions. This may happen in prolonged driving at low vehicle speeds for considerable amount of time (driving in heavy city traffic), pro- longed running of the engine in idle condi- tions, use of adulterated diesel etc.

### Warning

In such cases, a DPF warning lamp will be illuminated indicating that soot regenera- tion is insufficient. PARK DPF Regeneration Procedure (if equipped)

### Specification

This procedure enables DPF regeneration strategy on vehi- cle through vehicle infotain- ment system. PARK DPF regeneration is only possible when the DPF tell-tale appears in the in- strument cluster. Follow the below steps to perform DPF Regeneration through Infotainment sys- tem. 1. Park the vehicle safely in a well venti- lated levelled open space and free of any flammable material in vicinity. Do not park vehicle in enclosed place, above grass (especially dry grass/leaves/ cellulose materials etc.) while doing DPF regeneration. 2. Ensure adequate fuel availability (10.0L minimum) and keep the bonnet open.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p405_img02` (page 405, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p405_img02.png`

### Concept

3. Shift the gear lever to Neutral in en- gine running condition and apply the parking brake. 4. Do not press Accelerator/ Brake/ Clutch pedal during the Park DPF re- generation procedure.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p405_img00` (page 405, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p405_img00.png`

### Concept

• Do not park vehicle close to any flammable material during DPF re- generation process to avoid fire in- cidents.

### Concept

• Do not touch, keep away yourself and kids from exhaust system to avoid burns/injury.

### Procedure

DPF Regeneration process will not start if CHECK ENGINE LAMP or MIL telltale is ON in the cluster. Take your vehicle to an authorised TATA dealer for assistance. While DPF regenera- tion is ON do not press the accelera- tor, brake, clutch pedals or change the gear from neutral or park or do not

text:
# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

## Knowledge

### Specification

Recheck the tyre and its pressure. If the tyre pressure is less than 130kPa (1.3bar, 19 psi) or if there are any visible cracks, bumps or similar damage on the side wall, do not continue to use the tyre.

### Concept

• After using the sealant you may drive no faster than 80 km/h and the damaged tyre must be replaced as quickly as possible (within a maxi- mum driving distance of 200 km.

### Concept

New sealant and replacement parts can be purchased from your authorized repair shop or dealer. Sealant bottles can be dis- posed with house-hold waste.

### Concept

For Normal Tyre - Checking/inflation Of Tyre Pressure Follow the below Process

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p340_img00` (page 340, confidence 0.989)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p340_img00.png`

### Procedure

• Remove the puncture repair kit from the luggage area. • Insert the power plug into the 12V power socket connection and start the vehicle in idling. • Remove the plug from the tyre valve and screw the inflator hose into the tyre valve • Press the switch to “I” present on the inflator and the motor will start to in- flate. • As specified pressure is achieved then switch to “0” present on the in- flator and compressor will turn off.

### Concept

• Check the tyre pressure again. If tyre pressure is too high, deflate the tyre to the specified pressure using the pres- sure “air release” valve.

### Concept

• Remove the inflator hose from the tyre valve and plug the tyre valve safely.

### Specification

• Remove the power plug 12V from the power socket and assemble it properly and keep the unit in luggage space again for next use.

### Concept

Remember that emergency road-side tyre repair kits only provide temporary mobility. You should consult a tyre specialist for advice.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p340_img01` (page 340, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p340_img01.png`

title: 11. Hydraulic Brake Assist (HBA)
text:
# 11. Hydraulic Brake Assist (HBA)

## Knowledge

### Concept

• The ESC, ROM, CSC system can- not prevent all Roll overs beyond the capabilities of Physics. The ca- pabilities of ESC, ROM, CSC equipped vehicle must never be ex- ploited in a reckless or dangerous manner that could risk the user’s safety. • ESC, ROM, CSC systems aid in providing safety & prevent acci- dents. However, the Safety of the vehicles always lies in the hands of the driver. 9. Brake Disc Wiping (BDW)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p42_img00` (page 42, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p42_img00.png`

### Concept

Moisture on the brake discs leads to delay in brake response time, the purpose of the function Brake Disc Wiping is to remove this moisture when driving in wet condi- tions automatically. The Brake Control ECU detects the probability of moisture on the brake disc with help of brake wet- ness model which uses the wiper infor- mation and the vehicle speed to trigger the BDW function which applies a very

### Concept

light braking in order to remove this mois- ture on the brake discs.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p42_img01` (page 42, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p42_img01.png`

### Concept

• The BDW system will not be able to sense water splashed on disc from situations such as water wash or water puddles.

### Concept

• In these situations, it is advised that the driver drive the vehicle slowly and apply the brakes gently until the brake performance returns to normal.

### Concept

10. Electronic Brake Pre-fill (EBP)

### Concept

Electronic Brake Prefill predicts a panic braking scenario based on the Accelera- tor Pedal release rate and prefills the Brake system so as to reduce the air gap between the brake pad and brake disc. This helps to improve the brake response time and braking performance in case of panic situations.

### Concept

During EBP activation, when the driver presses the brake pedal, the brake pe- dal will be a bit hard this is intended behaviour as the elasticity in the brakes system is reduced by prefilling the brake system.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p42_img02` (page 42, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p42_img02.png`

### Concept

The brake assist recognizes from the op- erating speed of the brake pedal whether the driver wants an emergency stop and increases the brake pressure automati- cally up to the ABS control range, as long as the driver keeps the brake pedal pressed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p42_img03` (page 42, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p42_img03.png`

### Concept

• The HBA system cannot prevent collisions, the capabilities of an HBA equipped vehicle must never be exploited in a reckless or dan- gerous manner that could risk the user’s safety.

title: 8. Roll Over Mitigation (ROM)
text:
# 8. Roll Over Mitigation (ROM)

## Knowledge

### Concept

• If HDC is faulty, The HDC malfunc- tion lamp remains ON in the Instru- ment cluster.

### Concept

• If HDC malfunction lamp remains on in the instrument cluster drive carefully and have HDC checked immediately at a TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre as soon as possible. 6. Hill Hold Control (HHC) Hill Hold Control is comfort function which ensures that the vehicle does not roll back when you start from standstill on a gradi- ent or on an inclined surface. HHC holds the brakes for a predefined time while you switch your foot from brake pedal to ac- celerator pedal thus preventing roll back. The moment you press the accelerator pedal, it releases the brakes and vehicle moves forward. The HHC will function on both vehicle fac- ing uphill and downhill if the following con- ditions are met.

### Concept

1. Vehicle must be equipped with HHC. 2. Vehicle must be on sufficient gradient.

### Concept

3. Parking brake must not be engaged. 4. Correct gear engaged a. Vehicle facing uphill– Gear should

### Concept

be in forward b. Vehicle facing downhill – Gear

### Concept

should be in reverse

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p41_img00` (page 41, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p41_img00.png`

### Concept

The HHC feature cannot prevent vehi- cle roll back in all scenarios, the safety of the vehicle lies in the hands of the driver

### Warning

The HHC warning lamp in the instrument cluster lights up when the ignition is switched on. It goes off after a few sec- onds if the system is healthy.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p41_img01` (page 41, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p41_img01.png`

### Warning

• If HHC is faulty, The HHC Warning lamp remains ON in the Instrument cluster.

### Concept

• Drive carefully. Have HHC checked immediately at a TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre as soon as possible.

### Concept

7. Traction Control System (TCS) Traction Control system is designed to control wheel spin during acceleration, when the driver requested torque is way greater than the tractive limits of the sur- face. In the event of loss of traction, the system minimizes wheel spin by control- ling Engine torque and by modulating the brake pressure on individual wheels.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p41_img02` (page 41, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p41_img02.png`

### Concept

For optimal performance of the TCS feature, the tyres must be in good con- dition and must be inflated as per TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre guidelines.

### Concept

The ROM function constantly monitors the vehicle behaviour with the help of the wheel speed sensors, steering angle sen- sor and inertial sensor and intervenes when the vehicle goes out of control and shows tendency to roll over. Roll over Mit- igation brakes individual wheels to reduce the speed of the vehicle to prevent roll over and to stabilize the vehicle.

text:
# INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

VEHICLE TELEMATICS (if equipped)

### Concept

Car is equipped with iRA - Connected car Technology which offers a host of fea- tures to the users through the “TATA Mo- tors iRA 2.0” Mobile Application (APP). The Vehicle is equipped with an Elec- tronic Control unit which monitors & rec- ords the data from various vehicle sys- tems like Engine, Transmission, Brake, Battery & other electrical systems. This data is then processed & used for provid- ing the connected Car features. (Refer the app walkthrough option in the mobile app to explore connected car features.)

### Concept

The Connected Car module records the following information:

### Concept

Vehicle Telemetry and Health

### Concept

This includes the periodic transmission of data from other vehicle ECUs & Electronic systems like EMS, ABS, Air Bag,

### Concept

BCM along with the geographical location of the vehicle.

### Concept

Vehicle Driving Behaviour

### Concept

This includes the location, speed, accel- eration, trip details etc.

### Concept

Event Based Recording This includes data generated during spe- cific events like vehicle collisions, intru- sion, etc. Connected data is used by TATA Motors Passenger Vehicle Limited for various purposes, including, but not limited to: • Providing connected car features through mobile APP. • Evaluation of Vehicle performance. • Research & improvement of current & future vehicle designs. • Troubleshooting & diagnostics of the vehicle. TATA MOTORS does not disclose the data recorded from your vehicle to any third party except: • After obtaining a written consent from the Car Owner. • Upon request from Law enforcing agencies and regulatory bodies.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

• Driver should follow all safety rules and regulations, traffic rules. Its driver responsibility to be alert and driver should have always control on vehicle even in ACC on mode.

### Concept

• Driver should have safe and proper distance from preceding vehicle and apply brake on time as per real situa- tion if system does not decelerate ve- hicle or does not maintain speed or distance from preceding vehicle.

### Concept

• Driver should not validate ACC fea- ture in real road conditions, incorrect way to use ACC may lead to severe accident and damage.

### Warning

• Driver should always follow ACC alerts or warning given by system.

### Concept

• ACC may decelerate slowly or may not stop the vehicle in time so driver should always be attentive and inter- vene through applying brake if re- quired.

### Concept

• Always drive in ACC active mode within speed limits.

### Concept

• ACC should be used in less or mode- rate traffic road conditions. Use of ACC where pedestrians crossing path is normal may lead to accident.

### Concept

• ACC may not detect target and decel- erate speed when any four-wheeler or two-wheeler cut-in immediately.

### Concept

• ACC should always use in well-con- structed and maintained road condi- tions.

### Concept

• ACC should always use on road where clear visible lane marking and sign boards are available.

### Concept

The steering wheel switches are used for ACC operations. ACC Cruise ON/OFF: This button is used to ON/OFF the ACC function. ACC Cruise RESUME/CAN- CEL: This button is used to re- sume to the initial set speed OR cancel the ACC function temporarily in same IGN cycle.

title: IN CASE OF FLAT TYRE
text:
# IN CASE OF FLAT TYRE

## Knowledge

### Concept

EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN

### Concept

• Reduce vehicle speed gradually, Avoid sudden steering movement or braking.

### Concept

• Pay attention to the traffic conditions as you do so.

### Warning

• Switch on the hazard warning lamps.

### Concept

• Stop the vehicle on solid, non-slippery and level ground, as far away as pos- sible from traffic.

### Concept

• Use the Jack on level, hard ground. Avoid changing the wheel on uphill and downhill slopes. Chocks the wheels, if the deflated wheel needs to be changed on slope/ghat area.

### Concept

• If possible, bring the front wheels into the straight-ahead position.

### Concept

• Secure the vehicle against rolling away.

### Concept

• Set the parking brake firmly and shift into “R” (Reverse) gear on level ground and while vehicle is in downhill position.

### Concept

• When the vehicle is in uphill position, shift the gear in first gear.

### Concept

• Switch off the IGN.

### Warning

• Keep advance warning triangle at a suitable distance behind the vehicle as an indication of breakdown.

### Concept

• Close all the doors.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p332_img00` (page 332, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p332_img00.png`

### Concept

If you drive with a flat tyre, there is a risk of the following hazards:

### Concept

• A flat tyre affects the ability to steer or brake the vehicle.

### Concept

• You could lose control of the vehi- cle.

### Concept

• Continued driving with a flat tyre will permanently damage the tyre and cause excessive heat build-up and possibly a fire. There is a risk of an accident.

### Concept

Loosen the nuts (as indicated) on the wheel in diagonal sequence. Do not un- screw the nuts completely before raising the vehicle using the jack.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p332_img01` (page 332, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p332_img01.png`

### Concept

• The jack is designed only to raise and hold the vehicle for a short time while a wheel is being changed. It is not suited for performing mainte- nance work under the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p332_img02` (page 332, confidence 0.991)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p332_img02.png`

# MAINTENANCE AND CARE

## Knowledge

### Warning

The lamp blinks constantly to in- dicate that the DPF needs to eliminate the trapped pollutants (particulate matter) through the regenera- tion process, it therefore does not indicate a malfunction. The lamp remains off dur- ing the entire DPF regeneration and it lamps up only when driving conditions re- quire the driver to be notified. To switch OFF the lamp, keep the car running until lamp, keep the car running until regener- ation is complete (ideally at 3rd gear, 60 km/h with engine speed over 2000 rpm). The process normally takes about 20 minutes. Note: Failure to obey the correct proce- dure for long distance when the DPF lamp comes ON can cause the warning lamp (MIL) to come ON. In that case, please contact nearest TATA MOTORS Author- ised Service Centre to restore correct DPF operation.

# I 9 to 18kg D, C, B, B1, A X IL IUF

## Knowledge

### Concept

A CRS in a closed vehicle can be- come very hot. To prevent burns, check the seating surface and buckles before placing your child in CRS.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p36_img00` (page 36, confidence 0.992)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p36_img00.png`

### Concept

Do not modify CRS in any way.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p36_img01` (page 36, confidence 0.987)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p36_img01.png`

### Concept

• Do not install a booster seat or a booster cushion with only the lap strap of the seat belt or a seat belt that is slack or twisted.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p36_img02` (page 36, confidence 0.99)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p36_img02.png`

### Concept

• Do not leave any toys or other ob- jects loose in the CRS or on the seat while the vehicle is in motion.

### Concept

IL: The seat is suitable for the ISOFIX child seats with “Semi-Universal” approval.

### Concept

IUF: The seat is suitable for forward facing child seats and is permitted for use in this weight category.

### Concept

X : The seat is not equipped for the ISOFIX system.

### Concept

*Rear outboard seating positions are suitable for ISO/R3, Class C CRS.

### Concept

Recommended CRS Positions (CRS That can be Used With ISOFIX System)

### Specification

0 Up to 10kg E X IL IL X

### Specification

0+ Up to 13kg C, D, E X IL IL X

### Specification

II 15 to 25kg X IL IL X

### Specification

III 22 to 36kg X IL IL X

### Concept

After a collision, we recommend to get seat belts, seats, ISOFIX, and top-tether anchorages (as may be applicable) inves- tigated at TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre. Each CRS should be used for one child only. The passenger airbag can be turned OFF manually through switch provided on side face of the dashboard at front passenger side. Visual signal of passenger airbag ON or OFF is indicated on the roof con- sole. When passenger airbag is ON, a rear- ward-facing child seat shall not be in- stalled on the front passenger seat. When passenger airbag is OFF, a forward or rearward-facing child seat can be in- stalled on the front passenger seat. While installing a rearward-facing child seat on the front passenger seat, passen- ger airbag must be OFF. Refer images in PAB Switch section.

### Warning

### Procedure

### Procedure

Press the button to resume the initial set speed OR cancel speed limit function temporarily in same IGN cycle. Press the button up (SET+) to increase the set speed. If user presses the button for short duration, then set speed will increase by 1 km/h and for long press set speed will increase by 10 km/h.

#### Visual References

### Procedure

# 20. Driver Doze Off Alert (DDOA) - (If equipped)

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

Auto Hold will be released when acceler- ator pedal is depressed in first gear or Re- verse gear (in case of Manual Transmis- sion) and R (Reverse), D (Drive) or Man- ual shift mode (in case of Automatic Transmission).

### Note

NOTE • When the vehicle is turned off keeping the Auto Hold in the ON condition, Auto Hold will get re- leased and EPB will get automati- cally applied. • For safety, for smooth take off de- press the accelerator pedal slowly when the Auto Hold is active. Auto Hold Turn Off

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p47_img00` (page 47, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p47_img00.png`

### Concept

In Ignition ON Condition, depress the Auto hold switch the Auto Hold indication in white colour will disappear from the cluster indicating Auto Hold is turned off.

### Concept

Auto Hold once turned ON will not be turned off automatically until it is disen- gaged by switch input from user.

### Note

NOTE Auto hold function will not become ac- tive if • Driver Seat bet is unbuckled • Driver Door is not closed properly • EPB is in applied condition

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p47_img01` (page 47, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p47_img01.png`

### Concept

For end user safety Auto hold will shift au- tomatically to EPB in below conditions:

### Concept

1. Auto Hold in Active for more than 3 minutes. 2. Auto Hold in Active state and Driver door is opened. 3. Auto Hold in Active state and Driver seat belt is unbuckled. 4. Auto Hold in Active state and Auto Hold switch pressed to disengage Auto Hold without pressing brake pe- dal. 5. Auto hold active and engine turned OFF by engine start stop feature.

### Concept

In above conditions Auto Hold indication will change from Green to white and EPB indication will be turned on in the cluster.

### Warning

1. Many road accidents are due to micro sleep activity of the driver 2. Driver Doze off Alert feature monitors the behaviour of the driver on a con- tinuous basis & detects patterns of a drowsy driver. 3. In case drowsiness is detected, au- dio/visual warning would be displayed on the Instrument Panel Cluster. 4. Driver steering behaviour along with the overall trip duration, time of the day, drive monotony are considered to detect a sleepy driver. 5. The function helps in accident reduc- tion by giving prompt warning to the driver to stay alert or take a break. 6. The function will reset once there is a driver change detected or sufficient break time has elapsed. 7. No additional H/W such as driver fac- ing camera is required.

text:
# MAINTENANCE AND CARE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Engine Oil Quality Monitoring Indica- tor

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p389_img00` (page 389, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p389_img00.png`

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a feature in the engine man- agement system which will monitor the engine oil quality throughout the lifetime of the oil in the en- gine. This will ensure that an oil change is requested only when really necessary. Once the oil quality reaches a threshold, the engine management system will ask for oil change by lighting the above lamp. This lamp will be blinking for oil change re- quest.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p389_img02` (page 389, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p389_img02.png`

### Concept

Depending on your driving conditions, the oil quality may get deteriorated sooner. For example, if you are driving predomi- nantly in highway conditions without straining the engine excessively, the oil lamp indicating oil change may appear later than expected. Similarly, if you drive continuously and for a long time in city at low speeds with frequent cold starts and short journeys, the engine management system may prompt you to change the oil sooner than had the car been used mainly in highways.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p389_img01` (page 389, confidence 0.995)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p389_img01.png`

### Concept

• Under no circumstances oil change intervals should exceed 15,000 km or 12 Months, which- ever occurs earlier.

### Concept

This behavior is absolutely normal, the oil change is intended to keep your engine at peak efficiency, and replacing used oil with fresh oil is normal maintenance and not a malfunction.

### Concept

As soon as this lamp is blinking, the oil should be changed as per oil change / ser- vicing procedure. Please contact nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Cen- tre immediately. Once the oil is changed as per the normal oil change / servicing procedure, the oil quality should be reset using TATA MOTORS diagnostic tool. The vehi- cle should never be run again after an oil change without resetting oil quality using TATA MOTORS diagnostic tool. If the vehicle is continuously driven ignor- ing this lamp, MIL, in addition to the above lamp, will be turned ON. Depending on the distance driven without oil change and oil quality reset, the engine will go into a soft or strong performance reduction mode.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_005_p389_img03` (page 389, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_005/p389_img03.png`

### Concept

The TATA HARRIER has been manufactured to give you eco- nomical and trouble free performance. To achieve this, please follow the instructions as stated. Your vehicle is entitled to three free services (labour only). The free service coupons are attached to the sales invoice. Please present these coupons to the servicing dealer while availing free services.

### Concept

1st free service - At 1000-2000 kms. OR 2 months, whichever is earlier. 2nd free service - At 7000-8000 kms. OR 6 months, whichever is earlier. 3rd free service - At 14500-15500 kms. OR 12 months, which- ever is earlier.

### Concept

All services other than free services are chargeable Servicing of the vehicle can be done at any TATA MOTORS Au- thorised Dealer Workshop or TATA MOTORS Authorised Ser- vice Centre (TASC). # STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

The engine emits poisonous ex- haust gases such as carbon mon- oxide. Inhaling these exhaust gases leads to poisoning. There is a risk of fatal injury. Therefore, never leave the engine running in enclosed spaces without sufficient ventilation.

### Concept

After starting, run the engine in idle speed for at least 30 seconds. Do not press accelerated pedal while starting the engine to avoid damage to turbocharger.

### Concept

Turn the key to ‘ACC’ position to switch off the engine. Before switching off the engine, run the engine in idle condition for at least 30 seconds and then switch off. This will allow the engine oil to lubri- cate the turbocharger, till its speed is fully reduced and also allow the unit to cool down.

### Concept

 A quick burst on the accelerator

### Concept

before turning off the engine serves no practical purpose, it wastes fuel and can damage tur- bocharger.  Do not switch off the engine

### Concept

when it is running at high speed. This will lead to premature turbo- charger bearing wear.

### Concept

Starting and stopping (PEPS) (If equipped)

### Concept

Engine Passive Start/Stop

### Concept

Start/Stop switch is provided on the dashboard towards the right side of steering wheel.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Your vehicle has power assisted brakes.

### Concept

The distance needed to bring the vehicle to a halt increases with the speed of the vehicle. Start applying brake anticipating the distance and slow down gradually.

### Concept

 Never use the brake pedal as a

### Concept

footrest.  If you rest your foot on the brake

### Concept

pedal while driving, the braking system can overheat. This in- creases the stopping distance and can even cause the braking system to fail. There is a risk of an accident.  Never press the brake pedal and

### Concept

the accelerator pedal at the same time.

### Concept

If you have driven for a long time in heavy rain without braking, there may be a delayed reaction from the brakes when braking for the first time. This may also

### Concept

occur after the vehicle has been washed.

### Concept

Brake performance may become poor and unpredictable if brakes are wet.

### Concept

After driving through water or washing the underside of the vehicle, test the brakes while driving at a slow speed to see if they have maintained their normal effectiveness. If the brakes are less ef- fective than normal, dry them by repeat- edly applying the brakes while driving slowly until the brakes have regained their normal effectiveness.

### Concept

Braking on downhill gradients

### Concept

On long and steep gradients, you must reduce the load on the brakes by shifting early to a lower gear. This allows you to take advantage of the engine braking ef- fect and helps avoid overheating and ex- cessive wear of the brakes.

### Concept

 Do not shift to lower gear on a

### Concept

slippery road surface in an at- tempt to increase the engine's braking effect, the drive wheels could lose their grip.  There is an increased danger of

### Concept

skidding and accidents.

title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Climbing Sharp Gradients on Loose Surfaces

### Concept

Start off smoothly in a suitable gear. Ac- celerate smoothly so that there is no loss of traction by over-revving of the engine.

### Concept

Choose a slope as smooth as possible and select the appropriate gear so that gear changing in the middle of the climb is not required.

### Concept

Changing gears in the middle of the climb can cause loss of momentum and engine stalling. Shifting to lower gear has to be done cautiously to avoid loss of traction.

### Concept

Under no conditions should the vehicle be moved diagonally across a hill. The danger is in loss of traction and sideways slippage, possibly resulting in toppling over. If unavoidable, choose as mild an angle as possible and keep the vehicle moving.

### Concept

If the wheels start to slip within few feet of the end of the climb, motion can be maintained by swinging the steered wheels left and right, thereby providing increased grip.

### Concept

If the vehicle stalls or losses headway while climbing a steep hill, make a quick shift to reverse and allow the vehicle to move back with the control of engine compression.

### Concept

Descending Sharp Gradients

### Concept

Depending on the severity of the gradi- ent, shift into appropriate gear. Use en- gine braking judiciously without over-rev- ving the engine.

### Concept

Brake application under such situations should be done very.

### Warning

WARNING When descending on sharp gradi- ents, NEVER turn the ignition key to the ‘OFF’ position. Emission con- trol system damage may result.

### Concept

Stopping the vehicle

### Concept

Turn the key to ‘ACC’ position to switch off the engine. Before switching off the engine, run the engine in idle condition for at least 30 seconds and then switch off. This will allow the engine oil to lubri- cate the turbocharger, till its speed is fully reduced and also allow the unit to cool down.

### Warning

WARNING A quick burst on the accelerator before turning off the engine serves absolutely no practical pur- pose, it wastes fuel and can dam- age turbocharger.
