### Concept

 Never place your arm over the

### Concept

airbag as a deploying airbag can result in serious arm fractures or other injuries.  Do not allow the passengers to

### Concept

lean their heads or bodies onto doors or place objects between the doors and passengers when they are seated on seats equipped with side and/or curtain air bags.  Do not place or stick any item/s

### Concept

in the vehicle, except at designated locations (such as utility bins, cup/bottle holders, boot space etc). Loose items may act as a projectile during a collision and cause severe to fatal injuries.  Please be aware that any unsecured item in your vehicle, such as your pet, unsecured CRS or a laptop, can become a potential hazard in the event of a

### Concept

collision or sudden stop, causing injuries to occupants in the vehicle.  Coat hooks if provided, must be

### Concept

used only for that purpose. Never hang heavy items on to those hooks. This could affect deployment of the air bags, and may lead to severe to fatal injuries.  ALWAYS contact your TATA MOTORS authorised service centre if the vehicle is damaged, even if airbag has not inflated.  ALWAYS contact your TATA MOTORS authorised service centre if any part of an airbag module cover shows sign of cracking or damage.

### Concept

If your SRS malfunctions, the air bag may not inflate properly during a colli- sion thereby increasing risk of serious in- jury or death. If any of the following con- ditions occur, your SRS is malfunction- ing:

### Warning

 The SRS warning lamp does not

### Warning

turn ‘ON’ when the ignition switch is placed in the ‘ON’ position for few seconds.  The SRS warning lamp stays ‘ON’

### Warning

after illuminating  The SRS warning lamp comes

### Warning

‘ON’/stays ‘ON’ while the vehicle is in motion.  The SRS warning lamp blinks

### Concept

when the engine is running.

### Concept

We recommend the customer to imme- diately visit TATA MOTORS authorised service centre and get the SRS system inspected if any of the above conditions occur.

### Concept

 Never make any modifications to

### Concept

your vehicle. The modifications carried out, but not limited to the vehicle frame, bumpers, front fenders, ride height, suspension, seat belts, interior trims, steering wheel (especially holders), are not acceptable. This will affect the intended performance of SRS system.  Fitment of bull bars, seat covers

### Concept

on seats with airbags etc, is strictly prohibited, unless authorised by TATA MOTORS. This will affect the intended performance of SRS system.  If you need to make any

### Concept

modifications to accommodate any disability you may have,

### Concept

please contact your Authorized TATA MOTORS Dealer for necessary guidance.  Do not tamper with SRS in any

### Warning

way. This will lead to unexpected performance of system and may cause serious injury or death. Airbag Warning sticker on front passenger Sun visor

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p25_img00` (page 25, confidence 0.982)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p25_img00.png`

### Warning

The Airbag Warning Symbol on sun visor reminds extreme hazards associated with the use of rearward-facing child re- straint on front passenger seat during airbag deployment

### Concept

Never use a rearward facing child restraint on a seat protected by an active Airbag in front of it, Death or serious injury to the child can oc- cur.

### Concept

Air Bag Deployment Conditions

### Concept

When front airbags should not de- ploy?

### Concept

Minor frontal collision : Seat belt of- fers adequate occupant protection in low severity collisions. The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trigger the airbags. De- ployment of frontal airbags is not benefi- cial in low severity collisions.

### Concept

Side collision: During a side collision, occupants tend to move sideways. Therefore, deploying frontal airbags in such situations will not benefit the occu- pants. Side airbags, side curtain airbags (if equipped) are specifically designed to reduce the injuries that can occur in side collision.

### Concept

Rear collision: During a rear collision, occupants tend to move (rearwards) away from frontal airbags. Therefore, de- ploying frontal airbags in such situations will not benefit the occupant protection. Head restraints and seat belts provide

### Concept

occupant protection during a rear colli- sion.

### Concept

Rollovers collision: During a rollover collision occupants may float inside the passenger compartment, if unbelted. This will increase the risk of injuries. Wearing seat belts provide highly effec- tive occupant protection during rollover collision. If your vehicle is equipped with a rollover sensor, both, seat belt and side curtain airbag can provide highly ef- fective occupant protection during rollo- ver collision. Front airbags, however, are not designed to deploy in a rollover as frontal airbags cannot offer any protec- tion in rollover collision.

### Concept

When front airbags deploy with mi- nor or no visible vehicle damage?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trig- ger the airbags. A severe collision to the vehicle underbody or suspension may cause airbags deployment. Examples in- clude rough road driving, running into a curb or other low fixed object that

### Concept

causes a sudden vehicle deceleration. Since the collision is underneath the ve- hicle, damage may not be readily visible.

### Concept

When front airbags may not deploy, even with exterior visible vehicle damage?

### Concept

The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trig- ger the airbags. The amount of visible ve- hicle damage is not always the correct indicator for airbag deployment. Some collisions can result in visible damage but no airbag deployment because the airbags would not have been needed or would not have provided protection even if they had deployed.

### Concept

When a side airbag deploys with mi- nor or no visible vehicle damage? The airbags are triggered only when there is a collision severe enough to trig- ger the airbags. If the airbag system senses sudden deceleration, a strong collision to the side of the vehicle’s frame can cause a side airbag to deploy. In such cases, there may be little

### Concept

When a side airbag may not deploy, even with exterior visible vehicle damage?

### Concept

It is possible that the side airbag does not deploy during a collision that results in visible severe damage. This can occur when the point of collision is toward the far front or far rear of the vehicle or when the vehicle’s crushable body parts ab- sorbed most of the collision energy. In ei- ther case, the side airbag would not have been needed nor provided protec- tion even if it had deployed.

### Concept

Child Lock (if equipped)

### Concept

Both the rear doors of the vehicle are provided with a child proof lock. Push the lock lever located on vertical face of the door downward before closing the door. The door which has been closed by acti- vating the child lock cannot be opened from inside, it can be opened only from the outside.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p27_img00` (page 27, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p27_img00.png`

### Concept

 Lift the lock lever upward to de- activate the childproof lock when not required.

### Concept

 Child safety lever to be used for safety of child for preventing them to open rear door while seating in passenger seat to avoid accident while vehicle is running.

### Concept

Anti-Theft Device-Immobilizer/ PEPS (If equipped)

### Concept

Immobilizer system is designed to pre- vent vehicle theft by electronically disa- bling the engine ignition system. The en- gine can be started only with vehicle’s original Immobilizer ignition key which has an electronic identification pro- grammed code.

### Concept

Vehicle Condition Immobilizer Lamp Status Vehicle State Meaning / Function of the state

### Concept

Ignition OFF Blinking Locked Vehicle Immobilized and awaiting electronic key

### Concept

Ignition ON OFF Unlocked Normal condition and ready to start the vehicle

### Concept

Ignition ON ON Locked

### Concept

- Problem with key (Wrong key used to start vehicle) - Problem with Immobilizer system. Contact a TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre

### Concept

Ignition ON Blinking Unlocked - Contact a TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre immediately

### Concept

Anti-lock braking system (ABS)

### Concept

ABS regulates brake pressure in such a way that the wheels do not lock when you brake. This allows you to continue steering the vehicle when braking.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p29_img00` (page 29, confidence 0.986)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p29_img00.png`

### Warning

The ABS warning lamp in the instrument cluster lights up when the ignition is switched on. It goes off after 2-3 sec- onds if system is healthy.

### Concept

 If ABS is faulty, the wheels could

### Concept

lock when braking. The steer abil- ity and braking characteristics may be severely impaired. There is an increased danger of skid- ding and accidents.  Drive on carefully. Have ABS

### Concept

checked immediately at the TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Cen- tre as soon as possible.

### Concept

 If ABS intervenes: continue to de-

### Concept

press the brake pedal vigorously un- til the braking situation is over.

### Concept

 To make a full brake application: de-

### Concept

press the brake pedal with full force.

### Concept

If ABS intervenes when braking, you will feel a pulsing in the brake pedal. The pul- sating brake pedal can be an indication of hazardous road conditions, and func- tions as a reminder to take extra care while driving.

### Concept

 The stopping distance required

### Concept

for vehicles with ABS may be slightly more than conventional brake system but ABS will still of- fer the advantage of helping you maintain directional control.

### Concept

 However, remember that ABS will

### Concept

not compensate for bad road or weather conditions or poor driver

### Concept

judgment. Drive within safety mar- gin taking into consideration pre- vailing weather and traffic condi- tions.

### Concept

Electronic brake force distribution (EBD) EBD monitors and controls the brake pressure on the rear wheels to improve driv- ing stability while braking. EBD provides optimal braking pressure distribution between front and rear wheels to optimize braking distance and to ensure vehicle stability by means of lowering braking pressure at rear wheels .

### Concept

 If EBD is malfunctioning, the rear

### Concept

wheels can lock, e.g. under full braking. This increases the risk of skidding and an accident.  You should therefore adapt your

### Concept

driving style to the different han- dling characteristics. Have the brake system checked immedi- ately at a TATA MOTORS Author- ized Service Centre as soon as possible.

### Concept

Additional safety features

### Concept

Cornering Stability Control (CSC)

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p30_img00` (page 30, confidence 0.919)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p30_img00.png`

### Concept

Corner stability Control supports / stabi- lizes vehicle during partial braking on curves by reducing pressure at required inner wheel of the vehicle.

### Concept

This helps to reduce probability of vehi- cle over steering during cornering.

### Concept

Based on wheel speed information off road ABS helps to avoid wheel lock on uneven surfaces like loose gravel, pot holes by reducing the stopping distance compared to standard ABS.

### Concept

Electronic Traction Control (ETC) The Electronic Traction Control system function (ETC) is designed as a slip con- trol system to prevent the driven wheels of a vehicle from excessive wheel slip.

### Concept

Roll over Mitigation (ROM) The main feature of the Roll over Mitiga- tion function is the detection of a rollover

### Concept

critical situation and to prevent the vehi- cle rollover. This is done by active brake interventions on selected wheels, thereby reducing the forces that cause a roll-over situation.

### Concept

Brake Disc Wiping (BDW)

### Concept

Water on the brake disc leads to a delay in brake response time. The purpose of the function Brake Disc wiping is to re- move moisture when driving in wet con- ditions automatically. To get quick re- sponse form Brake and better decelera- tion.

### Concept

Electronic Brake Pre-fill (EBP)

### Concept

The Electronic Brake Prefill (EBP) func- tion reduces the air gap of the brake pad and the brake disc. The function is trig- gered after a sudden release of the ac- celerator pedal due to an unexpected emergency brake situation. By actively pre-filling the brake-system the brake re- sponse time is reduced and results in a shorter stopping distance.

### Concept

Hydraulic Brake Assist (HBA)

### Concept

In a dangerous emergency situation, most drivers don't use the full available performance of the brake system, be- cause they brake too soft. The HBA func- tion detects the critical situation and builds up additional brake pressure to reduce the braking distance.

### Concept

Hydraulic Fading compensation (HFC) In dangerous fading situations most driv- ers operate the brake pedal with a small or regular braking force and they never reach to the maximum possible vehicle deceleration. The HFC function improve the stopping distance by eliminating re- quired pressure build-up lag by the driver.

### Concept

Dynamic Wheel Torque by Brake (DWT-B)

### Concept

The main goal of the function is to im- prove the agility of a vehicle and to ena- ble a more direct steering. This is mainly achieved by braking interventions at the

### Concept

inner wheels during turning. DWT-B re- duces understeer tendency of the car and a higher curve speed can be achieved.

### Concept

Engine Drag Torque Control (EDTC)

### Concept

On slippery road conditions during in- gear Braking or Shift down of gear or sudden throttle release on a curve road. This causes high Engine drag on the driven wheel resulting into brake slip sit- uations without any brake application. This makes vehicle highly under steera- ble. EDTC controls such brake slip on the driven wheels by increasing the engine torque to makes the vehicle stable and steerable.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

 IGN relay turns OFF, ACC relay re-

### Concept

 Amber colour LED on start-stop

### Warning

WARNING When vehicle is in OFF mode ( ACC, IGN and Crank OFF) and user tries to lock the vehicle from outside by pressing any door handle switch and if PEPS detect smart key left inside the vehicle, then audio warning / chime comes ON.

### Concept

Make sure that parking brake is en- gaged and vehicle is in neutral gear.

### Concept

Press the clutch pedal fully and crank the engine. Do not press the accelerator pedal when starting the engine.

### Note

NOTE The Starter protection system fit- ted in this vehicle does not allow you to crank the engine until you fully press the clutch pedal.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p135_img00` (page 135, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p135_img00.png`

### Concept

Release the key as soon as the engine starts. Repeat if engine does not start.

### Concept

The Starter protection system switches off the starter when it is continuously cranked for more than 10 secs. In such a case, get the key back to ‘OFF’ position & wait for 30 secs.

### Warning

WARNING The engine emits poisonous ex- haust gases such as carbon mon- oxide. Inhaling these exhaust gases leads to poisoning. There is a risk of fatal injury. Therefore, never leave the engine running in enclosed spaces without sufficient ventilation.

### Concept

### Concept

text:
# 1. Seat backrest angle adjustment

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Concept

Front seat adjustments

### Concept

Following seat adjustments can be car- ried out manually.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p123_img00` (page 123, confidence 0.979)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p123_img00.png`

### Concept

2. Seat height (if equipped)

### Concept

3. Seat forward / rearward adjustment lever

### Warning

WARNING Do not adjust the driver's seat while driving. Adjusting the seat while driving could cause the driver to lose control of the vehicle.

### Concept

To change the seat back rest angle, lean forward slightly and pull up the lever ( 1 ). Adjust seat backrest until it reaches de- sired comfortable position. Make sure that lever returns to its original position and seat is securely latched.

### Note

NOTE Adjust the seat backrest until your arms are slightly angled when holding the steering wheel.

### Warning

WARNING Never travel in a moving vehicle with the seat backrest in an exces- sively reclined position as this can be dangerous. You could slide un- der the seat belt in a collision.

### Concept

2. Seat height adjustment (If equipped) To raise the seat, pull and continue pumping the lever ( 2 ) in the upward di- rection until the seat is at the desired height.

### Concept

To lower the seat, pump the lever down- ward until the seat is at desired height.

### Concept

3. Seat forward / rearward adjust- ment Lift lever ( 3 ) and slide the seat forwards or rearwards. Release lever and make sure that seat is securely latched.

### Note

NOTE Adjust the driver seat position in such a way that the driver will be able to operate the control pedals conformably.

## Knowledge

### Concept

CAR CARE AND VALUE ADDED SERVICES

### Concept

Cleaning of Windows, Front and Rear Glasses

### Concept

Clean the windows inside and outside with commercially available glass clean- ers.

### Concept

This will remove the haze that builds up on the inside of windows. Use a soft cloth or paper towels to clean all glass and plastic surfaces.

### Concept

FAST TAG is pasted on front windshield from the inside. It enables Electronic toll collection.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p208_img00` (page 208, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p208_img00.png`

### Note

NOTE Do not attempt to rip or tamper the tag. It will disable the functionality of the tag.

### Concept

Waxing and polishing is recommended to maintain the gloss and wet-look ap- pearance of your paint finish.

### Concept

1. Use good quality polish and wax for your vehicle. 2. Re-wax your vehicle when the water does not slip off the surface but col- lects over the surface in patches.

### Concept

Polishing Polishes and cleaners can restore shine to the painted surface that has oxidized and become dull. They normally contain mild abrasives and solvents that remove the top layer of the finish coat. Polish your vehicle, if the finish does not regain its original shine after using wax.

### Concept

Interior fabric cleaning tips

### Concept

1. Stains should be treated immedi- ately. If left for a long time, they can leave a permanent mark.

### Concept

contain artificial colors in the stain creating liquid or semisolid sub- stance. The colorant may leave a stain if kept for longer time.

### Concept

3. Stain should not be removed by rub- bing. As far as possible, try to blot or lift the stain with cloth or plastic spat- ula and then clean the remaining stain with cloth or sponge.

### Concept

4. If the stain has dried, then gently brush off the material and then press with damp cloth or sponge till it dis- appears.

### Concept

5. Do not use household detergents to clean the fabric.

### Concept

6. Always use clean cotton cloth for cleaning.

## Knowledge

### Concept

pressure Uniform wear

### Concept

Excessive center tread

### Concept

Check for inflation and condition of your vehicle tyres periodically. Check the pressure in the tyres when they are cold. Keeping the tyres properly inflated gives you the best combination of riding com- fort, handling, tyre life and better fuel ef- ficiency. Over inflation of tyres makes the vehicle ride bumpy and harsh. Tyres are more prone to uneven wear and damage from road hazards. Under inflated tyres reduce your comfort in vehicle handling and are prone to fail- ures due to high temperature. They also cause uneven wear and more fuel con- sumption.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p186_img00` (page 186, confidence 0.956)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p186_img00.png`

### Note

NOTE Every time you check inflation pressure, you should also examine tyres for uneven wear, damage and trapping of foreign objects in the treads and wear.

### Concept

Recommended tyre pressure in Cold condition (Laden / Unladen)

### Concept

Tyre size Front Rear

### Specification

33 psi / 2.27 bar 33 psi / 2.27 bar

### Note

NOTE In case of Air filling in hot tyre con- dition, increase tyre pressure by 3 psi over specified cold pressures.

### Concept

Tyre pressure sticker location

### Concept

On B Pillar near driver seat.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p186_img01` (page 186, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p186_img01.png`

### Concept

Tyre rotation To increase tyre life rotate the tyre at specified intervals or earlier depending on the operation of vehicle.

### Concept

The illustrations shows how to rotate tyres when normal or temporary spare wheel is fitted.

### Concept

For steel wheel rims with spare steel wheel rim

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p187_img00` (page 187, confidence 0.982)

- Image: `doc_008_p187_img01` (page 187, confidence 0.961)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p187_img01.png`

### Concept

For alloy wheel rims with spare wheel of steel wheel rim (if equipped)

### Concept

Incorrect wheel alignment causes exces- sive and uneven tyre wear. Check wheel alignment at specified intervals.

### Concept

Wheels of your vehicle are balanced for better ride comfort and longer tyre life. Balancing needs to be done whenever tyre is removed from rim.

### Concept

If the vehicle vibrates abnormally on a smooth road, have the wheel balanced done immediately.

### Concept

Special care for tubeless tyres

### Concept

 While removing tyre from wheel rim

### Concept

and mounting it back on wheel rim, take precautions not to damage tyre bead. Use tyre removal and assem- bly machines. Damage or cut on tyre bead may cause gradual loss of air and deflation of tyre.

### Concept

 Do not scratch inside of tubeless tyre

### Concept

with metallic or sharp object. Tube- less tyres are coated with impermea- ble layer of rubber from inside which holds the air inside the tyre. Removal of this layer due to scratching may cause gradual loss of air and defla- tion.

### Concept

 If wheel rim gets damaged in service,

### Concept

get the wheel rim repaired/ replaced immediately. Running the vehicle with damaged rim may cause defla- tion of tyre and subsequent dislodg- ing of tyre from rim.

### Concept

 Maintain recommended inflation pressure. Over-inflation, in particu- lar , may cause puncture or bursting of tyre.

### Note

NOTE  Life and wear pattern of tyres de-

### Concept

pends on various parameters like tyre pressure, wheel alignment, wheel balancing, tyre rotation, etc. It also largely depends on ve- hicle speed, load carried, usage, driving habits, road conditions, tyre quality, etc. In case fault is suspected to be due to poor qual- ity of tyres, the same may be taken up with concerned tyre manufacturer.

### Concept

 For steel rim, Red dot of tyre to be

### Concept

matched with blue dot of rim while re-fitment.

### Concept

 For alloy rim, Yellow dot of tyre to

### Concept

be matched with valve of rim while re-fitment.

### Concept

Remote Key Battery Replacement (For Flip key)

### Concept

Remote control key contains a battery, which is housed under the cover.

### Concept

If red LED on remote flashes for 5 times after operating any button on remote. It is recommended to replace battery at a TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Cen- tre.

### Concept

You should, however, proceed as follows if you wish to replace the discharged bat- tery yourself:

### Concept

1. Open the key blade.

### Concept

2. Press off the battery cover with your thumb or using a flat screwdriver at the points of the arrows.

### Concept

3. Remove the discharged battery from the key by pressing the battery down- wards at the point of the arrow.

### Concept

4. Insert the new battery.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p189_img00` (page 189, confidence 0.984)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p189_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_008_p189_img01` (page 189, confidence 0.976)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p189_img01.png`

### Concept

5. Ensure that the “+” symbol on the battery is facing upwards. The cor- rect polarity is shown on the battery cover.

### Concept

6. Position the battery cover on the key and press on it until it is heard to lock in place.

### Concept

Use CR 2032 battery only.

### Concept

An inappropriately disposed battery can be harmful to the environment and human health. Dispose the battery ac- cording to your local law(s) and regulation.

### Concept

Smart Key Battery Replacement (For PEPS variant)

### Concept

1. Open rear side of key (battery cover).

### Concept

2. Replace with new battery in the smart key battery slot.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p189_img02` (page 189, confidence 0.985)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p189_img02.png`

### Concept

3. Close the battery cover.

### Concept

4. Ensure that the key cover is intact properly.

### Concept

On Board Diagnostic (OBD II) System

### Concept

Diagnostic connector is located on RH side below the steering wheel.

### Concept

On board Diagnostics or OBD, is an auto- motive term referring to a vehicle’s self- diagnostic and reporting capability. The OBD system allows continuous diagno- sis of the components of the vehicle cor- related with emissions. This system warns the driver, by turning “ON” the Malfunction Indication lamp (MIL) on the

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p190_img00` (page 190, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p190_img00.png`

### Concept

instrument cluster, when a fault causes emission levels to increase.

### Concept

The OBD system also has a diagnostic connector that can be interfaced with appropriate diagnostic tools, which makes it possible to read the fault codes stored in the Electronic Control Unit, to- gether with a series of specific parame- ters for Engine operation and Diagnosis. This check can also be carried out by the traffic police.

### Warning

Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) warning Indicator

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF). DPF is a me- chanical filter that physically traps par- ticulate matter from diesel engine ex- haust gas.

### Concept

DPF traps the particulate matter in the following way:

### Concept

 Filtration – Particulates / soot are collected in the inlet channel of the filter.  Regeneration – When the filter

### Concept

channels are filled up with soot, they are cleaned automatically by the en- gine management system. This pro- cess is known as DPF Regeneration and this will happen during normal running of the vehicle.

### Concept

DPF equipped in vehicle normally regen- erates automatically which is controlled by engine management system.

### Warning

In certain specific driving conditions, DPF regenera- tion may not happen auto- matically as the desired temperatures required to regenerate soot may not be achievable due to specific driving condi- tions. This includes prolonged driving at low vehicle speeds for considerable amount of time (driving in heavy city traf- fic), prolonged running of the engine in idle conditions etc. In such cases, a warning lamp as indicated above will be illuminated in the instrument cluster in- dicating that soot regeneration is insuffi- cient.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p191_img00` (page 191, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p191_img00.png`

### Warning

This warning lamp switches ON con- stantly to indicate that the DPF needs to be regenerated. This lamp does not indi- cate any malfunction.

### Warning

The warning lamp remains OFF during normal vehicle behavior and lights up only when driving condition requires the driver to be notified. When this lamp is ON, keep the car running ideally at 3 rd gear, 60 km/hr with engine speed over

### Warning

2000 rpm until regeneration is com- pleted and warning lamp goes OFF. The process normally takes about 20 minutes.

### Note

NOTE Do not shut down engine till the

### Warning

warning lamp goes OFF. If DPF regeneration process requested above is not fol- lowed for a long distance and the vehicle is driven with warning lamp ON, it can cause MIL to be turned ON. Once MIL is ON, please contact nearest TATA authorized service center. Service should connect the TML diag- nostic tool and conduct DPF service re- generation as indicated in the diagnos- tic tool. Insufficient DPF regeneration resulting in the above lamps can also happen if the vehicle is driven with adultered die- sel.

### Concept

Service Instructions

### Concept

The TATA HARRIER has been manufactured to give you eco- nomical and trouble free performance. To achieve this, please follow the instructions as stated.

### Concept

Your vehicle is entitled to three free services (labour only). The free service coupons are attached to the sales invoice. Please present these coupons to the servicing dealer while availing free services.

### Concept

1st free service - At 1,000 - 2,000 kms. OR 2 months, whichever is earlier.

### Concept

2nd free service - At 7,000 - 8,000 kms. OR 6 months, which- ever is earlier.

### Concept

3rd free service - At 14,500 - 15,500 kms. OR 12 months, which- ever is earlier.

### Concept

All services other than free services are chargeable.

### Concept

Servicing of the vehicle can be done at any TATA MOTORS Authorised Dealer Workshop or TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre (TASC).

### Concept

Warranty claims can be settled by any TATA MOTORS Author- ised Dealer Workshop or TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre (TASC).

## Knowledge

### Concept

If your vehicle is parked under the sun, you can cool it down fast by following the steps given below:

### Procedure

1. Start the engine. 2. Turn on A/C by pressing the button. Make sure the temperature control is set to maximum cool. In case of FATC set temperature to ‘Low’ mode. 3. Set the blower to maximum speed 4. Open windows half, set air direction towards face and fresh air mode. 5. # WARRANTY - TERMS AND CONDITIONS

## Knowledge

### Concept

8. This warranty shall not apply to normal maintenance ser- vices like oils & fluid changes, head lamps focusing, fas- tener retightening, wheel balancing and alignment, tyre ro- tation, adjustment of valve clearance, fuel timing, ignition timing and consumables like bulbs, fuel, air & oil filters and gas leaks in case of air conditioned cars.

### Concept

9. This warranty shall not apply to any damage or deteriora- tion caused by environmental pollution or bird droppings. Slight irregularities not recognized as affecting the function or quality of the vehicle or parts, such as slight noise or vi- bration, defects appearing only under particular or irregular operations are items considered characteristics of the ve- hicle.

### Concept

10. This warranty shall be null and void if the car is subjected to abnormal use such as rallying, racing or participation in any other competitive sport. This warranty shall not apply to any repair or replacements as a result of accident or col- lision.

### Concept

11. This warranty is expressly in lieu of all warranties, whether by law or otherwise, expressed or implied, and all other ob- ligations or liabilities on our part and we neither assume, nor authorize any person to assume on our behalf, any

### Concept

other liability arising from the sale of the car or any agree- ment in relation thereto.

### Concept

12. The buyer shall have no other rights except those set out above and have, in particular, no right to repudiate the sale, or any agreement or to claim any reduction in the purchase price of the car, or to demand any damages or compensa- tion for losses, incidental or indirect, or inconvenience or consequential damages, loss of car, or loss of time, or oth- erwise, incurred or accrued.

### Concept

13. Any claim arising from this warranty shall be recognized only if it is notified in writing to us or to our authorized dealer without any delay soon after such defects as cov- ered & ascertained under this warranty.

### Concept

14. This warranty is fully transferable to subsequent vehi- cle owner. Only unexpired remaining period of war- ranty applies.

### Concept

15. We reserve our rights to make any change or modification in design of the car or its parts or to introduce any improve- ment therein or to incorporate in the car any additional part or accessory at any time without incurring any obligation to incorporate the same in the cars previously sold.

### Concept

TATA MOTORS LTD. is committed to produce vehicles using en- vironmentally sustainable technology. A number of features have been incorporated in TATA MOTORS passenger vehicles which have been designed to ensure environmental compati- bility throughout the life cycle of the vehicle. We would like to inform you that your vehicle meets emission norms and this is being regularly validated at the manufacturing stages.

### Concept

As a user you too can protect the environment by operating your vehicle in a proactive manner. A lot depends on your driv- ing style and the way you maintain your vehicle. We have given a few tips for your guidance.

### Concept

 Avoid frequent and violent acceleration.

### Concept

 Do not carry any unnecessary weight in the vehicle as it

### Concept

overloads the engine. Avoid using devices requiring high power consumption during slow city traffic condition.

### Concept

 Monitor the vehicle’s fuel consumption regularly and if

### Concept

showing rising trend get the car immediately attended at the Company’s Authorised Service Outlets.

### Concept

 Switch off the engine during long stops at traffic jams or

### Concept

signals. If you need to keep the engine running, avoid un- necessary revving it up or stopping and starting.

### Concept

 It is not necessary to rev up the engine before turning it off

### Concept

as it unnecessarily burns the fuel.

### Concept

 Shift to higher gears as soon as possible. Use each gear

### Concept

upto 2/3 rd of maximum engine speed.

### Concept

 A chart indicating gear shifting speeds is given in this book.

### Concept

 Ensure that recommended maintenance is carried out on

### Concept

the vehicle regularly at the Authorised Service Outlets.

### Concept

 As soon as you see any leakages of oil or fuel in the vehicle

### Concept

we recommend to get it attended immediately.

### Concept

 Use only recommended grades and specified quantity of

### Concept

 Get your vehicle checked for emission periodically by an au-

### Concept

 Ensure that fuel filter, oil filter and breather are checked

### Concept

periodically and replaced, if required, as recommended by TATA MOTORS.

### Concept

 Do not pour used oils or coolants into the sewage drains,

### Concept

garden soil or open streams. Dispose the used filters and batteries in compliance with the current legislation.

### Concept

 Do not allow unauthorized person to tamper with engine

### Concept

settings or to carry modifications on the vehicle.

### Concept

 Never allow the vehicle to run out of fuel.

### Concept

 Parts like brake liners, clutch discs should be vacuum

### Concept

cleaned. Do not use compressed air for cleaning these parts which may spread dust in the atmosphere.

### Concept

While carrying out servicing or repairs of your vehicle, you should pay keen attention to some of the important engine aggregates and wiring harness which greatly affect emis- sion. These components are:

### Concept

1. Fuel injection equipment’s - pump, rail, injectors, nozzles and high pressure pipes.

### Concept

2. Air Intake & Exhaust system, especially for leakages.

### Concept

3. Cylinder head for valve leakage.

### Concept

4. All filters such as air, oil and fuel filters (check periodically).

### Concept

6. Electrical connections.

### Concept

7. If the ‘Service’ lamp continuously glows, please take the ve- hicle to a TATA MOTORS authorized service outlet.

### Concept

8. Catalytic Converter.

### Concept

9. EMS wiring harness i.e. electrical connections to all sen- sors and actuators.

### Concept

This Owner’s manual contains further information on driving precautions and maintenance care leading to environment protection. Please familiarize yourself with these aspects be- fore driving.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

When towing a break down vehicle, cer- tain precautions and procedures must be taken to prevent damage to the vehi- cle and/or components. Failure to use standard towing precautionary measures when lifting or towing a break down vehicle could result in an unsafe operating condition.

### Concept

To ensure proper towing and to prevent accidental damage to your vehicle, take help of a TATA MOTORS authorized dealer or a commercial tow-truck ser- vice.

### Note

NOTE Make sure that the parking brake is released; vehicle in neutral gear position and steering wheel is un- locked. The power steering func- tions only when engine is running. Hence, during towing the steering efforts will be more.

### Concept

 Never get under your vehicle af-

### Concept

ter it has been lifted by a tow truck.  For towing a vehicle, the best way

### Warning

is to use a wrecker. Alternatively use a rigid tow bar.  Switch 'ON' the hazard warning

### Concept

indicators of both the vehicles to warn other road users.  Limit the speed to 20 - 30 kmph.  In case of brake failure, use the

### Concept

parking brake to control the vehicle.  Fasten the tow rope or tow bar at

### Concept

the towing eyes. Otherwise, the vehicle could be damaged.  When towing, pull away slowly

### Concept

and smoothly. If the tractive power is too high, the vehicles could be damaged.

### Concept

 Unscrew the screws (1) & (2) with the

### Concept

help of screw driver which is provided in Tool kit.

TATA MOTORS shall not be responsi- ble for any such claims, dam- ages/loss or any deficiency of ser- vice of the ASP.

### Concept

 Vehicles will be handled, repaired &

### Concept

 Services entitled to the customers

can be refused or cancelled on ac- count of abusive behavior, fraudu- lent representation, malicious intent and refusal to pay the charges for any charges related services and spare parts during service or on pre- vious occasion on part of the cus- tomer.

 On site repairs may be temporary in

### Concept

nature. The completion of repairs does not certify the road worthiness of the vehicle. The customer is ad- vised to ensure temporary repairs carried out onsite is followed by per- manent repairs at a TATA MOTORS Authorized Workshop at the earliest. Terms and conditions and service coverage, exclusions etc. are subject to change without notice.

### Concept

Maintenance and Service

### Concept

Periodic maintenance is essential for en- suring long trouble free performance.

### Concept

Have your vehicle serviced regularly from TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

### Concept

There is a large network of TATA MO- TORS Authorized Service Centre to help you with their professional servicing ex- pertise. Scheduled maintenance infor- mation is provided which makes tracking routine service easy.

### Concept

The following checks can be carried out between the recommended scheduled maintenance services. Take help of our authorized service centre for assistance.

### Concept

 Engine coolant level

### Concept

 Brake/Clutch fluid level

 Washer fluid level checking & top-

 Tyre inflation pressure including

 Be careful not to touch a hot en-

### Concept

gine, exhaust manifold and pipes, muffler, radiator and wa- ter hoses.  Do not work on a vehicle with the

### Concept

engine running in an enclosed space, unless you are sure of enough ventilation.  Keep all open flames and other

### Concept

burning material (such as ciga- rettes) away from the battery and all fuel related parts. If you need to do any work inside the engine compartment,  Switch off the ignition  Never reach into the area where

### Concept

### Concept

Engine Oil Level checking

### Concept

Turn it ‘OFF’ and wait for 5 minutes for the oil to return to the oil pan. Be sure the vehicle is on a level surface.

### Concept

Take out the dipstick, wipe it clean, and reinsert it fully. Pull it out again and ex- amine the oil level. It should be between ‘MIN’ and ‘MAX’ level. If not, top up with recommended engine oil.

### Note

NOTE The oil consumption depends upon the driving style and the con- ditions under which the vehicle is used.

### Concept

 Do not remove the filler cap

### Concept

when the engine is running.  Do not add oil above the MAX.

### Concept

mark. Oil level above the MAX. mark may cause engine dam- age.

### Concept

For location of Engine oil filling cap and dip stick, please refer Engine Compartment.

### Concept

Engine oil quality Monitoring Indi- cator

### Concept

Your vehicle is equipped with a feature in the en- gine management system which will monitor the engine oil quality through out the lifetime of the oil in the engine. This will ensure that an oil change is requested only when really necessary. Once the oil quality reaches a threshold, the engine management sys- tem will ask for oil change by lighting the above lamp. This lamp will be blinking for oil change request.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p181_img01` (page 181, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p181_img01.png`

### Concept

Depending on your driving conditions, the oil quality may get deteriorated sooner. For example, if you are driving predominently in highway conditions without straining the engine excessively, the oil lamp indicating oil change may appear later than expected. Similarly, if you drive continuously and for a long time in city at low speeds with frequent cold starts and short journeys, the en- gine management system may prompt

### Concept

you to change the oil sooner than had the car been used mainly in highways.

### Concept

 Under no circumstances oil change intervals should exceed 15,000 km or 12 Months, which- ever occurs earlier. This behaviour is absolutely normal, the oil change is intended to keep your en- gine at peak efficiency, and replacing used oil with fresh oil is normal mainte- nance and not a malfunction. As soon as this lamp is blinking, the oil should be changed as per oil change / servicing procedure. Please contact nearest TATA authorized service center immediately . Once the oil is changed as per the normal oil change / servicing procedure, the oil quality should be reset us- ing TML diagnostic tool. The vehicle should never be run again after an oil change without resetting oil quality using TML diagnostic tool.

### Concept

If the vehicle is continuously driven ig- noring this lamp, MIL, in addition to the above lamp, will be turned ON. Depend- ing on the distance driven without oil change and oil quality reset, the engine will go into a soft or strong performance reduction mode.

### Concept

 The appearance of this blinking

### Warning

warning light or symbol is not re- lated to the amount of oil in the engine, so if the light or symbol comes ON and blinking, never add / top up engine oil but con- tact the nearest TATA authorized service center to have oil change and reset.

### Concept

Brake/Clutch Fluid Level

### Procedure

Pull the notch and release the top cover. Remove the cap and check the level. Top up if required.

### Concept

For location of Brake/Clutch Fluid Container and filling cap, please refer Engine Compartment.

### Concept

Engine Coolant Level

### Concept

Check whether the coolant level is be- tween the ‘MIN’ and ‘MAX’ marks pro- vided on the coolant reservoir.

#### Visual References

When the coolant levels is low, top up with recommended coolant up to ‘MAX’. level.

### Note

NOTE In case of emergency, a large amount of water without engine coolant may be added in order to reach a vehicle service location.

### Concept

Whenever coolant has been added, the coolant level in the coolant reservoir should be checked few times after driv- ing the vehicle to confirm correct level.

### Concept

For location of Engine coolant con- tainer and filler cap, please refer En- gine Compartment.

### Concept

Topping of the coolant should be done in the auxiliary tank only.

### Concept

Make sure that only TATA MOTORS rec- ommended coolant is used. Mixing of different coolants may harm your en- gine’s cooling system and its compo- nents. Do not add extra inhibitors or ad- ditives to the coolant. These can be harmful and compromise the corrosion protection of the engine coolant.

### Concept

 The engine cooling system is

### Concept

pressurized, particularly when the engine is warm. When open- ing the cap, you could be scalded by hot coolant spraying out. There is a risk of injury.  Let the engine cool down before

### Procedure

opening the cap. Wear eye and hand protection when opening the cap. Open the cap slowly half a turn to allow pressure to es- cape.

### Concept

Power Steering Fluid Level

### Concept

The level of the power steering fluid should be between the MIN. and MAX. mark on the side of the power steering fluid container. If the level falls below the MIN. mark, add recommended fluid.

WARNING  Do not start the engine without oil

in the power steering system.

ing fluid reservoir during refilling or top up.

### Concept

Windshield Washer Fluid Level

### Concept

Check that there is washer fluid in the tank. Refill it if necessary. Use a good quality windshield washer fluid, diluted with water as necessary.

### Note

text:
# 5. Outside Ambient temperature

## Knowledge

### Concept

DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

### Note

NOTE  AFE value is estimate of fuel economy. It may vary signifi- cantly based upon driving condi- tions, driving habits and condi- tion of vehicle.  Average Fuel Consumption will get Reset to ‘0’ when Battery is removed and refitted.

### Concept

3. Distance to empty (DTE)

### Concept

The above image indicates approximate distance in ‘km’ that your vehicle can travel with available fuel in tank.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p72_img00` (page 72, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p72_img00.png`

### Concept

DTE values may vary significantly based on driving conditions, driving habits, and condition of the vehicle. It is an estimate value of the available driving distance.

### Concept

The DTE will update with new value when fuel is added more than 7 Litres at a time.

### Warning

If low fuel warning light turns ‘ON’, fill the fuel tank immediately regardless the value of displayed DTE.

### Note

NOTE If DTE is displayed as ‘---‘, then take your vehicle to the TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

### Concept

4. Instrument Cluster Illumination

### Procedure

Instrument cluster illumination & back- light illumination will turn on after Park lamp is ON. Illumination can be changed by SET but- ton short press (less than 1.5 seconds).

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p72_img01` (page 72, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p72_img01.png`

### Warning

WARNING The Clock and Instrument Cluster Illumination settings should be done only when the vehicle is in stationary condition for safety pur- pose.

### Specification

This displays outside ambient tempera- ture in units of °C with the resolution of 1 °C. The temperature sensor shows the front bumper of the vehicle, therefore the temperature reading can be affected by heat reflection from the road surface, engine heat and the exhaust from sur- rounding traffic.

Semi-automatic Operation

You can manually select various func- tions of the climate control system when it is in fully automatic mode. All other features remain automatically con- trolled. title: STARTING AND DRIVING
text:
# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

Steering lock cum ignition switch (If applicable)

### Concept

The ignition switch has the following four positions:

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p131_img00` (page 131, confidence 0.983)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p131_img00.png`

### Concept

LOCK - This is the normal parking posi- tion. Key from lock can be removed in this position only.

### Concept

“LOCK” position prevents normal use of the steering wheel after the key is re- moved.

### Procedure

To release the steering lock, insert the key and turn it clockwise to one of the other positions. ACC - Accessories such as the infotain- ment system can be operated, but the engine remains ‘OFF’. Steering gets un- locked. ON - This is the normal operating posi- tion. All electrical systems are ‘ON’. START - Turn the key further clockwise to the START position, (spring loaded) to start the engine. As soon as the engine starts, release the ignition key, which re- turns to ON position. While cranking, all accessories will be momentarily ‘OFF’.

### Concept

Illuminated Key Ring (if equipped) When the vehicle is unlocked, the illumi- nated key ring glows up. This helps to lo- cate ignition switch in the dark.

### Concept

The engine can only be started when the gearshift lever is in “N” position with the clutch pedal firmly pressed.

### Concept

Starting and stopping (without PEPS)

### Concept

Starting the Engine Make sure that parking brake is en- gaged and vehicle is in neutral gear. Press the clutch pedal fully and crank the engine. Do not press the accelerator pedal while starting the engine.

### Concept

The Starter protection sys- tem fitted in this vehicle does not allow you to crank the engine until you fully press the clutch pedal.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p131_img01` (page 131, confidence 0.98)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p131_img01.png`

### Concept

Release the key as soon as the engine starts. Repeat if engine does not start.

### Note

NOTE The Starter protection system switches off the starter when it is continuously cranked for more than 10 secs. In such a case, get the key back to ‘OFF’ position & wait for 30 secs.

text:
# 2. Average fuel economy (AFE)

## Knowledge

### Concept

DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

### Concept

1. Instantaneous fuel economy (IFE)

### Concept

Monitor IFE bar graph to achieve better fuel economy.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p71_img00` (page 71, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p71_img00.png`

### Concept

IFE display does not show Fuel Economy of last drive.

### Concept

The above image indicates fuel economy of current drive when ignition is turned ‘ON’.

### Concept

The display does not show actual value unless vehicle is moving.

### Concept

The indication on the display may be de- layed if fuel consumption is affected by driving pattern.

### Concept

 IFE will vary frequently as per driving pattern.  IFE display does not show Fuel Economy of last drive.  At every ignition ON fuel gauge will be displayed in place of “In- stantaneous fuel consumption” bar graph irrespective of user se- lection screen.  User can toggle between “Fuel Gauge” and “Instantaneous Fuel consumption” bar graph using SET and MODE Button.  User selection to IFE screen will NOT be allowed if fuel is below 1/4 th tank level.  During vehicle running if LCD screen is in “Instantaneous Fuel consumption” bar graph mode & if fuel gauge reduces to 1/4 th tank level then LCD screen will automatically goes to fuel mode.

### Concept

Trip time, Average speed and Trip dis- tance will reset to ‘ 0 ’ when respective Trip meter is reset.

### Concept

Average Fuel Economy will be displayed as ‘--.--‘for initial 0.5 km of respective trip. Once 0.5 km distance is covered, Av- erage Fuel Economy will be displayed.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p71_img02` (page 71, confidence 0.898)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p71_img02.png`

### Concept

Even after 0.5 km distance covered for particular trip, if Average fuel economy is displayed as ‘--.--‘, then take your vehicle to TATA MOTORS Authorized Service Centre.

## Knowledge

### Note

NOTE Use antiglare position only when necessary, as it reduces rear view clarity.

### Concept

Outer Rear View Mirrors (ORVM)

### Concept

You can adjust the outer rear view mir- rors manually by joy stick or remotely by knob. Adjust the outside rear view mir- rors to desired position.

### Note

NOTE Objects visible in mirror are actu- ally closer than they appear. Al- ways make sure of the actual dis- tance from the road users travel- ing behind by glancing over your shoulder.

### Concept

Motorized outer rear view mirrors (If equipped)

### Concept

The switch to adjust the motorized mir- rors is located on the driver’s door. You can adjust the mirrors when the ignition switch is in the “ACC” or “ON” position.

### Concept

To fold / unfold the ORVMs, keep the Se- lector switch in center position (i.e. nei- ther ‘L’ nor ‘R, position) and then toggle down.

### Concept

away), always engage in first gear.

### Specification

# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Front Fog Lamps (If applicable) Front fog lamp is located on front bumper. When visibility is poor due to fog, snow or rain, use the fog lamps which improves visibility as well as mak- ing it easier for other road users to see you.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p95_img04` (page 95, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p95_img04.png`

### Concept

For switching ‘ON’ the Fog lamps, either the Head Lamp or Parking lamp must be ‘ON’. Operate the front fog lamp switch pro- vided on fascia to ‘ON’ or ‘OFF’ the fog lamp.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p95_img00` (page 95, confidence 1.0)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p95_img00.png`

### Concept

An indicator on the switch will be illumi- nated when the front fog light is ‘ON’.

### Concept

Cornering feature: For front fog lamp cornering feature the Head Lamp must be ‘ON’. As you turn steering wheel to left or right, the corresponding fog lamp will automatically get ‘ON’. Rear Fog Lamps (If applica- ble)

Operate the rear fog lamp switch pro- vided on fascia to ‘ON’ or ‘OFF’ the fog lamp. An indicator on the switch will be illumi- nated when the rear fog light is ‘ON’.

Puddle / Ajar Lamp is provided on driver, front passenger & rear doors trim. It will be ON only when particular door is in open condition.

text:
# DASHBOARD AND FEATURES

## Knowledge

### Warning

Warning Lamps Color Indicator Remarks

### Warning

Speed limit warning indicator Amber

### Warning

Illuminates when ignition is switched ‘ON’ and goes ‘OFF’ after 4 Seconds. When the vehicle speed cross 80 km/hrs. then Speed limit Warning indicator turn ‘ON’ along with for every 2 minute chime shall be sounded (Audible warn- ing). If vehicle speed crosses 120 km/hrs. then along with Speed limit Warning In- dicator, Chime will start continuously ON till the vehicle speed is above 120 km/hr. If vehicle speed is between 80 km/hrs. to 120 km/hrs. then chime will be- come less frequent but Speed Limit warning Indicator will remains ‘ON’ con- tinuously. When the vehicle speed is reduce below 80 km/hrs. then Speed limit Warning Indicator along with chime will gets turns ‘OFF’.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p82_img00` (page 82, confidence 0.953)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p82_img00.png`
- Image: `doc_008_p82_img01` (page 82, confidence 0.826)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p82_img01.png`

### Warning

The warning light or symbol switches on constantly to indicate that the DPF needs to eliminate the trapped pollutants (particulate matter) through the re- generation process, it therefore does not indicate a malfunction. The warning light or symbol remain off during the entire DPF regeneration and light up only when driving conditions require the driver to be notified. To switch off the warning light or symbol, keep the car running until regeneration is complete (ideally at 3 rd gear, 60 km/hr. with engine speed over 2000 rpm). The process normally takes about 20 minutes. Note: Failure to be observed the appropriate procedure for a long distance when the DPF warning light comes ON, can cause the warning light (MIL) to come ON. In that case, please contact nearest TATA authorized service center to restore correct DPF operation.

### Concept

Vehicle Parking for Long Duration (Non - Use Maintenance)

### Concept

If you want to park your vehicle at one place for long duration, following care is to be taken:

### Concept

1. Park the vehicle in covered, dry and if possible well-ventilated premises. Engage a gear.

### Concept

2. Remove the battery terminal cables (first remove the cable from the neg- ative terminal). Ensure that battery is fully charged.

### Concept

3. Block the wheel or engage in the gear mode.

### Concept

4. Clean and protect the painted parts using protective wax.

### Concept

5. Clean and protect the shiny metal parts using commercially available special compounds.

### Concept

6. Sprinkle talcum powder on the rub- ber windscreen wiper and lift them off the glass.

### Concept

7. Wiper blade lifting sequence during cleaning / replacing, first lift front passenger side wiper blade, then driver side blade.

### Concept

8. Slightly open the windows.

### Concept

9. Cover the vehicle with a cloth or per- forated plastic sheet. Do not use sheets of imperforated plastic as they do not allow moisture on the ve- hicle body to evaporate.

### Specification

10. Inflate the tyres to 0.5 bar above the normal specified pressure and check it at regular intervals.

### Concept

11. Check the battery charge every six weeks.

### Concept

12. Do not drain the engine cooling sys- tem.

## Knowledge

### Concept

 Check the fuel level when the ve-

### Concept

### Warning

ing and sudden acceleration due to the movement of fuel in the tank, the fuel level display may fluctuate or the low fuel warning lamp may turns ON/OFF earlier or delayed than usual.

### Warning

If there is any fault in the system, Low fuel warning symbol will start blinking. Take your vehicle to the nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised service station.

### Concept

 At every ignition ON Fuel gauge

### Concept

will be displayed in place of “In- stantaneous Fuel consumption” bar graph irrespective of user se- lection screen.

### Concept

### Concept

Gauge” and “Instantaneous Fuel consumption” bar graph using SET and MODE button.  User selection to IFE screen will

### Concept

### Concept

screen is in “Instantaneous Fuel consumption” bar graph mode & if fuel gauge reduces to ¼ the tank level then LCD screen will automatically goes to Fuel Mode.

### Concept

When the ignition switch is in the “ON” position, this gauge indicates the engine coolant temperature.

### Concept

The indicator should stay within the nor- mal, acceptable temperature range be- tween “H” and “C”. If the indicator ap- proaches “H”, overheating is indicated by red bar.

  - File: `images/doc_008/p68_img00.png`

If the coolant temperature reading is very high, the engine coolant tempera- ture tell-tale flashes with an audible buzzer. In this case, stop the vehicle, switch ‘OFF’ the engine and cool it down for some time. Contact the nearest TATA MOTORS Authorised Service Centre im- mediately for rectification.

### Warning

WARNING The Red bar on high coolant tem- perature warning indicates over- heating that may damage the en- gine. Continuing to drive the vehi- cle when engine overheating is in- dicated can result in severe engine damage or fire.

# EMERGENCY AND BREAKDOWN ASSISTANCE

## Knowledge

### Concept

Loosen the nuts (as indicated) on the wheel in diagonal sequence. Do not un- screw the nuts completely before jacking the vehicle.

#### Visual References

- Image: `doc_008_p159_img00` (page 159, confidence 0.993)
  - File: `images/doc_008/p159_img00.png`

### Concept

 The jack is designed only to raise and hold the vehicle for a short time while a wheel is being changed. It is not suited for per- forming maintenance work un- der the vehicle.

### Concept

 Use the jack on level, hard ground. Avoid changing the wheel on uphill and downhill slopes. Apply wheel chokes if ve- hicle is parked on slope.

### Concept

 Engage the jack at the correct jacking location.

### Concept

 Before raising the vehicle, se- cure it from rolling away by apply- ing the parking brake and wheel chock. Gear shift knob to be en- gaged in first / reverse gear.

### Concept

 Do not use wooden blocks or similar objects as a jack under- lay.

### Concept

 Never place your hands and feet or lie under the raised vehicle when it is supported by the jack.

### Concept

 Never run the engine when the vehicle is supported by the jack and never allow passengers to remain in the vehicle.

### Procedure

 Never open or close a door or the tailgate when the vehicle is raised.

### Concept

Assemble the Jack handle and wheel spanner (as shown in jacking fig).

### Concept

Position the jack vertically and raise it by turning the jack handle clockwise until the jack sits completely on jacking point and the base of the jack lies evenly on the ground.

# STARTING AND DRIVING

## Knowledge

### Concept

### Concept

while decelerating, do coasting in gear and not in neutral or with clutch pedal pressed.  Consider using the car AC when you

### Concept

really require. Consider using lower blower speeds rather than higher for cooling as at higher blower speeds it consumes more electric power which is ultimately drawn from engine by burning fuel.  Avoid unnecessary extra electrical

### Concept

loading on the car.  Stop the engine wisely at traffic sig-

### Concept

nals. Switch ‘OFF’ the engine at the traffic signal only if the stoppage time is high (typically more than 30 sec).  While driving on highways, drive with

### Concept

windows closed. The more you open

### Concept

the windows the higher will be the re- sistance to the vehicle at higher speeds which will reduce the fuel ef- ficiency.  Do not over speed; follow the speed

### Concept

limits. More the speed, higher the ex- ternal resistance on the vehicle which will finally result into unneces- sary consumption of fuel.

### Concept

The more you look after the engine when it is new, the more satisfied you will be with its performance in the future.

### Concept

Avoid rapid acceleration and prolonged high speed running of the engine for the first 2,000 km.

### Concept

Do not exceed the following road speeds during running in period.

### Concept

1 15 2 30 3 45 4 60 5 80 6 100

### Concept

Avoid heavy loads, e.g. driving at full throttle, during this period. Change gears judiciously.

### Concept

While cruising, brief full-throttle acceler- ation within the limits of local traffic laws contributes to a good break-in. Wide- open throttle acceleration in low gear can be detrimental and should be avoided.

### Concept

Avoid excessive revving up of en- gine rpm. Do not keep engine at idling for long duration.

title: CAR CARE AND VALUE ADDED SERVICES
text:
# CAR CARE AND VALUE ADDED SERVICES

## Knowledge

### Concept

Your vehicle is subjected to many exter- nal influences such as climate, road con- ditions, industrial pollution and proximity to the sea. These conditions demand regular care of the vehicle body. Dirt, in- sects, bird droppings, oil, grease, fuel and stone chippings should be removed as soon as possible.

### Concept

Following these tips while washing your vehicle.

### Concept

1. Always wash your vehicle in shade and the surface is at room tempera- ture.

### Concept

2. Wash with mild vehicle wash soap like ‘Car Shampoo’ and use a soft bristle brush, sponge or soft cloth and rinse it frequently while washing to avoid scratches.

### Concept

3. To avoid scratches, please wear soft gloves. Remove finger rings, nails, wrist watch while washing.

### Concept

4. To remove stubborn stains and con- taminants like tar, use turpentine or cleaners like ‘Stain remover’ which are safe for paint surfaces.

### Concept

5. Avoid substances like petrol, diesel, kerosene, benzene, thinner or other solvents that cause damage to paint.

### Concept

6. Dry your vehicle thoroughly to pre- vent any damp spots.

### Concept

7. Rinse all surfaces thoroughly to pre- vent any traces of soap and other cleaners as this may lead to the for- mation of stains on the painted sur- face later.

### Specification

Do not direct high pressure washer fluid/ water jets (Pressure above 0.5 bar) at electrical devices and connecter during washing. This is to prevent malfunction / failure of electrical system due to water in- gress.

### Concept

After drying the vehicle, inspect it for chips and scratches that could allow cor- rosion to start. Apply touch up paint where necessary.

### Concept

text:
# 5. Hill Descent Control (HDC) (If equipped)

## Knowledge

### Concept

STARTING AND DRIVING

### Concept

On wet road or during light showers, “Aq- uaplaning” can occur. “Aquaplaning” is the loss of direct contact between the road surface and the vehicle’s tires due to a water film forming between them. Steering or braking the vehicle can be very difficult, and loss of control can oc- cur.

### Concept

The best advice is to slow down when the road is wet. The wet mode is designed for driving in the rain. It is characterized by having bet- ter traction and handling so you can ef- fectively and safety drive during these conditions.

### Note

NOTE If you have driven for a long time in wet road without braking, there may be a delayed reaction from the brakes when braking for the first time. You have to depress the brake pedal more firmly. Maintain a greater distance from the vehicle in front.

### Concept

Rough Road Mode optimizes the vehicle behavior for driving over rough road or other unyielding obstacles.

### Concept

Braking performance is also tuned to support Rough road surfaces as com- pared to other drive modes.

### Concept

System allows improved rough road per- formance to be more easily accessible to all customers specially novice or inexpe- rienced user.

### Note

NOTE Cautiously drive the vehicle on a rough road or off the road. Otherwise, the tires and wheels may be dam- aged. After driving those areas, in- spect the tires and wheels.

### Concept

ESP monitors driving stabil- ity and traction.

### Concept

If ESP detects that the vehicle is deviat- ing from the direction desired by the driver, one or more wheels are braked to stabilize the vehicle. The engine output is also modified to keep the vehicle on the desired course within physical limits. ESP assists the driver when pulling away on wet or slippery roads. ESP can also stabilize the vehicle during braking and acceleration.
